title: FIVE STARS with a couple caveats  Just ordered a second one for HARRY!
text:
Here's a pic of my Tortie, Rowan, by her carrier and cat cube (looks at over a dozen cat cubes, LOVE this one, link below) and Harry, my newest addition six month old.

THIS CARRIER was the BEST I could find and I looked at over a dozen.

This review is re the carrier, but had to mention the cube because they both LOVE IT and best one I found.

HARRY LOVES to sit on top of the cat cube shown in link below. ROWAN likes to be inside.

https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B093T71RFL/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
After literally looking at over a dozen cat carriers, soft with mesh and hard plastic, I decided upon this one because my MAIN concerns WERE SAFETY and SECURITY.

If you have a dog that chews or a cat that claws and chews, they can make quick work of a soft carrier.

Some of the hard plastic carriers also had some downsides of doors not being secure.

HERE is why I chose this one and my experience so far:

SECURITY AND STABILITY - THIS is bulky, yes, BUT it will easily keep my young cat secure. If you have to leave your pet in a crate, carrier for even minutes, you want to know it CAN'T get out. Just make sure you latch this door and your pet isn't going anywhere.

SIZE - My young cats are still growing, but this crate will EASILY accommodate them full grown. I got them each their own crate, even though as they're still fairly small, it COULD hold them both.

INSIDE FLOOR OF CRATE - it doesn't come with any type mat, which was fine with me, but it really needs something. My cat LOVES this bed (bought her two) and it easily fits in this crate! So I just use her second bed in it if she needs to go somewhere.
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07JXHNZGQ/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

AND one of the BEST parts, they don't seem to mind being in them. The tortie sometimes just goes in and lies down on it (I have put her small bed in it as the floor is just plastic, but she seems to LIKE the plastic floor).

CONS:

While pretty straight forward re attaching bolts, and I did it alone with any tools (71, female, not handy), if you have any arthritis in your hands, wouldn't hurt to have an extra pair of hands. It would also help putting this up on a table or large counter, rather than putting together on the floor.

The instructions aren't really useful, but that was ok, I figured it out. PUT the door in FIRST, which seems pretty obvious, but make sure you snap that in first, then work on the bolts.

BOTTOMLINE: GLAD I got it, would get it again, and if SECURITY is your biggest priority and you want for more than a five min trip to the vet where you will be with your pet the whole time (soft mesh carriers? really?), THIS could well be the best carrier for you, even though it is bulky. My cat's safety was my biggest priority in choosing her carrier.

title: A Bit Frustrating To Set Up At Times, But Nice Light
text:
I have been trying to get a decent set up for taking photos of jewelry and pottery for a business I am trying to get going. The smaller lights that I had were just not doing the trick. I got this one to help.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes with the tripod base separately packed in a box. The rest of the pieces come jammed in a foam tray. You have to put the cord together with the two pieces and the transformer box.

CONTROLS
This works great when it comes to changing the light brightness or the temperature. I have to say that the different lights respond very well.

CORD
The cord seems plenty long enough, but in some locations, you might need an extension cord.

ARMS
The arms and swivels are a bit frustrating at times to figure out. They can easily get turned too far one way and you have to undo them to get them to work right. It is not that big of a deal if you get the hang of it. It is handy to have the lights in one direction or two different ones too.

PERFORMANCE
The light is great for taking photos. I have tried it in many directions with different temperatures. I have to say this is one of the nicest lights I have used so far. It really gives precise lighting if you need it in a variety of directions.

STURDY
This tripod is very sturdy. It stands up well and does not wobble or seem unsteady at all. I am very happy with this.

HEAVY
This is a heavy light, no doubt.

CASE?
There is no case with this. I have to say I wish this came with a case. It would be a lot easier to tote around and protect if it had a case.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This light is a nice light. It works well and has a wide variety of settings and directions it can go. I find it sturdy and easy to work with, although I wish it had a case.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This really needs a case to protect it and carry it around. Other than that (which is why I removed a star) I think this light performs very well and I love it. Now I just need a better camera than the one I wasted hundreds of dollars on that is lousy.

title: Will not last
text:
I purchased this [[ASIN:B004PB8SRM Tetra 77850 Whisper Air Pump, upto 100-Gallon]] last December. This pump was always a bit loud but it grew to be an annoyance. Our tank is located in our living room and I got fed up with having to turn the TV volume up to drown out the pump. The pump worked for its purposes at first. After about three months, the pump no longer could provide my bubble bar and treasure chest with enough air.. the bar was barely a trickle and the chest hardly ever moved. Yes, I did check my gang valve. The problem was not with my gang valve. So, with the noise and the inability to control the flow, I finally decided to replace my Tetra with something different.

I purchased the [[ASIN:B0013LN10Q EcoPlus 2 Air Pump, 2 Outlets]] two weeks ago and I could not be more pleased. It is decibels quieter and is actually more powerful. I have one 18" submersed bubble bar and one treasure chest in my 20 gallon tank. The lines are run to a gang valve and then a line runs to the pump. This pump is capable of supplying both the bar and chest with the proper amount of flow on the lowest setting. My old Tetra pump had no flow setting control - I considered this and its noise its two downfalls for me and my setup.

I really like the setting control knob on the top of the pump, although I do not see myself needing to turn it up from the lowest setting since with my current setup turning the knob any higher causes my treasure chest to darn near float. LOL! This pump is certainly a very nice device that I foresee lasting me quite some time. When it does come time for a replacement, I will not hesitate to purchase another EcoPlus.

title: Solid Drive Enclosure; Works with Windows and Linux
text:
Drive carriers and enclosures are a convenient method for converting internally mounted drives to USB connectivity. This particular enclosure is for 2.5" SATA drives and supports USB 3.0 speeds. So far I have gotten excellent results with it and am pleased with it.

This is a tool-free device; no screwdriver or wrench is required to open this enclosure or install a drive in it. The cover slides off with a little pressure to expose the plug for the drive and the drive simply pops in. In the box is a foam pad that attached to drives that are not thick enough for a solid fit when the cover is replaced. Once assembled with a drive, this is a solid and compact enclosure that feels a lot like a Passport drive though it looks a lot nicer and feels a little more substantial.

I plugged the drive into a machine running Windows 8 and the system immediately recognized the drive and the partitions on it. I was able to use the drive without issue.

I tried a couple of different configurations for accessing this drive under Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL). First, I tried to access it under RHEL running in a virtual machine. I was unable to get the hypervisor to expose the drive to the OS which is a configuration issue, not a compatibility issue. To determine this for sure, I plugged the drive into a machine that runs RHEL natively with the GNOME desktop. RHEL immediately recognized the drive and opened a Nautilus window with the filesystems on each partition exposed and I was able to navigate the filesystems without any issues. I could not ask for better results.

I put a 500GB SDD in this enclosure and plugged it into a USB 3.0 port and got insane speeds. I could not be happier.

This is a great drive enclosure for 2.5" drives and it works great under Windows as well as under Linux. For the price, this is a great enclosure that works very well.

title: Superb protection
text:
I received this as a free review sample. Although it's designed for notebooks, I am using it for my 10.1 inch tablet and for that it's perfect.

One of the main reasons why I rated this so highly is the protection that it affords. Part of the reason why it's so slim and light, yet protects so will is the interior has an arrangement of raised, circular shapes. They provide cushioning on both sides of the interior. They also greatly reduce shock in the event of a fall. I tested that by taking a functioning - but no longer used - Acer Aspire One notebook and dropping it from waist level inside this bag on a hard floor. There was no physical damage to the exterior of the Acer and it powered up and operated normally.

The exterior of the bag has a spongy feel that also diminished shock, so the protection is twofold. Other features I love are the heavy duty seams and zippers, and even the color scheme. On the latter, there is enough red to catch my eye when I am packing my gear and doing a visual scan to make sure I did not leave anything behind. I have 'forgotten' black cases in the past, but this one is hard to miss.

Do be aware that there is a slight chemical odor to this bag when you first unpack it. That will go away in a day or less, but it's there and you need to know about it before you make your final purchase decision. Also carefully read the part of the product description that states, ' If your laptop screen size is 14 inches, and the maximum thickness greater than 28mm (0.11"), please do not select this bag.' That will save you some frustration if your laptop is too large for this bag.

title: Sleek design, nifty tech, and terrific sound quality...
text:
Replacing my altec lansing speakers from the early 2000's. Honestly, I'm not an audiophile. My altec speakers were pretty good speakers too, and I can't tell the difference. My upgrade is simply cosmetics. This logitech set is black and sleek, looks more modern. My altec speakers were grayish, very early 2000's design.

I like the nifty wireless controller that looks like a little echo dot, but it's smaller. So coming from speakers in the early 2000's, my first question was.. Can this function like old school speakers if I don't care for all the tech? So I simply used the 3.5mm connection method from my dell to the logitech, but there was NO SOUND. So you have to at least power up the wireless controller for the first time. Because under the controller is a button to switch from bluetooth to wired. Press the WIRE option, and you will then get audio. After this, if you remove the batteries and take away the wireless controller, the speakers will continue to work as 3.5mm connected speaker. You just have to turn on the wireless controller on the initial set-up. So this is good. My concern was what if the wireless controller is lost or damaged? If that happens, then you would like the speakers to go on like old school speakers connected simply by 3.5mm. So I'm happy to report, this will function without the wireless controller module. I'm not even sure turning on the wireless controller in the initial set-up is absolutely required. Your PC my pick-up sound the moment you plug in the 3.5mm jack. For me, I had to turn on the wireless controller during the initial set-up.

Another thing I wondered is if I connect a bluetooth device, say my smartphone, to these speakers, then disconnect, will the speakers automatically revert back to wired? The answer is no. To connect to a bluetooth device, you have to press the bluetooth pairing button under the wireless controller, and it will stay in this mode even after you disconnect. You have to press the "wire" button to get back to 3.5mm.

One more thing, the left and right speakers have 2 slots in the back to insert the stand. So you can configure it to stand vertically or horizontally. Conclusion... I love the sound, the sleek design and the technology. 5-Stars.

title: An great game, with limited appeal
text:
I agree with many of the other reviewers on this page. I am talking exclusively about the single player campaign, which I have managed to get a third of the way through. Dungeon Siege does a number of things very well - graphics and simplified character creation - while sacrificing character depth, interaction, and basically everything else that makes a roleplaying game special.
Good stuff: (1) There were points at which the graphics made me pause to admire the landscape - in particular the trees swaying in a light drizzle and fog falling off the walls of ice caves. All of this requires some hardware of course. I bought the game when I had a 600 mHz iBook with 256 MB RAM and a 16bit graphics card, but recently had it replaced with a 933 mHz iBook (I love the things) with 640 MB RAM and a 32bit card. On the first computer I turned everything to low resolution and got rid of the object detail and particle effects and the game was doable. On my current computer, I've maxed all the settings and the game consistently stuttered only during a snowstorm, where I guess all the falling snowflakes pushed the limits. Considering that the graphics are a major draw, if your computer can't handle them you might want to think twice about buying this game. (2) The system of character creation is simplicity itself. At the beginning you decide what your character looks like, and the game starts. Your three abilities (Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence) and four skills (Melee, Ranged weapons, Nature magic, Combat magic) all start at the same low level. They are raised by doing related things, so regularly casting a fireball raises Combat Magic, which in turn raises Intelligence, and higher intelligence gives the character more mana points to cast spells. It's so simple that it quickly fades into the background of the game, and makes Dungeon Siege approachable especially for players who don't want entire lists of abilities, skills, and derived charts to worry themselves with. (3) No upload time! Wherever the characters go there is a never a pause while the new area is uploaded, which makes gameplay one continuous experience. Big "Oooooh!" factor here. (4) Great inventory control. With a single click, the computer will organize the inventory of a character. There's a spell which turns an item of loot into gold, at a slight cost. And the best innovation of any game ever - mules! Honest to the maker four footed mules that you can load with all the loot.
Bad stuff: (1) Almost entirely linear play. There are a few side areas to wander into but the game is mostly (journey during which you kill everything in sight) followed by (safe place where you can buy and sell supplies/companions/mules) followed by (another journey of death), etc. (2) Simplified characters. I'm one of those people who likes the sub-charts of derived scores as part of my character, and finds the decision about whether or not to raise my Blacksmithing skill gripping. There's not enough detail and control of your character. (3) Storyline essentially disappears early on. The game starts with a quest to tell the authorities about a new danger, but the plot is quickly abandoned for a combat free-for all. Despite talk about your character being the hero of the land, it is possible to dismiss your character and replace him/her with a hired mercenary!
I'm not against combat-fests and I really enjoyed Diablo, but I think what makes this game particularly uninspiring is its puzzling lack of attitude, or what might be called soul. Even really bad games, which Dungeon Siege is not, usually have someone who was inspired to make it and the maker's enthusiasm comes through somewhere in the game. I don't know if the speculation about it being because it is a Microsoft product are correct, but in the end there doesn't seem to be anything to this game except pretty images, good programming and killing stuff, which may be enough for some players.

title: Very quiet, has adjustable flow
text:
I have this installed on a 5.5 gallon, standard tank.

This filter, while is was a bit strong for my old betta, is perfect for the new guy, now that my other passed away. (In other words, great for a healthy fish, not so much for an elderly fish.)

It is very nearly silent, which I appreciate. I like to hear a little bit of the water movement, but I'm not too fond of the motor noise in filters.

One of my few dislikes is the very short intake tube. I would like to have the option of extending it another 2". It's also not very efficient at getting debris out of the water after a water change.

It does have an adjustable flow. Again nice, but there's not a whole lot of difference between high and low. I'd like to turn it down to the minimum during feeding time, but "low" is still a strong enough flow to sink the floating pellets in a hurry. (It's just not strong enough to pull them into the intake tube.)

Beyond those little things, I do think it's a little overpriced, but then again, I have 5 other filters sitting around now and returned two ohers that couldn't be used/didn't work in that tank.

Overall, I'm pleased with this, and will probably buy another one or two to keep on hand for small tanks.

title: Only Partial Blackout for Person Sitting Alongside Leaning In
text:
This 3M EASY-ON PRIVACY FILTER FOR IPAD2 offers fairly decent privacy, but it doesn't black out your screen for someone standing behind you (looking over your shoulder) or black out the screen completely for someone sitting beside you and leaning in. It offers privacy for the vertical (portrait) iPad position only--which is actually a nice feature, since you can hold your iPad up in the horizontal (landscape) position to share with anyone and everyone nearby without removing the filter.

Installation is extremely simple. You stick small adhesive patches on each of the four corners of the stiff plastic filter, then gently stick the filter onto your iPad. (Check to make sure you have an iPad 2 or 3rd/4th generation iPad, because the cutouts for the home screen button and front-facing camera must match up.) The filter goes on bubble-free, without any need for a cardboard "squeegee".

The privacy filter is easy to remove. The kit includes a heavy plastic sleeve for storing the filter after you've added the corner stickers, and also includes four extra corner stickers for when the first set of stickers wears out. You need to use some care when removing the filter: on my first attempt, three of the sticky corners stayed on the iPad. Probably that was because I applied the filter on top of existing screen protector film and pressed the corners down firmly. On my second application, I pressed the corners down quite gently, and the stickers stayed on the filter when I removed it for the second time.

Because the privacy filter doesn't completely black out the screen when someone is sitting close by you, I rate it at 4 stars ("I like it" on the official Amazon scale).

title: Well worth the money to get better performance
text:
I bought this camera to replace one of those cheap $20 cameras with the LEDs on the front. While the old cheap camera will prove if a car pulled out in front of you or if the light was green when you drove through the intersection, it couldn't give you more detail than that.

This DVR has crystal clear true 1080p video that puts the cheap camera to shame. This may have cost 3x what I paid for the cheap camera, but the image is 10x better. This camera has great low light image quality. Some will say that the image is noisy, but that is what you get with any digital camera that costs under $1,000. My cheap one was worthless in the dark. The 8GB micro SD card that was included was made by Samsung and so far holds about 1 1/2 hours before being written over. (Recording at 1080p, 3 minute files and using Wide Dynamic Range) The camera was ready to go right out of the box. All I had to do was change the date and time. The manual was well written and easy to understand. The suction mount holds tight and the ball head can be articulated to any position you need. The power cord was plenty long enough to hide it and run it in the overhead, down the passenger side and back to the 12v power supply in the middle console.

As with anything in life, you get what you pay for and you have to balance what you want with what you can afford. As I said before, a $20 camera will tell you if a blurry car pulled out in front of you during the day. But this camera will show you if they were on the phone.

Answers to common questions;

Q: Is this camera HD?
A: Yes the camera records in 1080p

Q: Does the camera turn itself on and off automatically?
A: Yes the camera turns on when the car starts and turns back off 10-15 seconds after the car shuts down. As long as you have it plugged into a 12v outlet that is only powered when the car is on. If the outlet is always on even when the car is off, the camera will not shut down unless you turn it off or remove the plug.

Q: How long can it record, what happens when it runs out of memory?
A: At 1080p, the highest setting the included 8GB card will hold between 1 1/2 hours worth of video. Once it reaches capacity, the oldest video file will be deleted to make room for the new file.

Q: How can I view/save files on my computer?
A: Remove the Micro SD card from the side of the camera and insert it into the included USB micro SD card adapter and insert it into your computer. Or if you want you can always take down the entire camera and plug it in to your computer using a mini USB cable.

Q: Can you read license plates?
A: Yes, but only until the cars reach about 20' away. Since the camera is a wide angle lens, it becomes hard to read. All Car DVRs suffer from this because they have wide angle lenses. I can read plates of cars that pass me too.

That being said, the documentation that comes with the game is THE PITS. It tells only the most
basic information, things you automatically know if you have ever played any sort of electronic game.
The game itself has a few notes that show up as a pop-up screen while you are playing.
It is okay if you memorize everything, but I know I couldn't do it all!

My biggest complaint is that the MANUAL should tell you what all those bloomin' power-ups on the
side actually do! It doesn't. When you use one, it moves so quickly, you can't really tell what it
did. I finally got it that the globe-type ball will destroy something like 11 tiles around whereever
you place it. The hourglass gives you an unknown additional amount of time to complete the level.

The rest? I don't know - they go too fast - I can't follow them.
The flame burns some icons up, but which ones? I don't know.
The purple globe does something, but no clue what.
And on it goes...
So, using them strategically is really hard!

I think a game is a lot more fun when it is explained thoroughly so I know what the goal
actually is - not a random stab at completion.

I am in the process of going through the game again under a diff ID to write things
down as the screens pop up. Seriously, how hard would that have been for the developers to do?!?
Basic documentation of the game, and it is missing.

It was okay, but never pay a huge amount for the game, and know that it is going to be
a stab in the dark the first time through.

title: It will turn your aquarium orange - not good when it starts killing fish
text: I have six DoJo Loaches (yes I am crazy about them) in a 50 gallon tank and they are all about 1 foot long and still growing so they will get their own 100 gallon tank in the next month or two (it's on order),  If you've ever had more than one DoJo you'll quickly realize these are the toddlers of the freshwater fish community.  They also can jump out of the tank and be out of it for more than an hour and still survive.  Impressive but you need a screen on top of your tank.  Anyway.  I threw some of these in and they went for them like a pack of piranhas but as far as I could tell they just chewed them up and spit them all out because i had a tankful of wafers and the water turned ORANGE.  It was late (like 2 am) and I'm trying to decide what to do when one of the first Rainbow fish dies, then the second and a third.  I grabbed my biggest net and managed to get all but one or two of the rainbow fish out and moved to my Gourami tank - went back and got the rest of them on the second trip so no more died,  I ended up doing nearly a complete water change at 2 am.  So it's hard to tell if they didn't like them or they were just full but wanted to chew on something but whatever is in these wafers polutes the water badly.  None of the DoJo's died but I've had them jump out of their tank and not discover them for more than an hour - somebody told me they have 4 swimbladders so they can hold lots of air before they diedl  Now I'm seeing little squabbles between my Rainbow fish and the Gourami - I never realized how assertive the rainbow fish are but after living with a a pack of DoJo's for the last 6 months I think they've become easily adjusted.  Once I get the 100 gallon tank, I'll move the Rainbows and Gourami to the 50 gallon tank the DoJo's currently live in,  So they'll have a lot of room to spread out and away from each other.  So far nobody has gotten hurt but i am missing a Tommasi Loach (very rare) that usually keeps hidden in a cave and I have to force him out during water changes - now I can't find him  at all and it's really broken my heart.  I never liked the rainbow fish from the moment I got them - they are just so boring and only a few are colorful compared to my very sedate but beautiful dwarf Gourami - so I may see if one of the local fish stores will take them.  UPDATE:  Why did I not read my own reviews again and I bought these.  This time for 5 plecos since they  are supposed to like them.  Like my DoJo, they enjoy chewing them up into a powder and then just leaving it alone.  The fish don't seem interested eiither - so I then have several piles of bright orange powder on the botton of my tank that's going to raise an already problematic ammonia problem.  The leftovers get siphoned out today and I'll never use them again.  At least nobody died (I fed a smaller quantity and the Rainbow fish have all died.  And this time I didn't feed enough to turn the water orange - but I'll have to wait for the water change to see if it goes orange then.  Please avoid these, it looks like all ingredients except the orange dye are fine.

title: Pros And Cons For My 2.5 tank (I Have A Lot Of Fish Experience)
text:
I have quite a few tanks. One thing I have been wanting is a decent 24 hour cycle light which fits my smallest tanks- a 2.5 nano tank.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a box which has a remote box built in line with the cord and plug. The remote is easier to access if you have an outlet strip up near the tank where you can see it easily. With a tank that has outlet strips in a difficult spot to see, this can be an issue when you want to glance at the settings.

SIDE HOOKS
The side hooks on the light slide in and out and they can come right out of the light if you pull too hard. That is not an issue unless you have a pet or child who might accidentally pull on them (or a stupid fish keeper on a bad day who we won't discuss right now.. LOL)

MY SET UP
I have a 2.5 nano tank set up with chili rasboras and blue eyed rainbow fish- the tiny ones. I have a single filter (only tank I have with one if I remember correctly) and some wood and simple moss on the tree inside.

HOW THIS WORKS
I set this at 8 am for the 24 setting at 8am. It goes on pretty bright and then works through a 24 hour cycle. IT does stay blue a long time at night- way after all of the other lights have gone dark. I have set my own 24 hour lights to get dark by 10PM or so. The dark period is not awfully long because at 6am it is getting light again.

PERFORMANCE
I like the lights. They seem a bit bright at times, or too long in duration, but honestly, the plants are growing better minus the overgrowth of algae I was having before. So, that is a good thing. Also, the fish seem more lively and active than when I had a simple daylight that went on and off every day.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although I wish I could make the night rotation longer with no lights on at all, as this is, it is the best light I have had for my nano tank ever so I like it.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I would like it better if it had a little longer dark period at night. Otherwise, it is a decent light and my plants are doing well as are my fish. And it fits my 2.5 gallon tank perfectly. I would by another one.

title: This 12.9" iPad Pro provides me with the great viewing experience I was looking for and is intuitive to use
text:
My boyfriend is an Apple lover and I prefer Android. I have a Google Nexus 7 that I love, but it's small. However, it was the iPad's 12.9" display that sold me on this version and the ease of setup and use that sold me on the iPad in general. Apple's reputation also sealed the deal.

When doing a side-by-side comparison, I seriously considered the 9.7" iPad Pro with its wide color and true tone display because that offers a richer viewing experience. Also, the 12-megapixel camera of the 9.7" produces more vibrant photos with better resolution than the 8-megapixel pictures taken with this 12.9" iPad Pro. Nevertheless, the large screen on this 12.9" is best for me. Portability was not an issue because I got this for home use to watch videos and to easily type on the larger virtual keyboard. I've had it for over one month now and love it. Set-up was a cinch. Battery power is also excellent and lasts for over 10 hours.

The one negative that I noticed is that Apple does everything in its power to control their users. For instance, I had to wipe out the "sent from iPad notice" when sending an email as I do not want to freely advertise for them. I also dislike how all my boyfriend's iPhone messages that use to go to my Gmail account, now landed only in iMessage on my iPad and none went to Gmail. At first I thought he was mistaken when he told me he was sending me messages and I no longer got them until I discovered them a day later on the iPad. This required I only use the iPad until we both figured out how to correct that. Nevertheless, I consider this a small annoying price to pay for what is a user friendly device that provides a rewarding viewing experience.

In addition to this iPad, I decided to purchase the [[ASIN:B008MOHLVC amPen hybrid stylus ]] instead of the [[ASIN:B016NY7784 Apple Pencil]] because I did not need the precision of the pencil. Also, since I am periodically using this for watching videos, I purchased the [[ASIN:B00PB2BF56 ZUGU CASE Prodigy Exec Thin Wake / Sleep Stand Protective Case]] which fits it perfectly and props the tablet up as high or low to the surface of my desk as I want it. Note that the ZUGU case will not work with the [[ASIN:B0186RZAWQ Apple Smart Keyboard]]; this keyboard acts like its own case. Thankfully, the virtual keyboard was enough for me.

Eventually, I'll teach myself more about my iPad via the online manual I downloaded. I love it so much that if my Google Nexus ever fails, I might just purchase the more portable 9.7" iPad Pro for when I want to carry around a tablet (which is infrequently).

I had MVC3 and traded it in and waited for UMVC3 and I completely wasted my time and money. Hard core fighting gamers will probably love this game, but I consider myself a casual to moderate fighting gamer. Here's the pros and cons:

Pros:
-Graphics are pretty cool and stylistic

Cons:
-Online mode is supposed to match you up with people your own skill, however I'm noticing many "beginners" and "rookies" are kicking my butt. Now, it's about landing that initial strike (which is good), but then being rewarded for it by doing almost unlimited air combos and taking all of your opponents energy for one initial hit. One opponent used Magento and took almost all my life with one consistant air combo. Go back to a thinking man's fighting game and not fast fingers and NO EXPLOITS. Knocking an opponent into the air and then slamming them back to the ground is fine, but this is just ridiculous.
-You can't quit an online match before it begins. This is especially annoying when you are put up against a way higher ranked player than you and you can't exit.
-Loading and saving. If this game isn't loading it's saving. If it isn't saving, it's loading.

I could go on and on about the game's cons, but unless you're a hard core fighting gamer, than stay clear away from this game. I am trading in my copy for Batman Arkham City or anything else really.

title: An excellent mouse with one major design flaw
text:
I love almost everything about the EC1 -- it's a comfortable, ergonomic, understated gaming mouse with driverless operation/configuration and exceptional accuracy. I used it for both work and competitive FPS -- it does not look out of place in the office, lacking the pervasive "gaming" aesthetic that is impossible to avoid these days, but performs better than other brands' rainbow-blaring peripherals.

There is only one problem: the side button actuation mechanism is inherently unreliable. This is a problem for me -- I bind mouse 4/5 for PTT for in-game comms, and an intense squeeze during a chaotic round will inevitably break it.

I first bought an EC1-A in 2018, and it lasted about a year and a half before one of the side button actuators snapped. I opened it up and discovered this plastic mechanism is designed to flex to transfer force from the horizontally-oriented button to the microswitch, which is mounted upright on the PCB. I bought an identical replacement in late 2019 and it didn't even last a year before the same thing happened.

I couldn't find a replacement part, but at least I was able to make a repair with epoxy. However, knowing the design will inherently cause it to fail once again, I hopefully purchased this new EC1; my thought was that they would have changed the mechanism or at least upgraded the materials. Six months later, it has suffered the same failure. I'm sad to say that as much as I love these mice, I'm going to have to start looking to other manufacturers. Should Zowie ever redesign the side button mechanism, I'll be coming back in a heartbeat.

title: Comes with EVERYTHING! But the average cell phone has better IQ
text:
Ok, to be fair I work with cameras for a living. I wasn't expecting this to compete with my cinema cameras or even popular DSLRs for video, but I was expecting it to at least hold up to the standards people are expecting from cell phone cameras these days. It doesn't. Aside from filling a 4K frame, there aren't a lot of positives to say about the video quality.
To be fair, this has a LOT of advantages over using a cell phone. Recording for long lengths of time onto an SD card is a big plus, not the mention the ability to mount it to a standard tripod and have accessories like a mic and light attached to the body (which are all included!). It comes with a wide angle lens (that is oddly called "macro", but no- it's not for macro shots, its for going wider) which screws on to the front, as well as a handle mounting bracket, an LED light and a microphone. It even comes with a 64GB card, a spare battery, and not one but TWO useful carrying cases (a large one for everything, and a smaller one for just the camera solo). But that's about all the positives I can say about it. If you are outside with a lot of light, you can get decent shots, but this isn't a zoom lens, the zoom is digital only. You can go wide with the external lens or just stay at a fixed medium without it. So no closeup shots for soccer moms. The dynamic range when using it indoors was pretty bad, worse than your average mid-range cell phone. Forget about low light. But that's ok, because the ergonomics of a camera make it better than a cell phone, right?
Well, sorta. Holding it with the strap and the flip out screen is nice. But the UI is confusing, it's hard to go back and watch clips you took because everything is kind of sluggish and not intuitive- once we went past the first page of recorded clips, it was really difficult to move to the next page without accidentally clicking and opening a clip for playback. It just feels really laggy to navigate. Then there's the mic input... it's actually a proprietary plug that goes into the charging/USB plug, and gives you a pigtail for USB on one side and a mic input jack on the other. Odd, considering it COMES with a mic, you'd think it would have an input directly on the body. But no, just this weird mess of wires. Everything about this feels like jumping through a hoop to make it do what you want, and at the end of the day you have to wonder if you couldn't just be better off getting a mic adapter for the cellphone you already own and putting it in one of those holster cages.
Speaking of cell phones, this does have an app which supposedly lets you remotely control and perhaps even copy files from it, but I didn't get that far. I tried to install the app but then gave up when I decided I didn't want to grant this all the permissions it wanted from my personal phone. And I didn't think the video quality was worth it either.
Oddly enough, I kind of like the accessories it comes with. The LED light is pretty nice, the mic isn't terrible either. But for the money, I feel like I would have rather skipped those accessories and just gotten a better camera for a little bit more. It feels almost like they realized this camera was a hard sell so they beefed it up with lots of a accessories for the price.
In conclusion, you DO get a lot of accessories for the money. It's not the worst camera I've ever used, and you can't really get a set with everything you need for any less so I'd say it's worth at least 3 stars for being a functional kit. But I can't really imagine a scenario that I would recommend it.

title: Wholesome Treats for Your Dog
text:
Sharing my house with a pair of dogs means having to make special adjustments to my schedule. It also means having to have plenty of food and treats on hand but I don’t want to feed my dogs just anything. I want the food and treats they eat to contain at least a minimal amount of nutritional value and quality ingredients. The Pioneer Woman Grain Free All-Natural Dog Treats measure up to these standards.

These treats are soft and chewy and the ingredient list is short and simple. Chicken is the number one ingredient and beyond that, there are only a handful of other ingredients. title: Excellent use of storage space, great construction and innovative features (but one shortcoming)
text:
I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I docked it a star is the active tablet window needs improvement (and that could have been one of the stand-out features if properly designed.) Here is the problem: it's the perfect size for an iPad Air 2, but could not accommodate my Tab 2 10.1 inch tablet. It did hold my Samsung Tab Pro 8.4 (even in an Otterbox Defender case). The vinyl window wrinkles and also reduces sensitivity when you interact with your tablet.

If the active tablet window is unimportant to you, then the rest of this backpack is a winner. Pairing my phone to the bluetooth speakers was as simple as flipping a switch and scanning for it on my phone's settings. And the speakers are loud with better than expected sound quality. I was pleased with that - some thought went into the speakers.

The padding is more than ample for protecting electronics, and there are sufficient pockets for the geekiest geek. What I like, though, is the storage areas are not overly complex. I own a Booq bag that is a storage dream come true, but almost requires a photographic memory to remember were all of the pockets are. This one is designed much simpler, but still efficient and effective.

Construction (except for the active tablet window) is first rate. The tablet window is marred by a difficult zipper, whereas all of the other zippers on this bag are sturdier and smooth. The outer fabric seems tough (I have not had it long enough to make any claims beyond that), and all of the seams are reinforced, straight and tight.

It's very comfortable and can be adjusted to evenly distribute the weight of a fully loaded pack. Considering that the bag itself is somewhat heavy this is a major plus for me.

I do want to note one thing about the backup battery: it is rated at (and stores) the full 4000mAh. However, like all batteries using this one's technology it's only 70% efficient, so expect about 2800mAh of usable capacity. That is not a flaw in this bag, but a reality that I wanted to point out so your expectations are properly set.

Overall, this is a well made bag with some innovative features (battery back-up and bluetooth speakers). If the active tablet window is not an important feature it's definitely worth considering. This one will be replacing my Booq because the storage is there without the complexity.

title: I Wish I Had These Sooner!
text:
For my uses, these are great. They were very well packaged and secure for shipping. The box is very nice and sturdy, lined with foam. I need to hear the environment around me. This has been an issue with previous earbuds. Commercials between videos or songs can get so loud! That is the deal-breaker for me, as it's a safety issue. These do not get too loud, even on the loudest setting, so I am able to remain safe. I don't have an issue hearing the sounds coming from the buds, but I'm not in high-traffic outdoor areas regularly either. My ear canals are unusually small for an adult. I was afraid these may be too-big, but they are snug. Any bigger and it may have been an issue. I used the smaller of the plastic tips. Over the ear designs are the only ones that have ever worked for me. I did look at some other models in the past, but I found them a bit more expensive than I felt justified to spend unknowing how well they may work for me. However, knowing how well these work, I find them to be a really great value and would have purchased them before if I had known how well they worked. It was only by chance they were up for review and I had been seeking a replacement on my old pair that I've been using for the past few years.

The Bluetooth is nice. I have a simple cell phone. It only took asking my phone to connect to work. It was the easiest that I have ever had with connecting anything Bluetooth to my phone. I liked this as I'm not the most savvy at using Bluetooth electronics. If I can do it, anyone can.

I'm not great at using the buttons as they are really sensors on the flat-side of the body on the earbuds. I'm getting used to it but they are touch sensitive and there is a correct spot and amount of pressure that works best. I'm still getting a feel for it and there is a slight delay, so it's very easy to double-tap. The included booklet has been helpful to learn to use these straight out of the package.

Sometimes I get down on the floor at the gym to use the foam rollers and stretches, other times I'm using them in the car to take calls. I've tried them at work as well. Every scenario has worked well for me. I really do wish I've had these before. Sometimes while getting my breaks at work, I would want to listen to things from my phone, but didn't want to risk disturbing my co-workers with some of the news and hobby related videos I enjoy. I asked a few co-workers if they could hear my earbud noise, they could not.

The case is very easy to use as well and fits easily into my pockets. I'm a lady, so my pockets are not always very generously sized. It charges very quickly, and I've not found myself running out of charge. I cannot speak on the long-term durability for this as they are new. If/when I experience any issues with the charge, I will be sure to post an update.

In summary, these would be better for users that need to hear their surroundings for safety. For those that want extreme high volume, they may not be as happy. They stay on my ears securely and the case works very well. I'm pleasantly surprised how well I like these and hope that they are durable since they are working so well for me.

Thanks for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.

title: Call of Duty 4-ever!
text:
Should a game's rating be punished if it's basically just an update of something that's already been done? I don't think so. If you like a good First Person Shooter, look no further than the Call of Duty series...whether it's Infinity Ward's [[ASIN:B000TG72TM Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare]] or Treyarch's Call of Duty: World at War...or both!...you won't soon get sick of storming the plethora of battle fields that the games have to offer on and off line.

World at War is a really fun game with extremely intense battle sequences. And an upside to World at War over Modern Warfare is that offline, split screen, campaign co-op is available so that you can play with friends or family.

In single player Campaign mode, you're back in WWII with a team of characters that are your band of AI brothers. I think that the AI was a little better in Modern Warfare, because in Modern Warfare there were some missions that you could rely on the AI of your squad to get you through; in World at War you're mostly on point and there aren't any chapters that you can breeze right through without firing your weapon(s).

As some familiar voices command you through (like Kiefer Sutherland), you fight your way through some intense chapters. The weapons aren't as good as the ones in Modern Warfare, but that was to be expected going back to WWII. However, the World at War weapons are a huge improvement over what was offered in [[ASIN:B000GA73O0 Call of Duty 3]] (including a flame thrower!!!). You're mostly shooting whichever WWII weapon you happen to have picked up (mostly from dead soldiers on the ground) along your objective route. Your objectives that guide you along are updated regularly as you complete each task throughout each chapter. And some of those tasks are brutal.

All of the chapters are really fun, but some of the chapters are really difficult. The early chapters are designed more to challenge you to correctly navigate yourself and your team to the correct objective and get a feel for the weaponry, but World at War gets progressively more fun and difficult at the same time.

Online multiplayer play is a different world, and very similar to Modern Warfare...you'd almost think that Infinity Ward and Treyarch were the same company; Activision did a great job in not fixing a system that wasn't broken for online play. No AI brothers online...just your fellow gamers. You'd better have your FPS skills honed if you think that you'll beat some of the online players. The more you play, the higher you rank allowing you to unlock more (fine tuned) weapons. Like Modern Warfare, once you level up to the best weapons and perks, the game gives you the opportunity to go "Prestige", meaning if you start back from level one you can level up all over again and be rewarded with a badge of honor and another slot to create a class of weapons / perks. Not me, pal. Unlike Modern Warfare, once I get to the highest level in my first level-up, I'm staying there for World at War; you don't get the flame thrower until the highest level, and I'm not turning that in after only one level of play...no way, man!

World at War even throws a multiplayer game modes at you that weren't available in Modern Warfare (like War and Capture the Flag).

Oh, and how can I not mention World at War's online co-op mode? I haven't played the campaign mode in co-op online; I have enough fun with my kids offline doing that. BUT...the online co-op mode of Nazi Zombies is a BLAST!!! You're holed up in one of the buildings familiar enough from one of the multiplayer maps. Outside hordes of zombies attempt to break through the boarded up windows and doors to get in and tear you up. It's your job to rebuild the barriers on the windows and take the zombies out before they can get in and get you. You'll also need to revive your teammates if they get taken down by a zombie. The room is 4-player max, and if one of your mates goes down you'd better revive him if you expect to survive yourself. Nazi Zombies mode is a real team effort, and it's as addictive as multi-player! The downside (as of this writing) of zombie mode is that there's only one map to play on (and it's only unlocked if you finish the single player campaign).

So all in all Call of Duty: World at War is major fun. I suggest that anyone with a PS3 NOT miss out on this super-fun, FPS game. Add it to your cart before [[ASIN:B000FQBF1M Killzone 2]] comes out and takes up all of your time.

The Dynabook Protege X30L-J1331 is great.  
It is ultra lightweight. Weighs about 2 pounds.

 There is also a port for earphones and it is Bluetooth capable.
And I really like the super long cord. It is long enough to move around without worrying about it becoming disconnected.  
There is also a fingerprint reader located on the computer.
 One feature that takes a little getting use to is the left and right mouse buttons sit at the top of the trackpad versus at the bottom. This is a little inconvenient and will take some getting use too.

It has an 11th generation intel core processor with 8GB of memory and a 256 GB  hard drive.
There is a cover that slides over the camera. A nice feature that adds some security.  The laptop itself is a dark blue and looks almost black.  The monitor/screen is clear and bright.
The operating system is Windows 10 Pro.  It also comes preloaded with Opera and I added Firefox.
 So far I have been impressed with the speed of how fast it works and how programs open quickly with no delay.  
This computer offers a lot of bang for your bucks.

title: Run & Gun = Run & Die
text:
Socom is a very cool game. I was (and perhaps still am) a [[ASIN:B0016B28WU CoD4]] online junky. Now I have some fresh new junk to get addicted to.

Why would I need Socom if I already have an online shooter that I'm addicted to? Because Socom is truly different. This is a team tactical shooter and CoD4 is run out into the map and kill as many people as you can shooter.

The key to success (for me anyway) in Socom is "stick together".

You play as either a Commando or a Mercenary. Once in a lobby you can switch teams and during intermissions the game will regularly switch your whole team back and forth from Mercenary to a Commando. You can create about 5 Mercenary profiles and 5 Commando profiles; and you can change the weapon loadouts in game.

There are assault rifles, submachine guns, light machine guns, shotties, sniper rifles, and one extra rifle from a group of 5 that are available depending on whether you're in a clan and what clan you're in (Spain, France, Germany, UK or US).

All of the rifles and the following gear and stuff are available to everyone; I don't think there's any unlocking or leveling up needed. Your rewards for quality play instead are status, medals & stars.

The gear is kind of cool, but I'm pretty sure that the best loadout is the simple one: M67 frag grenades. The missile launchers are effective, but cumbersome. The claymores have to be detonated versus the CoD4 kind that blew up if an enemy walked near it. So for now, I'm sticking to the grenades.

One thing to note is that each weapon needs to be equipped. In other words, there's not a dedicated button on the controller to throw a grenade or switch to a launcher. You need to bring your selected secondary weapons up on a display by pressing O. Once a secondary weapon is selected you can switch back and forth between it and a primary weapon by pressing L1 (no, L1 is not your sight button; sight is up on the D pad...and to get off your sight you must press down on the D pad). (You can custom configure the wireless controller to your own liking if you don't like the default or other presets.)

The attachments for your weapons are plentiful: scopes, regular and laser sites, silencers, bipod and grenade launchers. Each attachment is not available on every weapon. And be careful, a laser sight will give away your position in night games.

Oh yeah, night games...you'll need your nightvision goggles for those. Navigating the maps takes a little getting used to, but as I said earlier, you should be pretty much sticking together with your team...follow them and take a position. That's right...there's some camping to be done here...but be smart: stay in one place too long and you'll be dead faster than you can say WTF!

And speaking of dead, I believe that you only get rewards by playing "ranked" matches. Friendly fire is on and there is no respawning. There are 4 v 4 matches, 8 v 8 and higher; so when you play Socom, in some matches you'll be atop the leaderboard with 2 kills. I personally have enjoyed the two smaller group matches, but that's a matter of preference.

So communicate with your team! Someone on your team is probably familiar with the map. Ask where to go. There's no stupid or noob questions here; the players that I've met got more mad when their team members didn't communicate and use their mics than they did when someone says "what should we do?"

Speaking of the mic, I bought the [[ASIN:B001C4DKG4 Stand Alone]] edition of Socom, because I have the [[ASIN:B0009B0IX4 Plantronics Voyager 510 Bluetooth Headset]] and it works great. But if you want to take advantage of all of the perks (like on screen volume and stuff) that were in the PS3 2.5 firmware update, then you should probably go with this edition that includes the new official PS3 Headset.

This game rocks. Some of the maps according to some of the folks that I've played with are carry-overs from past Socom games. That gives Socom vets a bit of an early advantage. But it won't be long before I'm navigating these maps on point instead of following my team.

Buy Socom if you play online.

Side note on initial game installation: If your PS3 is set to auto-start discs you might need to disable that the first time you plug in the disc. After you put the game in, you'll see two icons on the XMB for Socom; one installs the game, the other starts it. Install the game first. For some reason even after you run the installer, the game installer icon doesn't disappear; just be sure to start that game with start icon going forward. After the installation I got an error message that said my "saved data" was corrupted....so I deleted the Socom saved data from the XMB (NOT the "game" data...the "saved" data) and the error message disappeared.

Another side note that made take away a star in the overall rating: As of this writing, there are major server issues. Load delays. Freezes. Choppy action and more. Slant 6 Games NEEDS to fix these. If you release a game that is online only, you should release it when you are ready to set the bar for online gaming...not be a work in progress.

title: Great economical option
text:
I ordered a 'Parblo A610 Pro Graphic Drawing Tablet, 10 x 6 Inch Android Supported Pen Tablet Tilt Function, 8192 Level' for review. My wife is a crafter who wanted to begin creating her own personal designs and had been looking for a Graphic Drawing Tablet. I would like to share her thoughts with you:
* It took her a little bit of time to figure out how to get the drivers and software to install.. She is not really techy so it may have been more my user error than the driver itself. It connected to her laptop with a USBC.
* Once the driver and app were installed on her laptop, the shortcut settings were quick to set up.
* The tablet itself is relatively lightweight, thin and easy to carry with you, in a laptop case or carry on.
* The surface itself is smooth and does not require a lot of pressure when using the tablet. You can customize the pressure level.
* It has taken her awhile to figure out that she can use it without a mouse, as she set up her shortcut keys to function as her mouse. I know, she struggles with technology.
* She started by using the tablet with PAINT and so far she has been able to create several simple designs.
* The pen that comes with the pad is larger in circumference then she would prefer, but it is comfortable enough in your hand. It took my wife a little bit of time to get used to its size.
* The pen seems to create precise lines as she is drawing on the tablet.
* The pen moves fluidly across the surface.
* The ability to draw with the pen on a tilt makes using it feel more natural.

Overall, this Drawing Pad is a well made, economical choice for a Drawing Tablet. The biggest issue was the actual set-up but once that was complete, the tablet and pen both have worked well for her.

I hope this review was helpful.

title: Good every day ultrabook
text:
The Asus has a sleek look with its silver brushed metal lid and slightly rounded sides. Between this and it being JUST under 5 lbs, it makes for an easy transport if you want a laptop to carry around.

I noticed immediately the ultra-fast sleep mode. As soon as the lid is closed the laptop goes into immediate hibernation. After opening lid and clicking to un-hibernate, the laptop is back to active within 2-3 seconds.

The touchscreen has a sleek design with a black outline around the active screen that frames the look of the screen nicely. If you put pressure on the top of the laptop lid it does not affect the screen at all which tells of the durability of the laptop casing. The touchscreen has very nice vibrant display graphics that allows it to be seen easily from various angles without too much glare.

The visuals of the screen are great, which make for impressive video viewing. Picture is great and graphics are very crisp whether it is a Powerpoint still picture on display or a movie. The audio is great, too. While not a gaming pc, this is a nice one for video/audio usage.

It is a very thin and elegant design. The DVD multi recorder fits nicely along the side panels along with three USB ports, a microphone jack, SD slot, network slot and HDMI port.

The grooved out design around the touch pad is a small detail that has a nice impact on the overall look of the keyboard and touchpad (the touchpad is a bit of a different design with the 'clicks', but honestly, at this point with various keyboards for various devices, I'm used to things being different and just roll with it. But FYI to buyer). Keyboard is nicely laid out with light/'chiclet' touch keys and touchpad is sensitive without being too touchy. Considering that I also have a Asus Ultrabook S500-CA with a twitchy as heck touchpad OOB, this is a welcome relief.

Battery life appears to be great as well. I had the machine in hibernate for approx. 6 hours after machine was fully charged and the battery was not even down past ½ charge after all that time. And while in use, it does last about 6 hours. Considering the size and weight, that's pretty good.

Now for some negatives (or at least not so greats).
Fan vent is on the bottom which can be seen as a negative to anyone that works with the laptop sitting on their lap. I would imagine that the fan would be blocked in this instance and would not function properly and possibly allow machine to overheat? Gonna need a cooler for this one while using it for any length of time.

No SSD at all?

It barely comes in under 5lbs. As stated, I also have a ASUS Ultrabook S500CA, which is a 15" screen and weighs less. It also doesn't have a DVD drive, so.... You're definitely adding weight here for that and a few other options (and losing USB and other ports).

No full Microsoft Office Suite/software (you'll have to pay to get more than a trial version or use something else). Just making that clear. - edited as before I had stated 'Windows'. Sorry for any confusion.

All in all, this is a responsive laptop with impressive visual and audio that can be useful to an everyday user. It probably has some drawbacks to someone needing serious processing (no SSD), but for a lot of users, this one is good. I like ASUS, I find them to be reliable laptops, their designs tend to be good, and this ultrabook is no exception.

For everyday use, I'd give this 4.5 -5 stars. Anything else, take off a star or two.

It is sturdy, well made, comes with a usb to ps/2 connector, makes my typing extremely fast, makes my reaction time in games much faster (recommend that if you have your keys bound to active when you let up on the key, instead make them activate when you press the key down, it will be much faster). I no longer have problems with being unable to press as many keys as I want. Moving the windows key to the right is super nice.

My only problem, and this is super nitpicky. The backspace button is next to the forward space button next to the right shift key. I normally expect it to be above the Enter key. I got used to this fairly quickly though, and really, the backspace is an invention of microsoft that I rarely use anyway unless I'm typing in a command prompt in windows.

Other than that, the layout is great, it is standard aside from the two keys I mentioned and the keyboard is super sturdy and have had no problems with it for this year and two months. I don't plan on buying a different keyboard to replace this for many years.

One other thing, the keys you press the most (for me wasd) will slightly wear off over time. After this year and 2 months I can still see them but they are noticeably faded. I don't know if they'll fade completely, but it doesn't bother me at all. I kinda like it honestly, makes it feel like an old friend.

title: A Great Space Epic
text:
I've heard of this game from awhile back and I didn't think much of it until I had a sudden urge to expand out of the FPS genre for no good reason. This game is the perfect remedy as it has the action of a shooter and the customizability and the free roaming formula of a RPG and a heck of a story to go with it.

Pros:
-Great storytelling and very in-depth. Each alien race has its own unique characteristics and history, including humans and how each race intertwine with one another is intriguing. It is very easy to get immersed into this universe.
-Superb writing. The story is dramatic when it needs to be, and humorous when it wants to be, and the game convey these emotions very well. Instead of just reading and choosing text options, most everything is voiced, and that is an impressive feat considering the quality of the voice cast and all the dialogue options available.
-Great blend of RPG and shooting. Abilites, weapons, and armor is fully customizable according to the class, and this customizability gives you an edge against certain enemies and sometimes putting you at a disadvantage against other enemies. This can be offset by the teammates you pick. The dialogue wheel is superb. Choosing to let someone live or die, or to be friendly or hostile is a blast and has the potential for many different combination of how NPCs interact to the player which goes into my next point.
-The decisions you make will transfer to Mass Effect 2&3. While the transfer from ME1 to ME2 isn't significant (but still cool to see cameos), I bet it has a significantly bigger consequence in ME3.
-Great price! It's was only $10-$15 when I bought it and I believe it is still in that price range.

Cons:
-Occasional crash and a few bugs. This is probably the biggest nuisance, but with the 1.02 patch, the crashes either dropped significantly (my personal experience) or stopped entirely (according to a friend).
-The action itself is decent, but not incredible. Weapons don't have quite the "bang" or "oomph" as some other shooters. The cover mechanics is not very well polished.
-Sometimes hard to keep track of which galaxies you have explored, leading you to backtrack to places you've already been, but don't need to be in.
-Leveling up through side missions can be a grind. This is specifically referring to the infamous Mako, a six wheeler you drive around planets. While I don't think it handles quite as bad as everyone says, it is certainly not refined, and it can be a pain to climb incredibly steep hills with it.
-Interiors are cut and paste and repetitive. During side missions, building complexes essentially have 2-3 templates: a normal 2 story building and 2 underground facility templates. Over a dozen side quests, these buildings will be exactly the same, with some crates, pillars, and miscellaneous objects arranged differently.

Note: I've heard a lot of people complain about the DRM. In fact, I was a little hesitant about purchasing the game because of it. I personally did not have any problems with it and especially with the 1.02 patch, it's even less of an issue. I am told the the game can be installed only 3 times, period. With the 1.02 patch, it allows you to install the game 5 times (that means it can be installed on 5 computers at a time), and each time you uninstall the game, you get an install back. Unlimited installs like the good old days is ideal, but considering I only play it on one computer and didn't run into the problem myself, I cannot count against it, only to make a note of it.

Overall, I've been pretty even between the (5) pros and (5) cons, but let me be clear. The pros far outweigh the cons, and even more so with the 1.02 patch. I am being very picky here, and that is because I have spent a lot of time on this game and enjoyed it very much. For a story driven, immersive, action oriented game, you can't go wrong with Mass Effect. This is one of my favorite games, even among other top of the line shooters, as many of those tend to skimp on the story and short single player.

title: Save your money
text:
I've noticed a consistant trend with Logitech products. If you buy their cheap/low end goods, you wind up with a pretty horrible product, whereas if you spend more money on one of their more expensive products, you usually get something great.
These headphones are definitely on their low end of things, and they fail to deliver. The 25$ you'll spend on these is 25$ too much. You will find you have wasted both money AND time ordering, waiting, and ultimately returning these.
Here are the ups and downs:
Pros: Almost none. The sound isn't completely horrible with these, but mind you, it's only passable. The cord is nice and long, and the remote built in to the cord is handy.
Cons: Horrible fit. These have a really poor ergonomic design, and I can't imagine them being comfortable for anyone. They feel as though they are constantly slipping off, and they provide poor ear coverage. There is nothing immersive about the sound or feel with these. The poor fit introduces pressure points on the ears and skull which quickly turn painful.
Normally, these comfort issues would prove problematic, except these headphones won't work long enough for you to worry about it. The microphone, I believe, has a manufacturing flaw which prevents a solid connection, rendering a staticy, unusable signal. The fact that the microphone is broken fresh out of the box is problematic. I experienced this on 2 different units. Occasionally it will work, only to quit working on a whim. I spent several hours tweaking system settings, only to realize and accept that the headphones were the sole problem, and that it was a manufacturing flaw.
In summation, these headphones are horribly uncomfortable and will most likely be broken within the first day (usually, straight out of the box). They are NOT worth 30, 20, or even 5$, as they don't work. Spend your money on a better pair. I'm sure Logitech makes some nice higher end headphones, but these are NOT worth your time or money.

title: It works, but odd design. Why front mic?
text:
The good news is that it DOES work, and sounds pretty decent for a cheap no-name brand. If you've installed a double din stereo before, it should be pretty familiar and straight forward.
But let's just jump right into the odd design. Why is there an "external mic" option that is RIGHT NEXT to the internal mic? Usually an external mic is supposed to be mounted somewhere closer to the driver's mouth (up by the visor or mirror, or over the dash by the steering wheel, etc). The purpose is to get better sound, and either having the internal one as a backup if you don't want to mount one, or using it to pick up ambient background noise for NR filtering. Having an external nub right next to the internal one makes ZERO sense at all! Why even have one?! If anything, making it lower than the internal one seems like it would get WORSE sound, and if the position were so good, why not make THAT where the internal one is? Not to mention it looks weird as heck.
The features seem to be functional at least, but it has a pretty noticeable lag to the user interface. If you're expecting an OEM style menu experience, you might be disappointed. This feels like an old-school web browser loading pages when you open up a feature. Compared to modern units like, for example an Atoto F7, this feels like something a generation older at least.
I want to give this at least 3 stars for functional purposes, but the truth is I know that you get a much better unit for not a lot of money more. I can't really recommend it unless it is on an extreme sale.

Kimberly R. Norton's helpful August 3, 2014 review thoroughly covers most aspects of this card. Actually, after spending a lot of time with the review sample that I received, this is a solution more than a mere card.

First, a caveat. This card requires a reboot of a Windows XP system before it's recognized as a removable disk drive. In a real medical emergency this could be an issue. Granted, XP is obsolete, but Murphy's Law would probably go into effect if you were in a time-critical situation. Plus, this is strictly a Windows based solution.

Now for the reasons why I love this. Foremost is the app itself. It leads you through the creation of medical information that is needed if you were being treated while unconscious or unresponsive. The text files can be read by any system, as well as uploaded to your phone. I have labeled my data card to note that the information is also on my smart phone - just in case the card fails for some reason. The heart of this solution is the app that created the medical data and the files that it produces.

The card itself is clever in that an 8GB flash drive is contained in the form factor of a credit card. The USB 2.0 plug slides out of a protected channel that does not appreciably add to the thickness of the card, so it will easily fit in a wallet.

In addition to the medical data this solution provides a scanner guard that you can use to sandwich your credit cards between that and the Medic ID Guard card. What this part does is guard against RFID identity theft, which is a very real problem. It does not take much to thwart thieves - wrapping credit cards in aluminum foil will do the trick - but this solution is much cleaner and is actually a side benefit. Prior to getting this solution I had been using [[ASIN:B00GC4RTKC RFID Blocking Secure Sleeve]]s. This solution, however, is a lot more convenient.

Bottom line: there are some things that I do not like about this solution, but the benefits greatly outweigh them. As I mentioned, the app alone is worth the cost of this solution because it allowed me to create complete medical data in a structured way. I could have never done that on my own without additional hours of research to discover what information is actually relevant.

Pros:
-Super polished, as is expected from a company like Blizzard
-Constant updates, keeps the meta changing and all content is free
-Microtransactions are only for cosmetics, even if you pay an extra $100 for loot boxes, it gives you no real benefit gameplay wise.
-Seems like Blizzard in general is mostly listening to the player base and trying to make them happy.
-Due to matchmaking trying to put you in games with other players of approximately the same skill, even people who are not very good at FPS games can enjoy this game.

Cons:
-Only competitive game modes exist permanently (so far, as of the end of 2016)
-With any competitive only game, the salt can get pretty extreme
-With most players, they will eventually have their fill with the game, getting burnt out on the game is a big problem.
-Blizzard pricing, which means, the game will likely never fall below $30 for the base game for the next 5 years.
-Microtransactions in a premium priced game, also, how little you get for money spent on microtransactions.
-Blizzard as a company is not very nice to any possible alternatives to the class-based competitive shooter genre, Battleborn was a stillbirth due to their aggressive promotion of Overwatch, even if Battleborn was closer to being like LoL than TF2 gameplay wise.

considering how little content is in the actual game, its surprising how much enjoyment you can get out of this game. The game was basically cobbled together from the remains of "Project Titan", and it is a surprisingly well put together game considering how it came about.

title: Of life, death, and dark desires...
text:
Montreal-based Microids, creator of such gems as Amerzone, Syberia, Road to India and Post Mortem, has created its swan song in the form of Still Life: Microids was recently absorbed by another Montreal producer, UbiSoft, shortly before the game's launch. Still Life was chosen as Best Adventure Game at the 2004 E3 convention, and it's easy to see why. Based partially on characters from 2003's Post Mortem (psychic painter/ private eye Gustav McPherson), Still Life tracks the parallels between a modern-day serial killer in Chicago and a similar case in Prague 75 years ago. Gus McPherson's granddaughter Victoria, or Vic, is a profiler with the FBI and has been assigned to work a case in Chicago involving a series of grisly prostitute murders.

The game begins with a stunning, fast-paced cinematic that ties together the modern murders with Gus' case in Prague, awash in sinister mood and a haunting choir soundtrack. Vic begins at the fifth crime scene, where a prostitute is found stabbed and drowned in a condemned building. Vic's partner, David Miller, is as green as they come, and instead of helping, ends up contaminating crime scenes with, as Vic dubs them, "Miller's little Martians," aka, vomit. Vic, with the help of her former Quantico professor/ Chicago coroner Claire, is left to piece together the killer's M.O. Before long, it becomes clear that the killer is baiting her with clues related to her grandfather's case in Prague.

The game is divided into seven chapters, split between Vic (modern Chicago) and Gus (1930s Prague). Microids previously flirted with the concept in Post Mortem, where several chapters were played by a secondary character. In Still Life, the convention works well: as Vic reads Gus's journal to gain insights into her current case, the narration dissolves into Gus's world in Prague and his dealings with the local police and the prostitutes that he is hired to protect.

The visuals in Still Life build on the gorgeous 2D environments of Syberia and Syberia II, although here they are suitably dark, gritty, and occasionally kinky. Modern Chicago looks like a slightly sinister Frank Lloyd Wright-designed playground, interjected with grimy, rat-infested buildings, run-down campus apartments, and the sterile, functional police headquarters. Prague is awash in fog effects, run-down buildings, junkyards, and forbidding sewer tunnels. The game takes place at night, and even the interiors are dark and edgy. Artwork plays a huge role in the game, so expect to spend a good amount of time scouring in-game paintings as clues to the killer's motivations and the degree of his twisted sexual fantasies. Some of Gus's earlier paintings from Post Mortem make appearances here as well.

The puzzles in Still Life are generally intuitive, with the exception of two of the hardest puzzles I've ever seen in a game: a torturous lock-picking puzzle in Prague, and an "escape the lasers" puzzle in Chicago. For the most part, puzzles are varied, inventory-based (with the exception of several slider puzzles), and not too difficult. The Chicago portion of the game is reminiscent of CSI, as Vic uses Luminol, fingerprints, and photographs the crime scenes for analysis. The game's inventory, however, is not so intuitive, and took a good deal of getting used to.

About the rating: rated M for Mature, Still Life seems almost an Adults Only title for its extreme violence, sexual portrayals, and mature subject matter, including graphic language from several characters. One of the Chicago cops borders on an insulting stereotype as he constantly uses the "F" word and other vulgarities. All of the cops, including Vic and her boss, use the "F" expletive with each other, and Vic made one comment so bold that it actually made me uncomfortable. Although there is no sexual footage outright, there is numerous innuendo, especially in the dialogues of the Prague prostitutes and in the S&M (!) club (Vic makes a comment about "battery operated boyfriends," and is hit on several times by a female S&M employee).

The most disappointing aspect is that the game's *very* open ending clearly sets up a sequel, although with Microids being absorbed by UbiSoft, it is doubtful that such a sequel will occur. One interesting experiment involved an online prelude to Still Life; before the game's launch (and currently the page is still available at [...] ), players got to explore Victoria's background and personal life a bit more in-depth, while introduced to a background of the game's characters and storyline. The online game involved deciphering codes, finding hidden clues in pictures, and cracking a serial killer's riddles. Even if the Still Life sequel was executed in a similar fashion, i.e., online, it would provide closure for all the hours of gameplay invested without a final answer as to the mysteries of Still Life.

Still Life, although violent, is creepy, beautiful, and artistic. With believable characters, an edgy soundtrack, gorgeous graphics, and a fast-paced, curveball storyline, Still Life was a joy to play. I can only hope that one day Microids will complete the trilogy begun by Post Mortem and Still Life.
