title: Good concept, but bizarre bugs
text:
I've tried a similar box to this one, I'm familiar with the concept and I really REALLY wanted to like it. But sadly, it needs some more quality control.
I've always loved the idea of a Android powered head unit, I've seen aftermarket ones sold for popular car models, and I was hoping this would give me that functionality without having to replace my radio. But sadly, I can't use this.
For starters, it takes a long time to boot. That means you are first going to be greeted with your car's normal radio display, connected to my phone over bluetooth, and then once I've already pulled out of my driveway and started down the road, THEN it finally shows up on my display.
That is, if it displays at all. It seems to do this thing in which is boots up, checks for display info, then reboots in the proper resolution. The instructions even imply it does this. The problem is, most of the time my carplay radio will freeze up when it does this. Not only will it get stuck and not display anything, but my radio locks up and MY TIME RESETS. It's the strangest thing. After looking at reviews here, it seems at least one other reviewer said it make his car radio go crazy, so I don't really understand what this thing is doing that might cause that, but at least it isn't just me!
And even when it DOES work, it has a similar problem to other Android-powered adapters like this: it is a cold boot every time, with no idea what the time/date is. This is a major issue because if I don't supply an internet connection, the mini computer in this reverts to the wrong date/time on the display which is SUPER annoying. Ideally, they should design this to have a small battery to "sleep" like a phone, so it can retain time/date function and wake up faster than a complete boot. The way this is designed right now is really a subpar experience, assuming you can get it to boot up at all on your system.

title: Can't take photos + no screen = not good
text:
This is my first GoPro and I'm underwhelmed.

Starting with the good: The camera inside is great for video. It can record at 5.3K resolution @ 60 FPS, 4K @ 120 FPS, or 2.7K @ 240 FPS. The video quality is really good. Crispy and clear. Love it.

Now the bad: first off, this thing CANNOT shoot still photos (??), which is absurd. If you want a photo, you'll have to record a video and take a screengrab. No idea why they didn't include a photo feature.

The second-worst thing is that there is no screen, front or back. While I obviously knew this going in, not having any preview display has been a bigger annoyance than expected. It feels like this is being marketed as a more rugged version of the Hero 11 Black, but I'd rather just throw a case on a Hero 11 vs. not having a screen.

A couple other missing features, it doesn't have any scheduled capture mode or GPS. Neither of those are important to me, but I figure I'd mention them.

There is a flip-out cover that has a USB-C port and an SD card slot. It does not support an external microphone (!) and does not have an HDMI out. It's possible it'll support the GoPro external mic in the future after a firmware update, but TBD.

The battery is not removable, which I think they did to save (physical) size on the device. The battery is billed to give 60 minutes of recording time at max resolution, which feels about right given my experience. Lower resolution or FPS will allow for longer battery life.

I'd pass on this. Too many missing features to justify a purchase.

title: These are NOT bone conduction headphones
text:
The only thing these headphones have going for it is a respectable battery life. Everything else is just a disappointment, unfortunately.

I've been trying to find a good but affordable pair bone conduction headphones because I keep a headphone on my head almost all day while I work and write my code but I end up shutting the rest of the family out and miss half of the conversations going on in the house. When I discovered open ear bone conduction, it seemed to be the perfect solution.

So far, I have not found a good one. The specific problems of this pair of headphones is that it is not bone conduction. It is a simple pair of speakers set next to your ear. There is no bone shaking going on. With bone conduction, you can put in earplugs and still hear the audio fairly clearly, with these, the sound is clearly muffled and hard to make out.

In addition, there is a half-second delay on these headphones meaning they are no good for watching videos. I have not experienced bluetooth delay in quite a few years so I wasn't expecting it. Further, there is no charging light, meaning there is no way to tell if they are charged or not.

title: 2 of my 3 cats give this 5 stars; however, I feel this is overpriced for the value received but there other beds are great
text:
Amazon combines reviews, so the top part of this review is for [[ASIN:B01NCWLOHH DII Bone Dry Modern & Fashionable Cushioned Pet Bed For Dogs & Cats - Medium Oval Lattice Navy - 20x28x8"]].

This medium size pet bed almost feels like it is made of nylon, so I suspect this would be easy to wipe clean. The center pad is reversible with the opposite side being a solid blue. The fabric design is also very attractive. My cat Ricky (first three pictures) certainly gives it five stars as does Stephen (fourth picture).

There are two negatives for me. First, the bed arrived misshapen which I cannot seem to straighten out. Second the cushion is unevenly lumpy. I also feel the current price of $51.99 is way too expensive for this medium-sized pet bed. I would have given this five stars if the price were around $35 and the bed did not arrive and stay misshapen. Two of my three cats, on the other hand, disagree with my assessment and give it five stars.

Note that the last four pictures are for my review of their [[ASIN:B01N7T611T DII Bone Dry Kennel & Crate Corner Snapping Pet Mat For Dogs or Cats - X-Large Rectangle Lattice Navy - 26x39x3"]], which is very nice and is competitively priced at $46.99. I had a kitty playpen that this would have been perfect for but I recently gave that away to a shelter. What I like about this pad is that it has snaps that can be used to secure the pad to the corner bar on a wire cage. The snaps are pretty tight as well. As you can see from the last four pictures, my three cats love this pad. In the last picture, Jake is exploring it. Both my cats and I rate this five stars in both quality and price.

UPDATE 8/3/17 - I also ordered [[ASIN:B01N6RVRW6 DII Bone Dry Kennel & Crate Padded Pet Mat For Dogs or Cats- X-Large Oval Quilted Black- 26x39"]] for my cats and they love it. One cat squeezed into the shipping box to get to the mat before I even had a chance to unpack the plastic covering. For the current price of $46.99, I think it is competitively priced. The last four pictures are of Stephen and Ricky on this matt.

UPDATE 10/8/17 - The [[ASIN:B01N7T611T DII Bone Dry Kennel & Crate Corner Snapping Pet Mat For Dogs or Cats - X-Large Rectangle Lattice Navy - 26x39x3"]] snap broke on one side. I have washed this about three times already and only snapped and unsnapped it four times. I guess it's just wear and tear but I am disappointed that I can no longer snap this on one side. Had I been using this in a crate, this would now become almost useless because it would not stay in place.

I bought this TV to watch DVDs with my 3 yr old granddaughter. We were streaming on my tablet, but it was not comfortable. With this TV we can snuggle on the couch & enjoy Dora & Molly 😉

CON: The tv stand is horrible. It’s super hard to screw in the 6 tiny phillips head screws. 1. Because the angle is so awkward no matter how you place the tv & stand piece. 2. text:
I've been following this game for two years, waiting for its release, checking in to see how much longer I have and even convincing my friends they should also buy it and downloaded the trial creature creator.

I'm glad now that I read these reviews, I had no idea such a thing like DRM existed, much less that it would be on this game and now that I know - it takes all of the fun out of buying it. I won't pay 50 to 80 dollars to rent a game and, unfortunately, that is what I would have to do. If my computer crashes, if I switch hardware or install it on my desk and laptop; there are many things that would cause me to quickly lose my ability to reinstall it. The fact that even if I really enjoy this game, love it and play it all the time, I will only be able to realistically for a few years before it will be useless. That's not an investment.

Sadly I am also a huge fan of the sims and I worry, will the Sims 3 be like this as well? Will I have to give up a game I have played since middle school (I'm now in college) because I simply can't afford and aren't willing to purchase a 3-time game and its expansions?

Thank you reviewers for posting your information and allowing me to know if I'm making a great mistake and Amazon for allowing us to review.

title: Worst player interface EVER!
text:
I had some time to kill after finishing the excellent "Mask of the Betrayer" and while waiting for "Fallout 3" to come out, so I thought I'd take "Mass Effect" for a spin.

All I can say is, "Buh-bye fifty bucks!"

I played the game for a couple of hours or so, then finally gave up in boredom and frustration.

Unlike most RPGs today in which you control most of the game functions and character actions with the mouse, this game is almost totally controlled by keystrokes. This is a step backwards in technology of about ten years, in my opinion, and slows things down incredibly. Further, it requires memorizing all the appropriate key functions; like stepping back in time from Windows to MS-DOS.

The character inventory system is clunky and counter-intuitive, and very cumbersome to manipulate.

Worse yet, you can't exit cut/movie scenes to re-enter gameplay, so if you're having to repeat an action from a save, you have to sit through these looooong cut scenes repeatedly.

Not ready for Prime Time, folks. Save your bucks!

title: Great Tablet, A Few Idiosyncrasies But Still Like It
text:
I have been using Wacom tablets for so long, I can not begin to tell you. Perhaps it would make a difference to say that my first tablet I got was before Painter hit the market when it was developed by Fractal Design.

My most recent tablet was a workhorse- the ArtZII Tablet which was a pro version graphics tablet. I never had trouble with it and it worked with everything, including most games, believe it or not.

Unfortunately, the drivers began to malfunction so much with WinXP that I was forced to get a new tablet. If I could have gotten a serial to USB conversion adapter, I probably would still be using it if I had a driver to use with it.

The Intuos5 Touch Medium Pen Tablet is a wonderful tablet. Thanks to the previous reviewers, I did not even attempt to use it until I got the clear plastic cover for the pad to keep my pen from wearing down the nibs. I am SO glad I did. Now I feel like I am at home like I did with the ArtZII pad.

WHAT I USE THIS WITH

I like to use this pad with handwriting added to documents to sign things.
I use this for Corel Painter
I use this for Corel Graphics Suite X5.
I use this for general mouse uses when I don't need to use a lot of words on a keyboard.

WHAT I LIKE

The touch feature is helpful when I want to turn a page in Painter just like I would in real life
I like the responsiveness of the pen
I like that the screen can be made larger or smaller with my fingers.
I like that the light goes on in the screen to remind me that it is on.
Auto keyboard that pops out allows me to do minimal typing and not have to grab my keyboard

WHAT I DON'T LIKE

Silly, probably, but the round programming spots on the left side drive me nuts. They are not marked, and I just can not get into them yet.
I don't like that every time I grab the tablet near the round rubber area, it sends the screen coming in- but it does go away okay
The screen changing from one direction to another does not always work smoothly. Sometimes it gets stuck

A FEW MORE COMMENTS

I have not really tried programming this pad at this point as I have had not had the opportunity to do so as of yet. I usually am in such a hurry to do some photo work or graphics or sign something that I grab, do what I need and move on. I hope to study it more in depth in the future and use it even more than I do now.

The programming in Corel Painter X3 seems to work beautifully with this pad which I very much appreciate. The touch levels are fantastic and I feel the closest that I have ever been to using natural media on a computer than I have ever been in the years I have worked on computers with natural media programming- as I said, that is quite some time now.

The pen stand is kind of annoying, I am not sure why they set it up that way, but it is something I can live with. The pen itself is comfortable enough to work with and relatively easy to operate without too much thinking or reading of directions.

I will update this review as I learn more about this system and let you know how I like it. So far, I am quite happy with it, and have had no crashes or lockups while using it. The drivers load up well and I don't seem to have any difficulties.

I am using Windows 7 on a system I recently built so am just getting to know it better.

title: Weird design that doesn't quite know what it wants to be...
text:
Is this a space-saving and portable keyboard that includes a 10-key, or a full size chunky mechanical keyboard? Ultimately this keyboard tries to be both and therefor succeeds at neither of them.

Pros:
+Made from high quality materials, everything works seamlessly
+Bluetooth functionality works fine, seamlessly switching between 3 devices
+Full 10 key mechanical keyboard that is barely wider than a MBP

Cons:
- The keyboard feels cramped due to the layout
- Too chunky to be portable, negating the benefits of the smaller size.

At first glance, the compact layout is extremely appealing. There are several concessions made in order to get the entire 10 key layout into these dimensions. On the right side of the QWERTY keyboard, the shift, control, function and command keys are shrunk to make room for the left, up, and down arrow keys. For the 10-key, the "0" key is shrunk down from its normal larger size to be the same size as a standard key. Combine this with the 96% size of the rest of the keyboard, and the whole thing just feels cramped. Now this might be an acceptable concession for a keyboard that is intended to travel with you. However, the keyboard is THICK, and without some sort of snap on plastic cover I wouldn't want to throw it into a backpack or anything. Ultimately, this keyboard is too large to be a useful portable keyboard for most people and too cramped to be a convenient desktop keyboard.

title: It has its pros & cons..but more pros!
text:
I bought the Switch a few months ago and now that I’ve spent some time with it (more than I’d like to admit ^_^) I wanted to leave a review.

The Switch has many pros over other consoles, it’s main pro being that it’s a portable console with games that previously are only found on PC or console. I am a PC gamer and my PC is an absolute beast with an 8700K & 2080 Ti BUT the reason I bought a Switch is because oftentimes I am out and about and can’t bring my big honkin’ PC with me. Obviously I prefer my PC but it’s nice to be able to play games like Witcher 3 and then when I have to go somewhere in the car or something I can seamlessly “Switch” to the Switch and continue my game.

There are some absolutely AMAZING games on the Switch: Zelda: Breath of the Wild, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, Witcher 3, Splatoon, Super Smash Ultimate, etc., which are worth buying the Switch. This is especially true for people with kids as most of Nintendo’s big hits are kid friendly. You may not want your very young children to play violent games like Call of Duty or Battlefield 5 but they can definitely play a similar kind of game with Splatoon 2 only instead of shooting bullets to kill people they’re splattering paint all over each other.

However the Switch also has its cons. Let’s start with Nintendo’s “E-Shop”. The E-shop sells games that are WAY overpriced. They charge $59.99 USD for games that have been out for years. The fact is you can buy physical copies of these games for less on Amazon AND you have the benefit of being able to resell the game later if you want too. Not so with digital games.

Then there is the price. Yes the Switch is $299 which is cheaper than Microsoft and Sony’s consoles but when you factor in the cost of necessities that are almost required for optimal play (Pro Controller, SD card, Screen Protector) the cost adds up quickly.

All in all though I do recommend the Nintendo Switch. It’s a great console for anyone who just wants to have a good time and it’s especially great for families or people with young kids who want to play games with them without worrying about violence, drug use, sexual situations, etc., that are in a lot of other games.

5/5 Stars

This is a nice keyboard.

The Pros:
-It has the extra row of keys that's within the pinky finger range. I've seen a similar keyboard with 2 rows that's on sale from Walmart for the same price, but the wonky fat space bar doesn't do it for me.

- $50 price range. The other keyboards with the extra row of keys tends to cost higher. So this is a fantastic steal. -It's practically plug and go if you have windows 10, although I think it'll be the same for other OS. All the media buttons works.

The negatives:
-The keys are higher than my old keyboard, and so I'm feeling the wrist fatigue just as I'm typing this. You'll have to use the wrist-rest.
-It doesn't have the metallic volume scroll piece, which I really wanted. The keyboards that do have that, is on the upper ends of "heck no" price range. The volume buttons will have to suffice.
-The keys aren't flat and thin like laptops

The IDC:
- RGB modular lighting.

I've looked through many keyboards, although I can't find what I wanted without being conned into paying more than $70; I'll settle for this.

Originally I was looking for a keyboard that was flat and thin like a laptop, which will have little space for crap to fall in, quiet key taps, an extra row of bindable keys, and as a plus - a volume knob that can be scrolled up and down.

NOTE: That wrist rest is a must. I'm feeling wrist pain while typing this review. I've never had that problem with my old crappy keyboard.

3/15/20 Update
OK. This is a damn great keyboard. Originally it's a 4/5 now it's a 5/5 for me. The wrist-rest is still definitely needed, but after getting used to it I don't notice any fatigue. The software is absolutely not needed. All the keys can be macroed or rebinded, you can change every color to ANY WAY you would want it (i.e. fades/solid color/ 3 sections of colors to mess around with/wave); in which case it does help set the mood when you game in the dark and it's still pretty damn quiet. title: Buyer beware--lens mechanism problems
text:
This camera was highly recommended from a very trusted source, and the reviews were mostly positive. I expected a lot from it, and for a brief period, (maybe 4 months) it worked well. Then the problems began. Lens errors. Yes, despite Canon's insistence that this sort of thing "never" happens, the mechanical lens error you will read about in other people's reviews (known issue with this camera) of this camera happened to me. I bought it hoping they wouldn't, but alas, I am apparently a sucker. Next time, I shall heed the warnings of my fellow Amazonites. No more Canon products for me....

As time wore on, the lens error became more and more of a problem. After another three months, I called Canon. The (arrogant) tech support guy just said, "Oh, this happens when the batteries are weak."

"Oh really?" I said, unwrapping a new set of Energizer AA's. "Let me just stick these puppies in here and see what happens... Huh. Well, would you look at that. So much for your battery theory pal."

After embarrassing him thusly, his only "solution" was to send the camera in for Canon to look at it (at my expense). This would take a minimum of six weeks, after which there was no guarantee I would not continue to have the same problem with the camera. I mean, come on--a design defect is a design defect, after all. I was certainly not the first person to have this problem with this camera. Not only that, but no camera for SIX WEEKS?? I would not have survived.

Sadly, before I could pack the thing up and send it in, I dropped it from the staggering height of three feet. You guessed it, end of camera. Canon makes cheap crap with poor durability and cheap lens mechanisms.

So guess what I did? Yup, I bought myself a Nikon. I've had three of them with ZERO problems over the years. This is number four. My replacement is working beautifully, and is smaller to boot. Excellent image quality too. I will not buy a Canon again. Fool me once, it's your fault. Fool me twice, it's mine.

Buyer beware.

title: PoE = only one power adapter needed! Almost perfect!
text:
First of all, the signal quality is great over my 300' of CAT5e cable going from my entertainment system in front of my room to my projector around the back (cable goes behind walls and snakes around furnishings to get where it needs to go). It is fast and responsive, and the lag seems minimal if any. I love that it can also be used as a pass through, and that it only requires power on ONE side! My old HDMI extender required a power adapter on both the tx and rx side, but this can actually send power over the network cable (PoE) so that the other side does not need its own adapter. Now THAT's awesome!
This is one of the primary reasons I was interested in this, as there are two times I use such an adapter: When I use my projector instead of my TV for movies, and when moving a camera around at an event that I want to send a live feed back to a screen or streaming box for. Currently I have to supply power at both ends of the network cable, but I imagined ONLY needing power on the receiver, and having THAT power the transmitter. For example, in the case of the camera, I could have the screen receiving the signal send power to the transmitter by the camera using PoE and be somewhat more free of tethered power on that side. Also, when using the projector, I could turn on the outlet controlling the projector via remote and have it power on the transmitter behind the TV as well. Less wires and outlet spaces where already difficult / congested is good! THE PROBLEM, however, is that this thing misses its potential by only sending power from the TRANSMITTER! In other words, I can send power from the tx with PoE to the rx side, but the RECEIVER can't power the transmitter! It only goes the same direction as the HDMI signal. This, to me, was disappointing as that's the side I wanted to save from having more wires to plug in. Not the receiving side. That side is never an issue to supply power.
So I was a little upset about that. But otherwise, it is a solid product that seems to do what it claims to, and so far seems more reliable than my previous setup. If it could send power using EITHER side, it would be perfect! So close this time!

IMPORTANT FIXES

Driver not found:
When I got the controller I couldn't get it to work on my PC because it couldn't find the driver. Turns out when plugged into a PC these are a modified XBox controller so it has full compatibility with PC games. So, to fix it all I had to do was go into device manager, right click my controller, click "Update Driver" > "Browse my computer for driver software" > "Let me pick from a list of available drivers on my computer" > then I selected the XBox 360 Wireless Receiver driver.

Stick drift:
Also, I haven't experienced this one personally, but I've seen it mentioned and it's easily fixable as well! Just hold the little button at the back until it vibrates, then immediately let go and press it again until it vibrates again. The controller will now be recalibrated!

With these fixes, this now feels like the perfect controller for me. If it breaks or has any other issues I'll update this review.

text:
I am reviewing the ‘TruSound TruWireless Noise Cancelling Earbuds | True Wireless Earbuds with Charging Case for Buds and Phone | Comfortable, Secure Fit | Immersive Stereo Sound, Deep Bass | Easy Touch Control Operation’.
Based on my experience thus far I would like to share my thoughts.

Pros:
1- The sound is decent but compared to other Wireless Earbuds that I have tried, these are pretty average.
2- The case is rechargeable via the included 18650 battery. This allows you to have extra 18650 batteries on hand which is an interesting feature.
3- It comes with extra ear tips.
4- It comes with a mini USB cable and even a USB type A to Mini USB adapter.
5- Aesthetically the earbuds look nice, feel comfortable and don’t protrude much when wearing them.
6- They stay in place quite well and do not randomly fall out.
7- Earbuds are held in place magnetically when in the case charging.
8- They pair up real fast and very easy. I have had no issues at all with pairing.

Cons:
1- I ordered these based on the description stating “active noise reduction is also a standout feature of TruSound ear buds, ensuring a distraction-free audio experience”. I took this as they had ANC or Active Noise Control. This is not the case. These “isolate” the outside sounds via the ear tip inserted into the ear canal. If you get the right tip fit, they do “isolate” the outside sounds but just not as expected.
2- No USB type C. In my opinion all new devices should have USB C charging.
3- The case is a bit bulky due to the fact that it uses the 18650 battery.
4- The case is plastic and uses two plastic tabs to snap the lid closed. The design makes it really hard to open the case once it’s snapped shut. I am worried that I will break the plastic tabs at which point I would need to use a rubber band to keep the lid closed.
5- The Stand-By time is not the greatest. I fully charged the 18650 battery with my own charger when I first got the Earbuds. I used the Earbuds briefly while initially testing them and when I went back a couple of weeks later to try them again, the battery was already dead. I have other earbuds that have this same issue. I should be able to fully charge my earbuds, keep them in my backpack for a few weeks and have them ready to go when I want to use them.
6- No IPX rating? Pretty much all of the newer Earbuds these days have some kind of waterproof rating. It’s not advertised so I am not really sure if they are.
7- No Bluetooth 5.0? These have Bluetooth 4.2+EDR which isn’t bad, but there are sync issues when watching YouTube, Netflix ect. It’s not bad, but it’s noticeable and I could not use these to watch videos for too long.

Overall these TruSound Earbuds are average, and I feel that compared to the flooded market of True Wireless Earbuds these are a bit overpriced. With that said, I do like these but, I do feel there could be some improvements made that would ultimately increase the value.

title: 2 for 2, failed buttons. Just get a Deathadder
text:
I wanted to like this mouse. I like the position of the buttons (particularly the toggle DPI that lets you have a "snipe" button - more mice need that) and the general shape of the mouse, but it's just got so many problems, including abysmal build quality (which is shocking for logitech)

For starters, it's weirdly draggy and a bit heavy, even wired and with zero weights in it. I can't see anyone wanting to add more of the included weights - the point of this kind of mouse is to start LIGHT and let you tune it, not start heavy and let you make it worse. Genuinely heavier than my full size WIRELESS teknet mouse that I use for my media PC.

The feet lasted okay, they're starting to feel worn after a year of use on an aluminum banshee pad mousepad (I usually got about 2-3 years out of a set of feet on a Razer Deathadder) And they're very sensitive to picking up schmutz. Replacement feet are not readily found, you're gonna be using teflon tape. The combination of really meh feet and really heavy/draggy weight makes the mouse wildly imprecise after only a couple months. Even with teflon tape over the feet, I still can't make a "clean" drag across my mousepad with a smooth cursor movement. Not even sure it would when it was new. The aforementioned teknet mouse still absolutely glides after years. I think it's just because the 502 has SIX absolutely gigantic pads, and other mice I use tend to have 3 or 4 much smaller feet at most, which keeps the inherent friction lower.

Cord is okay if used with a mouse bungie.

The scroll wheel is abysmal. It has a side/side rock, which is already not good for a proper gaming mouse (they all have a habit of mis-registering mouse 3 clicks) but this is easily the worst I've ever experienced. I am used to the design, but this one is so bad and vague that I had to straight up disable the rocker, so now I only get about 15% of my middle clicks mis-sensed. The ability to unlock a scroll wheel is nice when I have to turbo scroll through a 300 page document, but again, in GAMING practice, is just one more way the scroll wheel feels incredibly vague and inaccurate.

mouse 4 is just set too far back. You have to press it with the knuckle of your thumb, which requires an incredibly awkward "palm pinch". If you use all the mouse buttons in a game, you're going to hate this thing so much.

And the thing is INCREDIBLY fragile. My first one's left click broke just sliding off my chair onto carpet, the whole mouse button itself sheared off. The second one's L2 switch itself is now failing, as it registers right click but doesn't register HOLDING it. After only a year, this is appalling. If you play MMO's, this makes steering an absolute nightmare. If you play FPS games, right click iron sight/scope becomes agony.

And there's something about this mouse that gives me really sweaty palms, which is weird because I have a kind of hybrid palm/fingertip grip that keeps my palm usually hovering just above the mouse

My deathadder was only replaced by this mouse because I suspected the skin flakes embedded in the chassis had evolved a new form of life. This one is getting hucked in the garbage because it fell to pieces in a little over a year and a half. I am staying away from Logitech for a few years after two absolutely atrocious peripherals and going back to the good old iron duke of a Razer Deathadder.

title: Perfect for critical listening
text:
Since there are some incredibly detailed and helpful reviews already I will focus on where these phones are best suited. I received mine as a review sample and have been using them for nearly a week to make sure I thoroughly test them.

For me these are best for critical listening, and especially raw mixes if you do recording. Of course they are not limited to that. The fact that these phones are fairly neutral across the entire frequency spectrum makes them ideal for listening to unmixed recordings, as well as music that you are studying or transcribing. The reproduction is so balanced that listening to albums with these compared to other phones - including some other Brainwavz models - is like night and day.

If you are listening to music that is heavily biased towards bass and drums these may not be the best phones for you. If you listen to acoustic music these are near perfect because you can easily hear every note. I tested it on a few jazz albums that I own as well as a broadcast of two friends from a local station that had been recorded directly from the sound board and it was wonderful to hear what was actually recorded versus what a biased pair of phones normally reproduce.

A few notes about comfort: these are light, do a great job of isolating ambient noise without totally eliminating it, and are easy to wear. I am not an IEM (in ear monitor) type of person, but these presented no problems even when I wore them for three to four hours straight. A big plus is this set comes with different sized foam ear pieces and a nice case (the [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]).

While these phones may not be for everybody, they are perfect for those of us who spend a lot of time critically listening to music and/or transcribing it. If you fall into that category you will probably love them.

text:
I got this to replace the PSU for a Dell E521 (about 3 years old, psu started making a nasty noise). The power rating for the original is 305W, so this one at 460W is more than adequate. (An online calculator suggested that I needed 365W.)

I would describe myself as relatively inexperienced at doing this sort of thing: I've replaced cards & memory & floppy/cd drives, but this was the first time replacing a PSU.

Removing the old unit and attaching this one inside the box was easy (just needed a philips screwdriver). The connections were mostly easy, but presented two challenges, one minor, one major: (1) The motherboard connector (P1) for the old one was a one piece unit, this one had two pieces, so I had to make sure I was connecting them correctly. (2) There is a single SATA cable, with three connectors, but my cd drive and hard drive were far enough apart in the box that I could not connect them both. Solution I'm going to try is a SATA y-cable (essentially an extender) from monoprice.com. I'll post an update about this once it's done. (BTW, I highly recommend monoprice for anything they carry: ethernet cables/connectors, parts, network adapters, etc. etc.)

Once I had it all in there, I plugged the computer in and started it up: everything worked fine, and the PSU was delightfully quiet. So far so good -- I'll post updates if I run into any problems over the next year.

title: Two sets of RCA inputs make it perfect for me
text:
Up front I will say that these fill a niche for me that was made possible because of the two sets of RCA inputs in the back of the main speaker. I cannot speak to the value for general purpose use or compare it to similar or competing products.

I use my speakers to connect both a bluetooth receiver (a [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]]) for streaming music from my smart phone, and a netbook to my TV. Please see my customer-supplied images at the top of this page for photos that depict how.

The bluetooth receiver allows me to stream music from my Droid X smart phone to the speakers. This is an important feature for me because I have most of my music collection on that device.

Using the second set of RCA inputs, and a [[ASIN:B00004Z5CP Belkin Audio Y Cable Splitter 1-Mini Plug/2-RCA Plugs (6 Feet)]] I am able to transmit my netbook's audio to the speakers, while a [[ASIN:B0002AHT0M Standard 15-Pin VGA Male to VGA Male Cable]] connects the netbook to my TV.

Regarding the sound: these speakers pump out clear sound that allows me to easily enjoy the full richness of my music up to 25 feet away. It favorably compares to my larger, power hungry surround sound system in quality, clarity and volume.

A nice feature that I personally don't use is the headphone jack in the front of the master speaker. For folks who are connecting these speakers to a desktop or laptop system to extend their sound capabilities, this is a plus because at night or in an office it gives the privacy you may need.

My only complaint is the power supply, which is more like a brick. Because of its size it takes up three outlets on my surge protector - one for the power and the size blocking two more. Please see my third customer-supplied image at the top of this page to see in detail what I mean.

As you can see, my use is somewhat unique. If you are looking for a set of speakers for your laptop or desktop, plus a smart phone audio or MP3 player and do not need bluetooth streaming, then you can dispense with my configuration that uses the [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]] and replace that device with a simple [[ASIN:B00004Z5CP Belkin Audio Y Cable Splitter 1-Mini Plug/2-RCA Plugs (6 Feet)]] that will connect to the audio out jack on most smart phones.

title: These Were GREAT To Use For Contractor Husband
text:
My husband has a lot of use for communication on jobs he has to do in the contracting world. We have had some jobs here at the house which required walkie talkie communication. Let's see how these performed.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
HOW ARE THEY BUILT?
These walkie talkies are tough. They come with the batteries outside of the units, so you have to put them in.

HOW TO PUT BATTERIES IN
You will need a very pointed screwdriver or a small Phillips head screw driver to get the battery cover off. When you screw it back in, it is pretty sturdy.

HOW TO TURN IT ON
The on button on the top is large and easy to cold, dirty, or gloved hands to turn on and off. You can also adjust volume.

CASE?
The case snaps on and off of the units. They stay hooked to the clothes pretty well as long as you are not moving around a lot. In that case, we found them most useful to hold the walkies in the pockets with the clip.

CLARITY OF SOUND?
The clarity of sound was superb. We were doing roof work on the top of a third story and they worked great. We also had to do work about 100 ft away from the point of origin of a wiring job, so we needed that for communication to test the connections. Again, they worked great. Very clear and worked very well.

TOUGH?
These have been dropped a few times and worked very well.

RECHARGING?
The recharging unit has a place for both walkies to be charged. The plug is separate from the base that you charge in. Each receptacle has a red light on it to let you know that the walkie is charging. The plug is small so you can use it on a power strip or in the wall outlet without blocking other outlets. Recharging is fast- within the hour- and they seem to last quite a while before needing to be recharged.

CLIPS
The clips have to be removed prior to charging.

CHANNELS
The different channels we used all worked well. We did not have to use them in a very busy area with multiple walkies, however, so we did not get to test it with a lot of walkie talkie traffic happening on a huge job site.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a very sturdy set of walkie talkies which charge up quickly and last a long time, these are fantastic for contract work and any jobs that we have had to do. My husband plans to take them to his jobs as well when needed. They have a decent range to them and are easy to operate even with gloves on.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. We really love these walkie-talkies. They have been fantastic so far for all of the jobs we have had to use them for. I will update if we have anything valuable to add in the future as we continue to use them over time.

The Box my items were shipped in was trashed and partially crushed.The boxes in the shipping box that my items were actually in we're also partially crushed. As for the package protection? Oh, Amazon decided to put a single, long strip of paper in the box and call it a day. I guess my order wasn't even important enough for actual bubble wrap, that or times really are that tough. The only reason I didn't demand a refund is because the actual items themselves are undamaged. Yes, I blame Amazon for the shipping, because until the customer is actually satisfied with the order, everything still falls into the provider's lap. I didn't choose who did the shipping, they did.

Now that my little rant is done, on to the actual review. As far as the product goes, I couldn't ask for better quality for the price. There's LED lighting, yet it is not super bright so it does not pierce your vision. The keyboard is water resistant. Yes, the keys are a little spongy, but it is barely noticeable. Personally, I prefer it that way. Dont confuse "spongy"with "cheap", there's a difference. The mouse has 1600 DPI, which is plenty unless you play e-sports, which I don't. As for the mousepad, I would almost say it is almost e-sports quality itself.

Overall, I'm not fully sure how this company can offer this product combo for this cheap. Normally, keyboard and mouse "gaming" combos are to be avoided, but I decided to take a leap of faith on this one, and I'm glad I did. I would certainly buy this again. Apparently, an exception to the rule has been found. Again, not saying this is extreme top quality or anything, but for the price, it's simply can't be beat. This product actually deserves a 5-star review most definitely, but the knocking off of that one star can be blamed on Amazon and the lazy shipping habits that they seem to have had lately. Shame on you, Amazon.

title: Tiny and smelly. Dogs love them!
text:
I originally bought a bag of these locally, and my dogs (who RARELY get any kind of treat) just went nuts for them.

After the tragic loss of my Great Dane in November, I adopted two adult dogs from separate homes in December and January. One went 6 days without eating more than a handful of food due to the stress of separation. These tiny treats, (really tiny when you're bribing a Saint Bernard with them) had a very strong odor that got her attention and helped kick her appetite back to normal. Yes, she's just fine now, and happily well into her training to become my next service dog.

The second dog I adopted is rather elderly (and surprisingly awesome) and stubborn. After a lifetime on crappy grocery store dog food, he did not like the idea of being switched to high quality grain free food. Again, the strong odor of these little treats incentivized him to eat the good food in order to find the tiny treats. He is also doing great now, with clean teeth, a shiny coat, he's free of hot spots, and missing the awful odor of a dog on corn based food.

I'm glad Blue Buffalo makes an assortment of good quality treats and foods, and that it has forced other manufacturers to raise their standards.

title: Apart From the L2/R2 Snag, Totally Fine
text:
This controller arrived during the last week of July, 2017.

Have been using it to play Final Fantasy XIV on my PC (Windows 10) for several hours per day since then. (Ok, 12-18 hours per day; I keep it on while writing, typing, transcribing, programming, etc.) It's not STRAIGHT usage, but I'd consider it heavy usage, nonetheless.

Anyway, it's now a few minutes into 29 October, 2017, and the poor controller began to show its age a few days ago, hence my frantic trip over here; you know the symptoms: your character can't move in a straight line, or else keeps running in circles, etc.
In my case, it's also that the system doesn't recognise a hard right turn on the right analogue stick (though I can still press it and get into first-person mode).

Am beyond tempted to open this thing up and see if some dog hairs or whatnot got in there (like the old skool mouses (mice?) that you'd have to clean out every few days, or if the issue is related to springs or gaskets or what.
Truth is, though, that I'm not confident in my ability to pry it open without completely destroying the plastic housing, so let's wait till the replacement arrives, eh?

NOTE: The button-pressing on this thing was never the most... reliable? Like sometimes it would take a shallow half-press to register, other times, it took a major SMASH until the press "counted." It was like this from the beginning, but only got worse as time went on. Again, not sure if it's an issue or materials or dog hair.

I'm grateful for the few months this controller worked "well" (or "well-enough"), and would buy again.

One thing, however--and I don't know if it's related to the game itself, or all USB-for-PC controllers, or THIS controller or what--but the BOTTOM trigger buttons/"bumpers" (L2 and R2 or LT and RT) have NEVER been recognised by my system (again, Windows 10, and NOT Steam version of FF14).
Like, since Day One. I've calibrated and mapped and tweaked like it's going out of style but alas, it was for naught. For the record, I also have a wireless controller for my Mac (SteelSeries, purchased from Big A--well, the other Big A that isn't this one), and IT refused to recognise the D-PAD, of all things. (Yes, lots of frustrations around here, lol.)

Anyway, my experience with this product is limited to the one I got, but I WOULD buy again, and would also recommend to someone looking for a solution to a tech situation similar to mine--as long as s/he knew that this thing would likely have to be replaced "at some point in the near future," which applies to everything under the sun these days (even pricier items).

Happy gaming to all,
SB

title: UPDATED-Works Wonders on Bratty Cats and Angora Rabbits As Long As The Preferred Person Uses It
text:
In our house, we have angora bunnies that have their own brushes. Their coats need to be brushed regularly, but sometimes our cat, a short haired tabby, will get a bit jealous of the attention that the rabbits are getting. Now that has all changed with the Perfect Coat Deshedder!

WHAT IS THIS DESHEDDER LIKE?
The handle of the deshedder is very solid. It is a dark aqua teal color with a black rubber grip that runs from the neck of the handle on the top to the grip area of the handle below that your hand has to use for gripping the tool. The handle is ergonomically designed and fits perfectly in my hand. There is a hole on the bottom that you can string a rope through for hanging up or hang through the hole itself on a large nail.

The head of the deshedder is bent over reminiscent of a razor, but at a bit larger than 90 degree angle from the handle. The metal part of the deshedder is a very substantial metal which looks like a razor scissor with its fine teeth and it seems like it would be sharp, but it isn't. The edges are not sharp and neither is the top or bottom of the metal plate that is used to run through the fur.

HOW DOES THIS DESHEDDER PERFORM?
I have to say that when I first used this comb on our short haired cat, I was not expecting anything miraculous. I was surprised, however, at the amount of fur that was coming out of his coat and how much nicer he looked. His fur was very soft and it did cull through the hairs on him to remove those that needed to come out. I got a substantial amount out but not so much that I was concerned that this was cutting his fur- it wasn't.

HOW DID OUR CAT RESPOND?
Our cat responded as if I was murdering him the first time I tried this on him. His face was so disgusted and irritated with me that our daughter was laughing really hard. That, of course, made him all the more indignant and he struggled and ran away from me.

Our daughter was taking a look at the tool when suddenly she looked down and our bratty cat was tapping her leg with his paw then pointing to his head. He wanted HER to comb him. He laid there for about 20 minutes relishing being combed with the deshedder AGAIN and it has been that way since.

DID THIS WORK FOR OUR RABBITS?
Our angora rabbits do best with a flat brush that has a lot of wire bristles in it, but I did try this deshedder on them and I must say that it worked nicely on them too. They have short haired heads and legs so I even used it there with success. Although I would use the brushes most often, I can definitely see a use for this deshedder on them when I needed to get into some areas that needed finer combing.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Well designed, easy to grip, and precise, this deshedder worked beautifully on our short haired cat as well as our long haired angora rabbits. It did take out a lot of fur that needed to come out but did not hurt our animals in any way. After they got used to it, they all seemed to like being combed with it and did not mind the activity at all. (Well, except our cat prefers one person over another of course). The deshedder is high quality and I am very impressed with it. It works better than any other similar comb we have used in the past and really improves our animals' coats.

I give this five stars.

UPDATE MAY 2016
Finally our cat has decided that he loves this comb so much that he does not care WHO uses it on him. I have to say it is now a serious blackmail device. Our cat can not be convinced to do anything he does not want to- until NOW. HAHA. All I have to do is show him the comb and he is a puddle of mush. Leverage- at last!

Needless to say this is still five stars.

title: Good game with potential to be a whole lot better
text:
I've played a number of MMOs, and LotRO has the usual time sinks, quests, and crafting as other MMOs. There's only a few things that makes LotRO unique, Monster Play and the fact that it's based on Tolkien's work. The graphical environment is pretty spectacular too, but the characters and the gear they equip fail to blend with the beautiful environment the game has, as the characters aren't modeled very well and the gear looks laughable. Seriously, 90% of the items look boring, re-used, and the boots that they all wear look hauntingly close to those 80's "moon boots."

The music is also very well done. I also like the fact that there's ways for people in a party to create powerful combination attacks via an event called a "conjunction." Depending on each party member's conjunction selection attacks can do massive burst damage, heal all members of the party, do damage over time to the monster, or increase the power of all members in the party (power is the stat that skills consume.) There are even special combinations that will summon aid to assist in killing.

Questing is the typical "gather X resource", "kill X number of Y mobs", "find X location", and "deliver X item." I doubt any MMO will ever break free of these types of quests, although one can dream.

The game is obviously for the casual gamer, as the leveling process is geared to allow people to advance at breakneck speed. Within a month and a half I hit the current level cap of 50. This is both a blessing and a curse, since the onus is on Turbine to churn out tons of content to keep level-capped players interested and playing. Bored players is a sure-fire way to lose subscriptions rapidly. Not coincidentally, there seems to be less people playing than at release time. This doesn't really come as a surprise since there were probably plenty of people just window shopping for a new MMO, but I can't help but wonder if a significant number of those who left hit the cap and had nothing else to do and so cancelled their account.

On to Monster Play. A novel concept, this gives players the opportunity to play as one of a select few monsters in the game to combat normal players in a special area isolated from the rest of the game. The main reason for isolating the Monster Play area is Turbine doesn't want the Player vs. Enemy side of the game mingled with the Player vs. Monster Player side, which could be frustrating since all monster players start out as a level 50 monster. It doesn't take a genius to figure out the level of frustration a new player would experience spawning in the new world and getting ganked by a level 50 monster again and again. But I digress... Monster Play is exciting because it's a way for an MMO to balance pseudo-PVP without having any impact on the PvE side of the game (just look at WoW and the juggling act they have to do to try to maintain balance between all the factions and classes.) It's fun to jump into an enemy character and join in fights with normal players, and it's equally refreshing as a normal player to fight against a human-controlled monster, as the fights with NPC monsters can't match tactics humans will leverage. This is also where LotRO fails to deliver, however.

The problem is Turbine's slow response to fixing bugs. The monster side of monster play has suffered since pre-launch days with a lack of desperately needed healing support, crowd control, and plenty of near game-breaking bugs. Other areas of concern that have major issues are the economy, crafting, and the Champion class (Champions lack any sort of skills that define the class as a desirable party member, and their "legendary" skills, which take a fairly large amount of time and effort to obtain, fail to live up to their name and are either borderline useless or there's a lower level skill that's actually *better* than the legendary!)

Other nice touches are built in voice chat, intuitive UI, and a fantastic story line. Epic quests are very engaging and well worth completing, not just for the experience and gear, but for finding out what happens to the NPCs involved and getting more insight into Turbine's vision of Tolkien's world, which is surprisingly very *very* well done (speaking from the perspective of a rabid Tolkien fan.)

To sum up...

The good:
- Beautiful environment
- Excellent music
- Storyline is incredibly compelling
- Several innovations present in this game

The bad:
- Bugs that have existed for months are still present, and Turbine has elected to release new content instead of address bugs as of this review
- Characters look very bad in contrast to the environment they're placed in
- Certain classes need borderline re-vamping
- Crafting is almost pointless
- Rapid leveling can be a potential problem, leaving players with nothing to do

I'd recommend this game for Tolkien fans especially, and also with the hope that Turbine can fix the bugs and continue to release compelling content. At this point I would highly suggest *not* getting a lifetime subscription, simply because I feel that Turbine is out of touch with their customer's needs based on months of reading posts in the LotRO forums and lack of response from Turbine. Granted there aren't many MMO companies who communicate very well or respond with customer complaints, but that's no excuse to perpetuate the stigma, and MMO companies shouldn't be rewarded with lifetime members who are stuck forever with a game. Lifetime membership pretty much equates to not being able to vote with what counts the most: your dollars.

Edited on 4/9/2008 to add the following:

I quit a while ago, but remembered writing this review. After re-reading it, there are a couple of things I wanted to add. Turbine's LotRO message boards are moderated by overzealous personnel who wantonly lock topics with no explanation as to why they were locked. This creates a serious level of frustration for people looking for answers, and finding their topics locked for seemingly no reason. BAD customer service. Also, after your account has been made inactive, the message boards are completely off-limits, and there's no way to keep in contact via them with people you'd been playing with for months. This also makes it next to impossible to get a feel for how the game is aging, since you can't see any of the forums. Talk about a stupid thing to do, this takes the cake.

After it's all said and done, if I could re-rate the game overall, I would give it 2 stars out of 5 for the horrific customer service.

Edited again on 11/12/2010 to add the following:

The game went "Free to play" recently. I'd been playing another MMO for years and was looking for a break, and since LOTRO was free I figured why not. I was curious to see what they did to make it "free" and how they've progressed the story with the various expansions they've put out. They may have done some things wrong, but one thing they did spot-on was with the story. It's simply amazing.

Anyway, I re-activated my account through free to play as a level 1 Hunter, and was happily plinking away at enemies, and soon found myself suckered into full-blown LOTRO addiction (again). I re-subscribed to get at my old level 50 characters. I didn't want to rely on all the micro-transactions they have for free accounts, and I also wanted to hit the content I'd never experienced since I had quit (namely Mines of Moria and Mirkwood Forest expansions.) The game has stood the test of time in almost every way. Since I'd departed they've added one very interesting way to advance your character: legacy weapons. It takes a while to explain fully, so I won't do that here, but suffice it to say that as you kill enemies and complete certain quests, your weapon also gains levels and allows you to customize it to a degree. I'm one of those people who don't mind "the grind", so this really appeals to me. I like getting weapon levels and increasing the stats on the weapon.

Also new (for me) is "Skirmish". Skirmishes are instances you can complete either solo or with one or more people. Inside a skirmish you have an NPC that you control to a degree. This is also another type of grind, as your NPC can have its stats advanced to be more effective. Skirmishes also reward you with points that can be traded for a whole slew of different things, ranging from gear, to cosmetic changes, to upgrading your legacy weapon. And best of all: it's FUN!

As far as the expansions go, Mines of Moria is AMAZING. Mirkwood? Not so much. Hard for Turbine to match what they had in Moria though, they really out-did themselves in that one. Enedwaith is a free update that I believe requires Moria that so far is turning out very interesting, and looks absolutely gorgeous.

Only disappointment is that after all these years, the monster player vs. player still SUCKS. People for the most part run around solo in a zone where working together should be mandatory. You're basically fodder, and die repeatedly unless you get lucky enough to jump into the zone when there's a raid happening and you get invited to the group. In other PVP games (Warhammer Online comes to mind) if you're not grouped up, you're almost always going to be outnumbered and die a horribly fast and messy death. That's pretty much what happens in the LOTRO PVP zone. The fact that Turbine has left the PVP zone virtually untouched all this time is very disheartening. I still firmly believe this game could have some of the best PVP gameplay out there since balancing the PVP in it should be simple, as only one side needs to be adjusted and will have zero impact on the rest of the game.

I have not been to the forums and really have no intention of it, as I called out in an earlier edit how bad the moderation is (or was.) I just stick to playing the game and go to wiki or other sites for information.

It got so hot on the bottom that it even cracked our dining table that we were using it on. We've been using this cooler for a few days now and it works great. We positioned the fans to be right under the hottest parts and it really helps prevent the laptop from getting hot. The fans are really quiet and I love that you can move them around to where you need them. The laptop sits nicely on the stand and it doesn't slip at all. I don't know how well it well hold up for long term use but so far we love it.

Update 9/28/11
This cooler is still working great and is very quiet. Every now and then it will start making noise but I find that if I unplug it from my laptop for a few seconds and then plug it back in, it's back to being quiet. It doesn't happen very often but when it does, it's easy to fix. I am still very happy with this purchase and highly recommend it.

title: Weight measurements comparable to my food scale; weight moves around w/small pets on tray
text:
[[VIDEOID:2776e094aabeb9f9b1bd0d105a29638c]] I have two food scales and I tested this for accuracy with a jug of popcorn and the weight registers within .05 ounces of my other scales. In the box is a tray, the scale, and an instruction pamphlet. Two AAA batteries are installed but the tape has to be removed. Although this is a small animal scale, there is nothing stopping anyone from using this as a food scale.

I installed the tray runners along the edge of the scale base. I then tried this with my very skinny and sick adult cat. He weighs a little over 5 pounds according to this scale (see photo), which I know is accurate. Note that the reading will NEVER be spot on unless there is absolutely no movement. This is typical of the scale I see at my vet's office. Since my pets move, the scale reading fluctuates with the movement, which I believe is to be expected. I did see a quick fluctuation with stationary objects but it always righted itself.

There is a TARE button to zero out the scale in case a container is placed on the scale and I only want to weigh what's inside the container. There are also five units of measurement - kilogram, pounds/ounces, fluid ounces, milliliter, and grams.

In summary, I think this is a very good scale that is simple to operate and has all the features needed to weigh a small pet or food (even though it was not advertised as a food scale). It weighs up to 33 pounds. The current price of $38.60 is competitively priced for this.

title: The greatest upgrade you can make for an old computer
text:
These are $20 a pop. This is the greatest performance to price upgrade you can make for your old computer.

Although I have been using laptops with SSD's since 2012, I have never exactly purchased one as an upgrade since they came always stock. However, prices have become so low for NAND memory that it is economically feasible to just throw these into all my obsolete computers to give them new life. I popped these in several very old Core 2 Duo laptops that my parents still use and now they run Windows 7 with ease even if they are only running at SATA II speeds. Anyways, 4k random read/write speeds are the most important for OS execution, so the sequential read/write speeds don't have to be the fastest.

You will need to purchase a SATA to USB cable as they do not provide one.

I also recommend that you use Aomei Backupper to clone all your partitions. EaseUS does not work very well with Kingston drives for some reason.

title: Really PREMIUM sound!
text:
I've heard a lot of wonderful things about the Sony noise cancelling sets like these, and let me tell you: it isn't just hype. The sound quality is excellent, and the noise cancelling is eerily amazing. I put it on my wife and kids with the noise cancelling off and then turned it on to demonstrate, and you can see each them suddenly smile like "whoa". Like my Sony studio headphones I use professionally for work, the actual fidelity of the sound it reproduces is excellent, and the microphone for calls is excellent despite being up by my ears and so far from my mouth (other bluetooth headphones I've tried were good for music only, the mic being up by my ears wasn't good enough to isolate my voice from ambient sound, but this definitely does a great job).
The app gives a ton of control beyond what I expected to really customize the experience. For example, I have mine set to auto-pause if the headphones are removed, and to turn off noise cancelling when it detects me speaking to someone, and then resume playback when the headphones are removed/replaced. These features are all customizable, as well as many more. But you need the app. And this is where the cons come in:
1) You really need the app to get the most out of this. I was thinking about pairing this with my desktop and/or TV, but without the app you have far less control, and to be honest I couldn't even get it to pair with my phone using just Bluetooth alone. There seems to be a way according to the instructions, but I couldn't figure it out without using the app installed.
2) For a set that costs this much, I'm surprised at how scuffed up it got after one fall from about 3 feet next to my car. Including pictures. This happened the day I got it. I'm not sure if there's anything that can be done about that, pavement is hard to recover from if anything is dropped, but it's something to keep in mind if you're spending this much money on a gadget. My studio headphones have been roughed around for years and held up fine.

All in all, I'd give it 5 stars if it weren't so reliant on the app to get the features going and/or more resilient to being dropped. Feels like I should deduct one for that. But as far as features and sound quality go, this is a solid 5 out of 5.

title: JBL Balboa Sub10 is a worthy contender
text:
Although the JBL Balboa Sub10 delivers very good performance for a relatively modest price, I would never refer to it as "the little subwoofer that could." That's because it's far from little; this thing is quite big by my standards. However, considering that the function of a subwoofer is to reproduce low-pitched audio frequencies, I'll accept that fact that it's the size it needs to be do its job well.

Because I live in a multi-family building and have neighbors with which I share walls, I have not been able to crank up the volume beyond medium. That being said, I have been quite pleased with the bass sound and have not experienced any distortion with this subwoofer at the volume range that I have used. Audiophiles who do not have cost as an object will no doubt want a more expensive subwoofer than the Sub10. However, for the rest of us who are just looking for a dependable, reasonably priced subwoofer for our sound systems, the JBL Balboa Sub10 is a worthy contender.

They still look perfect and new. The elastic still holds great. But they start leaking through the PUL. This is usually after 3-4 YEARS of daily use. (2) You aren’t using enough absorbency in the diaper. If the wetness just sits on the PUL without proper absorbency, you’ll have leaks. (Usually from around the leg seams or the back label seem.) title: What a Hack Job
text:
The original Army of Two was a fun and unique game. There are not a lot of true co-op games these days and so the original was pretty cool in that way. There was a good bromance between Rios and Salem and stuff that required you to work as a team. There was also a semi-interesting plot, weapon customization and a pretty good variety of locales. Playing the game again, it can be a little easy since everything is kind of slowed down and the bosses get repetitive, but it was still a good game.

40th Day suckered me in with their demo. Based on that, I thought it was going to be a good game. There was a long intro that seemed to hint at a decent plot, improved graphics, new features, better gameplay and a lot more weapon customizations. Then, after the first level, everything went downhill. The plot that they spent so long introducing ended up being totally useless. You have no idea who the bad guy is until the second to last level, and you have no idea why everything around you is happening. After a while it seemed like they just gave up on the plot. The ending of the game is just plain dumb and makes you wonder what they were thinking. It's not like the first one had the most enthralling storyline ever, but compared to 40th Day it was a work of art.

Some new features were cool, like the ability to run (although it is the same button as heal, which leads to you running away from your partner when you try to heal them sometimes), but stuff like the hostage grab rarely ever came up. The morality choice seemed interesting at first, but then slowly tapered off into nothing.

The new weapon customization seemed awesome at first since there was so much to choose from and it was wayyy better than the original game for getting it done quick. But then you start to realize that there is just too much crap there. Dozens of barrels and scopes and stocks that cost thousands of dollars but really don't do much, stupid skins for your guns etc. For some reason, you can buy 57 barrels for the M4 but there are only three pistols. Plus, when you die, it resets to the defaults, which can be really annoying if you want a certain kit to start a level but you keep dying.

I thought this game was an improvement over the first one, but in hindsight it was all smoke and mirrors. Seemed like they had all these ideas and put them in a demo level and then they just went on cruise control from there. The bromance, humor and originality of the first game is sorely missing in this one.

title: Really solid for the money, good value compared to Sony WH-1000
text:
There's a lot that I like about these Philips headphones. All the classic features you'd expect from a higher-end over-the-ear style wireless headset are there, including support for an optional 3.5mm jack with included cable in the box, and they even threw in an airplane adapter and carrying case.
It's got soft ear cups and padded head bar, and a pretty awesome NC system. Here's the thing: I own a pair of Sony WH-1000 headphones so I was expecting to be somewhat spoiled and biased about the sound quality and build. And I am. The Sonys are still some of the best and the standard by which I judge other headphones in this style. BUT... at the time of this review, the price of this Philips product is less than half of what I paid for my Sony. Are the Sonys better? A little. Are they twice the price better? NO WAY. This is far better quality in sound and build than the cheapo bluetooth headphones, and if I didn't try them side by side with my Sony, it'd be hard to tell them apart. The feature set are similar, including the app control which actually made the phone really easy to pair as well.
One thing I actually really like about these is that there are more buttons than the Sony alternative. A dedicated button for mute, a dedicated button for noise cancellation, and of course power/pairing. But there are also touch sensitive controls on the ear cups, which I did not realize at first. I have mixed feelings about touch controls, I feel like they are easy to accidentally trigger, but so far it's actually been pretty good.
I think for the current asking price of around 150, the pros are solid enough to be worth recommending.

We recently adopted a 5 month old puppy and she has incredibly itchy skin! title: Quite Surprising Sound For This Price Range Of Headphones With A Few Disappointments
text:
I was looking for some replacement headphones for two sets in my family when I had the opportunity to try out some of the new Carlos Santana line of headphones. Let's see what happened.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These headphones come in a great box which will appeal to fans of Carlose. It is well decorated and presentation is done so well, it would make a great gift. These are the black ones, and there is also another set available in white under a different listing.

ARE THESE REAL LEATHER?
According to the case,t these are leather padded ear cups and the lower half of the headband. I am still not sure about this. It is possibly bonded leather. Bonded leather is made from leather scraps chopped up and blended with binders. Sheets made of this mixture are printed with leather look imprinting. Technically it can be called leather, but it really is not leather as I define it..

EAR CUSHIONS AND HEADBAND
These black headphones are comfortable. I can wear these headphones longer than many others I have used. My daughter who ended up with these, uses them constantly and raves about them. These can be worn for several hours without a problem. She has sweaty ears and these are not nearly as frustrating for her as many others.

CORD FOR CORDED LISTENING
This comes with a cord which is only 38 inches long. That is a bit short for me. I find it is annoying and not quite as long as I would prefer, but my daughter does not use it so I guess it is not a problem for her or if you are like her, you won't mind either.

HOW DO THESE SOUND?
We are all surprised at how really good these sound. The bass is well defined and clear/strong, and the mids and highs are definitely clear and not muddy. The bass is not overwhelming either, which is a problem with some headphones.

HEADPHONE CONTROLS
The controls can be a bit difficult to read, but once you know where they are, you can figure it out pretty quickly. The +/- and play/pause buttons are separated by the noise cancellation button which is good.

HOW ARE THESE ADJUSTABLE?
These adapt to all sorts of comfortable positions.. They go longer, tilt in and out and rotate from side to side.

ARE THESE ABLE TO FOLD TO BE COMPACT?
These do fold flat and compact if you need to travel with them or store them in a smaller storage area.

CASE?
This did not come with a case.

SOUND CANCELLATION PERFORMANCE
The noise cancellation is awful. It hardly works. When noise cancellation is turned on, the sound gets pretty compromised. It becomes almost muffled in a way and the base definitely goes down.

OTHER FEATURES WITH THESE HEADPHONES
The ability to know how much power is left on the headphones while using the phone is nice, but it does not help if you are using these some other bluetooth device and not a phone. During phone calls, people hear just fine and we can hear them too (several of us tried this feature with our phones)

THE BOTTOM LINE
At this price point, these headphones are a step up from what I usually get when getting headphones for this price range. The sound is well defined and well balanced. Compactness for storage is great, and the comfort is also very good. The only disappointments are noise cancellation, short cord for corded listening, and buttons being a bit difficult to read.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. With better performance from noise cancellation, these would be really really good. As they are, they are still pretty great. They are a great gift to yourself or someone else and are some of the nicer headphones I have used in my journey through headphones of all sorts as well as those the family has obtained. They are not B&O or Turtle Beach, but they still are pretty good.

title: A good game, but not Starfox64
text:
One of the main reasons most people will buy this game is expecting a grand successor to the classic Starfox64. Unfortunately this game does not deliver that.

Don't take me wrong, this is by no means a bad game, but just like StarFox Adventures, this game is not truly the successor to the Nintendo 64 game. The game does not continue and exceed the 'original' game. The main interest for fans- Arwing battles- hasn't been improved upon at all. In fact, aside from improved graphics, they could be considered a disimprovement from the previous games. There is no real innovation in the bosses. They are much the same as bosses from previous games, their weak spots are more evident than ever, and require nothing but mindless blasting to defeat. Powerups such as bombs and hyper lasers have been almost eradicated in this game and are rarely used. Flying an Arwing is still fun, but emphasis in this game was shifted elsewhere.

Instead of concentrating on great Space Battles, a large portion of the game is spent on foot with a blaster. While this part of gameplay isn't poorly done, it's somewhat boring when all you really want is to fly your ship. The game creators did a decent job at creating a balance of power between the arwing, landmaster and pilot, but ultimately we aren't really interested.

The format of the game has also taken a change. Whereas Starfox64 let you choose your root through the Lylat System (greatly increasing replay value in my opinion) Assault only has one course of action and focuses on a linear storyline. Starfox Assault is significantly longer than Starfox64 and so replay is mostly limited to individual levels instead of replaying the entire game to achieve a higher score.

Still, replaying levels will allow you to earn awards and unlock special features for multiplayer. Multiplayer mode is fast-paced fun and can provide hours of great gameplay.

Despite my criticism, StarFox Assault is still a great game, whether you're a fan or new to the Starfox series. Just don't expect it to be the great replacement for Starfox64. For that, I think StarFox Command for the DS might turn out to be a better pick, or you could just wait a few years for something new to come out on the Wii.
