title: Dangerous!! NO QUALITY CONTROL & Higher Phosphorous than Renal Failure cats should have
text:
Anyone with a cat with Chronic Renal Disease, should read ALL the 1-star reviews first!!! I do not know why this product is showing an overall 4+ review rating. I think that is more for the dog food, not cat food.

I ordered this canned food and as many mentioned, it smelled awful, but after a day, my cats ate it. What worked well is the hydrolyzed protein which basically breaks up protein smaller than normal which helps sensitive stomachs and aids easier digestion. With 4 cats with chronic renal disease in Stage 2, suddenly, the vomiting stopped, which was great! HOWEVER, the small expensive food cans had A Lot of bones too large for any cat to chew or swallow. My cats just spit them out or ate around them.

At first, I just threw them away, but after I bought another box of food, there were so many bones I started saving the larger ones. I had almost a full container before I accidentally knocked it over and lost in the drain. Still, you can see those I saved in the picture, with a pencil eraser as size comparison.

Read on and see other pictures of many people who posted 1-star reviews showing blue & white plastic pieces in their food. A LOT of issues with Quality Control!!! They say everything is upscale, quality and made in regulated facilities. PHOOEY!! No USA regulated facility would allow all of these foreign substances at dangerous sizes allowed in food that is NEVER recalled!!!!! Check the dates of the complaints!

Finding food these kitties will eat isn't easy nor cheap!!! At first I believed their marketing and ordered from Amazon. But the last order I received was from Chewy and was different. I called the USA office in Florida and was told it was only the packaging, so I kept it. But once I ordered it, I noticed it didn't smell the same, there were no bones...which I thought was good. However, my cats would not touch or go near the food. They ate the other formula...but not this one. That's when I went back to Amazon to check reviews. I WAS SHOCKED.

When I read others complaining about sharp large plastic pieces in the food, pictures of various blue plastic throughout the food, and others complaining that their cats wouldn't touch the new formula, plus people saying they too were told it was a new package only....I realized the USA office wasn't telling people the truth. That may not be their fault. The company may not be telling them the truth and they are just repeating what they were told.

This wet food should have been pulled from the market due to quality control issues and should not be allowed to be sold as it is very dangerous to cats. Upon reading all the 1 star reviews, I realized that the formula did indeed change in another big way. The old formula had salmon and lamb in it. The new formula has no salmon at all. Also newly included was pig liver and lamb lung. Major formula changes!! Cats were attracted to the salmon...now there is none. Not sure why but my 4 cats will barely touch this food now. I kept thinking they'd get used to it, but after one cat started getting weaker and weaker...and not eating either the dry or wet food...I panicked and gave some other food. OMG, the next day the cat was walking again!!! I felt horrible that the cat was just refusing to eat because of that food!!

That's when I went to check the dry food to see what was in it since they cats weren't eating it either. I had just bought the dry food, but they wouldn't touch it either. To my surprise, the ingredients was not written on the bag. HOW ODD!! I thought that was required in the USA??? I immediately realized this company does not operate with the same controls as a USA company. Since this is the only Renal food I know that does not require a vet prescription, I got very concerned they had virtually no quality control because all these issues had gone on for a long time. I immediately went out and bought new food at the vets office, and removed all this food & threw it away. I didn't even trust giving it to a shelter because I didn't trust it and wouldn't want any other cats to get sick from it.

I haven't found were to complain about the quality control yet, but its definitely NOT with the USA office in Florida .

DO NOT TRUST THIS COMPANY OR THEIR MARKETING BECAUSE everyone who has complained, has similar stories. Quality Control is not adequate if it even exist and it isn't worth hurting your loved pet over.

Amazon needs to separate the dog food reviews from the cat food reviews. And they need to separate the dry from the wet reviews. It appears the dog reviews are better than the cat reviews....at least I didn't see anything dangerous to the dogs like there are for cats. They can hide a lot of negative reviews by combining all the reviews for all of the brand!!! DO NOT GIVE TO YOUR CATS!!

title: easy to use, nice clamshell design, but a little bit too flexible.
text:
The Samsers Wireless Portable Folding Keyboard is only 1/2" thick when folded, and of course, half that when undfolded. It is quite thin and portable. It caught my attention because it supports pairing with up to 3 bluetooth devices simultaneously and with many of us having multiple devices (phone and tablet is quite normal), these devices are great for someone like me.

The clamshell design means that the keys are protected when closed. It also holds itself closed magnetically, and powers on my simply opening it. Pairing is easy: hold the function key and press one of the Q,W, or E keys to select one of the three bluetooth slots, then press the big "connection" button on the left bezel of the keyboard. This all seems pretty slick to me but I did have one concern with this keyboard's design and that is the hinge system. When the keyboard is open, it is quite easy to twist it with just a little bit of pressure. It means that I'm always extra careful when I'm taking it out of my bag.

In terms of functionality, the keys are a the same size as the ones on my laptop and has the same amount of travel as well, although they are a little bit louder than my laptop's keys when typing. I'm using this keyboard to type this review right now. What I found is that the keys are a little bit unresponsive. I keep missing letters every few words I type. Just in this last sentence, I had to go back about 5 times to correct missing letters. This defeats the purpose of purchasing a keyboard to type more quickly on a mobile device. Perhaps if you are normally heavy-handed when you type on a keyboard, you wouldn't face this issue.

Something that I wish this keyboard had is a touch pad. If this device can be both a keyboard and mouse, it would be much more useful.

Overall, the Samsers Wireless Portable Folding Keyboard is a good device but ultimately, it has a couple of shortcomings that keep it from being great.

title: This Frustrated Me TERRIBLY  Let Me Tell You Why
text:
I am pretty good at making things work with computers. Peripherals often need some kind of coaxing or tweaking to make them work well. This, however, was beyond help. Let me explain..

WHAT IS THIS KEYBOARD LIKE?
LAYOUT
This keyboard is what I thought I had been waiting for for years. I have been using my third PC Concepts Ergonomic keyboard that I have used since the early 1990s. I used them because they are set up far better than any of the Microsoft ones. The problem is that they are not USB so I have to have an adapter to use it in USB slots.

TOUCHPAD
This keyboard is set up almost exactly like the other keyboard I have been using. The only difference is the touchpad is in the middle of the keyboard instead of on the right side like it is on mine.

SETTING UP
I was VERY excited to try this. I put my hands on it and was so excited- the spring in the keys and the way that they worked in typing was fast and effective. I could not wait to plug it in! Surely this was worth the VERY long wait for a keyboard like this.

HOW DID THIS WORK?
The box claims that this is plug and play. I plugged it in and ..nothing. WHAT? First the system claimed that there was nothing there. Okay, so I changed USB ports. The mouse signed in haltingly, but no keyboard. I removed all drivers, and then re-installed them. Nope. Nothing. First the touchpad would stagger and no keyboard. Then the keyboard would work but no touchpad. It was very erratic and no matter where I tested it, it would not work correctly.

I tried everything to troubleshoot this thing. Finally I figured out that somehow it appears that thistouchpad/ mouse driver shares the other mouse driver that is in the system. That means that my Wacom pad was no longer working as well as usual. It seemed to be fighting.

Finally I got the keyboard to load up. I began typing. I even considered keeping the keyboard and not hooking up the mouse (probably not possible). Then it happened. I began to type the word "keyboard"

Here is what came out..
keybooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooard.

Did the key stick? Nope. It sprang back. I tried again. Typed fine. Suddenly it happened again. oooooooooooooooo

WHY DIDN'T I JUST GET THE KEYBOARD WITHOUT THE TOUCHPAD?
I got this because due to a wrist issue, I have NEVER been able to use a mouse. Touchpad is all I can use. I also do not have the room on my desk for a mouse pad due to my Wacom tablet. Using the Wacom tablet is not convenient most of the time for regular touchpad use (non-graphic) or I would use that. When I want to do productive work, I want the touchpad in my keyboard.

BACK IT GOES
I tried EVERYTHING to get this to work correctly. I was really hesitant to try another one because at THAT price it should not be this difficult to use. I even tested it on another machine. It worked but had occasional hiccups too.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I wanted this to work SO BADLY. There are just too many issues that made it frustrating. The touchpad not working (seeming to share the regular mouse driver causing other devices to lag along with touchpad not working) , the key repeating, this should not be happening for a keyboard that costs this much. When I put my old keyboard back, the Wacom and touchpad in the old keyboard worked beautifully.

MY RATING
ONE STAR This was very upsetting and try as I might I could not get this to work. I had to send it back. I want so badly to have a keyboard like this that actually WORKS before my remaining keyboard stops working It is really old.

title: Some flaws/glitches....  but XBox 360 controller works quite well
text:
UPDTAE: I was getting a horrible clicking sound from the DVD drive when this disc first started up. I upgraded the firmware and the clicking sound went away.

*****

I had a hard time finding online a review/statement that said if the XBox 360 controller hooked up to the PC would work well with this game: it does. I still have to use 'z' for prone and 'j' for drop weapon, but just about everything else can be found on the controller. And before they say it: YES, most hardcore gamers could/do use the keyboard and perform certain functions faster than the XBox controller.

I did, however, find that flying the VTOL was much more responsive and easier with the keyboard.

Walking is slow, and sprinting is the equivalent of what walking should be. A hack for this and other traits is possible.

A lot of effort was put into the environment and the little things you tend to find here and there. I didn't find it too repetitive or blocky, though others may disagree.

More effort should have put into the the hit points and hit areas for the enemy. What I found:
- head shots do not always kill an enemy (aside from the sniper rifle),
- some enemy can take up to three or four clips of ammo to bring down, whereas the guy next to him goes down with a shot to the chest. Those that wear a beret or camo head gear take more shots to bring down, sometimes up to a dozen head shots,
- shooting the back of the head is nowhere near as effective as the face,

There is also some missing AI when it comes to you slowly walking up to a group of enemy in the pitch dark: they always see you coming, even if their back is turned. Not very realistic. You have to prone-crawl your way up to them in order to hide, or use the cloak. Basically, you could be 100 yards from the enemy in near-total darkness and they always have a bead on you, even if you are in heavy brush or behind a rock.

You could be prone in the middle of a wide dirt path in daylight and they would walk right by you.

The vehicles are nerfed quite a bit. Keyboard is easier to maneuver them. Better vehicle controls in Halo 1+2 with the controller than in this game.

The helicopters are way more durable than they need to be. An rpg can demolish a building, but do nothing to a helo? It takes two shoulder rockets to bring down a helo, and a glancing blow does not count, it has to be dead on. In one part, the doors open on a helo and you can launch a rifle grenade or throw one inside it and that will do the trick, but shooting a grenade at the underside does nothing.

The jellyfish-looking alien things are kind of lame, enough said there.

BLOCKING INTERNET REQUESTS:
Yes, you can block the game from connecting with EA and nothing will happen to your game. I use AVG, and have chosen to permanently block the game's request to access EA -- no problems with the game. I say this because some have written that you have to have an Internet connection to use the game... not so.

So, a lot has been put into the environment of the game, but some realistic interaction could be improved upon.

Let's face it in some fighting games they will have multiple people who feel the same!(I am talking to you Street Fighter) Still love it though.

GOOD/PROS:
1. The story for a fighting game is pretty damn good. The story feels like a DC Comic story. If DC would have allowed for a higher rating, let's say M rating, I feel like they could have shown more story, like how Superman lost control because of the "drugs". Much more emotion are captured through animations, video, and dramatic music versus characters narrating or explaining what happen earlier. 4.0 / 5.0
In order to get a five it would need a longer story which could have been done.

2. The graphics are nice, nothing more nothing less. You will not see photorealistic graphics or high level of physics. 3.2 / 5.0

3. Sound is always half the experience in movies / video games, the other half is of course cinematics. The soundtracks could have been better and louder in some parts more than others but there really was no room to put in. This is a great story however not enough emotion to drive it. So all you have left is background music for different stages. I think it's appropriate and it fits well. 4.0 / 5.0

4. Characters all feel like they should, example Superman move sets are all punches! He only knows how to use his fist which goes well with him. Superman has no need to execute advanced fighting techniques because he is known for always holding back. Batman has a head-butt, an appropriate parry since he is known for a master of parry's. Every characters fighting style felt appropriate according to that character. The voices are done by their original voice actors for the most part that was pleasant :) 5.0 / 5.0

Total AVG = 4.05

CONS/ BADS

1. Not enough custom skins to unlock, come on give me more! This is our only way to express ourselves while playing online.

2. Needing an IOS device to unlock certain aspects of the console version..... WHAT KIND OF #### is this? Not all of us have an ios. You wont be missing anything critical from the game but still we love to unlock everything they made this more... inconvenient.

Conclusion

Good game, you can expect solid 5-7 hours of story mode campaign. This won't be a game where you can invest a few dozen hours like Mass Effect, Skyrim or so on on story mode. After you beat the campaign you do classic battle mode with each character if you desire to see a short clip showing a small side story. After that you go online meet some friends and do different types of matches. Not much replay value afterwards, you just go online and find a new challenger to push you :). That's all there is to a fighting games. My rating was based on rating the Fighting Game Genre, which in my opinion is a proper way to rate games. You compare sports video games to sports video games. FPS to FPS in order to have more consistency in rating.

title: Lack of info for PS3 controllers, and terrible design.
text:
I have two complaints.

Complaint #1
-----------------
They really leave you in the wind with this product. I figured it out, but I'm wondering about people who are not as resourceful. The description implies you just plug it into the Switch, and you start pairing. That is not the case, at least it's not the case for PS3 controllers. There are no instructions, so naturally, I went to 8bitdo's website. On their site, there is something called the PS3 PAIRING TOOL. Sounds like what I need, so I downloaded it. In the downloaded folder is a README file. How often do people read the README files? Luckily I did! It says that before I can launch the software, I need to install a program called the SixaxisPairToolSetup-0.3.0.exe, or I can "Temporarily disable driver signature enforcement." For this 2nd option, there is a bunch of screenshots showing you how to do it in windows. I tried the 1st option first, and after installing the sixaxispairtool, it told me to restart. After restarting, normally a software will launch itself to help you along where you left off, but not this one. Once you restart, it was gone. LOL! So I thought maybe the magic has been done, so I proceeded to launch the PS3 pairing tool, but it didn't work. It would not recognize my ps3 controller. So I decided to try the second option, temporarily disable driver signature enforcement. For this option, I recommend you guys put all the instructional screenshots in your dropbox, then you can follow along reading the instructions from your phone. Because doing these steps will put you in a RECOVERY mode, so you can't view those screenshots anymore. They didn't make this accessory for everybody. They made it for techies and tinkerers who will go out of their way to make it work.

Complaint #2
----------------
8bitdo isn't too good at adapter designs. Take their Gbros adapter for example. It doesn't fit wavebird receivers, not because it isn't compatible, but because of the design. So Retro Fighters basically just built a new shell for that receiver and fixed the issue. So it isn't too surprising to me that this wireless receiver is a bad design too. Why did they make the usb brick casing so fat? You have to imagine that many people have two ps3 or ps4 controllers, that they may want to buy 2 receivers like I did. Well, two receivers will not fit at the same time on the Dock side ports. If you want to use two, you'll have to use a USB A to A extender, or a hub. There is one more usb port in the back of the Dock between the HDMI and Power ports. Guess what, it won't fit there either. If I try to squeeze the brick in, it will lift the power and hdmi cables from their ports at an angle, and this can especially damage the power cable.

I like to imagine this is what happened during product development...

8bitdo: "This is a beautiful design, and when our fans buy ONE receiver to add ONE PlayStation controller, they will be very happy."
Employee: "Should we design it so TWO receivers will fit on the side ports? Maybe also make it fit on the 3rd port in the back? Also, we might want to add a step by step manual for ps3 controllers"
8bitdo: "What's your name? You are fired!"

text:
I have worked with a lot of Bluetooth speakers and I have seen a good variety in features and sound quality. I have a set of Monster headphones and they are excellent; I expected the same from this speaker. It’s a good speaker, but it has a weakness in the sound profile.

It pairs and connects quickly and without any issue. I was able to connect it to my computer without any problems and it was ready to go in less than 20 seconds. In terms of connection speed via Bluetooth, this one is slightly faster than most.

I really like the fact that the speaker has a slider switch for power instead of a button you have to hold down. It makes knowing the speaker is on very simple and it also makes it very simple to power off. This is a big plus to me and is one of the best features in my mind.

I tested the sound quality fairly extensively and make a few important observations, most of which were positive but there was one important issue. The speaker has good volume (controlled by the source) and excellent operational range - I went as far as 30’ and there were no cut-outs or crackles, a good sign. The sound profile though is slightly problematic. The bass is strong - very strong - and is enough to dominate the whole sound output. Many speakers and headsets are heavy-handed on the bass, so this is not totally unexpected but is a bit heavy for my tastes. The highs are good and everything is clear and crisp. The midrange is very flat to the point of being practically non-existent, likely because the bass is as high as it is. Because the midrange is so flat, the output has a tendency to be dull and lifeless.

This is not a bad speaker and it is a decent choice if you want a small and strong speaker. But, be aware that the sound profile is unbalanced.

title: Comfortable grips, but some button missteps
text:
As far as grips go, the EJGAME joycons are pretty comfortable. They fit onto the Switch well and and the Switch still fits into the dock without issue. They're more comfortable to hold for a long time playing than the original joycons.

However... gameplay itself presents some issues. If you're used to Nintendo controllers, those original controllers have very stiff, clicky buttons that have very shallow travel. The EJGAME buttons are incredibly squishy. They have deep travel, and you'll actually end up pressing them in to where your fingertips are hitting the controller casing. If you do any precision gameplay, like platformers or rhythm games, these squishy buttons are really going to throw you off.

The bumpers are also something to get used to. On the original controllers, they wrap around the side of the controller a little, so you can actually hit them with your knuckle--you don't have to fully wrap your finger around the controller to hit the bumper with your fingertip. The bumpers on the EJGAME controllers do not wrap around the sides of the controller at all--you have to use your fingertip to hit the bumper, which means more, slower motion.

After playing for a while, I did get used to using a lighter touch with the buttons, but my scores were still tanking on my favorite rhythm game, mostly because the contact on the button presses is just so slushy. But the controllers are comfortable, and if you're just going for long RPG, visual novel, or other non-precision gaming session, these are pretty nice.

title: actually works nicely
text:
The concept is simple enough... it pulls out and retracts and there's a slide-lock, like a measuring tape. The brilliant thing is I think this is well enough made it won't break after playing with it a few times. I haven't had it long enough to prove this point but Flexi has certainly been around that long and I haven't heard that they're rubbish.

Here's a few things about how I use mine. I bought it primarily for tracking. It's not legal for most competitive tracking events which require a 10 meter (~33 foot) long-line, but this 8 meter tape is more than long enough for practical purposes and you don't waste any time or your second hand line-handling. The tape, I guess it's nylon or polyester, seems to stay free of weeds and stickers unlike cotton lines that seem to grab everything. The line won't burn your hands either since you don't even touch the line.

I clip mine to a harness. I wouldn't like to clip it to the collar because the brake is not smooth. On a really soft dog, just the retractor can be perceived as a correction. But if the dog starts to take off, clicking the brake really slams them. With a hand-held line, there's no abrupt changeover from freespool to locked. The dog should have no problem slamming on their harness though. I just wouldn't do it with a collar.

A smoother brake would be a nice idea, but it's not clear it could be done without considerably more weight or expense. I imagine a lever type drag brake like on a big game fishing reel. It would be progressive but still able to stop the dog quickly.

The weight of this thing is a little high for a leash but not bad at all compared to a 30 foot biothane line. The bottom line is I wouldn't use it in lieu of a 6 foot leash but compared to tracking lines, I think it's a winner.

Update after a little more than 1 year -- My 26' Flexi Explore failed after a trip to the beach where it ingested some salt water and a little sand. The tape would sometimes fail to retract. I took it apart and found it was reasonably serviceable. I cleaned it out and put it back together with a dab of grease on the plate where the edge of the coil spring winds and unwinds (it's greased at the factory as well), and some light silicone lubricant between the plastic spool and the case. But I found that the leash still jams when pulled out to full extension and it won't retract without pushing the spool manually to unjam it. I reassembled it a couple times to try to get it right and had to give up. It will either jam at full extension or fail to fully retract. I took a star off for this failure. It might be repairable with a replacement spring, but the cost of a new one is low enough to consider it disposable after a year of frequent use.

Otherwise I have found the retractable so useful, particularly when I need one-handed control. I actually decided to take Flexi's seriously after reading about a patrolman in Afghanistan who uses a Flexi Giant -- why? to allow the dog to track on-line and still keep his weapon hand free. With a traditional 10m long-line, line-handling takes two hands. I track my dog in IPO and have to use a regulation 10m line, but otherwise I prefer the retractable for one-hand operation. I don't handle a weapon in our peaceful society, but I've often got my hands full with children or the things that accompany traveling with them. Most of my dog-walking for the dog's sake is off leash in rural or wilderness areas, so my leash use is often in urban environments where society expects dogs to be leashed. A short leash is ok, but for more than just a short walk, like when you're going to be out all day, for many, many hours with the dog, I think the dog appreciates a little more freedom than a short leash when the opportunity presents itself.

In any event, I'm ordering another Flex... this time probably going with the Giant version in hopes of getting a little more durability.

title: Wonderful, but not without some faults!
text:
I enjoy the occasional game and decided I wanted to get back into handheld gaming. While cell phone games do have plenty of engaging time-killing games to offer, I was missing games with some depth and story; like Zelda! So I decided to go back to my roots and get a Nintendo console (my roots are the old DMG-1).

After a shockingly small amount of research, I went and impulse purchased the New 3DS XL. If this is your first 3DS, be sure to pick up a charger as well, since, unlike just about any other device that NEEDS a charger, this system does not come with one! Taking the device out of the box, the first thing you will notice is the pristine shiny surfaces that greet you! The exterior is shiny, but don't expect it to stay pretty. It will pick up finger prints if you just look at it. Not only that, but I had scratches on it after a couple weeks of keeping it in my bag (in a pocket that was microfiber lined and all by itself).

Next thing you will notice is the weight. This device actually has some heft to it! It is only 1 or 2 tenths of an ounce lighter than the original Nintendo! I found that I did get a but of hand and wrist strain during the first could days of play. Just something to keep in mind!

Another thing you will notice is that the hinge is a bit flappy. When you open the hinge, you will hear it snap into place in two positions (and by snap, it sounds and feels like you are doing something wrong). This wouldn't be a problem since the second position is where you will want the screen opened to, but the screen moves within that position. I play a lot from a reclined or laying position, so I do notice the top screen wobbling quite a bit. I would estimate that the movement is about 5 degrees. It is enough that, if I am playing while laying down, I often find myself awkwardly positing my index fingers so they wrap around to the front of the device to keep it from moving while I am playing. I have seen video of New 3DS XLs that do not have this issue with the hinge, but most people seem to have it, and people who have contacted Nintendo say that Nintendo does not consider this to be a defect.

Even with all of the negatives I have listed, there is still so much to love about this device. The top screen is beautiful and sharp. The Super Stable 3D does great (even when you play in the dark). The console comes with a few interesting games, so even if you don't by games right away, there is definitely lots of interesting stuff to do on the device. The e-shop is great and even has some great games that you can get for relatively cheap including some old NES and Gameboy games. The controls are generally ergonomic, although I find that the D-pad can be a little uncomfortable if you are playing a game that uses that instead of letting you use the thumb pad. Streetpass and spotpass add a whole other dimension of entertainment. There are a lot of great games available for the system for almost any genre. All the old Nintendo franchises have games for the 3DS that have a terrific balance between familiar characters and new spins on gameplay that develop the story.

title: Small, Simple Treats with Quality Ingredients
text:
Dog owners know that dog treats are a part of the dog caring and dog- loving experience. We don’t want to deprive our dogs of treats but we also do not want our dogs to eat treats that are low in quality with lots of fillers and other potentially bad ingredients. If this concerns you, too, then a good option is Visionary Pet Foods Chicken Crunchy Biscuits for Dogs.

These treats are small in size. They are crunchy, too, with little or no smell. That means you won’t gag when you open the bag but it also means your dog may not be so anxious to get one of them. This is fine by me, since I think it’s good to have treats like this to alternate with the ones that are more pungent and that make my dog drool and with one that are longer- lasting, which these are not.

The best quality of these treats is the ingredients. There are only a few and they are mostly meat, with no grains. You can feel good about serving them to your dog and because there is a large number of treats per bag, they are useful when you want a quick reward to feed your dog or a fast, simple, and efficient bribe to get your dog to do what you want.

Treats matter when you’re a dog and quality matters when you’re a dog parent. These treats from Visionary are good treats for those times when you want something that’s small and quick that still maintains a good level of quality. I recommend adding them to your dog’s daily treat routine.

title: Sounds great and super comfortable
text:
These are excellent for listening to audio in a noisy environment such as an airplane or bus. I wasn't expecting much out of the noise reduction system at this price point but it was pretty decent. Even more useful, however, is the ambient noise mode which will allow you to hear some of the background noise in case you need to be aware (someone talking to you or if you need to hear traffic on a bike, etc). I've used modes like that on modern Sony headphones, and was surprised to find it on something in this price range.

But above all else, I'm most impressed with the comfort of these. The cushion feels premium, I don't know how else to describe it, but it reminds me much more of headphones from brand names that cost several times what this does. The build quality looks much better than my cheap wireless headphones too. The only thing I wasn't impressed with is the call quality with the microphone. But that's sort of par for the course, as only the truly name brand higher end ones seem to get that right- putting a mic by your ears and still somehow picking up your voice over the background noise is a neat trick that isn't copied well by other brands.
Otherwise, for just music and audiobooks with some decent NR and comfort, this is a great value!

title: Banna plugs are different than reuseable than RCA connectors.
text: Banana connectors fit much tighter than a RCA connector and for a person unaware of the difference; it would be easy to cause damage on ether end of the speaker wire to the female connected components. Therefore, I would recommend studying the literature or talking to the manufacture (for both connected ends if necessary). For instance,: in most cases if unaware, it would be easy to cause physical damage simply installing a banana male into a female component just by the tightness, (no clearance between M/FM parts that can fool you into thinking this is as it should be because the male banana is designed to squeeze into the female end and, probably remain as such even after someone trips over an AV receiver  speaker wire, and the A/V falls on the floor because the banana connector was so tight you could lift the A/V by the speaker wire. A banana male connector is designed to expand during installation. If you are in need of banana connectors, these connectors are extremely well made and are a very good bang for the buck.  They are also reusable and do not need any special tools other than basic wire strippers.

title: So GLAD To Have This Case
text:
We have two rather large cats. That might sound crazy for a carry case this size, but after our last experience, trust me, it is best. Let's take a look..

WHAT IS THIS CASE LIKE?
As you can see from the photo, this is a two toned gray case. The case comes in pieces. You have to put it together yourself. The assembly is easy and the cage goes together well.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
We need extra room for our cats because they are VERY active. When the case is too small they really freak out. This one is really nice, having extra room for pacing if waiting at the vet's office is taking longer than they would like. The gate went on well and shuts tightly. The screws all went into the top and bottom easily and hold it in place nicely. When the vet needs to get our our male cat, unscrewing is easy.

HANDLE
The handle is good, but I always prefer to carry with two hands when I can.

BREATHING HOLES
There are plenty of holes which is good. Our male cat does better in this case, as our female, well she has a tendency to bite like a dog and gnaw at things like this. Each hole has her paw sticking out from it at least once a minute.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a good solid straight forward carry case for medium to small dogs or large cats like we have, this was a good choice for us. Although I prefer a top opener, the sturdiness of this one is a little nicer than the other top opener we have. The handle is good and the case is solid and not difficult to put together.

MY RATING
Five stars. You can take the case apart to store it if you need to save space- just remember to put the parts in plastic zip locks and store them between the top and bottom which stack inside each other when not assembled.

text:
If you have a Thunderbolt 3-equipped computer, this drive provides speeds approaching the highest-end built-in SSDs. Case in point: I have a 2018 MacBook Pro with top specs. Its internal SSD is a screamer. And, as you can see from my screen shots, the X5 is right in the same neighborhood. These tests were run on my computer while it was running a bunch of other things (Word, Excel, VMWare Fusion, Mail.app, Safari with about 15 tabs open), so it represents real-world use.

And, as you can see, the X5 is really fast. If you need speed and have Thunderbolt 3, this is a great drive.

Installation was easy. My Mac recognized the drive right away. I could've just used it, but Samsung provides a utility on the drive for enabling its onboard encryption and keeping its firmware up to data. Recommended.

(But do make sure your computer has Thunderbolt 3. You can't tell just by looking at the ports, as TB3 is implemented as a superset of USB-C. So, Thunderbolt 3 is USB-C but the converse is not true. Similarly, previous-rev Thunderbolt interfaces aren't forward-compatible to TB3 devices. Some of the one-star reviews of this drive are clearly from folks who didn't know these issues.)

title: Overwatch is a fast-paced first person shooter that brings a sense of sheer delight to the genre not seen since Team Fortress 2
text:
15 million players can't be wrong, right?

Overwatch is a fast-paced first person shooter that brings a sense of sheer delight to the genre not seen since Team Fortress 2. It's not the most competitive of games (bizarre hit boxes and tick rate, balancing issues, these hold it back) but it's easily one of the most fun. Featuring a massive cast of heroes, the learning curve is steep but rewarding. "Training" and "Quick Play" modes help the novice practice and prepare themselves, while offering seasoned players a less-pressuring respite from the "Competitive" mode, where things get a bit more serious. And you'll want to train extensively - each hero is unique and has their own play style and personality, no clones here.

Content-wise, the game can feel a little sparse but Blizzard is clearly hard at work. Just a few months after launch, they've added another hero (for free!) and a fun summer event with special cosmetic unlockables (cosmetics, incidentally, are the only things you can buy outright - no pay to win here) and its own mode of play (which is absolutely a ball.) The game does sorely miss a single-player campaign, especially with the enticing depth of characters and lore. However, this feels like a game that will grow for a long time, so it's not one you'll be quickly bored with.

Graphically, the game ranges from good to adequate, and while it's not exactly stunning in any regard, it generally performs reliably, which I'll alwys prefer. It really shines in sound design, however. Sound cues are clear and really, truly important in this game, adding an extra layer of depth. The music is fun and atmospheric without being intrusive, though not much is memorable besides the main theme.

Five stars do not indicate a perfect game, of course. There are bugs, there are balance issues, there is that really weird tick rate. But Blizzard is listening, communicating, and always updating. This is the most fun I've had with an FPS in ages, and for that, five stars for sure.

title: Disappointing - The Low Price is Justified
text:
This is my first exposure to Panasonic Active Noise Canceling (ANC) headphones. This particular model is very inexpensive relative to most ANC phones on the market, and unfortunately the low price is justified. These phones fall short in a couple of important areas.

First and foremost, these are ANC phones and the ANC function does indeed work. That said, the degree to which it works is in line with the pricing. I have a very specific fan in the house that I use as a benchmark, as most ANC phones are able to nearly completely wipe out the white noise that this fan generates when on the lowest speed setting. The Panasonic phones kill a good bit of the fan noise but allow more noise than almost every other ANC set I have tried. In the office I tried these phones in an area serviced by two large air handlers that generate a lot of noise and these headphones did remarkably well though still not as well as most other phones I have tried in the same environment. Now, when compared to the likes of Bose, Panasonic does a very poor job but then again they cost maybe 15% of what Bose costs. When considering this price differential the Panasonic phones do a decent job with their ANC which should be acceptable by most for traveling.

One area where these phones fail, though, is in build quality. These headphones are extremely lightweight and they feel very flimsy and fragile. These are not the headphones to take when traveling frequently. To add insult to injury, they come with a cloth carry bag which offers absolutely no protection at all beyond serving as a dust cover.

Worse, though, is the miserable sound quality. I don't know if my specific headset is the problem but while I have a decent full range of sound, everything across the spectrum sounds slightly tinny and hollow. I was encouraged that Panasonic does not overdrive the bass as many manufacturers tend to do and instead delivers a fairly balanced spectrum, but this does not make up for the poor quality of sound. As these are inexpensive headphones I would never expect them to be audiophile quality, but the sound should absolutely be much better than it is.

I was encouraged to see that Panasonic includes a 2-prong adapter in the package, but then they omit the 1/4" adapter which is something I actually use.

Panasonic has made a very inexpensive ANC headphone and unfortunately the low cost is justified. While the ANC capabilities are within reason for the price range, the sound quality and build quality are severely lacking. If looking for ANC phones for the purpose of using the ANC function, and keeping costs low is important, then these phones may fill that need acceptably. However, if sound quality is in any way important, these are the wrong phones and will sorely disappoint.

title: This monitor is great for my multi-window work
text:
I work full-time from home and, over the years, have increased the size of my monitor because…why not, right?

I’m online all day long and currently working with so many windows, it just made sense for me to upgrade again recently and go with this 34-inch monitor.

I have always been drawn to the curved screens and decided I would just treat myself. It’s almost comforting to have that curve kind of wrap around you visually. I think it actually helps me stay better focused.

I set up a pleasant and not too busy (for me) background that frames whatever I’m working on. Sometimes I just center everything in the middle and other times I spread many of my windows out so I can drag and drop, reference something, etc. I honestly think this speeds up my work and makes me more productive.

I’m still learning what works best for me but look forward to turning this screen on every day.

I’m not yet into gaming but perhaps someday I will make that leap. I can see this wider monitor immersing the player in the game. The colors are rich and there are all sorts of ways to customize your preferences. I’m sure most gamers know what to look for, so check out the specs to see if this is the monitor for you.

I’m reviewing from a working aspect and am very happy with my purchase.

I’m glad I went with the height-adjustable model. I had my last 23-inch monitor on a separate monitor stand and that took up some valuable room on my desk. This LG monitor has the curved base (I’m sure to better have it balanced) and I work around that quite nicely. My keyboard can sit on the base comfortably, if I have to move it for paperwork I need to review.

I feel this is a good value and I trust LG products. I do recommend and would purchase again if needed.

title: Luigi's Mansion (Gamecube)

I would highly recomend this game for all ages of play. So have fun and enjoy the search for Mario in the haunting game Luigi's Mansion.

box that it all came in. What cat can resist a new box? From here on out, I will refer to this new scratcher as the CCAS, for obvious reasons.

That being said, we have scratchers of some sort in every room of our place. This keeps them from deciding the furniture looks like fun.Our smaller cat Katy loves cardboard, and loves to scratch at an incline, so this was a natural for her. We have the flat one [[ASIN:B0002ASD6G Cosmic Pet Cardboard Scratcher with Catnip]], but wanted to try this one too.

Ours came totally sealed up with a small bag of catnip included. There is a shiny mylar ball attached from the inside and visible to the cats through the circular cutouts on both sides. (Note that our Mau found this right away and was very interested in trying to get it out! At one point, he managed to pull it out enough to bite it and was trying to remove it. He turned the scratcher over instead. Since it is cardboard, no harm, no foul.) I sprinkled a light bit of catnip on the scratcher to see what they'd think of it first. Cosmic Catnip is their favorite kind anyway, so I did not anticipate any problems (even though the bag did not have any scent at all. Also, ours did not have the C/C label on it, like it is shown in the product photo).

I posted several photos of our cats' first encounter with the CCAS. I'll try to get some more with a clearer shot, but I wanted to catch the first reactions. It was popular right out of the box! Nascar was the first to try it out (because Katy was sleeping). He loved it! Now, you'll note in the background of my pics that you'll see an Emery Cat scratcher back there too (the arched one). My daughter bought that for Nascar for his birthday. We thought he'd love it. Nope! He didn't want anything to do with it. The texture of that one is VERY rough, like an emery board, and we think it was uncomfortable on his paws. He loved the feather thing that came with it, and that was all. It has sat taking up floor space for 4 months.

Nascar was after the mylar ball first, but then spent time climbing around on the CCAS, laying on it, scratching it and sniffing every square inch. He then went to play with the brown paper shipping material for a little while. By this time, Katy realized something was going on and came in to check it out. She was immediately on top of the CCAS, rubbing it, scratching it and enjoying it! Now, she scratched the opposite way than I thought she would... I thought she'd be on the floor and sort of drag down the cardboard. Nope! She sat on it at the back and scratched from the lowest part back towards herself! Oh well - as long as she likes it!

Both cats adored the mylar ball, and I think it would be fairly easy to replace once it comes off. There is a washer attachment underneath the replaceable scratching surface. I could see hiding a few more of the mice in there as well, just for fun.

I am SO happy we bought this one. They have been playing with it all night. Nascar has tried to chase Katy away from it, claiming ownership, even tho it is a share toy. (Note - we bought this for their Christmas gift (don't laugh - lots of pet lovers give their pets gifts!), but I was too weak. I gave it to them right away.) We are probably going to get one for downstairs too, just because they are enjoying it so very much.

I highly recommend the CCAS. You can use any kind of catnip with it that your cat likes, or leave the catnip off entirely.
It probably won't matter, because the cardboard is such an attraction for the kitties. The company also sells replacement cardboard inserts, so no need to buy the entire scratcher again either. All in all, a great value, great cat item, and results in happy kitties.

title: Flexible, low-profile, great for MP3 players
text:
I use this to connect my MP3 player to a 3.5mm jack I installed in my car's center console. The low-profile 3.5mm connector was very important to me because I wanted to make the connection as slim as possible to avoid accidentally torquing it, catching things on it, or applying pressure to the jack when moving things in and out of the console.

It works quite well for this purpose. the connector is slim - about as slim as they come, such that it basically clamps right up against the side of the player and the wall of the console. The plug itself feels solid and has a small snap when connecting to things. The cable is soft and almost as flexible as a woven cord, even if it does prefer some orientations to others. Sound quality is typical - which is to say, as good as every other cable I've owned.

The only thing I didn't like about the cable was the colors - it really doesn't go with the car interior and stuck out as a result, a bit distracting. So I used a Sharpie Pro - the big chisel-tip type - to turn it black. It is cotton sheathing, so this is quite viable. I was careful - after inking the entire cable and letting it dry, I washed it in warm water, then dried it and ran a soft, clean rag over it about a hundred times, until it came away basically clean. After the fact, while you could tell the original black bits from the inked threads, it's just different shades of black, rather than looking blotchy. I imagine using something like RIT black dye would be about equally effective, if you heated it and let it soak for a good long while.

So I would recommend it. The braided cable looks premium and is much easier to work with than its equally-thick rubber counterparts. This makes it easy to handle the MP3 player while it is still plugged in.

title: A new standard
text:
First of all, I'll say like everyone else, that the game is amazing. I wasn't sure I'd like it as much as I did but most of it works great.
Back when shadow of the colossus (sotc) 1st came out I remember thinking that this is what I'd like zelda games to be. And in many ways this game reminds me of sotc. Some similarities:
*The horses have a mind of their own which you guide
*Stamina limitations for climbing etc
*Gathering of fruits and animals (lizard tails in sotc)
*The Devine beasts can be liken to colossi
But while sotc was a simple game, zelda botw has taken most of those ideas and evolved into a much more elaborate game.
Weapons and shields break, don't really love it but sometimes you genuinely have to prepare your gear before certain tasks are done.
There are tons of things to gather.
Your preparation can lead to frustrating battles or comfortable victories.
Unfortunately the game is so open that the story is given in recollected memories and early in game discussions. This due to the fact that most of the game can be considered optional content.
Exploration is the heart of this game, there's always something interesting to be discovered or do, some alternative way to defeat a group of enemies... There's always something. It's great how lively this world feels.
A nice touch is how the climate affects you and the various ways in which you counter these effects. Too cool? Spicy food and warmer gear. Thunderstorm? Put away your metal gear. Its all interesting and fun, you sometimes need to explore more and discover new stuff that would make these trips more comfortable.

One note is the learning curve, because it's so open, you can find yourself feeling pretty overwhelmed by the enemies you meet up. While this is mostly due to not being prepared, you can die a lot and meet some challenges.

May edit this review when I experience more but so far the game is awesome, a must have for everyone that has a Wii U of Switch.

title: Solid Conclusion with a Few Things that Could Have Been Better
text:
If you haven't played Corpse Party or Corpse Party: Book of Shadows you are going to be very lost without a wiki. That's of the biggest downsides to this game. Luckily you can get these two games from the playstation store to download - what I should have done. Nonetheless, the third installment of this series was intriguing enough to make me backtrack and go look for the other games. That being said, now having played the remake of the original, I feel like I have something to compare it to.

I liked that you can hide from the enemies in this game. though it does make it frustrating because a lot of times you need talismans to make them permanently gone. But that's the challenge in this game. I liked the addition of the flashlight and all the traps and tripwires that litter the grounds. It gives the school a much more ominous and hostile feel. This school really does want to claim your life. The fact that the school is in 3-D also helps add to the feeling that you are really there.

I did not like how it kept skipping back to the real world. That is my biggest nitpick. It gives you a break from the horror and if you want that, you'll like it. But you aren't supposed to get a break from the horror! You are supposed to sweat and feel the pressure of being trapped in that place. It's part of what creates Corpse Party's horror element for me. Also, I will straight up say I hate the Mary Sue. You'll know who when you play it, it's kind of obvious. Seriously. Poor substitute for Mrs. Yui. The whole time I was praying for that character to meet a gruesome end. I hated that character that much. Her attempts to seduce a child were more nauseating to me than some of the aspects of the game that were designed to actually be nauseating. Aiko on the other hand, I absolutely adored. The things in this paragraph are a big part of the reason it got 4 stars from me. They went way too moe and way too anime in what is supposed to be a conclusion to a disturbing set of events. Way too anime and not in the good way. It's annoying even at the best of times and does not work for this genre. If they would have stuck more to the actual worrying about their friends that went ahead of them to Heavenly Host and finding clues about that instead of a completely useless and stupid hot springs scene, it would have been okay. I got the feeling at times that even Satoshi was aggravated at how he was getting railroaded in this story.

On the other hand, if you like Ayumi and Yoshiki, this is a good thing for you as this focuses primarily on them. I just really wish we'd have seen more of Satoshi and Naomi getting to do something useful instead of it coming in so late in the game.That's the only problem I have with the story. But the events that were unfolding did make me curious enough to stick around and see where this ending was going. And I do like that the ending can be interpreted in different ways depending on whether you watch that last scene.

title: It's OK as DLC
text:
This is a _very_ short campaign. Before going into the campaign itself:

Installation was much easier than installing the original game. Probably due to the fact that, by now, you have the Origin client installed, and the DLC installs thru that. Once installed, it does NOT show up on the main list of games, and the order receipt shows "no serial number necessary", so it was a little confusing at first how to actually PLAY the DLC. It doesn't appear in the main menu under "Downloadable content".

Once the DLC is installed, you "Continue" an existing game, and you'll trigger a new quest to start playing the DLC. You have to be level 10 to trigger the quest, but if you've finished the OC, you should more than meet the requirements. This is rather an interesting method to activate the DLC, and I liked it.

I was level 40 (the max), have most of my skills maxxed, and a nicely outfitted character who migrated right into the DLC campaign.

This said, consider the rest of this review to contain possible spoilers.

As I said, the DLC campaign is very short, and most of it revolves around building your new keep, which is a very sweet residence indeed, a miniature town. In between running the restoration quests, you complete the main story quests for Dead Kel, as many of these quests will intersect. So you'll be in the area anyways.

One word of warning, and a definite spoiler, once you begin the final Dead Kel quest, going into his dungeon, make sure you have enough inventory space to loot every chest and pile, because once you vanquish Dead Kel, it looks like you cannot return.

I didn't log how many hours I played until I defeated Dead Kel, but it was certainly less than 10, and probably something you can hammer out over a weekend. As I said above, since I was maxxed out on character, at no point in playing did I get that "oh crap" feeling, where I was in over my head. That's kind of unfortunate, and as annoying as it is to reload an earlier save, it's all part of the challenge.

Playing a game is not always about rushing to the end, and in this DLC, there are ongoing quests you can keep playing. These are similar to the "tasks" in the OC, and entail you talking to some of the denizens of your new castle, as you dispense justice or take on other challenges.

I have not tried to go back to the mainland of the OC, but I do know you cannot fast-travel to e.g. Rathir, so I don't know if there is a method to return...

There was no increase to the level cap, it's still level 40, and I really didn't find any loot that exceeded what I already had, save a few pieces of armor. I did miss some of the chests, so I'll go back and loot everything I can.

title: Awesome game, open world, tense firefights
text:
I'd never played any of the OFP games before this one and I'm impressed, it has been too long since there's been an approachable military tactical like the GRAW and Rainbow Six Vegas games. One thing you should do if you are only a slightly more than casual player is get a trainer/cheat, otherwise it's too realistic and it seems like you would die a lot as you are expected to work miracles in some missions. It's also not that large of a game in terms of GB's and the missions and number of commands are not ponderously huge like the ARMA games.

The missions are made pretty clear by HQ and you have HUD checkpoints and objectives as well as a map to keep you moving towards the objectives. Commands to your team are easily done with the radial menu in game by pushing the Q button and navigating to your command via the WSAD buttons. This is also how you call in support like mortars, artillery and airstrikes. You can also give commands via the map screen but it's not really recommended as the map is only zoomable to a grid size, not a tactical size. Once you give your command you announce it in the grid coordinates, which seems a little overdone when you are just ordering your team to a point you can see, I can see this making sense for out of visual contact things like the artillery and the like though. A bad thing is that when you order your team to move to a point it seems it takes them a long time to get there or they don't move there when under fire, what's the point of ORDERS then? Another thing is if you have to jump out of a vehicle and run to stay alive your team NEEDS to be ordered to follow you, as if.

Vehicles are pretty straight forward to get into and either drive or be a passenger and you can switch to a swingman view for this if you want. You can only see immediately in front while in swingman/follower view though instead of using the mouse to look left/R/behind so that's a negative aspect of the vehicles. All I saw that you can use is 4 wheel cars, no tanks or planes.

The missions are pretty huge as far as ground to cover and non-planned objectives and there's a good variety of shoot em up focused ones and stealth missions. I'd like to see some city combat situations though instead of the almost total mission time in the mountains/fields. Also I've been in mission and seen the time of day ambient light change which is a nice touch. At times the checkpoint autosaves can be a little too far apart if you do go down but it wasn't a big problem with my God mode trainer. You can also fail a mission by not doing certain things in an allotted time or being detected when stealth is a mission necessity. At times it does seem to be a long time just hiking to your next objective but it leaves vehicles and enemies at good points in between to break it up.

I found the weapons to be accurate graphically and in sound to real assault rifles as I've fired a few of the real things. Also the difficulty in hitting a target seems about right. If you've never fired a weapon at a target you can't possibly know how much skill is involved, it's hard to hit a target at 8 feet with a 9 mm handgun due to many factors and this is also true of any other firearm. So that's not a legitimate gripe.

Overall graphically this is pretty good for the huge environments, It seems to make a nice tradeoff in that respect. Every little thing in the game is not top quality detailed like buildings or vehicles but that's not the real fun of the game anyways. The characters and weapons are nicely done and that's what you see most of the time anyways. I'm not sure how much of a system hog this is as I have a quad core 6600 and an 8800GT and 3GB RAM so most games don't touch my system but it doesn't seem to be unreasonable. It auto detected my system about where it should be at 1680x1050 and it ran smooth at all times. The sound was great, very nice buzzing bullets and helos as well as ambient outdoors sounds.

One thing I'd like is to choose my own loadout, it's pretty ridiculous going to take out an AAA site and not even carrying a heavy weapon capable of taking out the armored AAA vehicles. You have to find one of the crates that are around with different, usually enemy, weapons in them to get what you need at times. I think at least one of your squad should carry a bazooka of some sort at all times. And it would be nice to choose a silencer and a scope other than a red-dot, look at the guys in Iraq and you'll see that at least one of a squad has an ACOG 4x scope. Usually it's the commander, which you are in this game, that has that. So you are at the mercy of what is given to you as far as weapons unless you want to take the crappy but scoped Chinese stuff off of a casualty.

The story is explained in flash/graphics instead of cutscenes at the very beginning of the campaign missions and that's fine. I found the story to be a little unbelievable though as far as Americans fighting for Russia's interests, I don't think anyone in the USA would want Americans doing that. It's hard enough to take Americans dying for ungrateful and undeserving Iraqis, Serbians, Africans and others. Who cares, in terms of strategic US interests, about an island north of Japan anyways? The part where the Chinese invade Eastern Russia is totally believable though, as when you have 1.5 billion people you need a lot of resources and there's a lot of that in E. Russia. The overall story doesn't really intrude on the game though and that's a good thing, this is just a straight tactical military simulator and that's how you look at it, one objective to the next.

Overall I loved this game and will probably play it again, especially since you can choose individual missions once you've finished the campaign or just go get a full save game on the net. Obviously this is going to have add-on packs like OFP1 did so it is a game that will last a long time. I'm getting the OFP1 GOTY edition which has all the add on packs included after playing this one, it's great and recommended!

title: Great universal charger
text:
As for all items made by Nitecore this charger is made in china. That being said I find their products to be high quality and well constructed. This charger is no exception. The charger is a great improvement from my Nitecore I4 as I can now select charging current when charging only one AAA or low mah battery. When I say selectable I mean from 300 ma to 750 ma. This is as far as the current adjustment goes, which is fine for most needs. The current does not stay fixed at those currents as the battery charges, but it will not apply more than the selected current during the charge cycle. It will not tell the capacity of the battery like many other chargers I have seen and owned. This charger purely charges and does not discharge so if your looking for one that does look elsewhere. La Crosse makes a nice one for NiMH and NiCad. The feature to turn the screen off during charging is nice, and was one of my biggest complaints with the I4. I use it to charge every thing from AAA to 26550 batteries. When charging the larger batteries an issue arises with how many can actually fit, and when I charge 26650 batteries that is only 2.
It is a great universal charger, and with the added Li-FePO4 charging cycle it makes it an easy choice for people that need a good solid charger that works for almost everything.

The primary lens I have on my camera is a good 18mm-55mm lens and it does great for capturing images that are a foot or more away. When I get much closer than that my camera is unable to focus properly and I end up with a crummy shot and I either have to give up or back up so that it can focus – not what I want most of the time. These magnifying lenses are a good solution, but there are somethings you have to keep in mind when using them.

I will start with a statement that should be obvious: make sure you have the correct lens size when you are purchasing add-on lenses like this set. This particular set can be used only with a lens where the thread size is 55mm. If you have a lens that has a different sized thread, you should consider looking for this kit in a different thread size. You can use a ring adapter, but getting the right size at the start is better.

There are four lenses in this kit, a 1x, 2x, 4x and 10x lens, each increasing in power as the numbers suggest. You can somewhat view these as magnifying glasses for your camera, but that metaphor is not completely accurate. They do magnify the image for you, but they allow a closer shot as well and you can get very close to your subject when you have one of these attached to your lens. Perhaps a better way to describe them is to realize that they make your camera very nearsighted and your camera can see close-up well and distance not at all when using these lenses.

The main thing to remember about them is that as they go up the scale in strength they introduce a lot more edge distortion. This is most obvious with the 10x lens. If you take this lens and hold it so that you can see things through it clearly in the center, you cannot help but notice a large area around the edge of the lens that is distorted. The effect is less then you get it close to something on which you wish to focus but it is something to keep in mind. If there is too much distortion, use a less powerful magnification lens.

These particular lenses have a little bit of heft to them but they are not what I would consider heavy. Because they are glass they are a bit more substantial than resin or plastic lenses.

Overall, these are nice lenses. I have been able to use them for taking very close shots that I otherwise would not be able to take with my camera, such as ridge detail on a penny or dot patterns on magazine print. These are not real-world examples but they definitely show off the capabilities of such lenses. If you are looking for good magnification lenses for your camera, this is a good set that works well. Just make sure you have the right thread size before you buy.

title: Lowepro SlingShot 202 AW
text:
The fit and finish of this bag are top notch. I've been camping and backpacking for decades and I have to say the quality of this bag and the workmanship are among the best I've seen. The nylon material is heavy duty and durable. The bag and shoulder strap are well padded for comfort and protection of your gear. The pack includes a built in micro-fiber cloth and two memory card slots in the main compartment. There's even a tuck-away all-weather cover in the bottom of the bag for inclement weather situations. The dividers in the main compartment are infinitely adjustable and all can be removed/repositioned. The pack includes a pull-out tripod holder/foot pocket and strapping system on the side of the bag. There's also a separate compartment at the top of the pack for personal items large enough for wallet, keys, an emergency poncho, etc. Also included are two smaller pockets on the back of the pack suitable for lens pens, notepad, pens, what have you.

This bag is huge. Easily as big as most hiking day-packs. There's room for everything and the kitchen sink. Currently I have my old Canon AE-1 with 80-200 mm lens attached. My 55 mm auxiliary lens. A half dozen assorted filters. Cable release. 1:1 reverse adapter AND my Kodak Z-650 point and shoot all in the main compartment.

Ease of use is incredible. The shoulder strap and waist belt are widely adjustable for people of almost all sizes. The zippers work flawlessly and fast never catching or hanging. The velcro throughout the pack is quite heavy duty and looks like it will hold up to years of abuse. All you need do is slide the pack from your back to the front of your body and the camera access section is right there. You never have to take the bag off to get at your rig.

Those are the pros.

Here are just a couple cons:
The micro-fiber cloth is not removable. I'm not sure what you could do if it became soiled or stained and needed cleaning. The strap for the tripod is not fixed to the pack and could easily be lost. The all-weather cover fits very tight to the bag (in and of itself this is a good thing, but...) it won't fit over any but the smallest mono-pod or tripod. My [[ASIN:B00005T3TI Ambico 54 Inch Tripod with Quick Release (V-0555)]] just barely fits on the pack.

I have no doubt this bag would last years for anyone from amateur to most demanding professional.

title: Stainless Steel vs Aluminum.
text:
This is my fourth Apple watch. I’ve purchased the series 0, series 1, 2, two series 4. One stainless, one aluminum. The 4 is such a great watch, I never felt the need to upgrade. I recently paid Apple $ 79 to replace my battery. They actually replaced the watch. I’ve never had a problem with any Apple watch. I purchased the 7, because of a great Amazon price.

Stainless steel vs aluminum. Both are great. I put one bad scratch on my aluminum crystal. It doesn’t affect function, and it only shows when the watch is dark. It happened when my watch hit the rough edge of our granite countertop. My SS has never scratched.

Why spend the extra money to get the stainless? If you want a GPS only model, the SS is $ 300 more than the aluminum. If you want cellular capability, the difference drops to $ 200. Due to health issues, my wife convinced me to get the cellular capability. In an emergency, these will call 911, even when your phone is not around, and even when you don’t subscribe for service. That’s important.

The series 7 has a blood oxygen measurement feature. During Covid, we purchased two different fingertip devices to measure blood oxygen. We were disappointed with both. The watch oxygen measurement works seamlessly. We consider it worth buying for that feature alone.

Summary.

If you want cellular capability, spend the extra $ 200 for SS. If you don’t, buy the aluminum model and save $ 300.
Both are great watches.

title: Another top notch product from Sony
text:
I'll admit, I'm a fan of Sony. I've owned all sorts of things from the brand, from the aftermarket stereo in my car to my professional camera equipment I use at work. They just make reliably good products. However I've mostly owned Samsung television sets just because it's what I had access to on a more regular basis.
I was therefore excited to try out this TV and see how it compared. To be honest, I really REALLY like Sony's color science. It's part of why I prefer their camera equipment, and it shows on this display. The contrast ratio and dynamic range are everything I wanted it to be and more. The skin tones as well, however the average consumer probably wouldn't notice or care about these things. Where the big differences lie in major TV brands these days is going to be features. The latest crop of Smart TVs have so many bells and whistles, you practically don't need anything other than an internet connection anymore. Unlike Samsung's UI which has embraces Amazon's Fire Stick style UI, Sony has gone the Google TV route. There are pros and cons to both approaches, although I think perhaps arguably there isn't as much free included content as Samsung (Samsung actually includes free live TV channels via "Samsung TV", which Sony does not have). But for all the content I actually WANT to see, Netflix, Prime, Disney+ etc, it works perfectly!

So why only 4 stars? This isn't the fault of Sony's TV, but I really wish they'd make it easier to spot and turn off... I really REALLY hate the default motion smoothing (aka "soap opera effect") that all the big brands use these days. As a content creator, I shoot videos in a particular frame rate on purpose. The motion blur or lack thereof helps tell the story in some kinds of scenes. But most TVs want to show off their high refresh rate and therefore use realtime smoothing algorithms to create fake overly-dramatic effects to pump out extra in between frames. The motion looks too smooth to the point it seems CGI (because it sort of is). It just looks off once you notice it, and Sony is no exception. You have to dig around and figure out what they call it on every TV just to make it look normal again, on this set it is called Motionflow and it can be confusing to turn it off. I wish manufacturers would make it a simple and easy to understand toggle switch... maybe even present it as an option to the viewer upon setting it up so they can understand what they are enabling and decide if they want it or not (I strongly recommend not!).
But again, that's true of all modern Television sets, on its own right this is a solid TV and I would recommend it.

title: Just as I F.E.A.R.E.D. -- A console port!
text:
What can I say that others haven't said? Nothing much, but F.E.A.R. 2 is a let down, and it's supposed to be a sequel. I was insulted on how dumbed-down the graphics, the gameplay and enemy AIs were. The graphics are what really ticked me off, although the original F.E.A.R. was not visually the best, but it was great for a 2005 game -- I managed to get 180fps on average with maxed settings, while F.E.A.R. 2 with it's watered downed graphics(also maxed out), I was locked at 60fps (without vsync). My specs are nowhere near high end, but I was surprised at this 60fps cap. If you played the first game, you can visually tell that F.E.A.R 2 is graphically inferior to that of the first game. Two other things that threw me off was the lack of mouse button support -- talk about a console port. A PC game made in 2009 does not support more than 3 mouse buttons!? Yes, F.E.A.R. 2 does NOT recognize your mouse's side buttons; If you want to program those buttons, you have to use 3rd party software to do so. Also there are no more quick saves, yup -- another step backwards. Your progress is saved via checkpoints.

Gameplay was disappointing as well. Leaning was completely removed; and of course they added the console "cover system", which doesn't help at all and I never once used. Story was surprisingly short. I was able to beat the game in under 8 hours without rushing the game. The scares weren't also that great, I was expecting some good ones, but was disappointed. As for multi-player, I wasn't able to play since I didn't want to make a GameSpy account.

Overall, F.E.A.R. 2 was not the game I was hoping for. It seems today, every FPS is a console port. I was hoping this wasn't a port, but it turned out to be with everything to the visuals to the gameplay, even the littlest thing was completely revamped for console systems. I don't recommend the game if you love F.E.A.R. and its expansion packs, this game is nothing like them. I give this game 2/5 stars; I saved it from the 1 start of death mainly because it's not one of the worst games I've played, but definitely one of my least favorite games.

title: Educational....
text:
This is a simple game and it doesn't take much to play it. You don't have to think too hard, either, but when not playing the "Top Trump File" can be read to learn more about who/what is on the card. I don't see it being something anyone would want to play on a regular basis, but for occasional play, it's a nice way to spend some time with others and it manages to easily get some education into my children's day. It also helps to pass the time if boredom is there. Even when not playing, it's fun just to look through the cards, at least to me.

To play, someone deals the cards to the players face down. The players then pick up their cards, so only one card is visible. The player to the dealer's left starts and picks any stat on their card to call out. The other players call out that same stat and the best number gets all the cards, which then goes to the bottom of that person's stack. The winner of each round picks the next stat for the next round. The game ends when a player has all the cards, and they win. This can take awhile to play, so the directions have instructions for a quicker version, too, along with details about what to do if 2 players both have the best stat.

Depending on what set it is depends on what stats are included. The "Greek Myths" set has Strength, Magic, Terror, Audacity, and Top Trumps Rating. The "Ancient Rome: Gods and Emperors" set has Strength, Legacy, Terror, Popularity, and Top Trumps Rating. The "Washington DC: 30 Things to See" set has Cost, Visitors per Year, Year Established, Visit Time, and Top Trumps(Must See). They all have a picture of some sort, along with more information about the person/place/etc.
