title: Two Laptop Cooling Pad Reviews *Updated*
text:
I have been considering a laptop cooling station for quite a while now. I had really hoped to review the smaller N5 mode which appears much lower than the N3 I was asked to review.
The first thing I noticed is the unit expects your laptop to have a USB port on the left hand side. Okay, the cable IS long enough to reach one of the two USB ports on the left side of my laptop but just barely. The on/off button and the extra USB port that's part of the base which is powered by the laptop's port that powers the cooling pad are rather out of the way and hard to reach. The port is also USB-2 only so if your machine is like mine make sure you leave the USB-3 open for things that require USB-3 connectivity.
The single fan is very quiet, I wouldn't call it 100% silent but it doesn't make that much noise. When it runs it gives an attractive blue glow. . . which you really don't get to see because the laptop's on top of the cooling pad. There are two removable clips on the base end which can be used if you want to use any of the five higher positions to stand the laptop at and they'll hold your laptop safely in place.
I was a bit disappointed in the height of this unit. My laptop is ¾ of an inch from front to back to front sitting on the table. With the addition of this N3 laptop cooling pad the height increases to two inches at the wrist rest and two and three quarters of an inch at the monitor end. That makes using the laptop somewhat uncomfortable. In the instructions it mentions that if you want to use this stand you should consider using an external keyboard and mouse. . . Sorry, but if I wanted to use an external keyboard and mouse I'd have bought a desktop computer. I have a desktop computer I was just hoping for a small lift to the laptop and a bit of extra cooling.
This unit left me disappointed. It's too high, too hard to reach the additional USB port and on/off button. The adjustability is quite impressive you can raise the screen quite high, eye level or even higher, but I just don't want to buy and use an external keyboard and mouse. To me, that defeats the purpose of having a laptop in the first place. Being disabled I bought a laptop because I have such a hard time using a mouse and the touchpad on the laptop was a blessing. Some users may find this useful or handy but I honestly did not enjoy using this at all.
I received this in exchange for my review.

*Update*
I also received the N5 cooler to review (all items listed on the same product page share the same review pool) the N5 does not light up like the larger N3 reviewed above. The N5 has its power switch and USB ports far more conveniently located on the center of the back of the Unit. The N5 does not have the ability to adjust the height or angle of your laptop. It raises the front one and a half to one and a quarter inches in height in the front depending on how you position the laptop. In the back the laptop is raised between two and two and a quarter inches. My fifteen inch Asus laptop overhangs each side by about a half inch but that doesn't seem to affect cooling. Although the N5 lacks the light up fans and height adjustability I think it's a superior cooling unit that could even comfortably fit in your lap. The N5 is a solid four-star item while the N3 remains subpar.
I received this unit in exchange for my review as well.

text: This was much heavier and larger than I expected.  It would be nice if it had a carrying handle on top, but since it runs on house current and not batteries, it's not portable, so the handle would only be useful for moving it.  The weight is probably because of the high quality built-in speakers.  The sound quality is excellent, compared to even good quality computer speakers.  It also sounds better than my stereo speakers.  The manual leaves a little to be desired, but the system is pretty easy to operate and most operations are intuitive.  The biggest disappointment I had is that the AM radio does not work; it is apparently set up for European standards and won't work in the U.S. from what I was able to find out. It is disclosed in the description that AM is not available in the U.S.  It does get FM stations with good fidelity and has an FM aerial.  There is an external input on the back, so you can play through the unit, which you might want to do because of the good sound quality.  They also include a connecting cable for this, which is a nice bonus.  Unfortunately no external output, which could be handy, but not a necessity.  Just insert a CD and it starts playing the CD right away.  Insert a USB stick and it starts playing any audio files on the stick.  At first I thought there was no slot for a USB stick, as it is not identified that way in the manual; it is identified as a phone charging port, a U disk port (maybe they meant USB) and for I-Pod reading.  This is just a one-CD at a time system; would be great if it could take multiple CDs.  The remote is okay and has all the functions you'll need, but is a little confusing at first.  I didn't test the Bluetooth connection capability to a cell phone, as I don't think I would use that function.  If you want a really nice sounding CD player than also handles other audio files on a USB or SD card that also has FM radio and you don't care about the AM radio not working, this is worth getting.  Would give this 5 stars if the AM radio worked.  This is actually a VW automobile disk player that has been converted by putting a wooden case around it and adding quality speakers; very clever idea, especially since this is a pretty decent CD player.  Also they include a demo CD with 18 tracks of popular well known songs, which is another bonus.

title: Honestly, VGA?
text:
This usb type-c dock is very, very nice, but it isn't quite perfect.

First, a clarification for those who aren't versed on USB Type-C ports: There is a wide range of features that a Type-C port will support -- it's all up to the manufacturer. Just because you have a Type-C port, it doesn't mean you will be able to use all of the features that this dock provides. Unfortunately, you will need to dig into the online documentation or forums for your device to find out what you will actually get.

Windows PC -- Almost all Windows PC's will be able to use the SD/MicroSD reader, the Ethernet port, and the additional USB 3.0 and USB 2.0 ports. On my minisforum u700, this dock provides two HDMI ports and I didn't bother testing the VGA port. So on my PC and my laptop, I'm able to take full advantage of this hub.

LG V40 -- I'm on the T-Mobile service running their Android 10 rom. In this ROM, LG provided a little-know desktop mode similar to Samsung Dex that makes the phone work almost as well as a desktop PC. In this mode, the phone takes advantage of the SD/MicroSD card reader to transfer pictures and files, connect to your network through the ethernet port, and provide a large-screen experience through the HDMI port. Connect a mouse and keyboard and you have a great desktop experience. Plex and Netflix works extremely well in this mode.

Nintendo Switch support -- NO

My gripes about this dock: Being an 11-in-1 dock, this really should have a 3.5mm headphone jack, instead, they provided a VGA port. If your computer has a type-c port, would you really NOT have an HDMI monitor/tv to plug it in? Also, the lack of support for Switch means that I'd still need a separate Switch dock when travelling instead of having one dock that supports all of my devices.

title: Very Good Game
text:
Lots of negative reviews so I was compelled to leave my own. One of the biggest knocks on the game is that it isn't as scary as the previous ones. I'm not so sure that is so true. The fright level for Dead space 1 was largely in part of the user not knowing what to expect. Dead space 2 was a little "less scary." Part 3 is even less because by now, most players are comfortable with the environment. Combined that with the fact that the protagonist, Isaac, is now a seasoned veteran in dealing with the necromorphs. I feel that the fright level is right on par with the current storyline. It's still scary, but you know what to expect.

I am no fan of shooters, but after playing Dead Space 2 it quickly became one of the best games I've ever played in terms of being immersed in the story. I moved on to play part 1 and now with part 3 am very pleased. The ability to modify and customize your weapons is a very nice addition. You may find yourself spending a lot of time modifying your weapon depending on the situation you're in.

They also introduced "side missions." Which is nice, but they seem like the main part of the game that was just labeled side missions. I guess they're optional but I cannot imagine anyone not completing them. One nice thing that could be added to the series in future versions is the option to create a non-linear path. For example, the ability to choose which planet or area you need to go to for whatever reason fits the plot. It could be molded to be like an RPG.

I left out a star because the story is a bit strange in the way that it attempts to introduce co-op with single player. I've only played single player but the story seems odd in the way that it tries to create a storyline that fits both co-op and single player. Additionally, it seems very easy. I started out on the hard level and there is an overabundance of health, stasis refills, and ammo laying around.

Overall, a very good game. Don't let the bitterness of the way that the game is sold or delivered determine the rating of the actual game.

title: Seems to help my old dogs get around better--and the young dogs want some too.
text:
I have two fifteen-year-old dogs who both have chronic pain issues and arthritis and general old dog maladies. They're the grizzled beagle and the tall orange dog in the pictures. I've been adding two droppers to their dinner every day, and they've both seemed a bit more chipper and puppy-like (as much as 15yo dogs can be puppy-like). I've given them both aspirin and gabapentin twice a day for over a year, and that is a miracle in itself. But the drops seem to give them a little more mobility and pep. I actually tasted the drops myself, and they have a mild, pleasant flavor. title: Portable, Quality Means for Listening to Music
text:
I like listening to music when I spend time in my backyard. I used to rely on my alexa for this purpose, but more often than not, the volume and clarity were not that good. A portable Bluetooth speaker was the answer and I found just what I needed with this Bluetooth, from Tpone.

What you get with this Bluetooth is a portable, chargeable speaker with that offers up to 18 hours of playback on a single charge. Getting it fully charged will take time, but after that, it’s a matter of pairing it with the Bluetooth on your phone. In about two minutes, it will be ready for use.

The sound quality you get with this Bluetooth speaker is quite good. I like the bass, and for my needs, the volume is sufficient. It’s not powerful enough to blast you away, but for what I need, the volume level works. I use it mostly when I sit on my back patio and/or jump in the pool. I don’t need extreme volume, so this works. There is a plus and minus button on the unit that at first seem like volume controls, but they are not. If you push these, the music will either advance forward or backward to the next song on the list. The volume is controlled by your phone or whatever device you have paired.

There are different colored lights on this speaker that react to the music, adding to the visuals. Again, for my needs, I really don’t care about the lights. But I can see how this could certainly add to the coolness factor for some people. The added colors and the way they react to the intensity of the music is a nice addition. Oh, and I like that I can use this to charge my phone. If a phone is paired, it could drain the phone’s power quickly while you play music. You can easily counter this by plugging your phone directly into the unit, helping to keep your phone charged.

Having the means to listen to music is an ongoing need for me. Whether I am listening to music in my backyard or taking a trip to a nearby beach, I need to be able to play my tunes and the easiest way is to use a portable Bluetooth speaker. This Bluetooth from Tpone delivers on most all counts. The easy pairing, the bass, and the overall sound quality make this an easy winner and an excellent Bluetooth choice.

text:
While I've used some Corsair products for ages, I was a bit skeptical when they branched out into peripherals. Some of my first experiences were a little mixed, as I found the offerings to be wanting vs the best MS and Logitech have to offer (though much better than the worst). Nowadays I find a lot getting near the mark, though falling a bit short. That summary mostly describes this mouse.

It comes in what's become a bit of a standard Corsair box--loud, yellow, yet relatively compact and could be even louder. The contents are easy to sort out, and you can be up and running in a basic sense in mere minutes. A quick download helps you get the full experience.

That experience is good--sometimes very good, but not great. The feel is a bit plasticy and rather light. The styling is busy without much reason for being that way, and the ergonomics never quite are great, no matter the thumb rest. The wheel feels kinda cheap (fyi I'm comparing to a Logitech MX and MX Master as well as some of the nicer efforts from Steel Series), and the LED options are a bit of a miss with the blue LEDs for DPI being locked in bright (and hot) blue. The DPI range is immense, but it's a bit beyond my needs.

It's not a bad mouse, and in use it works well. I feel totally in control with this, and I've yet to have any usability issues. It's the off ergonomics, feel, and customization that leave it close, but still a bit short. Much of these "cons" are subjective, so YMMV, but for me, it's a 4 star mouse

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This comes in a jar with a little scoop in it. The dosage is written on the outside clearly and you measure so much per day into the cats food and mix it.

The aroma of this is pleasant and not repulsive.

Our cat has had no issues when I put this on the food no matter what food it is to help her digest. She eats it readily.

Our cat was having issues because we had to substitute canned for her for a while due to the lockdown. We make our own raw food for her, but as you know, meat was wiped out for a long time. This smells good, is well received by our cat and seems to have cleared up some issues she had with temporary use of packaged food when the raw we make her was unavailable.

title: Yep it works but remember it's on there!
text:
So. It does it's job. Does it very well in fact because we wound up performing an unintentional test on one of these. Which actually pointed out a pretty noteworthy aspect of these kinds of protectors that folks might want to keep in mind when getting this.
Read past the pros of this protector for details....
Pros:
They go on easy (3 applications so far with zero problems).
-Plastic protectors are kind of hit or miss with me but these aren't.

They also come off easy and clean.
-The one I removed had been in place for almost 2 years. Adhesives can solidify over time but this one didn't seem to.

Cons-
Just 1 and, it's not the fault of the protector.

Owners *have* to remember that these things are glass.

So, the way these things work is that they take the impact that otherwise the screen itself would take in addition to protecting agains scratches and scuffs. This is, if you're think about it, a really goos bonus feature for a protector to have.

However.

It's. Glass.

My husband forgot this fact when he dropped his Switch onto hard pavement one day. It landed in juuuuust the right way to make the smallish drop damaging.

And, yes, the protector did its job. Yay.

Unfortunately, the protector did its job. Lol.

If you know where this is going have a cookie and move to the head of the class while I catch everyone else up because, what happened next was that the protector cracked (like it was SUPPOSED TO) and the husband came home, practically in *tears* because he thought his beautiful and beloved console was ruined beyond repair.

I love my husband.

To be fair, he didn't remember that the protector was glass so was understandably assuming that the crack he saw was on the Switch itself. Thankfully, I was able to remove the broken protector that had given it's life in service to the Switch and purchased a new one easily.

Still, the incident proved two things to me:
1) These things *really* work! So you won't regret getting one.
And
2) You kind of have to remember *how* these things work! Or yes, you may suffee a mild heart attack if/when it's ever put to the test. Lol.

So, yes, good purchase and well worth getting. Thanks. :D

title: Excellent GPS Navigator
text:
I bought a Garmin Nuvi 1450LMT for my wife for Christmas, after researching the market and trying to find a unit with the best balance of features against the price. I have two Garmin hand-held GPS receivers that I use for geocaching so I am comfortable with Garmin's GPS products, so I settled on this unit feeling confident that it would meet my wife's needs in a GPS for the car. I was right.

This particular Nuvi has a large, bright display that is easily readable in direct sunlight, which was one area of concern for me. I have seen some electronic devices that are not readable in bright light such as direct sunlight and I was pleased to see that Garmin took care to ensure that the Nuvi would fare well in any lighting.

When we first put the Nuvi into service we were unsure how long it would take before it would acquire satellites and be ready to navigate. Pleasantly, even before leaving the garage the Nuvi found the satellites and was ready to navigate in a short time, usually less than a minute.

The Nuvi has a clear, understandable voice when she (?) speaks which is a big help. The maps are very easy to read and interpret, giving very clear indications of not just what roads to take but what lane to be in while navigating so as to be ready for turns, merges and more. It's very much like having someone give precise directions and pointing to a map right there in the car.

The display shows a lot of important and useful information, including time to next event (turn, exit, etc.), speed limit, travel speed and more. One of the most important is the traffic delay indicator, something that comes in handy when trying to deal with rush hour traffic or traveling around a major interstate exchange such as the DC Capitol Beltway system. It is nice, too, that is shows the speed limit and then marks the travel speed, turning said travel speed red when it is greater than the speed limit.

One of the few complaints I have about the Nuvi is that, when there is a long distance to go until the next turn or exit, the Nuvi is silent and says nothing at all until roughly one mile away from the next turn/exit. When this happens it is almost a shock to suddenly have a voice in the car. Given a choice, I personally would prefer that the Nuvi speak up every 10 minutes or so to avoid that surprise.

One very weak spot I have encountered with windshield-mounted devices is the actual suction cup used. All too frequently, the cup is either very difficult to get stick on to the windshield or it does not hold well enough, letting go very unexpectedly while driving. Garmin did a very good job with their mount, making it super easy to attach to the windshield and making it adhere very well. I have never had any suction-cup-attached device attach and adhere as easily and predictably as the Nuvi.

One reason I chose this specific Nuvi is for the lifetime map and traffic updates. To buy these as an after thought is very expensive though they are very important if you want the GPS receiver to remain useful.

Updating the Nuvi is easy (though, understandably, it is a time-consuming process). Connecting the Nuvi to a Windows 7 64-bit laptop the OS immediately recognized the device and installed drivers. A quick visit to Garmin's website resulted in a browser plug-in being installed and shortly after that I was downloading the updates for the Nuvi. The updates are large, of course, and this is the reason the updates take a while, but the process itself is practically painless.

Some reviewers complain of the Nuvi not charging and navigating at the same time. That has not been our experience. When plugged in ours has worked just fine.

Our experience with the Nuvi 1450LMT has been very good and we're delighted with it. It does an excellent job with navigation, it's easy to read and understand and the map updates are the icing on the cake.

title: Lasted me 4 years. Wish it would still work.
text:
I bought this charger base for my wii remotes in April of 2010, so I cannot say I didn't get quite a bit of use out of it, but the unit has all but reached the end of its usable life.

From the start I'll say that I would recommend it, were it not for the issues I have now. If you're okay with getting 4 years out of it, by all means, buy the thing. It looks amazing, everybody wants to know how it works, it charges the remotes well until the batteries stop taking a charge, and having boxed it up and moved several times while I had it it shows absolutely no wear. It will charge through the traditional remote sleeves (not the black ones, though, unless you cut them) which beats the heck out of having to strip them down to replace traditional batteries. This model charges only 2 at a time, but there used to be a 4 remote version available.

The biggest problem is the lacking availability of replacement battery packs which line up correctly with this charger. I would love to continue using it, but the batteries hold absolutely no charge.

For the 4 years I had and used this product, There were 2 primary issues. The first was that, after a while, the magnet did not hold the battery in a position which lined up correctly to charge it. This can be worked around if one wraps the remote's safety strap around it in such a way that the light turns blue, but it's still annoying. The other issue was that the back button on the remote rests directly on the cradle itself, so if the remote is on when place on the charger (which will probably end up happening more and more the longer you own it as you won't be able to use it for more than a minute or so before it dies) it will start hitting 'B' for you at random.

One great feature on this item is that there is a USB jack on the back which will charge anything that charges on a usb connection - I used to use it for my iPod. I would (and probably will) buy this again, but they need to get on making the replacement batteries available.

text: I ordered these Bose Frames Audio Sunglasses, Rondo, Black - with Bluetooth Connectivity for my wife as she loves her Sunglasses and listening to music while on the go. Before I handed them off to her, I paired them up with my Android device and played around with them a bit (so that I could show her how they worked of course haha) My fist impressions were how amazing they sounded without having actual earbuds. The sound is crisp but definitely not loud and booming as the speakers don't fit into your ears however for what these are, and meant to used for, they perform quite well. Don't expect an "immersive" experience with these, but more of an "awareness" experience, to where you can enjoy your music on the go and still experience the world around you. Call quality was decent and others can hear you clearly unless you are in a noisy or windy environment but this is pretty normal for most Bluetooth headphones. I never experienced any issues with the sound "dropping out" in either speaker and neither has my wife. As for the construction of the sunglasses themselves, I felt that they were well made and on par with a mid price ranged pair of sunglasses. The magnetic charging cable works great and I love to see this in more products as the Micro USB cables and ports seem to be the first thing to break. The cable it'self could be a little longer in my opinion but on the plus side it's less to get tangled and much easier to tuck away into the included soft pouch (which by the way works great to clean the lenses). Once you put them back on you have to push the easy to find button (bottom right front temple) and you will hear a battery status prompt and "connected to" prompt. title: Poor Tool to Help Train Your Dog
text:
I breed and own Goldendoodles and have raised dogs for my entire adult life. I have learned some facts concerning barking that are important to understand - their in instinctual, protective barking used to communicate when your dog senses danger or used to alert you then there is what I’ll refer to a nuisance barking.

It’s the nuisance barking that as a caring pet owner we want to curtail and eliminate as much as possible. This behavior can come about for a whole host of reasons and the key is figuring out what is triggering it in your dog. Most of the time nuisance barking is attention seeking behavior and caused because your dog is bored. The key is not to feed into the behavior. If they bark like crazy and the response is you pay attention - even if it’s yelling at them - they achieved the desired result and the behavior was reinforced.

I have used multiple similar devices - both fixed units, such as this one and anti bark collars.

This particular anti bark collar is not effective. While there are sensitivity settings I found they are either far too sensitive, alerting when the dog moves or scratches, or not sensitive enough, not alerting when the dog barks. Either scenario will prove ineffective in training. Consistency is the key.

This is not a product I recommend.

As a kid I remember playing Pokémon Red on my Game Boy and Pokemon Yellow on my Game Boy Color and have so many fond memories of it.

title: Unintelligible voice commands detract from this game
text:
We bought this game because we already had and liked Jay Jay Earns His Wings. This game has an identical interface. There are several activities that must be accomplished in order to do one final activity. Before starting each new activity for the first time, an "animated" sequence is shown with the original character voices (their mouths move and that's about it). After completing all activities, the reward is getting to play and compose music on the "Sparkleberry tree." There are three skill levels to choose from.

The activities focus strongly on phonics--letter and sound recognition. There is also a spatial component (steering Herky in a maze), and some color recognition. One major problem with the activities is that there is no way to have instructions repeated, and many of the commands are difficult to hear. "Find the letter that makes the sound...." and you are left wondering, Was that a T? a D? an E? My 4 year old son and I BOTH had trouble understanding the instructions, and we have no problems with our sound system. Unfortunately, you can't move ahead on the game without getting the right answer, so we had to choose between making random guesses until we got it right or exiting.

In the end, my son was also disappointed with the "reward" of being able to play music on the Sparkleberry tree at the end of the game. This type of activity is featured (and better executed) on many other children's computer games. He was hoping for something to color or print out like you earn with the Jay Jay Earns His Wings game, which I'd recommend instead of this one.

title: Depends On Your Intended Use- Ours Was To Replace OLD DVD Player
text:
We have an old DVD player in our basement that tries to up convert but it is not always that great. It has some nice features that were great when we got it, but we wanted another one to replace it that did not take up so much room.

WHAT THIS WAS USED TO REPLACE
The DVD machine this replaced was a really old Philips. It played all regions. No fancy settings, except a sleep timer setting that shut it off after so long. The menu was ancient and very clumsy to navigate.

DID THIS PLAY AS WELL AS THE OLDER ONE?
This DVD player played DVDs as well as the older one. So far we have not had any issues with it. It was only hooked up to the HDMI and the used a mini USB to USB cord the plugged into the outlet. We made sure that it was powerful enough to run the player.

PICTURE
The picture was comparable to the old DVD player- perhaps a bit nicer in some cases. I am actually surprised that it has performed as well as it has.

TRAVEL
I have to say that traveling to a cabin we go to occasionally was nice. We are able to bring this DVD player with us to plug into any TV and watch some DVDs if we want to. It is without TV service so DVD is the only way to really have entertainment if we want it.

DOES IT PLAY BLURAY?
This is not designed to play BluRay.

ANY ISSUES?
This is not a top of the line DVD player with super high definition. If you are looking for that, this isn't it. Is it good DVD quality? Yes. I think so. If you have the right set up, it is a great way to take up little room and still be able to play DVDs. I am not sure I would have this as my permanent player in my bedroom or anything. But it is great to use once in a while at home or travel.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although this is not fancy or super high quality, it plays DVDs as well or better than our old player so we are happy with it. The footprint is small and it is portable.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This is a decent player and so far has been good in a pinch to use for playing DVDs. I like the small footprint and portability especially when we have to go somewhere for a while. It is nice to be able to tuck it into our luggage/bags to take with us. The remote is a bonus.

title: Great Rendition of a Classic Game ...
text:
I bought this as a sneaky attempt to get my wife into playing video games. It didn't hurt that we both enjoy competing against each other every night at 7:30 while watching the actual show. Not knowing how well this game was going to work on the Wii, I pulled out all stops and ordered the WiiSpeak as well (which seemed to be the only logical way to create a more authentic Jeopardy! experience). While I think the game is definitely fun and a worthy purchase, there are a few frustrations that shouldn't come as surprising.

First, the positives:
- the game offers a realistic Jeopardy! experience visually ... everything on the show is represented in this game (from the occasional quirky categories to the sage-like mannerisms of the Alex Trebek Mii character.

- you can customize your Mii with items you earn by winning and with the WiiSpeak, you can even record "happy" and "sad" exclamations when you answer a question right or wrong (however the repetitive nature of the exclamation can be irrititating).

- the categories are varied and deep. Like the real Jeopoardy!, you can end up with a whole board of categories you have no clue about ... chalk one up for the educational quality of video games.

- the game allows you to modify the difficulty level, response method and time allowed to respond.

- The mini-games between Jeopardy! rounds are fun and allow you to win items to customize the game.

- The optional WiiSpeak is not a requirement to play this game.

Now, the drawbacks (which are mostly associated with the Wii itself):
- Although the WiiSpeak is optional, it is preferable for realism. The problem I experienced is that it only seems to work if: the settings on the WiiSpeak are perfect, you speak in a clear, concise and loud manner and there is not a single sound being made outside you answering the question. In other words, if you have a dog, kids or the dishwasher going or if everyone is laughing and enjoying themselves ... forget it. The sensitivity adjustments for the WiiSpeak are not always helpful either.

- Being able to type responses requires a keyboard in my opinion and using a Wii controller to spell words was frustrating for me personally (thankfully spelling the first few letters will generate a list of answers to choose from as a shortcut). The game does offer a multiple choice option for answers that eliminates the need to spell the answer, but I didn't like seeing all the answers. I don't fault the game for this as it generously gives the player three answering methods to choose from before the game begins.

- I am not aware of the opportunity to expand the database of answers in the future.

Overall, I think this is a great rendition of the real thing ... fun and challenging. I'm not a fan of spelling with a controller, but the more I play, the more I see improvement in my "console controller dexterity". I think most Jeopardy! fans would enjoy this game.

title: Great color and affordable DSLR video monitor
text:
As a freelance camera operator, I'm no stranger to these. This is clearly designed for us low budget video shooters using small DSLR style cameras, which is why it uses a Sony camcorder battery plate and designed with a hood for outdoor viewing. It has some pretty great features for the price point, including crop mark overlays, peaking indicators, and individual color channels. That being said, it can be used for all sorts of things, such as a Raspberry Pi monitor, backup camera screen, or even a second monitor for your laptop (that's a fun one!). It even has included sound, something a lot of these monitors do not, more on that later.
This is really designed for video use, and for that it does a pretty great job for the price. It comes with a hotshoe mount adapter to put on top of your camera, and uses standard batteries (most LED lights and other accessories also use these batteries, so you probably have some already if you work in video). The colors are vivid and sharp, more accurate than my Atmost Ninja 2 recorder screen, and nice and big for focus checking.
The hood is a nice touch as well, but it requires the snap on frame to attach, and the frame has a weird problem in which it partially obstructs the HDMI port. Maybe I'm just doing it wrong, but I found I needed to leave that corner off the frame if I wanted to use the HDMI plug.
Speaking of the HDMI plug, it comes with one included which I thought was pretty rad of them, but it isn't the more modern micro HDMI type, but the slightly older MINI one. That's the outdated kind that older devices use (such as 3rd generation Intel laptops or cameras like the GH2), but pretty much everything made in the last few years has been using the newer micro one. So it seems weird that they included this one. Personally, it will come in handy because I DO have a laptop that still uses that plug, but I don't intend to use it with this monitor. All my cameras that use that plug are long gone at this point.
Another couple of things to note: The focus peaking is pretty much useless. It oversharpens the image and thinks high contrast parts of bokeh are "in focus", which is weird. Thankfully my Sony cameras have peaking built in so that isn't much of an issue. Also, the screen is large enough and is HD enough resolution (not full 1080 but more than 720) that you don't really need peaking to tell what's in focus. You can see it with your eyes. Also, if using with a camera that is outputting a 16:9 image, you have to change the screen size setting from the default, which is to maximize the screen. Everything looked a little stretched because the display is a little taller than the output of my camera until I turned that off.
As far as sound, I mentioned earlier that this monitor has a speaker. That's good for when you want to review footage on the monitor, and even better if using with a Raspberry Pi or monitor for other things where it might be your only source of sound. It is also really useful if shooting with a Sony A6000 or similar smaller camera that doesn't have a headphone jack... this offers a headphone jack so you can monitor off the HDMI feed. That's pretty useful right there! But don't forget, when you turn the live view back on, you are going to get major feedback from the mic to the speaker unless you quickly turn the volume all the way DOWN first! Or just leave headphones in if that's how you roll.

It is important to note however that it will not accept a 4k signal. The actual resolution is 1280x800, and it will accept up to 1080p as an input, but more than that fails. At the time I'm reviewing this, it seems that there are similar monitors that can accept a 4k input for around the same price. I'm guessing they are updated versions of the same design, as there are no monitors that actually have that resolution for this price, rather they just accept the feed and down-sample to 1280x800, just like this one. So at the end of the day, it probably won't matter if it accepts 4k or not. Some cameras don't like outputting a different resolution than they are recording, so if you are recording in 4k and outputting 1080p, that might be an issue. Otherwise, this is a solid value.

title: Really like it so far
text:
I haven't had this for very long yet, so I can't comment on longevity, but so far I like it. I take it for granted that there will be some sacrifices when using this type of mouse, I just don't expect to get the same flexibility and usability in terms of various buttons and their placements, so I can't really knock it for being a bit worse in that area than some regular, non-ergonomic options. It works very well and the buttons are easy to click and have a nice "click" to them (unlike cheaper ones). Of course, it takes some time to get used to an upright mouse if you haven't used one before, but after a while it becomes easy/natural.

Regarding the wrist angle, I had some wrist pain and in the past I'd used a cheaper upright ergonomic mouse to help. This is not carpal tunnel, I get joint inflammation on the top side of my wrist, so it may be a bit unusual.
When my old ergonomic mouse broke I decided to try a more expensive one in hopes it will last longer. I can't provide any definitive conclusions on whether this particular aspect of my "treatment" really does anything. My ultimate conclusion is that while treating with other things (e.g. braces, compression, cold or hot), using an alternate device sometimes to change the stress points probably doesn't hurt. Sometimes when going back to use my normal mouse, just putting my hand into position seems to cause some strain, so I think this upright position is helping some. But my experience is that if I use anything for too long, I'll find some joint and/or muscle getting stressed. I'm concerned that this upright mouse position may not be as good for my elbow. So my conclusion is mix it up to spread out the strain rather than hammering on a single weak area, and try to be more careful in the future to start treatment sooner, when I see the early warning signs of strain, before it gets bad.

title: IMHO, It's Either a Das or a Matais If You Want a Mechical Keyboard
text: Computer users searching for the next best thing in mechanical keyboards will undoubtedly take a gander at models made by Das and Matais, two top makers. I have keyboards of each brand, both selling for about $125. There's this one, for my Mac Pro (with Cherry MX Blue keyswitches) and the Matais Tactile Pro 4 (with Alps keyswitches) for my PC. I bought the Matais several  months back and liked it so much, that I set out to buy the equivalent model for my Mac, Pro with the Mac-specific keys. However, I didn't like the look of the Matais Tactile Pro in Apple-style white. All the keys were cluttered with two or three icons or letters and the whole thing just looked too messy. I guess the Steve Jobs design ethos has worn off on me. I'll add Matais says its Mac keyboard is very similar to the famed Apple extended keyboard from years back. If you remember and like that keyboard, you'll probably like the Tactile Pro. I'd read good things about the Das, so I decided to try it. My verdict? I give the Matais a slight edge, based on personal preference for the feel of the switches and not the features or quality of the keyboard, which are first rate. These are solidly built keyboards and I think most typists would be happy with either brand. I was as a journalist for more than 30 years and I know a good keyboard when I pound on one. I used to love the fat chunky keyboard that came with my earliest Mac, IBM's early keyboard and the Atex newspaper publishing system keyboards, but I'm getting off track. As noted, the Das uses Cherry MX switches and the Matais uses Alps switches. You'll have to do your own research to learn about the nitty-gritty differences among switches, but here's what I noticed: The Matais is more "clicky." You have to give the keys a good poke to trigger a response. The Das keyboard action is slightly softer and you don't have to tickle the keys with the same commitment because they're not as springy and don't travel quite as far as the Matais, from what I can tell. The difference in keystroking is noticeable but not dramatically so. If you like to bang away on a keyboard and you enjoy the clackety-clack sound it makes, you'll like the Matais Alps switches. Don't get me wrong, the Das Cherry switch also has a nice feel and I guess that's what most mech keyboard buyers go for. And it's a wee bit quieter so you might prefer that if you're in an open office where noise levels might be an issue. The Das has two USB ports on the side and a cable with two USB plugs on the end, so keep that in mind if you're low on USB ports. It also might make a difference to some people: The letters on the Das are all lower case. I like the crisp unknown-to-me font the maker uses on the keys. All in all, I'm tempted to send this one back and try the Tactile Pro 4, despite its ugly looks.

Blue Buffalo is good food in my opinion. Two of my three adult cats loved this. Unfortunately, my oldest cat would not even try it. Instead, he just walked away.

In summary, two of my cats' love this food and dug in immediately. My skinniest cat that is about four pounds now, would not touch this. Despite his response, this food was a hit but it is expensive. It is good for kittens or adult cats who need the extra calories to put on weight.

title: If you are in the Samsung camp this is great
text:
There are more than enough helpful reviews, product specs and Q&A, so I am going to focus on this tablet for folks who are upgrading from another Android tablet, and especially another Samsung. I'll say up front that the biggest reason [for me, anyway] is the extra screen real estate and resolution.

I had a small surprise in that mine did not come with Amazon apps pre-installed like they did on my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch, White) 2013 Model]] that it replaced. Locating the App Store application so I could install all of the applications that I have purchased was a bit of a hassle, but I finally got that resolved. Like my older Samsung tablet this one is a little less than spectacular when it comes to streaming music to a speaker via bluetooth. I do not know why Samsung cannot get it right on tablets because I have never experienced any issues streaming on my Note II and Note 3 phones.

Another issue of which you need to be aware is this tablet is thin and flexible. I knew that in advance and purchased a [[ASIN:B00KCDBD2E Samsung Galaxy Note Pro 12.2-inch Case Cover]], which in my opinion is one of the better cases for this tablet. The hard shell part of the case into which you insert the tablet provides a rigid casing that allows zero flex. No matter which case you ultimately select I strongly recommend that you get one.

You may have issues with some apps if you opt to install an SD card to expand your storage, or if you are moving an SD card from another tablet to this one. The KitKat version of the operating system will not write to SD cards under certain conditions. There is a free fix called SD KitKat Fixer by JRummy Apps that you can get from the Play Store. I highly recommend it. As a side note, I had no issues with this SD card: [[ASIN:B00N2ROG9O PNY Turbo Performance 64GB High Speed MicroSDXC Class 10 UHS-1]]. It is an inexpensive way to max out your memory. I have heard that this tablet will work with 128GB cards, but I have not tested any so cannot say for sure.

If you are accustomed to Samsung's user interface you will feel right at home. For me, after the little challenges I mentioned above I was fully up and operational on this tablet in a few hours. A lot of that time was reinstalling purchased apps from Amazon and the Play Store, tweaking my settings so that they mirrored those on my Tab 10.1 (which are identical to my Note 3 phone), and this feels as comfortable as an old shoe. A much larger old shoe to be sure, and it's incredible how much extra screen space you get going from 10.1 to 12.2.

title: Great lens and sensor, bad shutter lag, audio and switches
text:
The wide angle lens is wonderful. The field of view and the speed (light gathering ability) of the lens can only be rivaled by high end camera and lens combinations costing six to ten times as much (admittedly those are superior in many other ways as well). Still, the point is that no other compact point and shoot camera can rival the field of view and speed of this one. Nevertheless, some things come up short of fair on the LX3.

The shutter lag is terrible. I am a very instinctive shooter that is quite capable in photojournalist style candids but I am almost always defeated by this camera.

I am not a photophile or electronic gadget spec sheet bench racer. I've done wonderful 8x10 prints with a 6MP camera and 10MP is enough to get prints after substantial cropping. I have huge film scans when I need them but I cannot realistically show dozens of megapixels on screen or in print for more than a handful of images. I also shoot in .jpg and it's great. I can't imagine the agony of terabytes of raw data jamming my PC.

I love the LX3 video quality for movies. It's ideal for Youtube and even Youtube HD. I do not like the Quicktime .MOV format or the weak compression algorithm. I wish it had H.264 and wrote an .MPG type format. It still beats the data format from a DVD camcorder though.

The audio quality for movies is terrible. Again, I'm not talking audiophile critique here. For comparison, my Sony DSC T9 (ultra compact point and shoot) has far better sound.

I hate the manual aspect ratio slider. If I shoot movies I want 16:9 but for stills I want 3:2 (of course). The LX3 requires that I remember to both turn the dial and slide the switch or I will end up shooting 16:9 stills.

Overall, it's a great camera. I hope they get the rest sorted out by the time I expect to buy another one in about 3 or 4 years.

title: Well designed and pro-level construction and features for transforming an iPhone 6 into a camera
text:
I received this as a free review sample. When I accepted this for testing and review I was a little skeptical. However, this has turned out to be a high-quality kit that will transform an iPhone 6 or 6s into a decent hand held camera, yet it will not interfere with other iPhone functions. With the case and attachments in place you can still make and receive calls, text, browse the web, etc.

This is actually the foundation for a more sophisticated set of lenses that will accept add-on lenses like the [[ASIN:B018TQUEYI 010 | bitplay Portable Add-on 3X Telephoto Glass Lens Compatible]]. As you can see from the product description this kit already comes with a basic wide angle/telephoto lens combination. It is not plastic junk, but a serious lens with a precision metal body that screws into this case. It has two parts - one lens screws into the other for combined or separate effects - and it is as good in quality and construction as the lenses that I used with a vintage Nikon SLR.

The case itself can be quickly removed to reconfigure your phone back into a ... phone. But while it is in camera configuration mode it feels just like a hand-held with a choice of grips, an integrated tripod adapter and even a leather strap. The case does not interfere with any phone function, and especially the iPhone's camera and flash. More importantly - for me - the case offers excellent protection. The lip that is slightly raised about the iPhone's screen is curved inward and adds protection for that critical area. The body of the case and two of the grips are textured so you can maintain a firm hold on the phone while shooting, even if your hands are wet.

Bottom line: this is not a gimmick or novelty - it is designed for folks who take photography seriously. I could not find a single flaw in the design from a photographer's perspective; nor could I find any faults from a build or design perspective. This is obviously not for casual users, but if photography is your passion and you own an iPhone 6 or 6s, this case merits serious consideration.

title: Wow!  No more, "What'd they say?"
text:
Thank you to all you wonderful Amazon reviewers. I'd never purchased a Bose product before, with the exception of possibly headphones at some point in time. We know the Bose sound is legendary, but I never really needed a Bose radio or CD player. The Solo caught my eye because I love my flat screen TV, but the speakers are only so-so at best. Like many other reviewers, I have trouble understanding some dialogue on TV. It's fine as long as there is someone around to annoy endlessly by asking "what did they say," but watching TV alone, I miss big chunks of the story & plot. The doctor says it's just "one of the vestiges of old age." Oh. Another one of those. Thanks, doc.

So, I wondered if the Solo speaker might help, and thanks to all my hard-of-hearing contemporaries here (or should I say THANK YOU), I saw all the reviews promising that I wouldn't have to ask "what?" every 2 minutes any more. I could jump for joy after hooking up the speaker and giving it a listen, although my doctor would probably advise against it. On my TV, unlike some others mentioned here, the TV speakers work along with the Solo speaker, so it's easy to mute the Solo and hear the difference between it and the TV speakers. It's amazing. The sound is rich, and big, and crisp in a way that my surround-sound system isn't. Most importantly, in answer to my wildest hopes, I can understand every single word of dialogue, even Christian Bale mumbling behind his Batman mask. No kidding. The Bose speaker took 20 years off my age, and reduced my waist by four inches. Ok, I am kidding about that.

As if all that isn't reason enough to get one of these gems, it has to be the simplest piece of electronics to hook up, set up & operate. It's simply two cords, one to the power outlet, and the other to the TV. They include all the cables in the box: digital optical, HDMI & RCA. Plug, plug, power. That's all. The remote is four buttons: power, mute, up & down volume. It's hard to believe that such intricate, complex sound can come from such a simple device. Thank you, Mr. Bose, wherever you are. Not only would I highly recommend this to my friends, I think everyone with a flat-screen TV owes it to themselves to get one. Seriously. This is the audio-visual experience I thought I was already having with 5.1 surround system.

title: I *LOVE* this camera!
text:
I'm just an amateur when it comes to photography. All I really want is an easy-to-use point-and-shoot camera that I can take on vacations to snap shots of places I find interesting, to use around the house to take photos of valuables for insurance purposes, etc. In other words, my expectations are pretty minimal.
That said, I'm extremely happy with the Kodak DC3400. This is my second Kodak digital (my first was a DC240), so obviously I'm pleased with the Kodak product line.
After unpacking the DC3400, I spent about 10 minutes getting it set up, and proceeded to take a few pictures. Another 10 minutes or so, and I had the photo software loaded on my laptop. Connect the USB cable, and I was able to load the photos onto the laptop immediately. The camera shows up as an icon, like a disk drive, which you can double-click to open and transfer the pictures to a folder on your hard drive -- piece of cake!
The quality of the pictures is amazing. I use the Ofoto service, and had some prints of some of my digital photos sent to my mother. According to her, you could not tell the difference between the digital images and those taken with a 35mm film camera. The colors were vivid, the images sharp -- just what you'd expect from the Kodak name.
I'll agree with most everyone else and say that batteries might be the only downside to this camera. It's definitely worth the investment to get the Kodak NiMh rechargables and the charger. The ONLY time I use NiCads is when I'm my NiMh set is in the recharger, and I need to snap a few pictures.
For the money, I don't think you can top this camera in terms of features, quality, and ease of use.

title: Charged my Lenovo right up!
text:
I have a discarded 7th generation Intel Lenovo I was given from an office to scrub and give to someone who's working from home during the coronavirus shutdown here in NY. Problem is, they gave it to me without the charger and I can't go back to the office and get it until they reopen the doors. Thankfully, it uses a standard USB-C shaped plug to charge. I have plenty of phones and tablets that use that, but apparently laptops need the more robust Power Delivery standard, and not the lower power of USB phone chargers.
Amazon to the rescue, with this excellent replacement PD adapter. I love that modern computers and devices are starting to embrace a standard like this going forward- Macbooks and PC laptops both use this now, and it's even backwards compatible with USB devices like phones and tablets (the reverse isn't true- I couldn't use my phone charger on this laptop, but this laptop's PD charger can charge my phone).
This device worked great for getting that Lenovo back up and running, very appreciative for a future full of standards!

Original review:
I ordered two of the 40 inch size, even though I could have gotten a smaller one for the smaller dog, he would no doubt have taken over her bed and the big girl would be stuck with a bed too small.
Hers is just right for a 45 pound dog. She can stretch out or curl up, either way. The bumper is really nice as a place for their heads. My smaller old boy is 25 pounds, and it looks like he'd have been fine one size down, but the fact that he has unused space doesn't seem to bother him at all.
Since I've unpacked these yesterday afternoon, they've hardly left them! Usually when we get up in the morning, we find one dog snuck onto the sofa and the other sleeping on the recliner. They are not allowed on the furniture, but we overlook this every morning. This morning, they were still in their new beds! That says a lot.
The sherpa is super-soft, yet still looks like it's sturdy enough to hold up well in the wash. Their old beds were from a different company and I was happy with them for several years, but they were a hassle to wash because of the zip washable cover on the bumper part was hard to get the giant ring of pillow back in. This says the entire one piece is machine washable, and I have a big front loader so hopefully this will be an easier wash. It looks sturdy enough, as I wash them every few weeks on bath day.
Twice a year we take a long road trip and the dogs mostly sleep whenever we're in the vehicle, so it's important that these are pliable enough to fit side by side between the back seat and back door of a very loaded van, and I can tell these will be just fine as they are very pliable. They also need to be lightweight, as when we stop at night we will carry their beds into the hotel rooms, and these are much lighter than their last ones, so these will be great for traveling. If I have any future issues, I will update.
Update:
I've washed these beds several times, and the dog hair DOES NOT come out! I've literally just spent an hour holding the nozzle on the Dyson to every inch to make these somewhat descent to bring in the house. These will never be clean enough, and will end up staying on the outside porch. I will order new ones with washable covers, hassle or not taking them apart- it's worth it. It was roughly a hundred bucks for the two beds, and didn't even get 6 months use. The dogs still love them because they are comfy, but they hold every hair in range. Pictures at the end tell the story. First are when they were new, then after I've spent my afternoon trying to get the hair out- which looks like it caused the pilling, then last pictures are of the one I still have to do. When my review sample arrived I had no problem connecting it to an old ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. It also connected without fuss to an Android TV box and functioned immediately. On the ThinkPad the settings out of the box took some getting accustomed to because the mouse was super sensitive to my every move.

After downloading the driver and manual - neither of which are included in the box - I was able to fine tune this mouse to my personal movements. In fact, I am not sure I can go back to a plain vanilla mouse again!

I am not going to repeat the very detailed specifications on this page, including actual dimensions, nor am I going to regurgitate the roduct description. I have included user supplied images of the manual and screen shot of the driver menu that will show the incredible array of settings and features. Here are a few of the reasons why I personally love this mouse and awarded it five stars.

First, every possible setting and button a gamer or power user could wish for are included. You can assign just about any function to any button, and set sensitivity levels at the inch-pebble level. Even the lights and display are configurable.

Second, this is a quality product from the braided, five foot cable that will probably outlast my sixty-five year old body, to the buttons, which feel solid and provide excellent tactile feedback.

Finally, while I had to downgrade mine to conform to my less than steady hands, I did use the maximum sensitivity on a few Visio drawings I quickly created. If only I had this mouse when I was a consultant who cranked out system and network diagrams like a demon possessed. As it is, the shape feels natural and ergonomic under my hand. And for good reason: the design provides for two controlling points (index and/or middle finger and thumb), and a pressure point where your palm rests and a support point at the heel of your hand.

I could babble on and on, but the images I uploaded show most of the settings and an overview of the mouse. As for the lack of documentation and drivers in the box. that is a smart move because you can download the freshest ones as soon as you log onto their site (URL is printed on the front of the box).

title: I Wish It Was Just A Half Inch Bigger But Still Handy
text:
I got this for my daughter who is involved in a business situation where a camera, laptop, and tripod (plus accessories) are required for product photos, posting, and keeping track of inventory. She is always misplacing things. I wanted this to be in one place for her. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is true to the photos with the listing. The case is padded, has a velcro flap on it which has a zipper in the front flap for flat things like our flat flash which we keep in a padded box, or cords, etc. The case itself has plenty of padding in it and non-abrasive soft fabrics.

CAMERA CASE
The camera storage has two adjustable velcro type walls in it so that you can make it bigger or smaller. The other two compartments are for storing lenses etc, and one of them has a flap, but the flap is not something you can fasten down. The camera that goes in here is a Fuji Finepix S1. The front lens sticks out quite a bit but it is stored on its back and is plenty protected by all of the padding.

ZIPPER ACCESS
There is a top zipper access so that if you have the flap down but need a quick access, you can quickly zip open the top and remove the camera.

LAPTOP POCKET
We have a laptop that I was sure would fit in there, but it is just about a 1/4 inch too long for the pocket. I thought it was a 14 inch, but it turned out to be 15 inch instead. A 14 inch laptop or tablet will fit in here perfectly. A 15 will not.

STRAPS
The straps on the bottom are adjustable to hold a tripod which is great to help keep all of this in order. When I want to make it easier to store, I remove the tripod and stand it next to this bag until it is time to use again.

SIDE MESH POCKET
This has a side pocket appropriate for a water bottle or can of coconut water, etc.

HANDLES
There is a single carry handle and a shoulder strap. The carry handle makes this a bit awkward, so we tend to use the shoulder strap except when we need to move the bag quickly.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Even though I wish this were slightly bigger to fit the laptop, it is my error, not the bag company, so I have to say other than that, this bag is well designed and does the job. It is a great way to keep all of the camera gear handy for the jewelry business it is needed for.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. It is not fair to remove a star for the misunderstood measurement, but this is not as handy for my needs as I had hoped. I am leaving this at five stars, because it is still handy to keep everything together for taking photos for the business it is intended for.

Since I do not have any laptops with USB 3.0 I could not test that speed, but a directory containing 19.4GB transferred via my USB 2.0 port in a little over twenty minutes. Blazing fast? Not by USB 3.0 standards, but darn quick form the ancient laptop (which may have actually slowed the process down.)

The real reason why I rated this so highly is the cost. I recall purchasing a 64GB SD card a year ago that was vastly more expensive (at the time) than this half terabyte drive. Of course the SD card was miniscule, but this drive will fit in a shirt pocket. For me this is a convenient way to not only back up my two laptops, but also my phone and two tablets. Those are backed up via a hard connection to my laptop because they require FAT32 while this drive out of the box is NTFS. I would have reformatted it, but it worked so well with my laptop that I left it as is.

If you are planning to use this with an Apple IOS or Android device only, you will need to reformat it via those operating systems.

This comes with a cable that is USB A on the end that connects to your laptop or OTG connector, and USB 3.0 for the end that attaches to the drive itself. The 3.0 end is a little tight in tolerance, but once it's perfectly aligned it slips in and holds firmly.

Bottom line: this is inexpensive mass storage that is great for backing up files and documents, storing large media such as movies and music, or transporting files to and from work.

title: Fantastic surge protector. When it's on.
text:
Got this one to use in my office. I used to have the standard 6-outlet bar for my computer and gaming setup, and an additional 3-outlet plug with USB outlets on the wall. I found that I was constantly plugging and un-plugging devices on the 6-outlet one, so I decided to get one that has a couple more.

I like this one in particular because it has the right amount I need for now. The last two toward the bottom are spaced a little wider than the rest, which is perfect for my bulkier plugs, namely my shredder and my MacBook Pro charger.
Haven't had the chance to use the phone plugs as we don't have a landline (Who does these days?). We purchased a multi-printer with the fax option, so maybe that'll get some use in the future.

Overall, great. This is my third or fourth Belkin surge protector, and I'm pretty satisfied with them all. They feel heavy-duty and sturdy, so I don't see them wearing out any time soon, no matter where we place them.

About a few weeks in after using this, I noticed that the switch would be turned off every so often. It was strange, because it hadn't happened to any of my other surge protectors. I asked my wife if she had accidentally turned it off while walking around the area, but she said no. It was really frustrating, because my chargers and alarm clock would turn cease to operate because of this, and I'd have to turn the switch back on every time and recharge my devices and reset my clock.

One morning, when I put my one-year-old daughter down so I could get my breakfast, I noticed she immediately shot for the surge protector and switched it off.
Must be the shiny red light.

title: Looks better than it sounds. 2.5-3
text:
My first thought when I initially saw the Motorola Sphere 2-in-1Bluetooth Speaker with Over-Ear Headphones was, wow. It is extremely attractive and would definitely appeal to the young folks. Ironically, our house is full of loud, music playing teenagers who have very clear ideas about what sounds good and which products they prefer to use. They like speakers and headphones that offer clear sound quality with bass. We have a Bose Soundlink speaker, and VModa or Sennheiser earphones. So unfortunately when I reviewed these, I was comparing them with others that I have used. While this product might look good (definitely a 5), it needs to sound good. And this is where I am disappointed – in the sound quality.
In a nutshell:

Attractiveness – The Motorola Sphere is attractive. It is black and looks like a head with headphones.The system looks nice on a bookshelf, desk or dresser in a dorm room, bedroom, etc.. I do love the look.

Set up – The directions for setting up the device are easy to follow. Once you pair the headphones and the sphere (separately) to your phone (via Bluetooth), it is pretty easy to use. There is sometimes a lag when you disconnect or switch between the sphere and the headphones. You might have to press the button on the headphones to make the sound switch between the two devices.

Headphones – They are adjustable and the sound quality is good via the headphones.

Sound Quality – The sound quality is not good thru the speaker. I’d give it 2.5 at the most. To me the frequency response seemed a little high, which is why the sound thru the speaker is hollow or missing something, no matter the genre (i.e., classic, jazz, rap, rock) played. But a plus is that the quality of the sound thru the headphones is better, it is more balanced and therefore rates 3.5-4 (although the bass is still not heavy).

In conclusion, while I love the look and concept (2 in 1 – speaker and headphones) of the Motorola, I wouldn’t recommend it. I would instead suggest investing a little more money and getting a better more quality speaker.

title: Sturdy climber, real carpet, cat approved
text:
--I just got this today! It came fully assembled in a big, sturdy box. The cat perch was easy to slide out. ((Before you destroy the box, it could easily be repurposed as an additional feline enrichment play item.)) I placed it near a corner that I have a few of their kitty climbers set up (basically to make my own mega cat tree without it being one unit that cant be moved around much). Placing it among the familiar items is just to introduce them to the brand new item, and to pique curiosity. That is my advice to you, especially if no one is taking an interest in it at first. Eventually I will find a new location for it. Next, and also a bit of advice, was to sprinkle on a generous dose of cat nip. One by one each of our four adult cats came over to check out the new item (ages ranging from 6-17). They jumped on it, sniffed it, got a good whiff of cat nip, scratched at the carpet, chewed on the feather, rubbed up on it, etc. Our two young labs were also intrigued. I will be adding pictures of everyone to show scale, and to show the material it is made of.
--I didn't notice it in the description, but I see it now, is that attached is a very nice feather toy that dangles under top perch. Feathers are a favorite in this household, so this was a pleasant surprise. Nice touch!! (now hopefully my labs leave it alone!)
--After looking at reviews, I chose this based on how sturdy it appeared, and that it uses wood composite (oriented strand board?) instead of, and real carpeting over short napped/smooth material that some climbers have (that my cats don't love). It was as nice as expected, as sturdy as I hoped for (this thing is not going to just tip over during a cat running up or down it) and the cats LOVE the feel of the REAL carpeting. The sisal wrapped scratching areas are higher up on the climber which shows that the designer has cats or at least understands cats. Additionally, the two perches are positioned in such a manner that it can easily be climbed up (or used as a climber to get to other high spaces). This is good use of space. The spacing between the two perches is adequate for cats to sit, sleep or play. The space between base and lowest perch has the least amount of space, but it is an area that is often dismissed anyway (though appears still enough room for a cat to crawl through). I had seen the similar sized but slightly different design of the other Large perch/condo offered by this company, and it was the spacing between each level that bought me to buying this one. The other had an additional perch, but given that they are same height, the spacing between each is less, and I am thinking most cats would prefer a little more space and less cramped feel. I am glad I went with this one.
--The other aspect that I like is that each perch has three low sides to it. It offers enough material to feel cozy, yet not so much that it hinders climbing or play behavior. The top perch is wide with short depth, and the bottom perch is more narrow but much longer/deeper. Both offer a lot of space without infringing on the other. While I don't see the base as hanging out/sleeping space, it is conducive to floor play, or toy storage. I can picture my cats batting toys around the base, or using the frame to pull themselves around.
--I will be curious how long the sisal twine stays attached, as well as the carpet. It appears to be attached well, but time will tell.
--Pleasant neutral color- beige.
--This would also be nice and sturdy for small dogs. The dimensions of the unit and the perches are listed in the description, and this one would be quite adequate for a small to small/med dog to sit on.

title: Steps lively for multi-tasking, responsive touchscreen, DVD RW drive, awesome battery ** APRIL 2016 UPDATE ***
text:
I've been using a 2009 17.9" Gateway Windows 7 laptop happily all these years until just recently when it began to cough and sputter and generally show signs of wanting to die. I nursed it for several months while shopping for a replacement and suddenly this Toshiba L55T-C/5388 appeared from Vine. Serendipity. I am writing my review from the Toshiba actually rather than my tablet which what I've had to resort to for the past few months - that's a nice change actually. My initial impressions after a week of daily use are pretty good overall with some niggling design complaints for the physical hardware.First - for the record ... I'm not a gamer - just a regular person using my laptop to write articles for the local newspaper now and then, do a lot of email, a lot of online shopping, some social media stuff, watch some videos now and then, sort and store serious quantities of photos and average net surfing. If I want to listen to music, I tend to use Alexa (the Echo) for that rather than my computer and we watch movies on the big television around here - though sometimes I'll use my laptop instead of my tablet for tv shows etc when I'm traveling.

This Toshiba has a very nice high definition screen and I haven't noticed any fuzziness or blurred screen edges etc. The HD video I downloaded from Amazon as a test sample looked as crisp and bright on the laptop as it did on our Samsung 1080p television. The sound clarity is very good for dialogue and background music - the full speaker running across the length of the front of the machine is really good and the volume is quite loud.
Additionally, the touchscreen is responsive, but not so sensitive that just brushing it will mess your page up or close an open tab. I did run into a couple of sessions where the screen would go to black as I was scrolling rapidly by touch - this seems to be a Windows 10 issue when using the new Edge browser and not a laptop physical issue. I haven't had a repeat of this in the Chrome Browser in a week. (It could also have been a fluke)

The battery life on this computer is freaking amazing! I've been using it for almost 3 hours now for a variety of things and it's currently sitting at 74% with an estimated 6 hours and 35 minutes run time left. By three hours of use, my Gateway would have already been at 10% and that's before it started having problems. Thus far, I have used this laptop for a five hour straight run - writing, with email refreshing in the background and music playing as a test at the same time and the battery barely hit 52% when I was finished working.

Uploading and transferring files from both the cloud and my old computer hasn't been as big a hassle as I expected. The USB 2.0 thumb drive I had handy worked just fine and everything came over intact. The cloud transfer was a bit stickier just because Windows 10 now wants to make unzipping files more complicated than before. (Thanks Microsoft) Additionally, the DVD RW drive works fine and I have had no problems at all uploading the software for my 3D printer and downloading files from the net for it. For those that are interested, unlike other reviewers, I had zero problems uploading and am now using Google Chrome as my browser etc. I've included a photo of my basic screen - the Chrome icon is right there. You just have download Chrome and then unzip it manually.

My one star deduction is for physical comfort. This is a light computer compared to my previous one and I appreciate that. However, the edges are not rounded off. They are sharp, square and pointy. This means that as you are typing - doesn't matter if it's on your lap or a desk - after awhile, these pointy bits will dig into your wrists or arms and this HURTS. My five hour marathon the other day left a little indention on my right wrist. That is just ridiculous. The second design flaw is the touch pad. It is very large and sits perfectly flush with the base of the laptop. This is pretty, but you tend to brush over it as you are actually typing and that can make the cursor jump - now you're typing in an entirely new location. These two issues are obnoxious enough that I am now looking for a way to create a little rubber bumper for the front edge of the computer and a wireless mouse.

In general, this is a nice replacement for my old workhorse Gateway - I've grown used to the smaller screen because Toshiba has made it very easy to enlarge the font and any image on this screen. The 8 gig of ram makes multi tasking and switching from things prompt and thus far, I haven't experienced any lagginess. There is some bloatware pre-installed (like with any computer), but it is easy to get rid of. WIndows 10 requires a learning curve of course, but that's not the laptop's fault. Four solid stars after almost ten days and if that changes, I'll update.

*********SIX MONTH UPDATE April 29, 2016 ********

After a little over six full months of regular, almost daily use, I have had no problems at all with this laptop. It just does its job with no drama. It streams movies, music and uploads photos and files to the cloud. It handles my word processing needs and email and all the regular stuff anyone does on a computer. It also handles my software for my 3-D printer with grace. I am still very pleased with the battery life and it has had no trouble connecting via blue tooth to my external speakers when needed. I still don't like the slightly sharp edges on the corners, but it's not the end of the world. All in all, this is a nice machine and I'm still using it and pleased with it in general.
