title: Another ineffective Hartz product
text:
Wondering how Hartz even stays in the pet product business.
I am guessing it is from a lot of one-time customers!

We already knew to not use flea products from them, and not to buy their
catnip (it comes from China, and the last box infected an entire tub of
catnip I'd had of another brand with some sort of strange little bugs. I had
to discard a huge amount of catnip!). Now I am passing on this product too,
and will never buy Hartz items again.

We just used this for our two cats. While they had no visible ear mites,
both were starting to scratch at their ears quite a bit, which is often the
first sign of mites starting up. We always treat both cats at the same time
so we can mark it on the calendar.

Well, this product irritated their ears so much! I did the right amount of drops in
each ear (and this item is extremely oily). I rubbed it in, then carefully wiped off the outer
ear with a cotton ball to get any excess. I did this a couple times that evening, because
they'd flip their heads and get more oil on the outer edge. I didn't want them ingesting this
if at all possible, so was pretty diligent about wiping the outer ear.

By the next day, our older cat's ears were fiery hot to the touch! It was like he had a fever.
He was still messing with his ears, but this time, it seemed more from discomfort than itchiness.
He was also trying to rub his ears on the carpet, never a good sign. By the following day, his
ear was so red, I was afraid it was going to need a vet trip. I took a warm washcloth and gently
washed his ears off to get any remaining medicine off his ears as much as possible. I took a Q-tip to
remove what I could a little bit further in, but you can't go very far in on a cat's ear.

Our youngest one hid from me for the rest of the evening, and I can only assume that she too was
not feeling well from the medicine. Around midnight, I went into the bathroom and found that she
had thrown up all of her dinner (from around 5 pm) into a big pile on the bathroom floor. She felt
miserable! I cleaned her ears as much as possible too - she probably ingested a little bit though
since she hid for several hours.

This stuff must burn like fire to the cats!
I know a fungicide is going to be a little uncomfortable - medicine does have to work.
But it doesn't have to be so painful, and cause the cats so much misery.

Hartz needs to get out of the pet business, or stick to just making dishes or balls.
Most of their stuff comes from China, and I think it must have a lot of loose guidelines there for
purity of product.
I am DONE with all Hartz items. You've caused my cats problems for the last time!

title: wonderful portable tablet
text:
Okay, I have officially bought into Amazon's kindle crack. This is not my first kindle (or second, or...). This tablet is definitely an improvement over the previous versions, it's more responsive, it handles video and web browsing so much better than the previous Fire generation, and I love the slimmed down version.

The overall design is an improvement. The video quality is great, and music does play with a decent quality. Love the feature where it can display lyrics while playing song (if the mp3 has the information), thanks to the whole X-Ray/Lyrics feature. There's a lot of new touches here that are fun. I really appreciate the volume and the power buttons being on the opposite sides of the kindle now (don't know how many times I've hit the wrong one on my Fire >.<).

Also, being able to have more than two browsers open on Silk now w/out it crashing all of the time is a great improvement.

Some minor quirks - not sure if it's me or the tablet, but still trying to figure out how to get pictures already taken from my phone onto the tablet and directly into the photo folder.

Have installed several apps without a problem, downloaded files and opened them, so far so good. The kindle goes everywhere with me (literally, it's the perfect size to fit in my purse). I wish there were more cover options for the 7", but it seems to be increasing the longer the kindle is out, and I think a cover/case is a must for one of these. This is the kindle that I do take everywhere, and on a recent trip, I used this more than my Surface as it has my most frequently used personal emails installed on it (easy to set up), I can access my social accounts, my music, and of course my books.

The battery is... eh, decent. I can keep it on and play music for a few hours, video less, and use it to read books for most of a day. It could use some improvement.

All in all, it's a great tablet that you can take with you.

title: Horrible Key Conflicts. Not for Games or Fast Typers. Feels Great.
text:
I've had this keyboard for a while, and am currently using it a work. Although it looks good and feels great to type on, there are some serious issues with it.

First, this is the closest non-mech keyboard that feels like a mechanical keyboard that I've found. The keys are not interchangeable with other mechanical keys, but are high quality so you don't have to worry about them fading/rubbing off, and feel good under the fingers. Keep in mind they have been polished by my fingers, so the more used buttons are shiny.

Typing: Fils filse files filse fils fiesl feisl. The number of conflicting keys on this thing are horrendous. If you are a fast typer, or ever press more than one key at once, this keyboard will annoy you. There is no conflict prevention with the number keys above the letters, and the pooling zones selected for the keys are not practical. Not only is there ghosting when pressing more than one key most of the time, but the other keys aren't even registered some times (I use one finger to type passwords on this keyboard). Because of this I had a hard time typing on the keyboard when I first got it; so much that I was wondering what the heck was wrong with me, not being able to type well all of the sudden (naive me didn't put two-and-two together).

LEDs: The LEDs start very bright, but the Number Lock key is hardly visible in daylight anymore because it has faded so much due to being on constantly. Therefore the quality of the LEDs used in the board are low.

All in all, if you are not a fast typer, or if you don't plan to play video games, but still want a sturdy keyboard that feels good, this might be the fit for you.

title: Console port done right.
text:
Gears of War is a 3rd person shooter developed by Epic Games and published by Microsoft Game Studios. It was first released as an Xbox 360 exclusive, and it went on to become one of the most successful games for the console. It was later released for the PC with some added content and better visuals to support the high end graphics cards.

You play as Marcus Fenix, a former COG soldier who was imprisoned for abandoning his post, and reinstated into command and asked to join the Coalition to fight Locust. The game is quite different from most 3rd person shooters in that, it relies heavily on cover mechanics. You take cover behind various objects during firefights, and stand up to shoot and duck back out of sight.

Even in the casual setting, there is some frustration to be had. Difficulty climbs quite steeply in these sections; I felt there should have been at least one checkpoint during these parts, instead there were none.

The sound track is good, but it could have used more variations. Every time there an action sequence, the same music kicks in throughout the game. Granted that the game itself is not very long, yet, listening to the same tune over and over again tends to get monotonous, and however good it might be. The effects are top notch, weapons pack a punch, especially the top gun and the six-shooter.

Weapons are fun to use. I especially loved the torque bow it reminded me of Rambo. In fact, the whole game feels like a big Hollywood movie. It's very slick and fast paced. The melee combat has some great moments. The chainsaw to the machinegun was a great idea; when you get a chainsaw kill on an enemy, the game takes over and it shows you slicing an enemy into half. As cool as this might be, it could have been implemented better, because sometimes it doesn't work like it should.

The best in the game for me are the visuals. Gears of War uses Unreal 3 engine, and it looks fantastic. I played the game in DirectX 10 mode at 1920x1200 with all settings on maximum on my EVGA GeForce 260GTX, and it looked out of this world. There is something about the art and environment though, while they are beautiful and unique, most of the game the environment is various shades of dirt. This can seem monotonous after a while. This could have used some lush green jungles as seen in Crysis. It would have looked beautiful in Unreal 3 engine.

Technically speaking, there is a nasty savegame bug that causes the savegames to disappear after exit. This happened a few times even after patching it. If you are playing offline, there is a fix, and also a way to backup the save games.

Over all it's a fantastic experience. Gears of War is an excellent port. It has all the qualities of a good port should have and some bad ones too. Controls are very well optimized for the PC. I have no hesitation in recommending this game.

+ Graphics
+ Sound effects
+ Level design
+ Fast paced gameplay
+ Cover system
+ Weapons, especially torque bow

- Savegame bug
- Repetitive soundtrack
- Uneven checkpoints on two occasions

Verdict - Must play

title: My 20 lb dog and I LOVE this carrier
text:
I ordered this only because it had free returns if it didn't work out. I was concerned because my dog weighs 20lbs and I just wasn't sure he would fit. I am so glad I finally decided to give it a chance. It has helped so much.

My dog is a shih tzu, bichon Frise mix. On his heaviest day he weighs 20 lbs. From the base of his neck to the start of his tail he is 16" long and he is roughly 10" tall to his back area. He also has a very long tail, I didn't put that in the measurements. I ordered the medium.

His breed cannot take the heat or long hikes. At all!! I always end up having to carry him. It was difficult to go very far while carrying him on my own. This carrier has been an absolute blessing! Do I feel the weight of him on my shoulders? Well, yes, but, it's much better than the alternative. Night and day difference in fact. I could carry him for long distances this way compared to not having him in the carrier.

I just support him by his front legs and every now and then would adjust the shoulder strap a bit. The strap is nice and wide and distributes the weight really well. In my case I am able to let him back out to walk until he gets overheated/tired again so I do get a rest. I just lower him to the ground and he is able to walk right out on his own.

He has not shown any preference with having one or two of his front feet out of the carrier. I haven't tried all four feet in and probably won't. Not sure how well he would fit in with all four? He may but I won't be trying it. I have no need to hook him in or close the netting around him since he travels well without it.

The picture I added for the review he was just put in the carrier and was panting a lot. I should have taken a follow up pic of him no longer panting and relaxed and enjoying the hike after just a few minutes of being in there.

Our warmest hike was in the high 80's and humid and we were out a good hour and a half. When the hike starts to be too much for him I place him in the carrier. (It does help to have another person there to help put him in but not necessary). Even though the weather is hot/humid he stops panting and is very relaxed after a short time in the carrier. Which tells me he's not at all too hot while inside the carrier.

Without this particular dog carrier I would never be able to bring him along for this long of a hike with our summers. I wish I would have gotten it sooner. I also like the two pockets. It fits his water bottle and my cell phone nicely!
Don't remember buying this and I don't recall my daughter playing it on the computer.

title: Great clothing pack!
text:
The Diesel Stuff Pack (SP) is an add-on for the Sims 3, which means you must have the base game to run it. The DVD works on both Macs and PCs. It features a bunch of adult clothes and some objects, all from the international clothing company Diesel. Mostly I bought it because I wanted more options for my adult male Sims, and that is exactly what I got.

I didn't get this SP when it first came out because I thought it was all hipster stuff. But it really isn't hipster at all. There are way more clothes in it than I even thought there'd be, and the men's clothes are of much higher quality than one normally sees in this game, which largely has focused on female clothes; I haven't traditionally been that impressed with EA's offerings for male Sims--either they lack a certain masculinity or seem overly twee or simplistic. These are fashion-forward clothes for men that actually look like stuff a normal guy would wear. There are skinny jeans, as I guess we'll never escape those, but also normal-looking hoodies, T-shirts, trousers, and shorts. The only real off-note here is that some of the writing on the shirts is in Roman letters, not in Simlish, but I don't reckon most people will mind all that much and most of the letters are "stencils," which means they're painted atop the clothes and EA has thoughtfully given variants for these shirts without the stencils. The textures of the pants especially look really nice and realistic, but not garishly texture-mapped like in the Katy Perry Stuff Pack.

I was much more dubious about the women's clothes, but very quickly became a convert. They're really nice! The walkthroughs and box art don't do them justice at all. The shirts aren't dumpy, as I'd thought, or fussy; they're tailored and feminine, with neat little touches like hemstitching. The T-shirts have interesting designs on them, and the trousers are realistic and well-fitted. Yes, skinny jeans abound, but there's a cool pair of flares that I'll use often.

So overall I think these clothes would greatly appeal to anybody who wants to significantly add to their adult Sims' clothing choices, especially people like me who aren't generally impressed at all with how EA does men's clothes. I was impressed by the good execution, the stylish vision involved, and the sheer number of clothes offered in this pack.

Of the 10 or so objects, they're not bad. The end table and coffee tables are really cool-looking; the bed, with recoloring, looks interesting and stylish. I love the mirror--it hangs well just about anywhere as an accent. The lamps are all right but not as nice-looking ingame as I'd thought they'd be. There's a white twill upholstered easy chair that is very casual and suitable for most rooms. I see this SP's objects working beautifully with "Contemporary Comfort" and the rock-and-roll sets. If you like this sort of furniture and deco stuff, you'll like Diesel's offerings quite a bit as they are well-executed. If you're more traditional, you might not.

I rated this pack so highly because it does exactly what it advertises. It does not pretend to be for all age groups and it is straightforward regarding the low number of objects and lack of hairs/accessories. If you want those things more than clothes, you're probably better off leaving this SP on the shelf. If you just want clothes and you like this sort of style, it's a great SP, one of the stronger clothes-emphasized ones.

title: You might find a camera with better recording.
text:
I wished this camera did not pushed the envelope in the 30x optical zoom. We tested this and on play back the picture was very granular and shaky. I mean really shaky. You will need a tripod to reduce the shaking effect. We compared the output with one of panasonic camera that also had a movie function and we found that was better than this HD camcorder (for about the same price).

However, the zoom button was not hyper sensitive and hence you could zoom in and out without the picture looking like you were traveling through the stargate (sorry, for the syfy fans). It was a very easy and light camera to use and the menu was not overtly complicated in that within one choice you do not have to go into many steps to get what you are looking for - in fact there are only 6 menu options and within each one there is up to 6 choices. Great ones that we found actually worked included the face chaser (useful for filming moving objects coming towards you!) and the noise reduction (reduced the wind muffles). The camera is on as soon as you open the side wing with the view - there is no longer a viewer for the eye (thank goodness).

Works great with good lighting - natural and artificial. But does not work too well with dimly lit rooms. We noticed that it really picks up the sound real well so try not to talk as you are filming as we found we ended up being more focused on that than watching the movie. The down side on this camera was that you needed to buy a memory card and a big one at that as there is no hard drive with this camcorder; what is available only allows no more than 5 minutes of movies.

The camera is okay, not great as you can get better pictures on a stand alone camera. There is flash light, which some camcorders do not have. More useful as a camcorder than a camera - so a tad expense for just a camcorder without a hard drive.

title: How to look like a pro (even if you're not)
text:
This Targus notebook case is a great way to carry around all your stuff and still look cool, professional and ready for action.

The good stuff:

1. It can fit notebooks up to 17" securely and safely. There's a strap to hold your equipment in place, it's nicely padded and has an adjustable inner wall for extra snugness. It even opens like a briefcase for easy packing.
2. The same compartment has three pockets with Velcro closures, a zippered mesh pocket and some slots for letters, warranty cards or other documentation. There's ample space for a mouse (optical, cordless, furry with tail), flash drives, cds and dvds, cords, headphones, bells and whistles.
3. The zipper for the notebook section can be locked with a padlock.
4. The front flap has an easy fastener, and also has a zip pocket, right at the front of the bag, perfect for passport and tickets when traveling
5. Lift the flap for another compartment, and more pockets, with slots for pens, glasses, keys, and whatever else you like to carry around.
6. The back has a padded Velcro-closing pocket for newspapers, magazines or other reading matter.
7. Yet another zippered compartment has two slots for important documents and not so important documents.
8. The handle is tough rubber, defying you to mess with it, and the bottom and sides are protected with a corrugated rubber strip. You can set this one down on the floor - it can take it.
9. Even if you aren't carrying around a laptop all the time, this case works fine as a large briefcase for work or travel, with lots of room for a change of clothes, product samples, toiletries (make sure they adhere to airline safety regulations), files, manuals, snacks, extra undies and more.

The other stuff:
1. If you have a 17" laptop, there's not enough space in the padded section to hold your power cord, but there are so many other compartments and pockets that this shouldn't pose a major problem - other than remembering where you put it. (There's plenty of space for a bottle of Ginkgo Biloba)
2. It's pretty durn heavy to lug around, especially for those already having to contend with a full handbag, cup of coffee and high heeled shoes
3. The generous number of compartments encourages you to carry around more stuff than you need - just in case of emergencies. (And then of course you can't remember where you packed them in the first place)
4. It tends to fall over if you don't put it down carefully or lean it against something.
5. The strap looks a little cheap compared to the rest of the case, and keeps spinning around, so you always have to check that the padded piece is on the inside, but it's easier to carry it by the handle anyway.

Sturdy, roomy, comfy and a tad bit clunky, but overall a good case for larger notebooks, work or travel.

Amanda Richards, September 22, 2007

The resulting image is the same quality as a print shop 4" X 6" photo. The photo is ejected from the printer with a white space on the top and bottom of the image. title: For those times when you need a little something to steady yourself
text:
First and foremost, this is a monopod, and should not be expected to perform the duties of a tripod. The two are not on the same playing field, especially if said field is not level, and the monopod's job is simply to hold the fort when a tripod can't go into battle.

Pros:
1. This monopod comes with its own little stand, and is perfectly capable of standing on its own three feet.
2. It can easily support a DSLR with a medium telephoto lens.
3. Set up is simple, requiring only unscrewing the bottom section, opening the legs and screwing the base back on securely.
4. Extends over six feet tall with two adjustable sections
5. Perfect for concert and theatre events in low or changing light, when a tripod either isn't allowed or is impractical.
6. Great for weddings and museum visits
7. You can sit with the monopod braced against your chair and your feet anchoring the legs for extra stability. (I also use a cable release)
8. Padded grip
9. Handy against attacks by stray animals in the wild.

Cons:
1. At the shortest it's still more than two feet long, and doesn't fit well in the external tripod section of smaller camera bags.
2. It's very heavy for all-day trekking around theme parks, museums, big city tours and the like.
3. No carrying case (but has a strap to fasten it on to stuff)
4. Little legs make a lot of noise when concealed (but see below)
5. A bit tricky on uneven ground if you want to use the legs

Things you can fix:
1. Needs a Quick Release head (albeit adding extra weight and cost)
2. Rattling feet can be muffled with a rubber band

Overall, I'm happy with this monopod, except perhaps for the length and weight. It does a great job when you're rushing around in crowded places where tripods fear to tread.

Amanda Richards, June 19, 2013

The lighting, general atmosphere, and sound effects work to increase tension perfectly. If you're a fan of robotics you'll enjoy building your personal arsenal of mods. I own a basic PS4, and I've experienced zero trouble with this game. Before you throw your hands up and dismiss the game, ask yourself how long has your PS4 been sitting in its own dust? How hot is it getting after hours and hours of gameplay? Check the space on the hard drive. I bet there are games there you haven't played in years. Clean it up, and if the game still doesn't work, then it's time for a new PS5. I think I'm close to needing one because the disc drive is failing.

I don't understand why Sony would release an unfinished game, although it's hardly a new phenomenon. But they are making amends. This game is fun and to me, it's a new experience. Now, go forth V and stir the pot in ways that make it most fun for you.

title: A backward step from Forza 6
text:
While there were the expected improvements in graphics and new locations and features, the overall gameplay has suffered in a few key areas. My criticism comes from being a fan of this series since Forza 3.

Here are the problem areas that really represent an overall decline from Forza 6:
1. No Toyota. Obviously this is a probably some legal snafu that relates to licensing and competition with another video game title, but this has never been an issue in the past and Turn 10 hasn’t been really forthcoming with information.
2. For some reason, they’ve put this huge emphasis on the physical drivatar. Like, driver gear is now a huge facet of the prize game. Every non-race menu features your driver standing around shaking his limbs. It’s so awkward and pointless.
3. The game wants to auto-homologate your cars for you. I preferred the past versions where you knew what your race series required and modded your own car accordingly, with the auto-homologate being an option. You can still do your own modding, but the menu interface is much less intuitive for this.
4. Game AI is as bad as ever. On normal difficulty, you have to go from 11th place to 1st (realistically) in 3 laps which isn’t hard, but it really forces you to play bumper cars most of the time to accomplish that. An option to run a qualifying lap would really improve this issue.

Overall it’s still fun, but they’ve emphasized all the wrong features as part of the evolution. Hopefully updates in the near future will address these issues, but as of now, I’d recommend 6 over 7.

I've always liked racing games. I can't say they were ever my favorite genre, but I enjoy them. I played Forza 4 on the 360 with an economy wheel and had a splendid time of it.

Playing Forza 6 with this was an entirely different experience. My hands were shaking; my heart was pounding. It has been a long time since a game did that to me. The wheel fights like a real wheel. You go into a skid and you need to struggle that wheel to go where you want. It's not so much strength as skills, and it's amazing. If you release the wheel slightly, like you might in a real car after a turn, it rights itself exactly as a real car will. It turns pretty much as much as a real car's wheel will in any direction.

You can, of course, attach it to a table or something like -- it connects with a small clamp tightened by two knobs on top that look like buttons (twist them if you're having trouble and the clamps with slowly descend or ascend) but if you're going to go with a wheel of this quality, you may want to go all the way with a wheel stand. It makes a difference in comfort and stability. On the folding table I tried the table tipped, the whole thing shifted around, and it was bad. With even an entry level stand, so long as it has a board to clamp this too, it is perfect.

If you want the most intense racing experience possible, you want this wheel. There are cheaper out there, but the quality difference is severe.

title: Classical gaming Bliss
text: So I’m sure if you’re on this page you know what to expect from Wonder boy, Or if you’re in the younger generation and have seen collectors play these games on YouTube or have played the remakes that have come out the past few years, Regardless wonder boy is known in the gaming community for its Platforming/RPG elements and revolutionizing a genre that wasn’t thought of until this title. Let’s start with part 1, It’s an arcade port. Think of it as an endless runner with being able to kill the enemies and platforming that gets gradually more difficult, It’s the weakest in the series but has held up pretty well! Part 2, An arcade port once again but the dynamics that are featured heavily in later monster world titles come from here, This game is the foundation of the game as we know it today so probably the most important one in the series, Be forewarned it is a quarter muncher as it is an arcade title but with an endless rewind feature and save states, You won’t have much trouble getting through it. There are some parts that I’m left wondering how you’re not supposed to spend $10 in quarters to beat it back in the day. As for 3 and 4 there’s a huge shift in quality and gameplay, These are not arcade titles but ports of the Sega console titles, They’ve honestly aged really well! After playing part 2 know what to expect from part 3, But part 4 is my personal favorite! It’s the metroidvania of the series very reminiscent of the Shantae series. This one is legit fun and I highly suggest that you check out the remake that came out not long ago if you like the original! (or you can just get the remake, which includes the original, Decisions decisions). The extras are honestly bare bones, You get an image gallery that looks like it was thrown together in 2 and a half minutes to make it look like the game has more content, Deff one of my least favorite parts of the compilation as it makes it look a little cheap. All in all it’s a nice compilation and worth the $29.99 and if you find it on sale even better! The classics are all here and you can change the aspect to full screen with crisp graphics or it’s original resolution or even throw in a CRT filter to make it look truly old school. It’s a 7/10 for me. I go by the .5 rating system by the way so it’s not a high 7, just an fyi! Try it out if you enjoy classic gaming! Hope this helps

title: I like to move it, move it ....
text:
Logitech says that their products are designed to move you, and this mouse sure lives up to that promise. Seconds after opening the beautifully packaged box, I was up and running and you can do it too. The instructions tell you everything you need to know, from how to put in the batteries (2 x AAA, included), how to turn it on (power button on the bottom), and where to insert the Nano receiver (USB port). For more features, Windows users can install the software included, and Mac users can go get the download.

Installation takes quite a few minutes, but once that's over, your mouse gets super powers, and can scroll from side to side (perfect for those extra wide pages), help you search the internet with the push of a button, and also navigate backwards and forwards between internet pages. How cool is that?

Here's all the OTHER good stuff about the VX Nano:

1. It's cordless
2. It's compact and cute, and oh so ergonomic (at least for small hands)
3. The MicroGear Precision Scroll Wheel (fancy name for the wheel thing between the buttons that you scroll with) has two modes: Hyper-Fast, for when you need to scroll down long documents at warp speed, and Ratchet, for when you don't have a long, long way to run. You switch between them by simply pressing down on the wheel. (Tilting the same wheel left or right gives you the side by side scrolling once you've installed the software)
4. There's a LED light to tell you when your batteries need changing
5. There's a compartment at the bottom of the mouse to store the Nano-receiver securely. Alternately, you can just leave the little thing attached to your notebook USB port.
6. The package includes a nice Logitech zippered case to keep your mouse snug as a bug in a rug.
7. You can use it on your desktop machine too. It comes with an "extension cord" that you plug into the USB port of your CPU, and insert the Nano-receiver into the little gizmo at the other end, and you're all set. I didn't even have to evict the regular mouse that was already living on my mouse pad.

Believe me, after you've gone Nano you'll never want to go back to cords again.

title: Basic “toaster-type cover” for a 36” (preferably metal) crate
text:
I ordered this for the rescue organization I am affiliated with because this can be used to partially cover a crate during transport or to provide a segregation barrier for upset or sick animals. Since a 36" metal crate was not at our disposal, I used a plastic carrier that was of lesser size. However, this is really for a square 3 foot metal crate, so keep that in mind when viewing the photos.

This reminds of me a no-frills toaster cover. Just pop it over the crate and then adjust as necessary. There are no hooks or straps for securing to the crate whatsoever. Even if there were, the dogs would probably chew on that. However, having an elastic band with Velcro that can go across the outside bottom of the crate in front and back, would be good.

FEATURES:

- The top part of the cover has a "peep hole" that is Velcro'd shut and can be opened to expose a crate's carrying handle - see first photo. Unfortunately, the demo crate did not have a handle.

- The front has a flap that can be rolled up and Velcro'd to the top via the hanging straps - see second photo.

- The left side has a small pocket for incidental items like a brush or cell phone - see third photo.

- The right side has a panel that can be raised to expose a mesh panel. This is to let air into the crate while still providing a barrier. The panel has Velcro in two spots so that it can be rolled up halfway or totally depending on how much one wants to expose the crate to air - see fourth and fifth photo.

- The back is fully zippered (as is the front) and can be opened up as well.

Overall, this is a decent cover but there is nothing that will allow this to stay in place when moving the crate around other than gravity. The current price of $19.99 is reasonable.

title: Arrived In A Nick Of Time- Long Haired Cat And Burdock Don't Mix (Plus A Caution)
text:
We have a long haired cat- the kind with the very very fine fur who is most like an angora bunny. When we first rescued her, she was a tiny kitten and her fur was not that long or thick. We had another short haired cat that she played with and loved to follow outside. He passed away, and now she is queen of the jungle- with very long thick angora fine fur.

She came in the house and I was horrified. Combing her is a task, but I keep up with it well. This time however, I almost cried- I did not know what to do. The burdock and little balls of velcro from another plant had completely matted her fur. No shaving, cutting with scissors or brushing was going to help her. I was very upset and then there was a sound outside. Amazon was dropping by a package. Inside was this life saver. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This tool is a very simple tool. It has a nice grippy handle which is easy to hold and use without losing grip on it. It has two sides. One side has only a four curved blades/brushes, and the other has six.

HOW DO YOU USE THIS?
The idea is that you drag this through the fur, and when you hit a matted area, the blades cut through, much like the principle of thinning shears that the barber or hair salonist will use on thick hair. It takes out some of the fur at the base allowing the mat to be easily broken up.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
Unlike our last cat, this one gets overheated easily. Having this is a godsend. Not only did it take out about 2/3 of the mats and sticky weed balls, but it also thinned her fur out beautifully. She does not have to look like she came out of a newbies gromming chop shop like in previous years.

CAUTION
It is summertime when I am writing this review. That means it is hot out. We do not have air conditioning, but we have a lot of fans going. If you plan to use this tool on a fine haired animal, I highly suggest that you get in a location with no wind or you will be covered in fur and it will be in your room for a very long time.

HOW DOES THE CAT LOOK NOW?
It is amazing. This tool took out a great deal of the mats, thinned out the fur of our adventurous cat perfectly so that she is soft, and looks normal , but she is very happy to be cooler.

THE OBVIOUS QUESTION?
There is an obvious question some of you might ask- "Why not just keep her inside?" This cat can not be kept inside. She is an outdoor cat and we tried a few times to keep her inside, but our house almost did not survive. She loves it outside, so this tool allows her to stay out and keep groomed at the same time.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This tool is a godsend. We have both angora rabbit and a long haired cat with angora like fur which both need grooming often. This thins out fur perfectly for summer, and also keeps mats at bay. It does not hurt the animals at all and works really well and quickly.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am VERY thankful for this amazing tool. It literally has made things tons better for us and our animals this summer. I highly recommend this if you have an animal with tendency to mat and who could use some fur thinning in the summer heat.

title: Sturdy Tripod Legs are Superior to Most
text:
The Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders is even better than I was anticipating and now I must purchase a new tripod head to get the most out of this high quality photographic instrument. To maintain a stable and secure foundation for a camera, this is outstanding -- attractive, easy to assemble, sturdy, and versatile. It arrives in a very nice cardboard box with a handle, so if you're inclined to store it in the box, you have that option. Also included is a black and orange carrying case with a shoulder strap and there is a little zippered compartment near the top of the bag for the hook, included hex key, car key, flash drive, roll of film or whatever you'd like to store. A hand crank raises and lowers the center column and it moves very smoothly, not too easy and not too hard. The tripod can simply be converted for macro shots with low camera placement. For low angle photography using very wide legs, the bottom half of the center column can very easily be removed by simply unscrewing the hook and turning the bottom ring. Very smart and pretty fast, too. Having the option to attach anti slip spiked rubber feet is a great advantage in snow or sand and adds to the stability of the tripod. When the tripod arrives, the large rubber feet are snugly attached and I doubt that they will be lost when removed to use the spikes or standard rubber feet. The three sectioned legs are extremely easy to extend with a slight turn of the amply sized twist locks and each leg has clearly marked segments for perfect measuring. They can be locked at the top, another stability and security advantage, at three angles (25, 50 and 80 degrees). If desired, a camera bag or weight can be hung from the hook on the center column. The rubber foam casing at the top of each leg makes for a very comfortable feel and aid in moving the legs and carrying tripod. Although there's a little bubble level, mine was dry, so customer service is sending me a replacement level. It's small and may be obstructed when a head and large plate or camera are attached, but it's a nice little bonus nevertheless. Changing the camera screw from 1/4" to 3/8" is another simple process that takes seconds. I'm not sure if the orange anti-shock ring really does much, but it can't hurt. This carbon tripod can hold 39 pounds and it weighs around 8 pounds. It has an ample extension and I'm very satisfied with it in all regards for use in the studio as well as in the field.

UPDATE: Vanguard CS is out of this world. When they promised to send a replacement bubble level, I was politely told it would be 2-3 months before they were expected from the manufacturer. Several weeks ago, I received a padded envelope containing a brand new perfect bubble level. It's rare that follow-up isn't necessary in a situation like this, but Vanguard clearly maintained the information to fulfill this promise. If I could award another star in my review, I would!

title: Small but capable music player
text:
The Philips GoGear Raga is the first exposure I have had to Philips' line of mp3 players and I was unsure of what I should expect of it. The price is comparable to other mp3 players of similar capacity so I expected it to be in the ballpark with them. For the most part I was correct, though there are a few things about which one should be aware when using this particular offering. It's a good product, but it has its quirks.

Setting up the Raga is easy. In the package is a USB cable that allows one to connect to a PC (packaging does not indicate if MacOS supports the Raga), and upon connecting Philips Songbird downloads and installs automatically. The installation is painless and does not take long, and a few clicks of the mouse along the way and the software loads up.

The first thing I tried to do was load music into the Raga, and once I got the music into Songbird the Raga disappeared from the available devices list. I am not sure what happened. I unplugged it and shut down Songbird, plugged the Raga back in and everything was as it should be, so I dragged 67 songs to the Raga for transfer. I saw two problems. First, the user has to know to drag and drop - there is no "transfer to..." option that I could find in any of the menus. The bigger problem, though, is that the transfer speed is abysmal and it took close to 2 minutes to transfer 67 songs that average 5MB in size. With my old iPod and with my ZuneHD, transfer speeds are appreciably faster. This doesn't make the Raga a piece of junk, of course, as the problem may be Songbird itself, but the transfer speed is something of which to be aware, especially if transferring large amounts of music.

Navigating to the newly transferred music is simple. For that matter, navigating the Raga is simple, period. Anyone with even slight familiarity with music players will have no problem finding and playing music on the Raga.

For comparison, I matched the Raga against my ZuneHD for playback. Of course, the Zune HD produced a more natural and clear sound, but only slightly. For the difference in price, I would have expected the ZuneHD to REALLY outperform the Raga, but this was not the case. In fact, when playing with the built in equalizers in both, I was able to get the Raga to get very close to the ZuneHD for sound quality. The difference was more pronounced with higher end ANC headphones, but this is unlikely to matter to the large majority of users.

The Raga has a tiny screen (the package says it's 1" diagonally) so this is not the kind of player one would want if frequently messing with settings and searching through. That said, the Raga is designed as a player to be worn with the included arm band, suitable for using at the gym. The ear buds that come with it have over-the-ear hooks to help keep them in place.

Considering the price and size, Philips has put together a very nice music player that will suit active users very well. It has some idiosyncrasies, in particular the transfer speeds, but it really is a capable player.

title: I've been looking for an affordable headset with surround.  This fit my needs.
text:
[[VIDEOID:bcce61b61b8337c3b68e072c0d20d249]] I had a USB gaming headset that worked fairly well. It had large speakers that gave the sound a "roomy" feeling, especially when paired with the driver software that it came with, but the wire was driving me crazy. I couldn't step away from my desk without removing a few things or I'd end up pulling away my computer with me.

So, I was in the market for a nice pair of wireless gaming headsets. I've come across many in the 30-dollar range but none of the descriptions for those touted surround sound. Eventually, I had to look in the 60 - 90 range.

This pair of OCG Gaming Headsets 2.4GHz Bluetooth Wireless Gaming Headphones were just what I needed. I wanted bluetooth capabilities because I wanted to have it as an option in case I wanted to pair it to two computers (one via dongle and one via bluetooth). I also wanted the option of using it with other gaming systems such as an XBox or Playstation. The usb dongle gives that versatility.

I really don't care much for RGB as they just make my computers distracting and I'm not a game streamer or youtuber (not yet, anyway, ha ha), but if you do like them, this headset has them...

So, what do I think? I'd been playing Uncharted 4 on my PC with my old pair of headphones and it sounded great. The surround didn't really seem like it worked very well. After I received the OCG, I plugged in the USB dongle and booted up the game. The game automatically detected the headset and showed that it was using virtual surround. Immediately, I found that I was hearing sounds that I hadn't heard before!

As the character walked around, I heard the jangling sounds of the equipment he had at his belt, I heard the companion character talking behind me and as I turned, her voice moved around my head. I was super impressed!

I then disconnected the dongle and tried the headset in bluetooth mode. The sound was a little muffled and there was almost no surround effect, even though the game still said that it was doing virtual surround.

So I'm definitely using the dongle for all my gaming. I love this thing!

title: Brilliant for fans of the Old Skool CRPG genre of games
text:
The first thing to understand about Pillars of Eternity (PoE) is that it is intentionally designed as a retro, old-skool gaming experience that plays the way CRPGs did in the "classic" CRPG era of Baldur's Gate/Planescape: Torment -- i.e., circa 1998-2000. This refers to the entire *experience* and gameplay, not just the "core". What has been updated is simply the graphic detail and resolution, which is full 1080p. Everything else, especially game mechanics, is a loving recreation of the old skool designs from the classic era. This includes movement, combat, use of text, conversation trees, and so on.

I say that this is the first thing to understand because if you don't understand it, you may be disappointed in the game. The game is not using "modern" or "contemporary" conventions when it comes to computer RPGs -- like you may have seen in the Dragon Age series or the Mass Effect series or Kingdoms of Amalur or what have you. It very consciously is using game design and systems that are from the "classic" era of ~15 years ago, to appeal to players who like those older systems very much, and the kind of gameplay that they permit. If you strongly prefer the more contemporary style of CRPG gameplay, you will probably be frustrated with the mechanics of PoE, again, because it is so old skool.

However, if you very much like the classic design and conventions, PoE is a feast of a game for you. You can micro-manage to your heart's content, engage in blow by blow combat akin of pen and paper games, immerse yourself in deep, textual lore for hours on end in a journey that is interesting, satisfying and rewarding ... if you like the mechanics. For someone who likes that approach to CRPGs, the game will be a fantastic experience, and is not to be missed.

title: Better than Elements, but still not great
text:
Heroes Chronicles: Clash of the Dragons follows the adventures of Tarnum, a former barbarian lord leading an elf king's army against the united forces of Mutare and her dragon minions. Just as in the companion game, Heroes Chronicles: Masters of the Elements, heroes are developed, quests performed, monster armies recruited and castles and territories expanded as the hero tries to fend off invading forces.

Terrain varies from sylvan to rocky to positively infernal and creatures match their homelands, ranging from flame-throwing demons, unicorns and battle centaurs to dragons of all types. Magic items, supplies and even spells can be bought or traded. Fundamental to success is establishing different types of strongholds that generate creatures of varied ability. The game uses the same engine as Heroes Chronicles: Masters of the Elements and gameplay revolves around adventurers leading troops, thus causing them to act more as "mules" to transport troops than heroic entities.

Combat can be tedious, though battles compared to those in Masters of the Elements are a bit more even. There are fewer "death-trap" scenarios, although they still occasionally crop up. Some unique conditions modify each scenario, such as rescuing a particular character or performing a quest to give you an edge in completing the mission.

Unfortunately, the game engine is somewhat flawed and the same problems that plague Masters of the Elements are evident here. The most glaring error is the separation of NPCs in the plot and as adventurer's in the game. It's possible to have a significant adventurer from the storyline die during gameplay, yet the narrative blithely ignores the event. Conversely, an adventurer can be kidnapped in the plot line but still be leading troops in the game. Ultimately, these inconsistencies destroy the impact of the storyline.

A good example of an inconsistency revolves around Tarnum's concern for Valita, a potential spy in his army. As part of a major subplot, the concern should be ill founded since, after all, you control Valita as an adventurer. Unfortunately, what happens to her has no impact on her role in the plot, as she can die and the plot continues as if she were still alive.

The end conditions for each scenario can almost always be solved through brute force alone, which detracts from the appeal of the entire adventure. It's even possible to resolve the ending without actually fighting the main villain. While Heroes Chronicles: Clash of the Dragons is an improvement over Masters of the Elements, it can't overcome the flaws of the game design.

title: The Long Awaited Hardcore JRPG for Wii U!!!
text:
If you own a Wii U and would love to play some good JRPGs, you should definitely buy this game! I have played Persona Q, Shin Megami Tensei IV, and Etrian Odyssey IV, and I must say that Tokyo Mirage is at least on par with the best of those three games. I have also played Fire Emblem Awakening, but that game is under a whole different genre, so I cannot really compare this game with Fire Emblem.

You may have heard many reviewers saying, "Tokyo Mirage is good, but this game is not for everybody." That is true but trivial, because it applies to literally every game. Not everyone likes Skyrim, League of Legend, Ocarina of Time, or Pokemon, despite how popular each of those games is. So I would just say, if you like JRPGs, you should definitely try Tokyo Mirage out.

You may also be dissuaded from buying this game by comments about how much this game was censored in North America. Personally, I do not think that showing less skin in a video game is a bad thing. On the other hand, I would be very disappointed with myself, if I paid 60 dollar just to see some virtual skin. Also, I really do not feel like sneakily playing this game in a basement or some secret chamber because of the suggestiveness of sexy characters. I want to share this awesome alternative to Pokemon with my 13-year-old brother!

Additionally, you may have heard people saying how hard this game is. In my opinion, this game is not as brutal as Etrian Odyssey IV, Persona Q, and Shin Megami Tensei IV. Of course you cannot just keep meshing button A throughout a battle like you will normally do in Pokemon, but the best choices to make in a battle in this game are pretty obvious. Yes, you will die sometimes in the game unless you are very careful, but you die in other games too, don't you?

I think the game's presentation is really beautiful and colorful. The frame rate is very consistent and the loading time is not long. However, I would say that the characters talk kinda slow in this game, which slows down the whole game. That is quite awkward since the battles are usually fast-paced. Honestly, for me, I am perfectly fine with that. I play this game after a long day of work, so the slow-paced conversations suit my slow mind. Lastly, the main story is well-written and the side stories are fun and meaningful too. That is all I am going to say without spoiling any of the tons of surprises the game has to offer.

If you have played the Persona series or Shin Megami Tensei series, you will probably enjoy this game. Unfortunately, if you are a Fire Emblem fan, this game is nothing like Fire Emblem. It is not a tactical RPG, and all the beloved Fire Emblem characters in this game are unplayable, at least not directly. But I will say this one more time before it gets old, if you like JRPGs, give this a try. One of the reasons why I bought Wii U in the first place is Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE.

title: Good Choice for Older Dogs
text:
When your dog starts to advance in age, you need to be careful about what you feed him/her. Older dogs have special nutritional needs and a dog food formulated to meet those needs is Nutro Max Senior Recipe Dry Dog Food.

Let’s first look at the ingredients with this dog food. There is no corn, wheat, or soy, so that is a plus. The ingredient list is mostly good, but there are a few items I would rather not see, and I don’t like that actual chicken ranks sixth on the list. Still, compared to other dog foods on the market, what this food offers is easily better than average.

With this dog food, the kibbles are small. They are dry and crunchy and take little effort for your dog to eat. I have two dogs and the older of the two is eight years old. He likes this dog food as much as any and he eats it willfully and happily. His younger sibling finds it okay, too. She isn’t quite a senior dog yet, but there should be no problem feeding this to other adult dogs.

Nutro is a trusted brand in dog food. Nutro Max Senior Recipe Dry Dog Food is a good choice for older dogs. It contains ingredients that are designed for a senior dog’s digestive system and health needs and while it doesn’t contain the most stellar list of ingredients, it is still better than most and a good choice for dogs aged seven and up.

title: Exchanged HD 518 for these
text:
Why I chose the 439 over the rest

Clamping force and comfort
I have a large head, and have read comments from other large headed reviewers stating that some of the other big brands are not comfortable for long periods of time. I can tell you that these are comfortable for both my large head, and others with smaller heads that have tried them. Not sure how they would be for large ears though. I have regular sized ears, and they fit perfectly.

Replaceable Cord
These are the only headphones in the lower-mid-range closed back Sennheiser line that has a replaceable cord. You would think that the 449 does (since it is a higher number) but it does not. Yeah I am pretty good with a soldering iron, but that doesn't mean that I actually want to use it.

Why I exchanged the 518 for these

Sound isolation
The open back design of the 518 was more prohibitive to my lifestyle than I had originally anticipated, as they leak more sound than I thought. You could actually hear the sound leakage in the next room if the doors were open, and the house was fairly quiet.

I watch a lot of cartoons and strange independent dramas. I also listen to ancient heavy metal, along with a smattering of other unlikely musical genres. Few people want to hear that combination of things spewing from my headphones. Now I can enjoy watching things like the Rectify (Especially the Drip Drip episode) without having to explain later to others in the next room.

Roku and Smart Phone use.
The 518 has a 1/4 plug, and the 439 has 1/8. I like to use the headphones with my Roku 3 remote a lot, and having a 1/4 to 1/8 adapter in my pocket with the Roku remote adds a lot of bulk. On the other hand, whenever I want to use the 439 on my old school stereo, I just use the included 1/8 to 1/4 adapter, which isn't really a hassle at all.

title: Best Wear OS for true Android users, but not perfect
text:
I will avoid the facts that this watch is outdated at launch by its hardware (processor). That, coupled with retail and even discounted price also are out of step with the competition. These two big gripes aside. The watch is good and likely the best choice going into 2023 for pure Android Wear OS users (not looking at Apple or Tizen overlay users.)

Its not perfect and Pixel users will benefit the most when paired to this watch. Its lost most of the lag recent watches from other Wear OS brands. Has all the sensors the majority of buyers could want based on watch tech right now. It swipes, it plays well with the apps made for it. It gives you the info you ask of it. There are even a few nice 3rd part accessories now to avoid Google Gouging for proprietary bands. And there are few quirks I hope they iron out soon. Mainly, when the phone is in Bedtime Mode. Make the watch do it too, or add that Zen Mode feature to the watch also. It sucks to have animals tripping the security cameras outside dinging on my wrist and killing my sleep score. The snooze/do not disturb button on watch fails too easily and you have turn it on/off manually everytime.

As many claim, the battery sucks. Sort of. I can go up to 36+ hours on a slow day, and many others can too. It will depend on too many factors to list. But basically your popularity with notifications and thinking you need the screen always on are the biggest battery hurdles. Most can get use to touch to wake. And maybe only having text, phone, front door doorbell and one email be allowed to bother your watch with notifications. Do you really need to know what cousin Billy had at Dairy Queen when he posts the same pic/vid on Facebook, Instagram, Tic Toc and YouTube, etc. Find a nice balance of wrist information along with what sensors you need checking if you are still alive. You can start the day and track everything till the next morning when you charge it again while you shower and get the next day started. It charges quickly. And most other Wear OS watches have the same daily charge requirements. Nobody on Wear OS is winning on battery. Or Turn every setting all the way up and have a spare charger puck ready for a mid day juice. If you go that route. I suggest a quick release band to ease the removal of the watch.

So, its not up to the level or price of the Ultra Apple Watch. And if you don't care for Samsung. Your love for stock Android will eventually lead you back to this watch. Unless you forgo ECG sensors. The price will drop soon. Cases are minimizing the fragility of an ALL glass jelly bean design. But when comes to keeping your phone pocketed and yet still have info relayed in a useful way. Pixel Watch is the best current albeit not perfect solution for now.

title: Turn all the lights off at night, I dare you.
text:
Ok the only thing that can sum up this game is as follows: Psychologically Damaging. I must say I've never been this afraid of a game. I've played all the Resident Evil games and I must say they were cake walks compared to this one (although I must say after a half-hour, RE lost its ability to scare me... even alone in my apartment with the lights off).
The big difference here is that in RE is dealing with corporeal things... sure they may be around corners or jump at you suddenly from the ceiling/window/grave/etc, but they are still just zombies. In the end they still have to come at you and you've got a nice arsenal of weapons waiting for them.
Fatal Frame is much different in that regard. In FF you deal with the ethereal, things that can appear and disappear at whim, and don't need to open a door to go through it. The worst part is that all you have to defend yourself with is a camera... which means in order to take out one of these specters, you have to stare the thing directly in the face first.
If you are looking for something to make you jump out of your pants, this probably isn't the game you're looking for. This game has a much meaner style to it. It simply heaps on the psychological trauma gradually, so that when you are done playing a session you feel emotionally drained, and not in any kind of condition to go to bed.
Aside from the high horror factor this game totes, it's also beautifully done. The ambient music and sounds set the mood perfectly, and the scenery is masterful. The setting of an old Japanese village is well picked, and the rendering of the village itself is superb. The only problem is that sometimes doors are a little hard to see, but that is mostly because I wasn't used to looking for sliding doors. Plus had there been western style doors, the setting would not have looked authentic.
The big hiccup for this game is the dual character setup. While you can move at a mild pace, not fast mind you, your partner takes up the rear with a horrible limp and no speed to go with it.
So all in all I would recommend this game. But for those of you expecting Resident Evil, I suggest you rent it first. This game is obviously not for everyone.

title: Work's great on the Wii
text:
I purchased this game when I bought the Wii and it works really well especially with a Gamecube controller. The plot of the game is that you (Mario) are visiting a distant land, when you are confronted by the citizens who accuse you of polluting their countryside. Mario is sentenced to using a water cannon to go around and clean everything that was ruined. You soon find out that there is a Mario lookalike (sort of a blue, watery looking Mario) running around with a paintbrush polluting everything. Your water pack has the ability to be a fire hose, jet pack, rocket pack and motorboat.

Now that the description is out of the way "Here we go!". The graphics are good for a game of its time. It has the overall feeling of Mario 64 but doesn't quite live up to the rep of a Mario game. The puzzles have the potential to be fun, but also incredibly frustrating. The variety of game play is also pretty abundant. However, this game has the absolute worst camera angles of any game I've ever played. Add that to the poor shadowing and you have a formula for a game where the player will constantly have to restart missions and climb sequences from falling off cliffs, not making the jump, falling into the water, falling from not being able to gauge distances, missing landings while using the je pack option, etc. Even Devil May Cry had better camera angles than this game and you can't control the cameras in that game. I even find it pretty annoying that I can't adjust camera controls, I'm very used to non inverted controls and this game is all about control inversion.

Anyway, that is my overall of the game. I'm not sure if this game is worth the $17 or $18 you'll pay in total from Amazon. But if you are a dedicated Mario fan go for it. I say just spend the money on Mario 64 and Super Mario World downloads for the Wii and play those. I think you'll derive much more enjoyment and the less frustration playing those games.

title: Works wonders
text:
I have a 65lb male Boxer who had never had his nails trimmed in his entire life. He became a member of my family a little over a year ago and I have been trying desperately to figure out a way to shorten his nails for both his comfort and my sanity (his clicking on my floors is enough to drive someone up a wall!).

The problem I encountered was that his quicks were right to the end of his nails (as is to be expected in his case). So, I know that I need to trim his nails frequently in order to encourage the quicks to recede up the nails. I have tried guillotine style trimmers and these are nothing but torture for both of us (I cannot keep a good grip on the wide handles and they are nothing but pinchers in his eyes as they apply too much pinching and not enough cutting). I have also requested that my vet help me out and, sadly, their idea of a nail trim is to use a pair of guillotine trimmers - no thank you.

So, after some desperate searching, I found and purchased this Dremel based on reviews here on Amazon and other pet sites. It arrived in a timely fashion and the packaging was easy to open. I did have to go online to find better instructions on how to insert the sandpaper band (the included instructions appear to be written by someone who is assuming the consumer is a Dremel wiz and already knows how to do everything - very annoying!). Once that hurdle was jumped, I tested the unit out on myself to see exactly what my dog will be experiencing. This tool is very powerful and can be extremely accurate, depending on the angle at which you hold it. I introduced my dog to it by letting him smell it, then turned it on and let him investigate and learn the sounds of both speeds. We seem to like the lower speed for most of the time and the higher speed for the initial sanding of the leading edge of the nails. In our case, it is too easy to go to short thus sanding into his quicks and making him bleed - so we are pleased with using the lower speed.

Overall, I can see this product serving its purpose - we simply have to be patient as encouraging quicks to recede can be a very time consuming project. Yet I have no doubts that I finally have the right tool for the task at hand. My dog seems to handle the Dremel very well (although I think it is because he is just an attention lover).. he will lie on the floor on his back and not fuss at all while I do each foot in succession. He is a little touchy on the back feet, but I think it is just him being slightly ticklish. Highly recommended by both human and Boxer alike!

title: Doesn’t Work With Synapse 3.0 Programming Software; Has Problems With Synapse 2.0 Software
text:
First, this RAZER BLACK WIDOW ULTIMATE ESPORTS GAMING KEYBOARD (Green Mechanical Switches (Tactile and Clicky)) is NOT a “Chroma” keyboard that allows you to change the backlighting color with Razer Synapse software. Instead the backlighting color is green only, and is subject to software adjustment in overall brightness and contrast only.

Second, this keyboard does NOT work with Razer Synapse 3.0, the latest version. If you already have that version on your Win10 PC, you will need to download Razer Synapse 2.0 (currently 2.21.21.1) to be able to make adjustments via software to the backlighting and the key assignments.

Unfortunately, the 2.0 software can’t load the image of the keyboard when you go to the configurations, so it’s hard to program the keys with the software. Also, having two versions of Razer Synapse on my PC played havoc with my Internet connection when I was connected to Razer Central--different browsers refused to connect to web sites (even Google) on the basis that my connection wasn’t secure, even though the connection had been secure by default. It had somehow gotten changed so it was NOT secure.

Fortunately, it is possible to dim the backlighting with the keyboard alone (FN + F11 or F12). It is also possible to program some keys with the keyboard alone (see the poorly written quickstart manual packed in the box lid).

Third, the backlighting is set to maximum brightness by default, and is annoyingly bright until you figure out how to adjust it. Something that I did NOT like is that only the numbers and letters on the keys are backlit. You have to peer at the keys to find the symbols, such as the @ symbol.

Fourth and last, the mechanical keys have a nice feel, and make a soft popping sound as you type. I like the “tactile, clicky” feature very much, but question whether the keyboard is worth the Amazon price (about $66) when the 2.0 software has the problems that it has. I’d rather put my money down on a keyboard that works with Synapse 3.0.

title: Really Nice Zoom Lens
text:
My family got together and picked this up for me during Fuji's sale/promotion in March. This is going to cover Christmas and birthdays for the next few years :)

Build quality is top notch. The zoom, focus and aperture rings are all nicely sized and very... grippy. The zoom itself is almost, but not quite, too stiff. I noticed no creep whatsoever. Autofocus is, expectedly, a bit slower than the kit lens but still decent. Image stabilization is impressive enough for hand-held shooting in low light at full zoom. Image quality is impressive. The included hood is huge, seriously huge. It's actually a little hard to get the lens cap on with the hood on. Speaking of the lens hood; my one gripe with this rig is when fully 'on' the lens the hood tends to rattle a little bit. I've found that backing off the connection a 1/4 inch or so keeps the hood from rattling and still keeps it firmly in place.

It does make my X-E2 a little front heavy but it's not that horrible. I'm contemplating buying one of the extension grips from Fuji for the camera. A nicely padded neck strap is a definite plus when carrying a camera with this lens mounted on it. One thing I've had to pay attention to is when switching back to my 18-55mm lens I need to be careful of how hard I twist the barrel to zoom in and out this lens is MUCH stiffer to use than the kit 18-55mm that came with my X-E2. I worry I may break the smaller lens after using this lens for an extended period.

Highly recommended.

title: Simple, but entertaining
text:
The first time I sat down to play this game, I played for a couple hours before realizing how much time had passed. It is extremely simple to pick up, for gamers and non-gamers alike. There is no concept of "lives", so you can never really lose if you keep trying - you just keep starting back at the beginning of the level you are on, and you get to keep all the crystals you have collected. You can earn gold, silver, and bronze trophies by completing the course quickly, and you can also collect special objects which unlock secret levels, new music, etc. The game is easy to learn, but difficult to master - getting gold trophies is HARD!

I imagine the game probably isn't as much fun once you have gotten all the way through it and received however many trophies you are willing to put the effort into getting, but in the meantime I'm having lots of fun with it!

Unlike the other reviews I see here already, I have not played Super Monkey Ball on the Wii; I found the previous Monkey Ball game I tried on the GameCube repetitive and boring after about half an hour, so take that into account when you read this review.

title: Terrible software, but it can work
text:
If you must use your computer as a tv, the gamebridge will fulfill your needs. However, the software package that ships with it (InterVideo Home Theatre) is terrible, and you may need to turn to a third party solution - I wasn't even able to get InterVideo Home Theatre to run. There is no troubleshooting documentation and Adaptec's support for the product is non-existant.

I eventually ditched the InterVideo program and used Dscaler to display the video stream from the gamebridge. This worked rather well, though it requires a lot of processor power to de-interlace the video stream. Unless you have a very fast computer, you'll have to settle for a reduction in image quality or suffer many dropped frames. After picking a de-interlacing algorithm appropriate for my processor's power, there was only the occasional stutter or rendering artifact.

In summary, using the gamebridge with a laptop won't be as good as a TV, but is entirely adequate if a TV isn't available. However, if you use a monitor that is detached from your PC, try a vga converter instead.

title: Finally, a game that isn't afraid to be smarter than you are
text:
This is one of the best computer games ever, and the best single-character role playing game.

After the first few hours of playing Deus Ex, I was impressed the complexity of the combat system. The tactical maps reward exploration, the hit point system is body-location specific instead of general (so a critical blow against a head is much different from one against a leg), and there are so many ways to approach a probem that it makes the "multisolution" system of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic look like Tic Tac Toe. The options of long-range sniping, getting up close and personal with melee weapons or unleashing with automatic weapons and grenades also contribute to a great first person shooter experience.

After the first day, I was impressed with how the game went out of its way to set the mood of another world, the fact that if you wander into the women's restroom an NPC will make a sarcastic comment, and how almost every non-player character has something to say. I was particularly blown away by how experience is awarded not for killing things, but for "exploration bonuses", "progress awards" and "achieved objective awards". Too many games reward the entirely unrealistic activity of looking for danger, while in Deus Ex there is little point to looking for an unnecessary fight.

I moved the game from the "really good" to the "ridiculously good" column after it passed the 'toilet' and 'Asian languages' tests. Have you ever noticed that people in computer games almost never have to go the bathroom, and that even large buildings don't have any toilets? And also that games that have a lot of toilets, such as the Fallout series, tend to be really good role playing games? Deus Ex has a lot of restrooms, with toilets that you can flush. The second test is one that I've never actually seen in a game - the use of an actual Asian language rather than a bunch of scribbles. Having spent about 6 years of my life studying Japanese, the fact that most games don't even try to use a real writing system for signs supposedly set somewhere in Asia is really annoying. Deus Ex does in the chapter set in Hong Kong, and it is so well done that I was able to tell stalls in the market apart by their Chinese-language signs. Major respect due to the designers for their attention to this detail that everyone else ignores!

Finally, when NPCs began to give in-depth speeches on the nature of the relationships among society, the individual and government I decided that this game was off the charts. It is the rarest of computer games - a first-person shooter role playing game that builds its foundation on ideas. The graphics are a bit dated, but the graphics are not the reason to play this game. title: Truly Couldn't Be Happier {Updated 04-04-2017}
text:
I knew, due to my disability, that I was going to need to find a professional installer to install this Boss Audio Systems B9351WRC head unit and wireless reverse camera along with two replacement door speakers I decided needed replacement (and wow, they really needed replacing). The installation took approximately three hours or so. The only problem which may not be a problem but I'm a worrier. The bracket for the wireless reverse camera somewhat, but not entirely, covers the plate expiration stickers somewhat. Other than that the head unit fit as good if not better than the stock radio fit. in the dashboard.
This radio plays AM/FM stations though there's very few decent radio stations around here. The unit also plays from USB thumb drives which plugs into a port under a panel under the volume/pause/power button. I put 600+ songs on a USB 2.0 16 GB driver and it played everything as far as I could tell. There might be a couple VBR or odd format MP3 files it may not play but I haven't gotten to them yes. Nothing's refused to play and even a couple that had imbedded album artwork actually showed up but so small it was almost impossible to see and I had no idea how to make it better. The instructions in the manual were basically "Play with things and see what happens!" more than specific directions how different functions work.
What I went with, is a 32 gig micro-SD card that had the same 600+ songs the thumb drive has. But with the micro-SD card you can close the hatch under the volume and control knob which you couldn't with the thumb drive. There's also an AUX input jack for old style MP3 players and phones.
The six inch screen is sharp and crisp. The backup camera, even with a streetlight thirty feet away had more than enough light to back out of my garage. I even backed down the street a ways in almost complete darkness and could see just fine with just the reverse lights on the car. Now as long as no cops have a problem with it I'm golden.
I tried home burned CDs and while it took a few seconds longer to recognize it played them fine. I tried store bought CDs and they played right off the bat. OH! and it plays DVD discs jut fine in case my passenger wants to watch a movie as we drive. I promise I'm no dumb enough to watch a movie while I drive.
According to the installer I can leave the micro SD card in the unit all the time. So, 600+ songs anytime I want which I can shuffle or randomly pick and play songs anytime I want. I couldn't be happier. With the stock deck I'd sometimes get to my destination just as the deck decided to recognize the CD so this deck is a godsend when I really needed a new one. Now with as many songs as I can cram into a 32 gig drive. Right now I've got 687 songs and tons of free space. I may have to start buying more music and ripping some more albums from my collection to add to my micro-SD card.
So I can play hundreds, thousands of MP3 songs on a micro-SD card. I can play CDs both homemade and store bought. I can watch DVDs on a pretty sharp (all settings can be changed in the system) the dimmer is a bit bright until it goes off completely but it's not too bad or too bright. There's a user setting EQ option as well as several other preset settings to choose from. There are options to add sound effects such as large hall, church, cavern, etc. I avoided them entirely and set my own EQ settings with the loudness off. The new speakers sound great for high end and midrange. The stock back speakers add some needed bass.
All in all? This is an affordable head unit with all the features and functions one could ask for. It comes with a remote that I'm not sure I'm even going to keep anywhere in the car. Anything you need to do can be done on the deck and no one's sitting in the back seat of a '07 Hyundai Accent, seriously. So the remote is useless but amusing.
I love this unit, the backup cam is awesome, The many ways to play music. The fit and finish, it's close to perfect.
This a little long and meandering review but I really like this radio and I'm glad I replaced the door speakers and went with a professional installer who's basically given me a lifetime warranty on his labor. I couldn't be happier.

Update 04-04-2017: It's been nearly six months since I had this head unit and backup camera installed. Radio reception is still bad, I still despise listening to radio so that's no big deal. Have kept a micro SD card loaded with hundreds of songs installed. Turn the unit on it automatically defaults to that. Everything is still working fine. Professional installation was worth the money.
