title: Decent components, poor execution
text:
Slept two nights with these headphones in their stock configuration and decided I could create something far superior.
For several years I’ve owned and extensively used a pair of the original wired SleepPhones. They are extremely comfortable. The drivers are only 2-3mm thick and sandwiched between two layers of felt. The fleece headband stayed in place without feeling constrictive. It was also easy to wash - open the hook and loop closure on the back, pulled out the speakers and wires, wash, dry, re-install.
By contrast, MusiCozy uses thicker drivers (granted, the frequency response is better than the SleepPhone drivers) then adds a rubber cover, then covers that with a thin jersey fabric. The headband was painfully tight, and I don’t have a big head (22.5”). After the first night, I stretched the headband over a small throw pillow for a day and that helped a bit. But the second night, the thick drivers hurt my ears so bad I took the whole thing off. I mostly sleep on my side and stomach. It’s also tricky to charge because the port is only accessible if you line up the slit in the jersey fabric just right. Some simple product testing would have identified these issues. But for $20, I couldn’t be happier….. why?
SleepPhoness wants $100 for their bluetooth units. I’m sure they are top-notch but I didn’t want to spend that much. Here’s my solutions: The entire MuziCozy headband was disassembled….all two components. The bluetooth receiver / battery compartment and speakers come out easily enough. The fake ‘control panel’ on the front isn’t needed. The speakers have a rubber cover that is not needed. Once that is removed, the speakers are only 3-4mm thick, which is good. I disassembled the wired SleepPhones as well. The felt driver covers were re-used with the MuziCozy drivers, then the whole thing was re-installed into the SleepPhone headband.
This is the best setup - the headband is comfortable, I can still use it to cover my eyes, the sound quality is improved, and the MuziCozy charge port is easier to access thanks to the large velcro opening on the back of the headband.
My girlfriend, by contrast, likes absolute silence while sleeping so she uses the MuziCozy headband to make sure her earplugs don’t fall out and to cover her eyes.
So the entire unit has gone to good use, just not in the way it was delivered. I’m happy with the results but the original product need some redesign.

title: Very fun game. However there are some gruesome parts that ...
text:
Very fun game. However there are some gruesome parts that are not suited for younger children. Detectives examine dead people, including dead children, so you do too. Soon, you’re investigating a series of similarly gruesome murders in the wake of the Black Dahlia killing (which was never solved in the real world), and you eventually uncover a city-spanning conspiracy.

As you progress from the traffic department to homicide, vice and arson, you tackle 21 cases that should each take 60 to 90 minutes to complete your first time through. The gameplay is actually quite simple. You walk around crime scenes, waiting for your controller to buzz in your hands to tell you to pick up a clue. Then you interrogate witnesses and suspects, listening closely, watching their facial expressions and piecing together the clues to decide if they’re telling the truth (and, more important, whether you have enough evidence to prove they’re lying).

If you miss a clue or react incorrectly to an answer, that doesn’t mean that you fail; it just means that the case may unfold differently. There are some action sequences, like chases and shootouts, but if you fail one of those a few times, the game just lets you skip past it, so those of slow reflex and clumsy thumb need have no fear.

Instead of action, the focus in L.A. Noire is squarely on basic storytelling elements like narrative, character, setting and plot: 322 actors delivered voice performances for the game, and their efforts are generally superb. The Rockstar hallmark — gritty, believable, wry dialogue — is on full display.

Yet none of Rockstar’s previous games have been so emotionally powerful.

That’s because the big theme here is the difficulty soldiers have in readjusting to civilian life and the profound social trauma that can result when that goes awry. As one of Phelps’s partners remarks on the way to another murder scene, Los Angeles in 1947 is awash in young men who got used to killing every day in the war, then returned and were expected to take orders from their wives. Not all of them could.

As L.A. Noire unfolds, through flashbacks the game also tells the story of Phelps’s own war history and his fraught relationship with the men under his command. Without giving away the plot, the stories of past and present end up colliding in spectacular, heartrending fashion. Like so many of his suspects, our hero has demons of his own, and like so many of his suspects, he does not handle them easily.

The accounts and effects of post-traumatic stress among World War II veterans upon their return are not often brought up, probably because the war itself was a huge victory for the United States, and because the country soon embarked on a huge economic boom. In that sense these stories have been obscured. L.A. Noire treats this very human reality with a deft, mature hand that lends all the police-procedural gameplay an emotional heft rarely felt in video games.

title: BOTTOMLINE if you use PINE PELLETS - DON'T count on dimensions - TOO SMALL for my SMALL cat
text:
IN THEORY, great idea. In practice, not as much.

I GET this is meant for clay clumping litter, but many of us like pine pellets better.

IF one doesn't SIFT in some way, it's very difficult to not dump GOOD pellets along with those turned to sawdust when urine hits them.

This works the opposite way if you use pellets. Rather than the clumps you want to get RID of, in the sifting tray, the GOOD pellets stay in the tray and sawdust falls through.

PROS:

LOOKS - Attractive looking the way boxes stack, liked the colors.

SIFTER - This is a pro and a con. I found just shaking it didn't work well and needed to use the scooper to move around the pine pellet litter (that's the only litter I like for my cat)
BUT it does work.

BIGGEST PRO is that I don't waste litter. Using non clumping pine pellet, you can easily waste too much trying to remove urine as it turns to sawdust.

IF you use pine pellets and don't want to WASTE, it's important to sift it somehow.

CONS:

NOT BIG ENOUGH! - I have a fairly small cat, not full grown. She's about 16 inches long, not counting tail.
She was putting her paws on the rim of the litter box and was going to the bathroom standing like that.

THE DIMENSIONS given are DECEIVING! They SAID they were the size of her previous litter tray. The dimensions are for the SIFTER which is bigger than the trays, it sticks out around the trays.

CAN'T really just SHAKE the sifter. I got sawdust all around the box. And takes too long (and I just started using this set up two days ago, and it's one small cat) to try too sift, using the scoop to spread out along sifter faster, but kind of negates part of the reason for sifter.

YOU STILL need to just pick up the poo out of the box if you use pellets. Not a big deal for my one small cat, but it's another step.

ALSO at some point you need to disinfect the sifter. You're dumping a litter box of used and still pellets going through it. Hardly germ free and I leave it in my bathroom near her litter box.

BOTTOMLINE: I SAVED my plain old, but large, litter box. I will keep that and just use the sifter and one of the trays to dump out pellets and sawdust and separate, but that takes up more room. I am looking at getting a bigger sifting box, I see Petco has an extra large one available on Amazon. In the meantime, my small bathroom is being taken up with one large regular cat pan litter box, the sifter and one of the cat pans that came with the sifter.

BOTTOMLINE: DO NOT trust the dimensions. My cat isn't large and wasn't big enough for her. IF it had been a LARGER size (I HOPE Arm and Hammer will make one at some point), this would likely have been five stars.

title: thousand happy
text:
Easily one of the best games I have ever played and really enjoyed. As a casual fan of the series I was excited about this game. I put 23 hours on it and still play it....got the PS Vita version on the cheap too so I'd have it on both systems. I prefer this one, even though it looks better and controls better on the PS vita. I like this one better because the bottom screen is your map (and of course there's just one screen on vita) and has convenient touch control on screen so you can easily deal with camera angles---almost as nice as second stick.
This game sounds incredible with a real orchestra...I looked it up online after hearing how great it sounds. Put those headphones on and crank it up. After you advance far enough in the game and open the Venue...you can use that as a "juke box" to play all music from the game as you unlock the selections. AWESOME. A lot of love and attention to details went into making this superb game.
Tons to do...all original main story which I thoroughly enjoyed and was surprised by the ending, battle coliseum, and Transtown....lots of mini-games, fishing, bug catching, exploring, collecting. Plenty of quests are on the game without any dlc....and are replayable. The game does mark ones that have been completed. This version offers two ----yes two save slots!

Custom Words are collected phrases that are equipped and changeable that do effect abilities in battle. Example--Program Chopper with the custom words and he yells, "I'm a doctor!" while healing you in battle, the phrase itself also ups his healing power. This can add hours of depth alone and keeps you fom hearing the same phrases all the time because it also changes the phrases your character yells in battles. All spoken dialogue is in Japanese....and there is a TON of voice work even in battles
but don't worry....you get subtitles that don't intrude. Run around---town and npc speak...tap your R button when it flashes on the screen and you
respond appropriately...little things like that make for a very enjoyable time. Battles also have timed actions as well as button combos. You'll love some of the moves you pull off! Easy, medium and hard are difficulty choices you can change during the game as well.

I have nothing negative at all to say about this gorgeous, colorful, exciting game and am really impressed with it. I've only been playing video games since 1977...lol...
and this is one of my all time favorites. I think people young and old would enjoy it and even though it helps to know the characters and their history, this is a new adventure so a person who has never even heard of One Piece could enjoy this game, I think.

title: Useful for Business, School, and Travel
text:
As much as we travel in my household, we need an assortment of luggage, backpacks, and other user- friendly containers. We have several different pieces and that’s great because it means there is always an appropriate bag for the trip at hand. But one area my household lacks a little is with smaller bags and that is what convinced me to add the Solo Gramercy Rolling Case Laptop Bag to my collection.

First and probably foremost, this bag is made to hold a laptop computer and it has a separate compartment for it. I like that the laptop compartment is quickly accessible because it means that, if you take this to an airport, you can quickly remove the laptop, as you are required to do. But this is much more than a place to store your laptop computer. It is also good for carrying books, brochures, and other paper items, with large and small compartments to keep everything organized.

I sometimes take very short trips that don’t require much clothing or grooming items and I was concerned at first that this bag wasn’t designed correctly to hold such items. But in fact, it is, provided that you don’t have much. As a man, I normally don’t need to take much with me anyway and I have found that I can fit what I need for a day’s change in clothing, plus my personal grooming items, plus my laptop, all within the confines of this bag. It won’t hold much more than that, so don’t think of using this as your sole piece of luggage for a multi- day trip. There isn’t sufficient storage space in that instance, but you can get away with using it for a one or two day trip.

To help maneuver, this laptop bag has four spinner- style wheels and a telescopic handle. This makes it ideal to drag along when you’re at an airport, but I should also point out that this bag is useful even if you have no need or limited need to use it during air travel. It’s also very useful when you need to carry your laptop and school or business books and documents from place to place. It’s better than a traditional briefcase because it has more ways to organize your items.

We like and need an assortment of bags in my household because we never know where we will travel next and what we will need. The Solo Gramercy Rolling Case Laptop Bag is a useful storage bag for airport or other uses and it has made an excellent addition to our collection thus far, as it has come in handy for both travel and business uses.

title: Before you buy please keep in mind of few things
text:
Please keep in mind the service is friendly. They will take back item, but there is a 20% restocking fee. The price of sending it back and the fee does not make it worth it. You lose money either way if you wind up thinking that you will get a hard, clear, LCD screen protector and find out the only hard cover is the one that acts as a shade to the screen. Once you close that part, you don't see your LCD screen.

It's not so much the service afterwards. It's the service of not being more clear on the words and the picture before hand. I had 2 options. Either buy from another site that actually has a hard, clear, LCD screen or from this one which I've thought was that and then some. Instead the screen cover is just the flimsy sticker that everyone sells for a few bucks. Those don't stick on very well without bubbles showing up. The few tries didn't go as smoothly as one would like so it makes the screen look worse.

If you want to buy the black cover/hood, the flimsy sticker for the LCD screen and the lens cleaner all in one then this is the set for you. If you're wanting a clear, hard, LCD screen protector to protect your LCD screen and camera better, this is not the one.

The idea is to invest in something that would protect the camera better.

Yes, the items did come within estimated time. But I've found it odd that it had a sticker on there stating it's time sensitive. It took 9 days to be delivered from CA when it usually takes 4-7 days for things to get to my state.

4 stars for the courteous reply in trying to resolve the matter, but the restocking fee isn't good.
1 star in not being clear about wording and pictures that is misleading.
3 stars for the items being alright.

In no way that I'm saying this is a bad seller. Just wish some things were more clear. I want future buyers to know what they're getting unless they want to be disappointed. For those who want a clear, hard, LCD screen cover for the Sony HX200, go to that well known auction site. But it's not sold as an auction which is good.

title: My 5th Ivisor.  Grid complaints commented on.
text:
Had one for my IPAD 3, my mini, my 2 Iphones, and now one for my IPAD Air. They are great. No bubbles.

A number of one star reviews mention the grid effect. When I sold my IPAD 3, I cleaned it and did notice a grid effect when the IPAD was turned off/asleep.

title: UPDATE-Utterly RIDICULOUS- Behaved More Like Bugs Bunny Cartoon Than Pet Carrier
text:
PLEASE SEE THE UPDATE AT THE END OF THIS REVIEW FOR MORE INFORMATION.
Here is the original review...
-------------------------------------------------------------
I don't often rate things one star, because I try to think things through a variety of scenarios. I figure if it does not work for me, that does not mean it won't be great for others. In this case, however.. well, let's take a look..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This thing comes in a plastic bag. There are absolutely NO instructions, NO place listed where you can find instructions, and no way to know what the heck to do with it. It comes all soft sided folded up like origami style. You are supposed to unzip zippers and rezip it all so that it magically becomes this wonderful pet carrier. It has lots of soft mesh screening, some small plastic poles/stays on the seams which come popping out no matter what you do. There is a reinforced mat in the bottom that will fold out so that this luxurious portable pet condo can be set up and little "Fifi" can enjoy and relax feeling so comfortable with two additional screened in porches while you wait for whatever. Yeah, right.

HOW DID THIS PERFORM
After 1 hour trying to make this work and the other members of my family wondering what the heck it was supposed to be for because it was so awful, I finally got it to point where this carrier was all zipped up, nylon poles popping out, and the sides opened up like little extended screened in porches and the handles were extended. I had already tried it zipped in the basic carrier shape, now it was time to test out this expanded capability. Let's see..

I put the cat in there. Oh my god. Did you ever see those Bugs Bunny cartoons where the characters all get in a fight and all you see is a cloud with arms, legs, paws etc going around like a tornado? That is precisely what happened to this bizarre pet carrier. The thing became like it was alive rolling around the floor as our cat proceeded to try to bite, claw, and destroy the entire thing.

Picking it up by the handles was a trip. Okay, imagine a tent outside on the ground. The poles are all in place and the tent is not staked to the ground. Now imagine, putting a handle on each side of the tent and lifting it up from the handles which are attached partway up the two opposing walls. What do you think will happen? Well, that is how this behaves with the animal in it.

WILL THIS LAST?
Well, it took me 20 minutes to get the cat out of the carrier. Yes, I said OUT. She was having so much fun in destruction mode that she was like velcro sticking to this carrier. I unzipped it all that I could and I could not shake this cat out of there. Every zipper being zipped was like a play toy and I got clocked with claws thinking I was playing.

At the end of 18 minutes, I was shouting, "Get out of the stinkin carrier, you stupid cat! GET OUT!" Finally with strong force I shook her out much to my husband's delight who was now laughing so hard others were coming into the room to see what all of the laughter was about.. Yes, they laughed too.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If I didn't know better, I would think that I was on a hidden camera show given this so-called carrier to use. I think that the only animal that this would carry decently would be a small one who is two inches from death, comatose and paralyzed from the neck down. Otherwise, the carrier is unstable, impractical, and frustrating to say the least. Vets do not have 20 minutes to pry your animal from this carrier, or they will at least charge you extra for it.

MY RATING
One star. If you are going to sell something as bizarre as this, you want to have some kind of instructions with it. You also want it to be stable- isn't that the idea of carrying an animal anywhere?
---------------
UPDATE
I have amended this review, because after another 40 min of work, a bunch of us finally figured out how to make this system at least work for carrying the cat in the carrier with the sides up. It still is not stable enough but it does work better- as long as the tiny nylon poles stay in place, which they don't want to do. We could get this into the car and the cat to the vet, perhaps, but it still is a challenge to get her our out of it and it really is not very stable for travel.

The expandable sides are good if you have to wait to give the animal breathing space and room to allow her/him to still play a little while you wait. Oh who am I kidding? Our cat would have this thing in tatters within a few uses. It just isn't that sturdy.

We still can not figure out what to do with the random hook and strap which has no loop or hole to put it in. We thought it might be to hold the floor into place but we can not find anything to hook it into. It could be to hook the animal to so they can play outside the carrier, but most small animals would just drag the carrier with them. It is very lightweight. With no instructions, well, we have no clue.

I am changing my rating to three stars just because it CAN work if you really work with it. I still wish it had instructions in it which would make it better and that the nylon poles didn't pop out of place making it LESS stable all of the time. I tend to want to put this at two stars, but the others are closer to three. So, the three is really two and a half. HAHA

We should not have to work THIS hard at an item to make it work.

title: Amazfit is still the best value!
text:
I've owned and had the opportunity to try out many different brand of fitness tracker watch, from Fossil/Wear OS, to Fitbit, Apple, and many of the cheapo brands too. I've said this before, but generally you get what you pay for, aside from the Amazfit brand watches. These and the Xiaomi Mi band series always impressed me, punching way above their paygrade. This latest edition just continues that legacy.
To be clear- there are some pretty neat features and apps that Wear OS / Apple OS will offer that this won't, but for the money this is the best value and user experience.
For starters, everything about the user experience here feels premium for the money. The battery life on this is killer. I charge it about once a month, maybe 2x a month. Granted I turn off features like lift-to-wake, but my experience with Apple and Wear OS devices needed charging daily in comparison.
The display is beautiful- a very vivid OLED, with very responsive touch screen. The animations are fluid and feel premium, and the display is large enough to easily read notifications and even responses from Alexa! That being said, this model lacks the speaker that the Pro model does, so while I can ask Alexa questions, I have to read her answers. I also can't answer calls since there is no speakerphone, however I can silence the ringer if I don't want to take it.
The sensors are improved over the series 2, however the functionality is mostly the same. In fact, if you have a GTR or GTS2 already, one might argue that this is a lateral move and not necessarily an upgrade, aside from one major new feature: With the new Zepp OS, Amazfit is going to allow mini-apps that can be installed on the watch. THIS is the big thing that is missing compared to other name brand smartwatch devices. So far there are only a handful of mini apps in their "store" and arguably not anything I particularly was looking for, but there is talk of an API being released for third party developers. Who knows, maybe we'll even get some basic games or other nifty features coming soon. I still have my GTS2 which I love as well as this, but I'm holding on to this for the potential app development in the future. Can't wait to see what Amazfit does next!

title: D&D Old-Style Goodness
text:
A long time ago, Neverwinter Nights (NWN) was the official Dungeons & Dragons game for America Online. At least, I think it was America Online. It was some subscription service. Whatever.

Anyway, it was a limited game engine of sorts that used the wacky Dungeons & Dragons rules to allow people to play together online. It was revolutionary in its day.

With the arrival of this latest version of Neverwinter Nights, D&D gets a steroid boost of immense proportions in the form of a real time 3-D game engine. Sort of.

NWN is both a module creation tool and an adventure. You can download other adventures or make adventures and host them just like a "real" Dungeon Master. It's the closest thing to creating your own MUD -- and you could conceivably make one bigger than most MUDs, with up to 64 players on simultaneously at one time.

I have created an adventure but never really hosted it. The time it takes is simply too much -- it's like all the effort of writing an adventure, plus difficulties of design. Worse, the first version I got of NWN kept crashing my machine. Since the patches, it's considerably better. In fact, NWN is made to be patched as opposed to game companies pretending everything's perfect (even though they know it isn't) on release. You just hit "update" and NWN updates itself.

NWN is made for a wide range of computers, so it scales the effects. This is definitely apparent when Maleficent and I play -- by looking over at her (slower) computer, you can see a world of difference. I have particle effects from waterfalls, shadows thrown from a dozen light sources, and glittering reflections in polished surfaces. Mal...well, doesn't.

In fact, for a long time we couldn't get the game to work at all on her computer, which drove us both nuts. It turned out that the only problem was actually the graphics card -- it had a particular flaw with the FEMALE MODEL TYPE. That's right, even though the graphics card had worked in my computer previously, because Mal was playing a female sorceress (who else?), it crashed over and over. It took a lot of work, but we finally got NWN to work on both our machines.

The adventure itself is compelling and massive. The box says over 60 hours of gameplay and they're not kidding. Since Mal and I tend to scour everything bare, we really did take up the 60 hours if not more. Additionally, there was easily room for both of us to play in the universe without feeling claustrophobic. We completed separate quests and then would link back together later. Mal's meaner than I am, so her character was more neutral. I played Talien as a paladin (you're surprised by this, right?). There's no satyrs in NWN however.

That said, there is a lot of flexibility. The third-edition rules are amazingly implemented in the game engine, which is a compliment to the developers as well as the creators of the third-edition rules. The choice of races and classes are balanced well. And NWN goes further -- there are rules that enhance the game, such as level-dependent items that players can't use until they're high enough level.

The combat system works exceptionally well and even the trade system works smoothly. Characters are more or less likely to be helpful depending on how high or low your PC's Charisma stat is. If your character is really stupid, he talks funny ("Me am strong!"). And there's always the nasty and the good choice. Maleficent had the opportunity to constantly ask for more cash, whereas I tried to always do the right thing. True to form, our alignments matched our actions.

The monsters are beautifully rendered in three dimensional form, taking the static artwork from the Monster Manual to new levels. Umber Hulks never looked so terrifying. And when a dragon gets up on its hind legs and walks over to swat you like a fly, it's positively nerve wracking. Still, not all the monsters are to scale -- the dragons and giants should have been larger. There are also quite a few monsters missing. But that's okay, because there's so much to explore that you don't miss it.

Mal and I beat the game at 15th level even though there were items for 16th level characters. I suspect two people playing the game (which is meant to be played solo) ultimately end up dividing the spoils and thus advance slower. I've spoken to other people who played NWN and felt that the game's difficulty plateaued too quickly. I played NWN as a paladin along with Mal and as a elven evoker -- in both cases I died quite a lot. It may be that fighter types have an easier time of it.

There were two major problems in gameplay that cropped up, however. Like all good (and bad!) MUDs, NWN has not perfected pet code. By pet code I mean the code that allows a player to control a monster or NPC. Henchmen are available in the game, a requirement for some particularly difficult areas. Every other chapter of the adventure, henchmen would bug -- they wouldn't listen to our commands, they would repeat the same phrase over and over, they would attack friendlies (!) or they would simply not recognize the PC as their employer anymore. Given that some NPCs are critical to survive, this became a big problem when we had to permanently dump the thief in favor of a cleric we didn't need. The problem always fixed itself when we entered a new chapter of the game, because the NPCs are essentially recreated at higher levels. Still, it's extremely annoying.

Much worse were the quest bugs, another feature that often hampers text MUDs. Sure enough, many of the quests simply did not work -- NPCs who were required to finish the quests disappeared or wouldn't recognize the item given to them. Unlike the henchmen code problem, the quest bugs I was able to manually fix by going into the code with the area creator and tweaking it. So that was a surmountable, but still annoying bug.

The campaign adventure series itself is surprisingly mature for its type, involving plagues, bad choices, murdered lovers, and vengeance. While the end battle is quite climactic (it took Mal and I several days to figure out how to beat the bad guy), the narrative summary is far too brief and without any accolades. It's sort of a "yay, you won, bye" rather than a true feeling of accomplishment.

Since I don't get to play much D&D these days, this is the closest thing to it. I haven't figured out how to play with my friends over the Internet yet, but we intend to and are planning to buy the expansion adventures (all of them!).

Is NWN perfect? No. But it is a fantastic world-building tool that manages to provide a really fun gaming experience that takes me back to the old days around a table with my friends.

title: The good ol' 3.5mm jack!
text:
I'm a fan of Panasonic's electronics, and have been since I first used their GH camera line for work, and the DVX prosumer cameras before that. I was excited for a chance to replace my working headphones with ones from Panasonic, however I found it interesting that the plug type was NOT MENTIONED on this listing! The last pair of headphones + mic that I ordered came with a USB plug. It worked fine on my laptop, but not on my phone or tablet, obviously. I want a regular headphone jack, as in 1/8" or 3.5mm (whatever you want to call it!) to be compatible with all my things, and not rely on the limitations of bluetooth.
I was a little bit nervous about buying this one since it doesn't say anywhere that it is, in fact, a standard TRRS headphone-jack sized plug, but I'm happy to report that it IS! And the sound quality is what I expected from Panasonic, a good value for the price. One thing to note, however, is that this requires both sides have a wire going to the plug. This is a seriously old-school design that I almost forgot existed. Modern headphones have a single point of cable that splits to the other side in the band, however this is more like earbuds in that there's a wire going to each side.
It's not a deal breaker, it works fine and some people may actually prefer that look, but personally I'm worried about it being another point of contact that could get snagged/rip/break/go wrong, and actually prefer the more modern single-side cable style. But this is still a great pair of traditional tried-and-true headphones!

text:
These are simply outstanding! I got these for my oldest son to test out for his Youtube channel and they improved his sound by a lot. What makes these different from other $40.00 headsets?

These feel insanely well made - let me explain this, okay?
They are *nice*. The band that supports over your head is cushy soft, and the cables that allow it to suspend in place and adjust is actually metal cord. Not plastic or rubber, but metal.
The ear cups fit perfectly over the ears without squishing, and are noise cancelling. These cups are metal mesh cased on the outside, which gves it a very high end feel. The mic is clear, precise in sound, and doesn't produce popping or other peaky anomalies when speaking.
We do have other costlier headsets around, but he and I prefer these - they just fit and sound better.
The mousepad included is basic and smaller, but a nice thoughtful addition .

I was sent these by Etekcity themselves to be a product tester for them. I did not, nor do I ever, get paid to review anything. I promise nothing to anyone, except to leave a detailed review within a certain time period - good or bad, it all depends on the product. I do get lucky when I get a chance to test something nice and well made, and is actually as good as they say it is: this is one of those rare occasions.

Yes, I do recommend these with one caveat - get these for a teen or an adult.They are too upscale in build for small kids to appreciate or maintain, and the effects and details would be lost or wasted on them. title: ciube style beds always a hit in my multi cat household, stackable
text:
Cat cubes are like super posh boxes, and we all know how kitties love hanging out in a good box. I have a few of these cubes (different brands) and for the most part they are all the same, all similarly priced. This Friends Forever cube bed/house is a little shorter than some, but is otherwise same dimensions. The opening is generous, which is important for our multi (chunky) cat household.

Collapsible for times when you dont want it in use. Has a fluffy padding for exterior upper bed, and a thin soft board for use inside the cube. You can swap them, but keep in mind that the thin board-like pad is meant to provide structure. If you plan to swap, then perhaps cutting out a piece of cardboard would help give it a frame (I may do that anyway as the thin board/pad is not all that firm to keep sides pushed out). The fluffy cushion may not be enough (take note of collapsing side).

Not mentioned, but these should be stackable if you happen to pick up more than one.

I wouldnt use this as a foot ottoman, and definitely not to sit on. This is much too lightweight.

Overall it is a good cube. Since I have 3 other brands (one is an Amazon brand) I would say this is the least sturdy feeling, but it will do. If I didnt already have a lot of familiarity with these style cube beds, then I may not have noticed the extra lightweight material (lighter by about 2 lbs).

text:
While I am not going to eat it, it does look good enough to eat, because the simple, nutritious ingredients are good enough to eat. It looks like a regular can of canned meat with some additional broth and veg/fruit bits (and of course vitamins and minerals). So while I was impressed, it would take my cat food testers to give me their non opposable thumbs up, or down.

My two 17 years old elderly kittens (shh, we don't tell them differently) are primarily on wet food these days. They both prefer a more wet based canned food. So any of them that clearly have broth or gravy is going to be much more welcome than a super dry brick of pate. Price wise, the harder pates are less expensive (you just get more), and my two don't think my attempts to moisten it up with warm water or broth is palatable. SO, I buy what they want, which they tend to like for a couple of days, then in true cat fashion they want something else.

Currently, they like this brand. They may despise it come tomorrow, but at least I know it is a contender for adding to the rotation. The variety of flavors seems good for them, as they prefer chicken or fish over other protein options out there. They seem to like the pumpkin over the sweet potato, so I am glad that that is only in a few of the cans. They like the pool of broth that sits around the flaked chicken or tuna. I imagine it would make a good kibble topper if you have a cat that needs some enticement.

Not a big factor, but just something I look at. Most small tins have a full 3 oz. This is a little shy at 2.8 oz. Usually I see less than 3 oz in the packets, only. We don't like the packets as they are annoying to get food out of. So I consider this a step up from packets, but I don't like that it is a little smaller in weight than the 3 oz standard. That is 2.4 ounces less in a 12 count box. I'd like to see foods kept at same weight/amount. If you are curious of price (I don't always mention price as our working budgets and needs differ, but since I am figuring it out for my own future decisions..) That makes it $.50 an ounce, or $1.39 per can, at current price of $16.68.

Overall, two non opposable thumbs up from my cat squad. I hope this review helped you today. Take care!

title: Don't let the 'shock' in the title scare you!  You don't have to use it!
text:
These e-collars have a great minimalist design, and seem well made, the quality is great, set up was easy-peezy- just hooked them up to charge first, and we were ready to go! The fact that it's a 2-pack is what sold me, because I have 2 pups. I can easily switch between the two collars to train. I did have to quickly learn which collar was on who, when I accidentally used the remote on the wrong collar.
I have two little 'devils' that LOVE to bark. I've tried just about everything with no luck, which is when someone suggested I try e-collars. I've never used a training collar before. It's the 'shock' that scares me. I wouldn't put my pups through anything that I wouldn't put myself through, and I definitely wouldn't want to be shocked. BUT, this collar has a vibration option, which is what I was intrigued with. I've tested the vibration on myself, and I'm fine with using it on my pups.
Two gripes: I wish the straps had more 'tooth'. They loosen up too quickly and easily. I'm thinking about replacing them with nylon straps with more tooth. Also, I wish there was a stopper on the wrist strap, so that it could be secure on my wrist when I'm out training with them. I added a stopper I had lying around to it, so that I wouldn't have to worry about it flying off my wrist while training (see photos).
Overall, I'm glad I wasn't scared away from these because they are 'shock collars'. You don't have to use the shock button. I've never used it on my pups, and I really don't have to use these too often because they learned fairly quickly on these. They're a great deal for 2, especially when they go on sale!

title: As good as the OEM cable that shipped with my Note 3
text:
I wanted a spare charging cable for my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and took a chance on this one. By that I mean that that other USB 3.0 cables that I have tried with the phone would charge it, but would not support full speed data transfers and synching. This one performed without issues and identically to my OEM Samsung cable that came with my phone.

The blue outer jacket is much thicker than the Samsung cable. Although it is slightly stiffer it's also pliable and easy to bend and coil. Part of the reason for the extra thickness is probably from the the foil and braid shielding. In fact, the shielding is one factor in this cable's ability to transmit data at such high speeds without error. Another factor is the gold plated connectors.

The bottom line is this cable seems to be the equal of the more expensive Samsung OEM cable. In my experience anyway. I have owned it for three months and it has been problem free in every respect.

I don't think I will be able to stick with this one program forever, but there is enough variety that I'm still going strong after 5 months.

There are a few negatives - the trainer can be annoying, the rubber band is not particularly resistant, it's irritating to keep removing and replacing the nunchuck, and once in a while, the program fails to register movements for no apparent reason.

But the good aspects far outweigh the bad. The little pointless trophies are inspiring. The weekly and monthly goals are achievable, and if you are a bit short on calories or hours during one week of a thirty-day workout, you can easily do a custom workout to meet the goal and feel good about yourself. The routines are varied enough to prevent boredom, but there aren't so many exercises that it becomes impossible to remember how to do each one. Also, the calendar rearranges itself if a workout is missed or an extra workout is done on a rest day - good for those of us with irregular schedules.

While weight loss is a good thing, my aim with this and similar programs is just to get a bit healthier. I don't enjoy the gym, and my allergy to bees makes me afraid to spend too much time outdoors in the summer. This is the first game I've found that seems effective and is easy to keep coming back to.

title: Not fantastic but OK
text:
If you expect things to look like daylight, you'll be disappointed. It is far better than an old Russian unit I have which was an early generation light amplification unit, (green glow type). What you have here is a lot like a B&W security camera with an IR illuminator built into a hand held portable unit.

As some of the other reviews indicate, in the beginning it will seem somewhat cumbersome and clunky getting used to the controls and finding the most pleasing contrast settings. Takes a while, but once you get used to it, it gets a lot easier to make it work like you want it too.

One problem is that if you are just moving around in very low light and want to take a better look at things, it takes time for your eyes to adjust from darkness to the brightness in the viewfinder and then going back. The best way to use it is looking through it for an extended time scanning the area of interest, keeping your eye on the eyepiece. Different types of scenes will take some adjustment to optimize the appearance. Some things reflect light better than others so the best scenario is watching a particular area for an extended period. Once your eyes adjust and you get the contrast dialed in, it works pretty well. The IR illuminators are surprisingly pretty powerful. At short distances the high powered one will "wash out" what you're looking at, but it does seem to reach out pretty good. The claimed 600 feet is a bit of a stretch except under the most ideal of conditions. If you have some ambient light, I think it is better without it. But in really dark country night where you can't see your hand in front of your face, it does a great job of lighting things up.

My feelings on it are mixed. The basic idea of a monocular fits that role of "occasional use" where you want a quick better look at something, but I think that is asking too much from such a device. Plan on spending some time to get a better look at things because your eyes need adjustment time. Once you get the unit dialed in for the scene your watching, it will work pretty well. It's not cheap by any means, but it does work and it's a nice compact package. If you want really high performance night optics, plan on spending a lot more. It will definitely allow you to see reasonable well in darkness, but you have to fiddle with it. A lot has to do with the application. The pros and cons have given me some ideas about building a special purpose device.

Overall, it's a big improvement on some of the early night vision technology. The more I use it, the more I like it and learn tricks about using it effectively. I am happy with it, but for the average person with little experience with night vision, your expectations may not be met and that's why I'm giving it 3 stars. You will need a little patience to go through the learning curve using it.

title: Etrian Odyssey IV: Legends of the Titan
text:
I hadn't heard of this game, or seen any reviews, but when I saw it on the new releases, I decided to pick this up on a whim. Sometimes such impulse buying can get you burned, like the recent SimCity release. But this game is certainly not one of those.

It is a nice mix of classic dungeon crawling using some of the newest technologies. If you're not familiar with dungeon crawling, basically you start out at a base town with a few services (buy, sell, etc), and then venture into a dungeon, but there is more than one dungeon in this game.

Also similar to some of those old school crawlers, usually you can only save the game while in town. You can make restore saves, which get deleted as soon as you start playing again, and there are a few special save points in the dungeons. But if you die in this game, you won't be doing the typical save/load routine. And yes, you'll die. And probably often.

The game is a bit difficult. There are two settings, normal and easy, but I am playing it on normal. The overall story is just to go out and explore, but don't be reckless. Recklessness will ultimately harm you, as will complacency. There are even a few early encounters that (try to) teach you the detrimental effects of being complacent.

Different than many modern games, where the dungeons are side-notes and the maps are fully revealed, where you can beef up and go nuke anything that moves without worrying about dying. So don't get trapped into EZ mode thinking here.

There are a few other features in the game that make it unique:

Primarily is the mapping system. If you've played any of the classic dungeon crawl games that did not have mapping systems, you might remember the old pen-and-paper maps we'd draw as you explore the dungeons. While the game has an auto-mapper feature, it's by no means perfect. You'll use the 3DS stylus to draw walls, make iconic notes, paint water, and so on. The maps are saved even at the dreaded "game over", so that particular hard work is not lost. Get used to mapping, it's necessary, and actually quite fun and enjoyable. Get used to spinning around in a 360 degree circle, and checking to make sure there are no secrets.

Oh, how I wish we had this kind of mapping system back in the days of the Bard's Tale!

Somewhat related to the mapping system is the auto-play. You can place various movement icons on the map (left, right, up, down), and press "START", and the game will automatically move in those directions. Kinda like a macro, but not a fully automatic. You can map out a circular patrol pattern so that you can keep walking around the dungeons waiting for random encounters, without having to keep pressing buttons. I know some players will frown on such "auto levellers", but try it. It eases the grinding which seems to be inevitable in these kinda games.

Another nice feature is the content delivery system. The developer blog posts QR codes to unlock items, quests, and so on. So far, there are only two such postings, but I hope they continue doing so. You use an in-game feature to access the QR system.

Like a lot of newer 3DS games, they try to incorporate StreetPass, which is interesting, altho since I purchased my 3DS during the initial release in January 2011, I've only gotten a single Mii Plaza StreetPass tag. But I'll still hope to see if I get other tags. Apparently you can acquire new characters in this manner.

Finally of note is the music and the graphics, which are also just as good. The graphics are nicely drawn, also evoking nostalgia for hand-drawn graphics, instead of perfectly rendered 3D models. The package I picked up even had a CD of the OST; dunno if the version being sold on Amazon does as well, since it does not specifically note it.

All in all, if you like old school hack-n-slash dungeon crawling games, you'll probably like this game. If you've never played one before, why not give it a try?

title: Absolutely one of the best games of its year.
text:
A RTS citybuilder with style, Anno 1404's expansion "Venice" hits the spot. It adds more missions and cool easter eggs to the already-fantabulous 1404 base game, along with new graphics and a retooled look. Combat makes more of an appearance here, but mostly it's an economy/balance game. You play a faction seeking dominance over all the rest. You create trade routes, scout new islands, and complete missions and quests to achieve your goals. As you gain population on each island, the citizens' needs expand--peasants will start wanting exotic spices, for example, but spices can only be gotten on the Middle Eastern-themed islands, so you end up building an intertwined trade network. When you get enough citizens on an island, you can start building huge projects like a humongous cathedral or Sultan's mosque, which convey distinct benefits to the islanders living nearby. And eventually you can purchase "seats" on each island's Council, which gives you influence over the governments there--and allows you to buy an opponents island out from under him.

Being able to create automated trade routes helps enormously with the micromanaging aspect of the game, allowing you to concentrate on the important stuff. The interface is blessedly simple and the game itself delightfully free from bugs and glitches. There are long-term missions, but the sandbox mode is the most fun, with each map having a distinct number in the database (and once you find a map you like, like 39950, you can enter it into the "generator" to use it again and again). Vast replay value ahoy!

One utterly charming thing about the game is that it gives you "awards" based on both serious and lighthearted things--anything from "you sank X number of enemy ships" to "you've hit pause X number of times." The announcer also thoughtfully warns you when you've been playing for 2, 4, and probably longer hours (I'm not admitting anything) so you can, as it suggests "go get a cup of coffee." If you happen to be playing on Valentine's Day, it'll thoughtfully give you a "rose" announcement and wish you all the best.

Last, I'm not sure if I mentioned this, but the graphics on "Venice" are sheer delight. The level of detail is astounding; it almost feels like overkill. Grass waves. Ships sway while docked in the harbor. Individual citizens visit theaters, swerve drunkenly arm-in-arm home from pubs, dance around maypoles, paint huge portraits, go shopping, and talk to their friends. You can zoom in quite a ways, rotate the screen, dip and swoop behind the dolphins swimming behind your ship, make this thing do whatever you want visually. The graphics alone would qualify this game as a contestant for Game of the Year.

As someone else said, thank goodness Germans are apparently way into these kinds of games, because it means awesome titles like Anno will get made. If you're American and haven't ever heard of this (I hadn't till I signed up for a European gaming service), definitely try it. You will not be disappointed. And if you're an American game designer, please play close attention: this is the right way to do a RTS.

title: Super basic dash cam; basic setup is relatively quick; memory card NOT included
text:
[[VIDEOID:8a05ea6494b6e1be751fa342867838c]] I purchased this to replace my wonderful DOD TECH LS460W dash cam that broke and which I absolutely loved. This package includes the camera, user manual, suction mount, and car power adapter. I had to supply my own memory card, so I used the 64GB ADATA microSD card from my previous dash cam. It can take up to a 256GB card per the manual.

I've used this four about a week so far (see video) without fully completing all the setup options. My plan is to eventually set this up fully in my house by using the 12-volt DC (direct current) receptacle of my [[ASIN:B00CMP3Z4E Clore JNC300XL 'Jump-N-Carry' 900 Peak Amp Ultraportable 12V Jump Starter with Light, CEC Compliant]] so that I don't have to sit in the car in the cold selecting the available options.

I was able to use this within about 15 minutes of receiving this by not changing any defaults. After unpacking everything, cleaning my windshield behind the rearview mirror, and running through the language, date, time, and formatting the SD card, I began recording. Note that this is supposed to turn on when the car turns on. It does not do that. In fact, sometimes I have to press the power button several ties before it will come on. I do not mind if I have to press it once but rarely does the camera come on the first time. The red recording light should come up automatically. If it does not, then the record button also has to be pressed.

Below are the PROS and CONS.

PROS
- Setup is relatively easy by following the manual's instructions.

- This one has a 1080p wide-angle video image as long as that is what is selected in the setup.

- The controls are user friendly.

- The camera is compact and has a relatively thin and tiny profile.

- The camera secures tightly in the dock. I did have to turn the knob on the mount because it was originally flopping around as a result of the mount socket being loose.

- No shaking is visible in the recorded picture which surprised me.

- The power cable is extra-long so it can be routed through the headliner of the car. I cannot do this since I have a convertible.

- The camera has a loop record feature so that it overwrites the previous recordings when the disk gets full.

-There's also a G sensor option that forces emergency recording on impact. Of course the only way to know if this works is to get into an accident.

- Date and time are recorded if set. I'm not sure how it remembers the date and time when the card is turned off because it does not have an internal battery and my 12V port is not powered by my car battery when my car is turned off.

- The camera has three modes - video recording, photo (to take a still photo), and video playback (to see what you recorded).

- The camera has a motion activated feature that's for use when not in motion. This only works as long as the car is running, is hooked to a battery pack such as the JNC 300XL, or a car whose cigarette lighter does not turn off when the car is turned off and it is set.

- The camera records sound in the cabin.

CONS
- There is no GPS stamp on this which means if one gets in an accident or captures an image, the GPS location will not be known.

- There is no speed recorded.

- There is no internal battery.

- The manual does not specify how many languages are supported.

- If the 12V connector in the car does not turn off when the car turns off, it is recommended that this dash cam be unplugged or it might drain the car battery.

- Exposure to extreme heat or extreme cold reduces the lifespan of the camera (as per manual warning). I believe this is to be expected.

In summary, I wanted a dash cam that was easy to set up and was relatively cheap. I do not need all the bells and whistles such as recording when parked, in cabin recording, an on-board battery, a rear camera, wifi, etc. This one fits my needs so far due to its simplicity. The only thing I miss is the GPS and speed stamps of my other dash cam. Those I feel should be mandatory on all dash cambs. I also miss the automatic start when the care turns on as this does not work that way on my car.

I will update this review if this dash cam fails prematurely. I expect to get at least 2 years of service out of this unit. I got my other dash cam in January 2015 and it lasted until November 2021, which is almost 6 years.

title: Total War's Finest Offering
text:
2 Total War games were released prior to Rome: Total War, which set the stage for one of the best PC strategy games. Shogun, it's debut, introduced the "chess piece" movement system, cut scenes for actions, historical updates, and real-time combat; while Medieval placed those elements in a more familiar, Western location.

Rome: Total War introduced a new movement system, which determined battle locations by armies' locations on the campaign map; no more were the battle maps randomly generated according to elements in a province, such as mountains, forests, or plains. It also introduced much better graphics in both the campaign and battle maps, as well as a better interface. It also introduced religious bonuses, such as experience, population, law, and happiness received for building shrines to certain deities..

I have played Rome: Total War since 2004, and I have conquered the Romans, and Europe with most available, and some unlockable, factions. I took elephants over the Alps with Carthaginian generals; I conquered the British Isles with the Germans; and I took all the lands historically held by the Greeks. I've mastered Diplomacy in the game, though it took some adapting to v1.5's more difficult Diplomacy. And I learned how to spread the plague to enemy cities.

The Gold Edition I own is a 4 CD set, with a lengthy manual for the vanilla game, a smaller manual introducing the elements of Barabarian Invasion, and a map of the known world, showing the location of each settlement in the game. The new Gold Edition I recently purchased came with 1 DVD. Needless to say, I was disappointed with the lack of manuals and the map I use every time I play. After searching through the contents of the DVD, I found a .pdf of the manual, but no map. Though I bought my friend a brilliant game, I feel that he was cheated out of the best resources the Gold Edition had to offer.

The lack of enclosed manuals with games is a cheap stab at gamers by producers who already treat us as if we're theives, install secret software we can't uninstall (SecuROM) to ensure we're not thieves, and make shorter and less interesting games with better graphics. What good does a .pdf manual do if we can't read it while gaming? The same question applies to Online manuals and maps. We continue to pay full price for games, yet the content enclosed becomes little more than a DVD and a URL to the game manual. Because Activision is too cheap to enclose the necessary accessories to this game, which were enlosed in earlier releases, I am giving this product an average score. The game itself is a 5/5 and has yet to be bested, and I'm looking forward to Rome II: Total War.

All in all, a bit of a disappointment, I was hoping to catch the wankers who keep spraypainting my carport.

Not sure of what the range is and at least in our house, it needed to be on the same circuit breaker as the base, but this could just be weird wiring in our house.

A nice feature of the camera is a motion detection feature, so you don't end up with hours of blank unmoving street view for example. For the recording, pretty much continuously, it takes about 2GB per night (this is with camera on from about 9pm to 8am). There is a way to look at the recorded footage in super fast motion, so it takes about five minutes to watch the entire night's events (use VLC);'oh, hello again, curious kitty who keeps hanging out on my porch.'

This is not an outdoor camera, but we are using it outdoors anyways (tried placing it near a window, but glare of light on the window blinded the camera). I don't have any need to record stuff indoors. Because of the camera we caught a strange creepy person coming up to our house while we were out yesterday, they also visited the houses of two of our neighbors. If not for the camera we wouldn't have known about this. There are a lot of strange characters in our neighborhood and there have been a few incidents; nothing major, a crazy woman tried to break in while we were eating dinner, a man with dementia was wandering around our bridge, kids stealing wood from our woodpile, you know, ordinary disturbances, so this person was exactly what we wanted to see while we weren't home.

The software allows for up to nine cameras to be in use, I can't even imagine that, but it might be cool to have another to watch our backyard, we might be able to catch the raccoons or the river otter who we've only gotten fleeting glimpses of.

title: Feed me, Seymour?
text:
I played through the first Halo and really enjoyed the single-player campaign. I never played the multiplayer game until I bought Halo 2.

Let's get this out of the way first: Halo 2's multiplayer is unparalleled. With a multitude of multiplayer games (Capture the Flag, Juggernaut, Team vs. Team, etc.) and a dizzying variety of terrains, there's plenty to keep Halo fans busy blowing each other up. The addition of the alien Elites as a playable character spice things up. You can also wield two weapons at a time, one in each fist, providing another combat option for those gunslingers that like their battles John Woo-style.

Unfortunately, Halo 2's single-player campaign is not as impressive. To whit, the alien Covenant's entire society is based on the idea that activating the giant rings throughout the universe (known as Halos) will put them on their journey of spiritual evolution. The reality is that Halo is a weapon designed to destroy the Flood, an infestation of aliens who turn human and alien alike into vicious zombies. And how do you keep the Flood from infecting every living thing? Why, by utterly destroying every living thing in the universe of course!

Play alternates between Master Chief and the alien elite known as the Arbiter. This gives the player both sides of the story, which is interesting...to a point. Eventually, the plot converges enough so that the two characters should really end up fighting each other. That would have been something, if the AI made you play through both battles from opposite sides by creating an enemy that uses your own moves.

But instead, about midway through the battle for the universe, a giant plant that looks like Audrey II from Little Shop of Horrors shows up. This planet, speaking in Jabba-esque guttural tones, rams the plot down our throats by grabbing the Arbiter and Master Chief and shoving them into opposite plot lines: the Arbiter ends up working with the humans, Master Chief ends up doing the alien dirty work.

Then things really get going, and just as Halo 2 hurtles towards the final battle on Earth...the game ends. I should have guessed something was up when, during E3 interviews about Halo 3, the CEO of Bungee only had this to say: "Are you ready to finish the war?" What he meant was, "Are you ready to finish the game you thought you were finishing in Halo 2?"

As you've probably noticed from my review of the second installment of Pirates of the Caribbean, I really, really, REALLY hate movies and games that fail to provide a whole story. It doesn't matter that this is part two of a three-part series. Writers and developers have an obligation to provide a full story; you CAN create a story with a beginning and end even though it's the middle of a series, as evidenced by The Two Towers.

Halo 2 is an improvement on the original, but it loses points for a weak campaign that forces you to play both sides, then throws in a talking plant to clean up the mess.

title: Great fun and replay value
text:
Let me preface this by saying I've never understood the "minigame" concept. I've never played games like Super Smash Bros. before. In my GameCube days, a multiplayer game was something like Mario Golf, Mario Kart or Mario Tennis. I didn't really have any inclination to think I would enjoy Rayman Raving Rabbids, but I had been reading so many great reviews saying that this was THE game to get for the Wii.

So I picked it up, and it's probably my favorite Wii game right now. The biggest thing about it that I enjoy is the humor. Many of the games aren't particularly engaging by themselves, but the way they are presented to you is hilarious. The behavior and especially the sounds for the Rabbids are hysterical.

The single player game is in the format of a gladiatorial arena. In the opening sequence of the game, Rayman is captured by the Rabbids and thrown into a coliseum-like stadium in front of a crowd of jeering Rabbids. You're presented with five doors, one of which is locked until you beat at least three of the other challenges. The challenges generally fall into four categories ranging from precision (requiring you to have good control of the remote/nunchuk) to dancing (where you have to shake the controllers along with the beat of a song to inspire Rabbids to dance). If you beat three challenges, you unlock the middle door that leads to the "boss" level, which is usually either a shooter or a race. If you complete all four challenges, you also unlock a song or costume option. After you beat the "boss" level, you get "escorted" back to your cell where you can change costumes, listen to the music you've unlocked, review and replay the series of challenges you just played, and even plot your way out of the evil Rabbids' clutches.

Once you start completing challenges in the single-player game, you can go back to play them in a challenge mode to try and get the best score in a single-player mode or play up to 4 players in a variety of vs. or co-op modes. After each game in this mode, you're presented with a web code that you can enter at Ubisoft's Rayman website that enters you into the world rankings. My one gripe with this is, why doesn't the game simply contact the Rayman site directly if an internt connection is available? It's a big hassle to write down the code, then run into the other room where the computer is to enter the code. Luckily for me I have a laptop, so I can have the laptop open right next to me, but that's not always practical for everyone.

The minigames (and there are about 100 or more of them) themselves are generally very short... no more than 2-3 minutes or so for the longest ones, with some of them being under 15 seconds (though the shorter ones are typically the ones that require more control, so they're a bit harder, and you'll probably try them over and over again). Each one has a clever title, like "Bunnies don't know what to do with cows" on a mission where you have to twirl a cow above your head on the end of a chain and throw it for distance. Some of the games are actually physically exhausting... after playing a few of the missions your arms will feel like Jell-O.

For someone who originally had no interest in the "minigames" genre of video games, I really love this game. Whenever someone comes over or we take the Wii with us somewhere, we generally pull out Wii Sports first, just because it gives people a chance to get the hang of the Wii controllers, but then we switch to Rayman and the real fun begins.

title: Lotus Spring, how does your garden grow?
text:
"The Legend of Lotus Spring" is the first game from Women Wise, a feminist group dedicated to producing quality games that appeal to a female gaming audience. "Lotus Spring" is more of an interactive exploration than a game per se: there are really no puzzles, no mazes, and no missions other than exploring the now-extinct Garden of Perfect Brightness in 19th century China. You play as Emperor Xian Feng and are searching for your love, the concubine HeHanQu, who, as a Han woman, was forbidden from marrying the Emperor, and the jealousy of the Dowager Empress CiXi proves formidable as she sends HeHanQu, or Lotus Spring, to an island in the middle of the garden. But Lotus Spring has disappeared and now you must find her....
"Lotus Spring" is filled with history and touches of now-vanished imperial China under the Qing dynasty. As you explore the many sights and locations in the Garden of Perfect Brightness you will stumble upon shared moments between the Emperor and Lotus Spring, many of which are poignant. Although not essential to winning the game, there are several exploration-type activities which are quite fun, including trying out various traditional Chinese musical instruments, brush painting, and more. Along the way you run across various animals and insects, although, much like Myst, there are no other people to interact with. The style is very similar to Myst, in a first-person point-and-click slideshow.
The pros:
+ Beautiful graphics that bring imperial China to life: intricate jade sculptures, bonsai, Chinese silks and dresses, dim sum picnic lunches, ancient musical instruments...
+ The originality and depth of the story
+ A touching love story
+ Exploring the reconstructed garden and the numerous pavilions, temples, shrines, etc. as well as the garden itself
+ Access to the lovers' shared dreams and entries in a diary
The only gripes that I have with "Lotus Spring" are:
- The music is too repetitive
- The doll cursor is annoyingly cute and overly large
- The pace may be too slow for seasoned gamers
Women Wise has also commissioned a novella based upon the real historical events that inspired "Lotus Spring"

title: Great litter for picky cats
text:
We use oko cat litter, the super soft natural wood. I love the bigger pellets of pine but our cat, little miss particular, started to pee around the house so we had to switch back to a smaller and finer litter.

This corn based litter is super similar to the oko wood, it is soft and almost powdery, like the clay litter my cat preferred before we made the switch to a biodegradable, evironmentally friendly litter. It doesn't have any artificial scents and it mixes well with the small amount of silica litter we mix in for odor control.

I can't tell the difference between this and the oko wood litter.

But here are the downsides;

It tracks like crazy! I sweep every flipping day. I use a litter map and I trimmed the hair on my floofball cat and we still have bits of littter all over house. The oko cat did too and the only way to stop the tracking was to switch back to the pine pellets (and learn to live with my cat peeing on furniture and laundry), no thanks.

It costs more than the litters at the store.

On the plus side;

1. My cat likes it. We spent $600 at the vet trying to figure out why my cat kept peeing on my son's bed, on the laundry, in the sink and it turned out she hated the pine pellet litter!

2. No dust.

3. No masking perfumes. I am perfume sensitive and the fragrance was just killing me.

4. You don't need a special litter box to use this.

title: It charges alkaline...  but mostly, it's an excellent Ni-MH charger.
text:
More than anyone, I really wanted alkaline charging to work like other rechargeable batteries but the sad reality is that they're just not made for it.

The reality of alkaline charging:
- Duracells seem to leak more than cheapo "Kirkland" brand from Costco.
- Energizers do not hold charge very well.
- All brands leak eventually.
- Takes a long time to charge.
- Unreliable even if successfully recharged -- usually, batteries are connected in series, which means that if one fails, the device will not work.
- Battery leak can happen while charging or while being used in the device, resulting in a very messy charger and messy device.

So after some dumpster diving (or at least, I raided the battery recycling bins at work), I came home with batteries of various brands. For a while, I really did use recharged alkaline batteries exclusively and kept my Ni-MH batteries in the drawer. What I found was that I needed to change the batteries a lot more often and I couldn't be sure that the battery would have a charge when I took it out of the drawer.

Leaking is a big problem. My charger now has one charging port that is stuck because the liquid got in to the spring mechanism and dried. I also have a couple of remotes and devices that had to be cleaned out because the batteries leaked.

In the end, I had to give up on the idea of recharging cheap alkaline batteries because of how long it takes to recharge and that it can leak at any time, potentially ruining your device (mostly, it's just oily and you need to clean it out with a tissue). I just couldn't trust those batteries.

So why did I still give this charger 5 stars? Although alkaline charging was a failed experiment for me, the charger is still a better-than-average Ni-MH battery charger. It has separate intelligent charging and LCD display for each battery and will trickle charge a battery even after the lights turn green. Other chargers that have the same features cost more -- and without the Alkaline charging capability. You really can't go wrong with this charger.

title: Speedy, Lightweight SSD External Drive
text:
I like tech. I've had a computer since the commodore Vic-20 came out. That being said I'm not into competing with or against other computers and computer users. I don't run testing or speed diagnostics on my hardware. If it works and feels or seems to be working as advertised and expected I'm completely happy. I just don't care to sit here are see how many micro-seconds faster my new drive is than my older ones.
All that being said I use external drives exclusively for maintaining backups of my personal files, photos, documents, music, eBooks, Etc. Everything else I can simply reinstall in a couple hours. I don't have that many things installed. My computing needs are simple. But I have lost files due to a drive crash so I meticulously make weekly backups of my important files. Currently I've been using two USB 3.0 Seagate Backup Plus drives to make my backups every Monday.
This new Samsung solid state drive is remarkably faster at copying files to than my mechanical drives and easily a quarter the size and weight of the Seagate drives. I had a couple hiccups when I first formatted the drive to NTFS (I had no need of proprietary encryption) and started copying my files over to the drive but after one or two false starts I got tens of thousands of files copied over with no more problems and have for several weeks just copied new files to the existing collections in their directories and once again this SSD drive flies through the process much faster than the Seagate drives. Now I have three complete backups of my files and feel that much safer and secure with three copies of my files and I love that there's no moving parts. The cable's long enough, about eighteen inches, to work fine with my laptop though someone with a desktop may want to invest in a longer cable.
I'm knocking one star off for a device this expensive not coming with even a cheap hard shell case or even a rubber plug to protect the USB port from dust. It's the one point of possible entry of foreign matter into the drive and causing damage or failure. For the price they're currently charging it wouldn't have been any real hardship to include a case or plug to protect this device.

title: I'm officially a hit with my sons! They love these headphones.
text:
I was looking for stocking stuffers for my two teenaged boys. Both had expressed an interest in the Beats by Dre. I don't know about you, but I was looking for a reasonable pair of headphones to accompany other high priced gifts (new Xbox, Laptop etc) they were getting for Christmas. BUT paying almost $200 for the Beats seemed unreasonable. So when these (V-Moda, Crossfade LP) were highlighted on Amazon on Black Friday, I seized the opportunity and purchased two pair (which was still cheaper than one pair of Beats), and hoped that I could rely on the reviews that I read. (Please note that I did read reviews for Beats, and found that the V-Moda pair received more positive reviews.) So with both sets of reviews under my belt, I begin to compare the features and was even more convinced that I had made a wise purchase. (Also note that later my sons were able to compare them with the Solo Beats by Dre and they still liked the Crossfades better.)

Features that my sons say make these a standout amongst most headsets:
* The overall sound quality is great and not too bass heavy.
*The over the ear covers (ear piece) have memory cushions. They are very comfortable and you can't hear outside noise (Of course I found this to be true when they could not hear me calling them. Of course, they may be ignoring me). I also can't hear the music that they are listening to.
* The volume or pause feature can be used from a control button on the cord. They even say that besides skipping songs, the rarely have to touch their devices when using these headphones.
* These earphones are versatile and can be used with multiple devices (i.e., the computer, Ipod, cell phones, etc). They are able to even use them in the car by connecting with the stereo.
* These headphones are stylish and attractive. I ordered one pair in Phantom Chrome and the other in Phantom Black.

And finally, what Mom likes about the headphones...well, the price. These headphones were reasonably priced and offered the same features as the Beats. And later when I compared them with the Beats, they appear to be better quality in terms of sound quality and workmanship (the Beats are plastic looking and don't seem to be as well constructed as the Crossfade, which seems sturdy).
Finally, overall for the money I think I got a top notch product. I highly recommend these to anyone on the market for some headphones and give this product five (5) stars.

title: A Rather Decent Monopod
text:
The Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod is basically (pardon the pun) everything you need in a monopod. It extends to a nice height and even at full extension it feels reasonably sturdy. Collapsing the thinnest section and using just the two thicker sections increases the stability greatly and still gives you a little over 51 inches to work with.

Build quality is decent. The locking cams are hard plastic but don't feel cheap and give a positive, tight lock when engaged. The foam grip isn't glued into place. It is just held in place by friction and the three screw heads that hold the camera mount to the monopod.

The monopod also includes a wrist strap held in place on the head of the mount by a split ring.

A carry bag is supplied. It's enough to protect the monopod though it's not padded and the shoulder strap is short enough to be more of a carry strap.

The rubber foot of this monopod can be retracted on its threaded mount to expose a metal spike foot for use in outdoor.

The only negatives I've found with this monopod are:
The wrist strap is rather small and I cannot fit it over my hand. For reference I wear a size large glove. For me this is more of a palm strap.

The soft foot has very little rubber extending past the end of the metal spike. I measured this at just slightly over 1mm. Moderate wear will surely leave the metal foot expose and potentially damage flooring.

All in all though this is an affordable and well built monopod and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.
