title: Casts a nice large soft lighting circle
text:
Anyone in photography will tell you that the bigger the light source, the better the light. Hard small harsh lights are the worst in regards to shadows and contrast, and make terrible eye reflections of the light. Ring lights are popular because they spread a more even and therefore softer glow, and have those signature round eye catch lights. But a GIANT ring light like this one? Makes a good thing even better!
I was playing around with it tonight, but in the effort of keeping my family private, I used a Darth Vader helmet as my subject to share. Pictures are labelled, one without the ring light as a control, then using it to create a side light and then again as a front light, and then a practical example of using it to cast a soft light on a scene (my kid playing- face edited out obviously).
I like that this light comes with a camera mount as well as a cell phone holder, and especially that it can run on either battery OR plug in power. In fact, it even comes with 2 Sony camcorder batteries to power it! It only comes with one charger, so thankfully I already have other chargers for that type of battery around my house as it appears to require both to be used at once (so charging them one at a time is very annoying). I wasn't expecting the batteries so I'm pleasantly surprised and would not deduct any stars from an otherwise fantastic product!

title: Don't Waste Yo' Time on Hillbilly Trash
text:
Played this at a friend's house. We sampled our way through this lame game. First there's the main line of play and that's when you take on the character of Willie's son John-Luke. You have perform certain quests to become a full-fledged Duckman. Quests like playing pranks on your family at the Office, racing Fan Boats in the Swamps, Catchin' Frogs, and Callin' Ducks with the Family's Famous Duck Calls. There's even a strange quest where you have to search for your Uncle Si's lost treasures with a metal detector. And those treasures can be from the usual to the bizarre. When I go detectin' I find coins, rings, beer and soda-pop cans, bottle caps, pull-tabs, rusty nails, and hopefully lockboxes. Lockboxes are always interesting 'cause you never know what you'll find hidden away. Could be lots of coins, jewelry, money, or maybe those family secrets they've been keeping all these years - like what's been in the news these past few years; especially child molestation, preaching hate, and you have to wonder why Phil does that; perhaps Phil and Si had a bit of explorin' with the other when they were teens.

Gameplay - the usual, but I get tired of hearin' these good ol' boys draggin' they lines like dey nevuh went fer schoolin'. It gits old. And it's stupid. The races are fun, but over fast. Then there's the killing of frogs, which I do not condone. Bullfrogs are a part of the swamp's overall ecology. They are put of nature's food chain, helping control insect populations, and in turn are food for large birds and reptiles (like snakes). Frogs don't hurt anyone, nor the environment. Sure they might have tasty legs, but Duck's are too.

Overall - it's stupid. Plus it appears that the game was created just to make money off the television show's many fans. Created a bit too quickly me thinks. This could have been a much better game if they had concentrated on the Family Business and Ducking Calling and Hunting. But how can you make an entertaining game out of that? Instead they built a game on hillbilly tasks, and it makes you wonder why a multimillionaire family dynasty would rather do that (the hillbilly way), then spend their money on the real thing. A Hillbilly Waterpark? Take you kids to a real one; you can afford it. A vacation at home? Take your family to Orlando and it's world famous Amusement Parks; you can afford it. And lastly, when you think about how they're portrayed in the game as your every day backwoods Bible toting, Jesus lovin' family, preaching God's good will by setting an example, you have to wonder why Phil preaches hate in his spare time.

title: Not a holodeck, a holo-phonebooth. Still plenty cool.
text:
I’ve given it a couple days, and I’ll try to keep it short.

Yes: It’s amazing. VR is amazing. if “being in a game” appeals to you as a concept, you will love it. I’ve only had short stints with the Vive and Oculus; but it doesn’t take long to figure, this is the best headset – when it tracks right. It’s by far the most comfortable, and with the best screen, resolution be damned. Black levels are great, colors pop nicely, and the lack of “screen door” is huge. The other two are sharper, but always look like LCD screens. 1080p isn’t great, but this headset is. Except for headphone issues, it’s perfect – while seated, or standing in ONE place.

Meh: cables, welcome to cable hell, there’s no way to make this orderly while in use (Neat people may hate). PS camera cable is only 6ft – boo. So it goes, first-world-problems right?

Nope: the tracking is not adequate. Take more than a step in any direction, jitters; extend your arms too far, jitters; turn around, jitters. Everyone who uses this with a Move game will exceed the limits of the tracking within moments. As soon as you become enthusiastic enough to test the limits of the move (by moving), it fails. You do learn the “rules” of where you should hold your limbs, so they can play nice with the sensor range, but this is the opposite of immersion. The interface doesn’t “transport” your arms they way it does your eyes. You can’t count on it to work, so basically any standing game that requires reflexes is likely a no-go with the move [I’d love it if I had to eat those words]. Note that all the real games such as: Rigs, Eve, or Drive Club (i.e. not “experiences”) are using the dual shock.
The PSVR achieves VR visually, but not physically – the tracking sinks that.

Sony selling this in a bundle without move controllers isn’t about you already having them (you don’t, they know you don’t). It’s because the PSVR does not REQUIRE them (hint here). The good games, that we might get, when we’re sick of being batman, will likely not use them. Aside from not being batman you’ll probably be fine without them. Sit down man.

So here it is: VR is awesome, it looks great. The level of immersion will probably exceed your expectations. However, all the wild, amazing games of your VR dreams (Lightsabers!, boxing!, Fruit Ninja!) will either miss this generation of PSVR, or suck a butt.

The games are pretty good, but that’s a different review.

Also: I have a surround sound set up, and I just use that instead of headphones. It’s fine.

title: Precise, but has a learning curve
text:
I received a review sample and after I got this up and running there was a slight learning curve before it felt natural. After I did become accustomed to it, going back to a regular mouse was a slight letdown.

While the instructions are a bit terse I am still giving this four stars because it's easy to set up. The subtracted star is for lack of clear explanations in the quick start guide for how to precharge the unit or even for explaining that the retractable USB cable that ships with it is only for charging and will not connect the mouse interface to the host system.

This mouse operates wirelessly via an included dongle. My old ThinkPad running Windows XP immediately recognized the dongle when I plugged it in, and the mouse as soon as I inserted the included battery and charged it up.

Once I became comfortable with the mouse I found that it was a lot more precise for graphics applications and games than a regular mouse. Note that the base is fixed to the pen-style handle. You move it as though it's a pen affixed to a sled. After you become accustomed to the buttons and the wheel placement you will be using this like a pro.

There is a LED on the top of the unit that shows the charging state. Once that light turns green you can disconnect the USB charging cable. I initially did not like this feature, but have grown to love it because the battery is rechargeable. Other wireless mice I have used in the past seemed to have a voracious appetite for batteries, so plus one for the rechargeable feature.

Bottom line: this is an excellent mouse that is less stressful than using a normal one. Set-up is a bit confusing, but if you have issues leave questions in a comment to this review and I will answer them to the best of my ability. If the company redesigns the documentation to make it clear to complete novices this would be a five star product.

title: Perfect Way To Protect Myself From The "Little Darlings"
text:
Everyone thinks their dogs are wonderful. Some people even feel they can do no wrong. As the landscape of our area has continued to change, people are moving in and out. That means new dogs.

Going for a walk can be a challenge. I had stopped trying for a while until I got this.

SIZE
The size of this tool is pretty good. It fits in the hand, hangs from the belt and has a handy wrist strap too. It is not too hard to grasp except with perhaps a slick glove in cold weather.

OPERATION
This works very well. The first button emits a siren, but it is not ear piercing. This is good for dogs that you need to startle in more than one way suddenly.

The 2nd button is for the high pitched ultrasonic noise that will stop dogs, but humans don't hear it. This is great for those dogs in your area that would be offended if the owners knew you were using something on their dogs.

The 3rd button is flashlight. It works well..

CHARGING
I found that this took a couple of hours to charge up, but it works quite a long time before recharging. Well, of course, that is because I only have to use it once in a great while. More use will run it down faster.

WHAT I USE THIS FOR
I use this for a combination of going for walks and my own yard. I have a yippy dog next door which kills rabbits and other small animals. I want him out of our yard, and usually he stays out. However, if he starts barking and coming over here, I use the silent mode. His owner does not know and I am happy.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is handy to have. It has made my walks more friendly again and my yard happier too. It helps avoid neighbors who get worked up if you use something against their little darlings.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I love that this is rechargeable and I love how portable it is. I have a new confidence in going for walks again.

title: Great when new, but it won't last.
text: This was a great joystick when I first got it.  The buttons are good, springs were good, the software is pretty good, physically it's very sturdy and it feels solid.  The problems started after a few months of use.  I started getting dead spots, drift and it sometimes didn't return to center in the games I played (physically it was centered, but the flight sim didn't think it was.) The bottom line is that by using pots (old style variable resistors) instead of Hall Effect sensors this joystick has a limited lifespan.  When the pots wear out or get dirty it's done.  I'd say 1 year of heavy use is a good estimate.  You simply can't expect pots to last too long when you are constantly moving them for hours a day.  They are really meant for occasional adjustment to volume and such in radios and TVs not for being hammered by continuous movement in a joystick.  Hall Effect sensors don't suffer this problem because there is no physical contact between the moving parts.  They use magnetic induction to determine the stick position.  So, save yourself some money and get a Hall Effect joystick like the Thrustmaster T-16000M Flight Stick or go big and get an all metal one like Thrustmaster Hotas Warthog, Replica Split Throttle System.  I'm not pushing Thrustmaster, but they seem to be the only company selling Hall Effect sticks now that Microsoft isn't making joysticks anymore.

title: Quality Soft Dog Food, Perfect as a Topper

Dogs love to eat but as pet owners, we are concerned about what we feed them. I know how much my dog loves soft, meaty food but much of what is sold on the market isn’t good at all, often loaded with chemicals, preservatives, and by- products. But there are some good soft foods and one of them is Nutro Pate Steamed Chicken and Turkey Recipe.

Packaged in small containers, Nutro Pate Steamed Chicken and Turkey Recipe has 100 grams of food per serving. This is too small to feed a large dog like mine, so I use it instead as a topper for his dry food. He devours it with abandon, as most any dog would. The meaty flavor is very much to his liking and it gets him to finish eating his dry food- something he is not always excited to do.

Like I said, the ingredients are part of the reason I try to avoid soft dog foods, but this one is easily better than most. Chicken is the number one ingredient, plus the food is free from GMO and contains no artificial colors or preservatives. I also like the easy to serve trays. You just peel off the top and serve. This is much better than canned dog foods, many of which require a can opener. And since the serving size is only 100 grams, it’s just right for a single serving. A can is often too much food, but this serving size is perfect for using as a topper.

Soft dog food should generally be avoided, but it is fine if the food is made with quality in mind. Nutro Pate Steamed Chicken and Turkey Recipe is definitely a quality, soft dog food and its meaty qualities are certain to be a hit with most any dog.

title: This Tablet Does What I Need It To
text:
As an old, retired guy, I find technology still significantly impacting my daily life in two ways. The first is that I spend a lot of time every day online - either gaming in my favorite MMO or binge watching the various streaming services. The second way is that I keep in touch with my far-flung network of family and friends via social media. Now, my desktop pc handles the first of those two very nicely. The problem is that I can get immersed for hours in gaming or in a good streaming show. Social media notifications break that immersion, causing me to move away from whatever I was doing to see what the latest notice was about. If I don't, it could be quite a while before I get around to checking my social media and responding to the messages there.

This is where a tablet comes in. I figured it would be nice to have a tablet that quietly beeped new notifications and allowed me to just glance over at the latest notice to see if it needed a quick response or not. Little did I know how hard it would be to find a low end tablet capable of that simple task. This is the fourth tablet I've tried and the first one which could do that one simple thing for me. The other low end tablets quickly crashed and burned for a variety of reasons. This is the first that actually continued to work after the first few days, giving me the notifications I wanted and that I could check out at a glance.

There are some issues with this tablet that folks should be aware of. The sound is tinny enough that I wouldn't listen to music or audiobooks on this thing. The visual quality is sufficient for modern movies and tv shows but vintage ones do look a bit fuzzy. The charge doesn't last quite as long as I'd like it to. The tablet needs to be charged twice a day, even when it's just sitting there beeping when a text message or email comes in. Charging once a day would be nicer but it is what it is. Still, this is the first low end tablet of four I've tried that actually does the simple task I want it to do. So for that, I have to give it a solid 4 star rating.

If you are unsure of which protector to choose for your Switch, I'd say you can't go wrong with Orzly. They make some of the thinnest protectors, and they're scratch proof. For the first attempt I tried the tape hinge method seen in various places on YouTube. That didn't work so well for me. I ended up having to reposition it, so I peeled it off and moved it a little, only to find a piece of dust trapped under it. I then tore it off and trashed it since cleaning both the screen and inside of the 1st protector seemed nearly impossible. I don't think you're actually supposed to use an alcohol wipe on the inside of a protector, and in any case I only had 1 more wipe. I moved on to the next attempt and simply eyeballed it as I set it down. I found that when I set it down the entire underside was still not adhered (i.e. it was all one big air bubble), so I could still shift it around a little to be perfect. I did this and then pressed down in the center to start the adhesive / bubble removal process. In the end I'm satisfied but this could've easily been a 1-star product if they hadn't included two protectors, or even if I couldn't do it in two tries. title: Amazing series and definitely worth your time (and money)!
text:
Sort of an interesting "game" to review, given that for its price, especially if you are new to Halo (kind of hard to believe given that I have loved Halo for the last 13 or so years). As for the content you get Halo: CE with both original/remastered graphics, Halo 2 with both original/remastered graphics, and both Halo 3 and Halo 4 in their original graphics. All are in 60 fps at 1080p if your screen supports it. As you play through, the graphics in 1 and 2 are beautiful, as well as 4 (even though techincally the remastered graphics of 2 are now better than 4's, I prefer the graphics in 4 the most) and then there is 3...On a straight play through if you continue through the games, you may find Halo 3 from a graphical stand point to be left behind, given that it has a major drop out as it has not received the HD graphic overhaul the first two have had. Other than that you can play solo/co-op on all missions, and ALL skulls are available for use out of the box. Additionally, terminals are now hidden and available for achievements in all 4 games and skulls are hidden for achievements in the first three games. Guaranteed the nostalgia and butterflies you will re-experience as you go through the iconic moments in the early Halo games will be worth the money alone.

Additionally you will get access to the Halo 5 multiplayer beta from Dec 29-Jan 18th, which I am definitely looking forward to. You also get free access to watch Halo Nightfall, which is still be released progressively. It details the journey of Agent Locke who will be a major hitter and likely playable character in next year's Halo 5: Guardians. It is very well done from the episodes I have watched thus far, a better series in my opinion than Forward unto Dawn was.

Lastly, you get the multiplayer. Despite what many of complained, and complained...and complained about, they are fixing the online play. Since getting the game on Black Friday, I have had only one problem getting into an online match, and that was before the last 3 updates which have majorly improved play. Now I don't have to wait anymore than I do for Halo matches back on the 360. Many of the maps are either true to their original forms in 1-4, or they have been updated and modernized. Its a real throwback getting to play some of the maps, like Lockdown, from Halo 2 any old fan will instantly feel at home in. Currently the only ranked matches are Halo 2, but they are updating every few days.

The controls now, are a major learning curve, at least as I found. I still have a hard time remembering that I can't just sprint in 1-3, lol, often resulting in death. They do have a controller setting, I forget the name off hand, that you can set so that the controls remain the same through all 4 games, which makes it vastly easier, given that until 3 you won't have any useable items like the pop-up shields or grav-lifts, and you won't have armor abilities until you play on 4 (which I believe means you won't use X or left bumper till 3 or 4). Makes for more smooth game transition and only a quick glance at what game you are playing, depending on the play list.

If you are worried, the campaign alone is worth it, but if you are only in it for the multiplayer, it is far to difficult to tell if it will work for you specifically.

Lastly, the game does require 90gb, at least for the digital download version, I'm not sure about the disc version. It took me forever to download the entire game (most of 2 days and based on my download speed, it shouldn't have actually taken more than 1.5 hours...). So be sure you have good internet and time on hand before you play. The multiplayer will also have 4+ updates you will now need before even jumping online, though they might all be combined for first timers now.

See you online!

title: A design flaw of the keyboard is a huge problem
text:
I am making these comments as a non-gamer. It may be that this keyboard is made specifically for gamers and not meant to be used by anyone else. However, I have owned for some time another brand of gamer keyboard that I use regularly, and it doesn’t have the design flaw that this keyboard does.

Pros

1. It's appearance is attractive, especially the fact that it lights up in blue when plugged in.

2. This keyboard comes with a mouse, and the mouse is also very attractive. It lights up in blue and red when plugged in.

3. This keyboard is both full size and compact in design.

4. The price is reasonable.

Cons

1. A design flaw of the keyboard is a huge problem! I have been typing on a computer keyboard for 40 years. And on every keyboard I have ever used, the Enter key is one key to the right of the Single-Quote/Double-Quotes (“Quote”) key. When you want to press the Enter key, you simply lift up your right pinky finger and move it over one key. Inexplicably, this keyboard includes an extra key between the Quote key and the Enter key! I cannot state strongly enough how enormous a negative this is. There may be some reason for gamers to have a keyboard designed this way, but the keyboard is useless for everyone else. It is simply unusable to me. As a touch typist, the first time I used it, I reached my finger to hit the Enter key and was shocked when nothing happened. I wasn't looking at the keyboard, and for several additional, frustrated taps, I tried again and again to engage what I naturally assumed was the Enter key. Then I looked at the keyboard, and I couldn't believe my eyes. I was hitting an alien key between the Quote key and the Enter key.

Why would anyone design a keyboard this way? If I tried to train myself to use this keyboard, I would quickly develop repetitive stress injury. It is much too far for my pinky to comfortably stretch to reach the Enter key.

Again, this keyboard may be designed specifically by gamers for gamers. But if you are not a gamer and just are looking for a glow-in-the-dark keyboard for a reasonable price, I highly recommend that you look elsewhere.

title: It's okay if you buy it cheap.
text:
This game is okay, if you buy it cheap. It's extremely linear, with not much of a story. It has some interesting things going for it, and a lot of bad. The game appears to be an open world, but it's not. It appears to be big, but there is really not a lot of things going on it. If your expecting Skyrim, run fast and far away.

The game has a ton of bugs in it. My favorite is water skiing off a mountain into water, and then drowning. I must have performed that move 20 or 30 times before I stopped going near ledges. Do not go near a ledge, or prepare to water ski off a ledge I drowned in a foot of water once, that was special. You think the game developers could have taught the bastard to swim! Another fantastic bug is when you got up close and personal fighting something, and your character goes into an epileptic fit. Your weapon gets put away, comes out put away, etc. The only way to fix this was to move away, then re-attack. The game had a lot of potential, but it's almost like the game company ran out of money and did as little as possible to finish it. Weapons and items were okay, nothing exciting. Anything worth buying cost way more money than you had. Here are a few Pros and Cons, which hopefully will help you make up your own minds on whether to purchase the game.

Pros:
1) Like a normal RPG, you can level up various skills throughout the game.
2) You can play as a fighting, magic using, or mixed skills character.
3)The world is gorgeous in places, including how they rendered the ocean.
4) Using magic is fun and looks cool.
5) Shooting enemies with a range weapons looks cool.
6) The way some of the enemies blend in with their surrounding is nice. Especially the Panthers. Though that's in the DLC.

Cons:
1) The area seem large, but there isn't really a lot going on in them.
2) There's not a ton of different enemies to fight.
3) I bought 100 arrows, that's it. Money was basically worthless.
4) Items being sold are so overpriced that you can only buy a couple of them throughout the game.
5) The game runs clunky, and things seem to pixelate a lot.
6) The quests are all fetch this and that. Boring and repetitious.
7) There is only a few people to talk to in each inhabited area.

So in my opinion if you can get this game cheap, and need and need a game to play, buy it. Just don't expect to much from it.

title: The dogs loved this food as a supplement to their usual food
text:
My friend runs a foster home and puppies are a revolving door. Before feeding this to any puppies, I tried this for my friend's dogs to supplement with their other food and they loved this food.

The kibble is dark and pellet shaped. This food is made in the USA from ingredients sourced around the world.

The ingredients are Cod Head, Whitefish Meal, Coconut Flour, Lentils, Whole Dry Eggs, Tapioca, Chicken Fat (Preserved with Mixed Tocopherols (Vitamin E)), Flax Seed Meal, Menhaden Oil (Preserved with Mixed Tocopherols (Vitamin E)), Coconut Oil, Natural Flavor, Marigold Petal, Banana Powder, Marine Microalgae, Chicory Root, Dicalcium Phosphate, Lecithin, DL Methionine, Taurine, L-Lysine, Lactobacillus Acidophilus Fermentation Product Dehydrated, Oligofructose, Yucca Schidigera Extract, Sea Salt, Kelp Meal, Vitamin E Supplement, L-Ascorbyl-2-Polyphosphate (source of Vitamin C), Niacin Supplement. Biotin,  Thiamine Mononitrate, L-Carnitine, d-Calcium Pantothenate, Riboflavin Supplement, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, Vitamin A Acetate, Vitamin B12 Supplement, Vitamin D3 Supplement, Folic Acid, Choline Chloride, Potassium Chloride, Zinc Proteinate, Betaine Anhydrous, Iron Proteinate, Selenium Yeast, Copper Proteinate, Manganese Proteinate, and Calcium Iodate.  

GUARANTEED ANALYSIS
Crude Protein,min  --> 30%
Crude Fat, min  --> 16%
Crude Fiber, max--> 3.5%
Moisture, max -->7.5%
Ash, max --> 7.5%Etc.

The ingredients are good except for the lentils —see my note below. Note that unless a dog has a grain allergy, it is not a good idea to feed them grain-free foods exclusively. The reason is that vets are finding an association between heart disease (such as canine dilated cardiomyopathy) and grain-free dog foods. This disease is mostly associated with the foods that have peas, lentils, other legumes or potatoes as their main ingredients and this food has lentils. Nevertheless, I feel it is okay to feed this food to a dog only to supplement a dog's diet and not as an exclusive meal. Note that puppy food tends to have more protein than regular dog food.

In summary, the dogs definitely enjoy this food and it is perfect as a complement to their regular foods.  I love that the bag has a Velcro seal to keep their kibble fresh. The current price of $21.99 for 5 pounds is pricey but still competitive.

title: Packs a punch for the size.
text:
I ordered the iHome Alexa Built-in Bluetooth Speaker Portable Wireless Waterproof Rechargeable Lights Up to Music, with Speakerphone, Passive Subwoofer, Carry Strap, Durable Shockproof Floatable Design (IBT158) to replace an old sub par portable speaker that I’ve had for years. The iHome is quite the upgrade with the built in Alexa, better sound and being waterproof. I’ve had this product now for several weeks and would like to share my thoughts.

I must say that the sound is pretty good and packs a punch in such a small size. It’s much better than the much smaller and several years old portable wireless speaker that I have been using. In fact there really is no comparison at all. Let’s just say that it is the best sounding portable wireless speaker that I personally have ever owned. My daughter who “borrowed” the older speaker some time ago (and she never gave it back) keeps asking to "borrow" the new iHome as she says, “it’s louder and sounds WAY better”. I absolutely agree with her. Plus the lights on this thing are a nice touch, and there are options (via a button on top) to cycle through and change the color options or turn them off.

Setting up the iHome for Bluetooth and Alexa was easy and very straight forward, and there has been no issues whatsoever. We are mainly an Android household however my oldest daughter uses an iPhone and everyone has had the same great experience. So far my only complaint is that the Bluetooth connectivity distance isn’t the greatest but with that said, none of my Bluetooth devices really have much range in our home so I am not going to knock points off for that. The sound out of this little guy makes up for the Bluetooth short comings and the bonus of Alexa being packed into this as well as the waterproof features make this a great value for the selling price.

One thing worth mentioning is that to use Alexa, you can’t just say “Alexa” to activate her. You do have to physically press a button on the iHome speaker to access her, which isn’t a huge deal breaker, but because of this, you can’t use other Alexa devices to make an announcement and have it broadcast to the iHome speaker. Being fairly new to the Alexa and smart home world, I am not going to hold this shortcoming against the iHome device. It actually makes sense that with this being portable, you wouldn’t want to have Alexa always listening and drain the battery while on the go. Speaking of Battery life, it's decent but not spectacular by any means. This is pretty subjective however as usually when I use the iHome, I'm listening to it at a pretty high volume ;)

Another observation is that this uses micro USB to charge, and I really would like to see more devices using the newer and better USB C charging capabilities.

As far as the “waterproof” capabilities go, I must report that I have yet to float the device in a pool or let the kids play with it outside while running through the sprinklers. I know that it says it’s waterproof and it absolutely looks like it would hold up to getting wet as it is very well built, rugged and quite solid, but I don't want to risk ruining this new toy that the whole family has been enjoying so much.

text:
My friend runs a dog foster home and I tried it on three of the dogs. We put this on top of their food and they ate it ravishingly. One problem we had is that one dog did not want to eat his regular food once he finished this. That dog started fighting with the other dog in an effort to steal the morsels that were left over in his dish. She quickly had to break up a dog fight.

DETAILS:

- This is designed to enhance and add variety to a dog's meals by adding this on top of their regular food.

- It's listed as 100% complete and balanced.

- Although it's manufactured in USA, the box does not say where the ingredients are sourced from.

- The box says it's made with real beef, yet beef is the 10th ingredient.

- There are 9 pouches of "moist" morsels. Each pouch is probably 4 ounces each since there are 36 ounces in the box.

- The pouches are clear plastic with no quantity or writing on the package.

The verdict, the dogs loved it to the exclusion of their own food. I can see using this to encourage a dog to eat a special diet food (even though they should not have any other food) or to encourage a sick or finicky eater. From this perspective, I think it's worth it's weight in gold. Other than this, I consider this an expensive (at the current price of $13.59 for 9 pouches), sort of unhealthy, food additive with ingredients that starts with meat-by-products, soy flour, soy grits, and high fructose corn syrup, etc. in that order.

The dogs give this five stars but I give it two stars for nutrition; hence the 3-star rating.

title: Dead spots are gone.
text:
This wireless range extender was fairly easy to install. The directions were straight forward, and the device was up and running in less than fifteen minutes. It comes with an CD, but we didn't have to use it. We did have to reset the IP address on the computer, but that may have a user issue and not related to the device itself.

It took a little while to find the best place to plug the device in based on our home's layout, but we found one that worked. In our house plan, the best place ended up being in the hallway at baseboard level. Fortunately, the device is small and plugs straight into the wall, eliminating any unsightly cords. It would have been nicer to have the device a little more out of the way. We were a little concerned about this thinking it might get kicked or knocked by the kids as they race around and play. That hasn't happened yet, but it is something to take into consideration if you have small children or pets around. We tried placing it in a less open area hoping to protect it a little more, but none of those areas produced a satisfactory result.

It's very easy to tell how much of a signal the device is receiving from the main router. Three bars is full signal, and one is low signal. The signal indicator light is easy to read and is quite bright. Since the device is in our hallway, it acts as a nice night light and would be rather distracting if it were in a bedroom.

The end result: the dead spots are gone. We can use all of our devices in the those areas without having to worry about losing a signal.

title: At these prices, get the 128!
text:
- I have tried so many different SD cards from various manufacturers, at various price points, in the name of trying to save a few bucks. It was really important to me back when a 128GB card cost $50 or more. They all do the same thing, so what’s the difference, really?
What I've found is that it can be extremely aggravating to put up with when the card does not perform well or does not perform at all. I have heard warning stories about cards that are advertised as one size and actually are another size, causing data loss. With that in mind, I have never tried using the very cheapest card or too-goo-to-be-true card deals. But I have purchased cards on sale at the drugstore or even tried some strange brands. What I have come back to is that it’s just not worth the trouble now that prices have dropped so low. When I am trusting 128 GB of data to a single card, it’s just not worth my time and aggravation to have a card that won’t perform. Furthermore, SanDisk cards like this one are all FAST ENOUGH. I’m not a pro photographer, and I don’t have time to figure out whether a card is Class 1 or Class 3 or whatever. I just want it to be good enough that it can keep up with my devices.

I have now purchased several SanDisk cards, and each and everyone of them has arrived in perfect condition and works perfectly every time. They are faster than any other card that I use and I've never suffered data loss. I am putting this card into my Fiio X5ii Digital Audio Player, and it works just fine. During the initial data transfer I have already noticed that the speed is adequate, and I never experience skipping when playing uncompressed high-resolution audio files. I have the same card for my Nintendo Switch, and it works perfectly.

The prices on these are so good now you have no excuse but to buy good name brand like SanDisk. Just buy it and don't worry about it.

title: Happy with the EVO ZxR
text:
I've been a fan of Creative HPs ever since I bought my [[ASIN:B000ZJZ7OA Creative Aurvana Live! Headphones]] HPs.

These have a similar sound signature, but the bass digs deeper. The mids and highs are slightly laid back, in comparison to the CAL!

The CAL! cannot, however, be used totally wireless. Using the bluetooth with the EVO ZxR takes some time and configuration. If you want to ditch the wire, it's totally worth it.

The EVO ZxR is a lot heavier than the CAL!, but not enough to bother me. I do like the way these look on me as well. The black & red coloway is pretty sharp.

The software is easy to install and makes these the most of the customization available for the individualizing sound signature to your liking.

These are also ridiculously comfortable. Despite the added weight, the padding on the earcups and headband are super soft. Headband padding is seriously lacking in the original CAL!

The ANC works well. When I was on the subway, I didn't have any issues with the sound around me, as it attempted to intrude on my listening experience.

These are pretty pricey, so I'd have to audition other noise cancelling HP's in the same price range before I would be able to say these were the best in their respective class. That said, these sound very good to my ears, they look nice on my head, they come with a durable pouch, that also has a zippered compartment for all of the included accessories.

The only downside I saw were the gaps in the instructions. The FAQ's and user forum can provide the information you need if you don't find the answers in the paper manual or quick start guide.

I'm impressed by the level of support, the comfort, the build quality, the quality of the included accessories, and the sound quality of these Headphones.

I would highly recommend them.

title: Great Workout and Dance Moves.
text:
I only bought this tonight, but I spent a good amount of time trying it out since I got home.

I'm not familiar with the Kinect (also got it tonight), so this is my first time using the controls. I found the menu on this game extremely easy to use. You hold your hand around waist level and swipe your hand to select an option. I had to do it a few times on occasion, when I didn't swipe far enough, but overall, it wasn't a problem at all.

The game comes with only the first three or four songs unlocked, and you can unlock the rest. I don't like when games do this, but I had so much fun with this one that I don't care much. You can choose easy, medium or hard levels. You can select "Break It Down", which takes you through each step of the routine, and then has you do the moves in order, in chunks - 6 or 7 moves at a time. This makes it easy to remember what you're doing when you finish "Breaking It Down" and move into the performance mode. You see little "flashcards" on the side of the screen to let you know what move you should be doing, and what moves are coming up. I played the songs on Hard mode, and I almost aced them. I'm a good dancer, but I'm also out of shape and in the process of losing a lot of weight. I was surprised at how well I did - but, lest you think that this game is too easy - it's definitely not. I assume (especially after reading other reviews) that the moves will get much harder.

Best part is that when I was done, I was sweaty and breathing hard. I panicked at first, after seeing the moves, that they were too easy. But, when they're put together, they pack a punch.

The Kinect did a good job of recognizing all of my movements. When you do a movement wrong, even if you're just holding your arm too high, the area that you're not moving correctly lights up red on the on-screen dancer. The game does want you to be pretty precise, but it doesn't freak out on you if you're not perfect.

And, I'm not gonna lie. I like the dancers telling me how awesome I am. Sometimes you need to hear that :)

The absolute best part, though, is the fact that each song (at least the ones I've played) have a "Freestyle" section - a short break where you can dance however you like. After you're done, you can choose "Pictures" from the menu and it would show you a sped up and extremely hilarious video of you dancing freestyle. I wasn't expecting this, and my boyfriend and I had a laughing fit over it.

I haven't played the Battle mode yet, and I have a lot more exploring to do - but, I highly recommend this game. It's a great workout and the moves aren't stale and stupid. I could actually see learning some dance moves from this to incorporate into a night of real life dancing.

There is also a "Workout" mode that I haven't explored yet, that monitors your caloric burn.

So many of the new Kinect games seem to be duds. This is not one of them.

I highly recommend this game for just plain fun or for working out!

title: A welcome addition to the collection even for South Park virgins.
text:
When I was a kid I was forbidden to watch South Park for obvious reasons. I admit that I was very interested in this game after hearing all the hype but have never watched the show except for one episode and the film.
Until now.

To prepare myself for the game, I started watching the show from the very beginning. I love it! After a few seasons I finally started to honker down and play the game.

I wasn't expecting a deep RPG game like Final Fantasy (of which I am a huge fan) or any other JRPG, but I still was pleasantly surprised by how fun this game is and its combination of exploration and fantasy and RPG. It reminded me more of the Mario RPGs: a little of the RPG element, but not as deep with just the right amount of fun.

There's tons of customization too, and my character has gone through a few wardrobes. Because I'm only through a few seasons in the show, there are some things that have gone over my head, but a few still that I understood and have actually laughed out loud about. There's much more depth and resolution in the game than what I'm watching now, and I heard it's pretty exact to how the show appears nowadays.

The game has extreme amounts of quality and polish considering, from what I've heard, its development background. There's much love in the game from Parker & Stone as there is in the show. They've seemed to get a firm grasp on Western society and pop culture, not to mention the mechanics of plot and gameplay, and the result is a fun experience that will keep you laughing--something comedic video games *should* be.

Background: I got my betta, Brimestone, from a Petco. I was torn because he had a mild case of fin rot but on the other fin (see what I did there? :) ) he was the only betta I've seen so far with his colors. The manager there just said that I needed to change his water more frequently. I did my research and I got Brimstone some Aquarium Salt as well (heaters also prevents illness). Anyway, this is my third heater.

My first heater was a 5 W heater and might have heated the water but I had just recently got a 5 gal tank. At the time, I didn't realize that I could use my 1 gal as a QT tank. Next, I got a preset 25 W heater with an automatic shut off. This heater barely heated up the water during the day and at night it barely kept within 70*C. Brimestone didn't mind the heater but he would always stay near it and only come out for food. I was told that I needed to put it in a 5 gal and not a 1 gal. I suppose it just depends on the heater. Now I have this 25 W heater and Brimstone loves it! He swims around the whole bowl (I know there isn't much room to swim) and he's much happier now.

Review: My heater did not come with instructions or suction cups. It does a light that lets you know when it's heating. I do not have it completely submerged (only to the top of the waterproof seal). It's very easy to adjust but it does a little bit to change temperatures. I got lucky and it was near the temperature I wanted the first time. I've only had it for a couple days but so far, Brimestone and I really like it. If the second heater doesn't work out, I'll definitely buy another of of these!

title: The Speaker Itself Is Good But Bluetooth...
text:
Bottom Line - The speaker itself is excellent but Bluetooth can be an irritating technology.

The speaker is lightweight and even has an attached carrying strap. Unlike a lot of lightweight products though, it doesn't feel flimsy or fragile at all. Instead it has a nice, solid, durable feel to it. While I am not an audiophile, the speaker has a deep, rich sound that I really like. It does well with audiobooks, music, and videos.

The problems seem to be with Bluetooth. One major issue is that the sound stutters while using Bluetooth. It's very noticeable when playing music and very irritating when listening to audiobooks. That's happened with every Bluetooth speaker I've ever tried. A google search indicates that it's a common problem related to the amount of information the computer is trying to pump out to the speaker. There's a checklist of possible issues to go through to try to fix the problem but the stuttering seems all too common with this technology.

Another issue involves changing modes on a Bluetooth speaker. To sidestep the stuttering I plugged this speaker into my computer with a standard jack. It worked fine and the sound was good. When I unplugged it to bring the speaker into another room with me, I had to redo my audio settings. When I plugged it back in with the jack, an audiobook played just fine but there was no sound while playing videos. Again, I had to go into the audio settings and fiddle with them to be able to watch a movie. I've had similar issues with other Bluetooth speakers.

If you are a techie you may be able to resolve such things quickly and easily. The less tech adept you are, the more hassle they will be though. Myself, I'm just going to leave the speaker connected to my pc via a good old fashioned jack because I like its sound. Bluetooth? Bah, I haven't got time to bother with it.

title: GREAT flash option for radio wireless setup - beautiful light quality.  iTTL + HSS work great.  Detailed comparison to Shanny:
text:
This past weekend I got to use both the SN600N and the Yongnuo YN568EX with the YN622 triggers. Basically both function completely with the YN622 triggers in both manual and iTTL modes. The only thing that I noticed with the SN600N was that manual power 1/1, 1/2, 1/4 all seem to be about the same output using the YN622 triggers - you have to lower it to 1/8 or less to start seeing lower outputs. Not a huge deal, but I'd like more output options. More on this below:

Here are a few details that a pretty important about these two alternatives to the Nikon SB series:

a) The 568 light is much higher quality - and I really mean the LIGHT quality. It is even, consistent, and clear. On the other hand, the SN600N is very scattered - what I mean by this is there are lines of brightness and darkness from the flash burst. This must be an internal flash "lens" issue - whatever the light is bouncing around and through within the flash is creating texture and light inconsistencies. This is not the case with the 568.

b) Yes, the SN600N is a more powerful flash, but in my opinion, it needs to have more levels of output on the lower end (1/256) because it's TOO bright for some situations. I use grids and modifiers during wedding receptions, and I like balancing the natural light with the flash output. 1/128 with the SN600N is equal to about 1/64 on the 568. I use the 568 at 1/128 quite a bit for details - so this was kinda a bummer to me.

c) The AF beam on the SN600N is better and more centered than the 568 - but they both need to improve designs. The ONLY reason I'm holding onto my Nikon SB900 at this point is the AF beam - which makes accurate AF possible in pitch black - no joke. The AF beam on the Yongnuo is a joke - they need to fix it on the 622 triggers too - it's basically worthless and too bright/annoying to the subject.

d) In my experience using the 568EX, the batteries get warm and stay warm, whether you're using the flash or not. If the flash is on, the batteries will get warm. It also EATS through batteries. I used to be able to photograph 2 weddings without recharging my Nikon SB setup (using SB600 previously) - now I have to recharge between weddings. I've upgraded to 2800mah EBL AA rechargeable (previously using Amazon 2000mah) and it has helped quite a bit.

So this is my current setup: SB900 on camera, 2x 568EX off camera group A+B for reception lighting, and then SN600N as group C for periodic fill. Rather than commit to a single brand, I'm using them all as tools for different situations, because they all work differently. I also am really enjoying the SN600N as on-camera if I don't need the AF beam - the quality of light is bright, crisp and rich - and the SN600N "brain" (basically how it works using iTTL mode) just works really well with Nikon - it's a very consistent flash, sometimes even better than my SB900. I like that it can zoom all the way to 200mm, too. If the SN600N had a better AF beam and better quality of light, I would ditch my SB900 and use it all the time. But I switch between the SB900 and the SN600N for different effects. I actually like the previously mentioned internal lens flash inconsistencies at times - it creates a grittiness that I like.

title: Great Choice, Excellent Price
text:
Update: After less than 60 days of owning the TV, the ENTIRE audio panel died. None of the external audio ports work anymore for no reason whatsoever. Worked fine, then boom just stopped working. Thought it was my soundbar, so I bought a new soundbar, but nope, soundbar works just fine when connected to the cable box. Amazon Prime was awesome in helping me return it, and I'll be picking up a more reliable brand. When it came time to purchase a new TV we approached it the same way we approached buying a house. We made a list of the features we wanted (a SmartTV with Wifi, streaming channels, Amazon Prime, 40” and affordable at around the $250 mark). After looking at our options in terms of price and convenience, we decided that it made the most sense to purchase it through Amazon Prime.

After much research, we decided that the TCL TV’s offered the best value, met our budget requirements, and our decision to purchase the TV through Amazon enabled us to purchase the TV with interest free financing over 6 months.
Appearance.
The TV came in a large box with the stand hardware: remote, power cable and batteries plus simple instructions that were in separate bags. You do not get a HDMI or any other cables. The TV has a simple non-fussy design with approximately half inch bezel all around. The stand that comes with it is simple and screws on with two screws at each side. The stand footprint requires about 8.5 inches of depth to stand on. I like that the stand is low profile raising the screen about 2” above the surface it is standing on.

Setup

The old analog phono inputs are on the back and quite hard to reach once the TV is up on the mantle and they protrude straight out the back which would require more space between the wall and the TV if you use them. The power cable plugs into a recessed area low down on the left side and doesn’t interfere with the location of the tv. All the modern input and output sockets are behind the screen on the right side about 8 inches back. We don’t use any subscription TV service; just a double bowtie antenna mounted on one of the gutter pipes at the back of the house. The coaxial input for the antenna along with three HDMI ports, an optical input, 3.5mm jack and USB socket are all here. We use two of the HDMI sockets one for the 1TB Media hub and the other for our notebook.

Once everything is plugged in and turned on. The TV introduces you to the basic setup process. It takes less than five minutes to find your way around. The remote is minimalist with the most basic controls on the front (Volume Up/Down toggle and mute buttons on the side). It’s small, unfussy and easy to use. The UI for the TV is not flashy but functional and easy to navigate. Setting up WIFI, registering your TV and introducing you to streaming channels and how to add them to your desktop are covered quickly and then you are left to your own devices.

Since we are just using an antenna we were initially a little apprehensive. Wondering how well that would work, or even if the TV had a tuner since everyone seems to use dish or cable these days. It has a tuner that works flawlessly. We managed to pick up almost 3 dozen channels many of them HD. A quick look online showed us a map of where the broadcast towers are and helped us aim our antenna for best reception.

In use.

The TV has a really nice clean picture and since it is an LED TV where a grid array of LED's light the screen uniformly rather than a couple of fluorescent lamps there is practically no limit to the viewing angle. The screen is not high gloss and prevents reflection and most glare from bright light sources. When turned on a non invasive 3” horizontal strip of illuminated plastic at the bottom shows you the TV is powered on. It flashes during startup and goes out when the screen is illuminated.

Image

Image quality is excellent BUT on initial setup it is on a bright echo setting. Which is very high contrast and overly saturated. I guess it is a power saving mode (claimed 16 watts) but it is a bit stark and overwhelming and shows some dithering on smooth color transitions as though it is running at a lower bitrate with fewer colors. When turned to theater mode the quality of the picture is MUCH better with very smooth transitions on subtle colour gradients.

Sound

Sound is similar. Like most LCD style TV’s this one comes with tiny speakers. Again the default sound setting seems to be very flat. Probably to conserve energy. There are about four presets and again we went with theater which gives the broadest range and warm midtones without overdoing the bass. It doesn’t sound too bad and is not thin and reedy like the default setting.

Smart TV functionality.

We originally wanted WIFI because as Amazon Prime members we get a lot of free on demand media. This is similar to Netflix where you can watch a huge catalog of TV and movies for free, buy or rent them for a small fee. The same goes with music. This worked perfectly.

What we weren’t expecting was the sheer volume of streaming media available for free via WIFI. There are hundreds of channels, many of them free to choose from, many mainstream ones that let you view their current episodes of popular shows on demand when you want to watch them. You can also sign up for pay for view services like HBO and showtime individually.

One nice thing is that the TV has a global search option. You can search for anything by title, director, actors name, character, keywords and the TV will find everything relating to your search and list what is available by channel. So you can easily pick out what you want to see.

Mobile devices and streaming from those devices

There are apps for Android and iOS as well as Windows. I was able to control the TV from all our devices. In many ways it is more responsive, especially if you need to type in text. If you have media on your PC there are Apps for the TV that will let you stream from your phone, notebook, desktop computer etc.

Streaming from those devices tends to work ok. I did find that the TV’s built-in media player was a little limited in supported data formats. Setting up our digital media hub with its own channel was very easy and luckily our Western Digital media hub has far more extensive support for many of the more exotic file formats like FLAC lossless digital audio. And other formats are more often limited to computers. The TV does support the more mainstream formats like mp3, mpg, jpg etc.

Conclusion

For us, this TV proved to be a very good and affordable purchase. Especially when you factor in the 6 months interest fee financing Amazon offers prime members. We did sign up for a free month of Netflix too. The remote has a dedicated Netflix and Amazon streaming button. But we were not that impressed with Netflix when our Amazon Prime membership offered all the same features and more thanks to the addition of Amazon Prime music.

When you combine all this TV’s features with our media hub and Amazon Prime we are a bit overwhelmed with the sheer amount of stuff out there to watch. Even if we had no antenna and just a WIFI internet connection. The vast number of free streaming HD channels is extensive making the need for TV subscription plans pretty much obsolete unless you have a very specific need.

We really like this TV and highly recommend it.

title: Fine Camera Strap
text:
I have a camera, a Samsung NX300, that I bought a couple of years ago that I use for everything. I prefer it to my camera phone and I like it better than my older point-and-shoot camera. It is not high-end by any means, but it is better than the average camera and I am pleased with it. It came with a neck strap, but the strap is the weak point of my camera – too short and not well made. I have been looking for a good strap for my camera and I was afforded the opportunity to review this one. So far it has proven to be a nice one and it works well for my purposes.

I have the “Color10” camera strap which is a blue background with a floral pattern. It is a cloth cover sewn to a thin leather backing – not the most heavy construction but just fine for a camera. The ends of the strap are sealed with large leather connectors that attach to the thinner nylon straps that fasten to the camera itself. Looking over the strap, there are no loose threads and the seams seem to be straight and tight. There’s no problem with the workmanship.

I was a little surprised when I looked in the package and there was a little envelope, with two rings and leather cut-outs so that one can attach the strap to a camera that otherwise has no suitable place to attach it. My camera has two small metal eyes that are not anywhere big enough to feel through the nylon ends of the straps but they can handle the rings without issue so there is no problem using this strap with my camera. This is a thoughtful inclusion – other straps I have seen do not come with these, so this one is better suited for more cameras.

The strap seems to be about the right length and it is very comfortable when I wear it around my neck. There’s really not much more I could ask of it – it is well made and it is comfortable.

I really like this camera strap. The manufacturer showed some thought in the design and made this strap workable without requiring additional hardware, and it is made well too. It is slightly more expensive than some other camera straps I have seen but I think the design and the inclusion of the rings and leather cut-outs justify the price. If you have a camera and you need a better strap than what came with it, this one is very much worth some consideration.

Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at minimal or no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Helpful Support For Aging Cat Especially
text:
I have been looking for supplements for our cats which help to strengthen the thyroid and support for digestion for our older cat. Let's see how this measures up.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This supplement is a powder. It comes with a scoop that measures a teaspoon per scoop. powder is not very fine so there will be specs of the supplement that mix with the food- not a fine powder. The smell is a bit fishy but so is flax so that is no surprising.

HOW TO GIVE TO CATS
The tricky part is READ THE INSTRUCTIONS. The scoop included is a TEASPOON. The requirements for most cats is only 1/8 TEASPOON twice a day or a max of 1/4 TEASPOON. That means you can not get lazy and just put a scoop into the food.

DO THE CATS LIKE IT?
Our one cat is not picky so she usually will eat this mixed into the food without any problem. Our elderly cat who has been experiencing damage from someone in our neighborhood who started poisoning mice and he ate some was not so thrilled at first. After it sits in the food for a while, it absorbs the liquid and then he will eat it with less protest.

ANY RESULTS?
I have to say that adding this to their food (we make their food using supplementation and raw food as recommended by the feline nutrition organization) it has been a great help to our aging cat as well as our younger cat. Their coats have improved and it has helped our aging cat to keep using his box successfully which has been a great comfort.

THE BOTTOM LINE
A nice big container, this supplement is more than enough for our cats for a few years (the expiration date is two years plus). A picky cat may not like it at first, but a less fussy cat should have no problems with it. We like it so far as it has helped a lot for our aging cat.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am happy to have this available. It is hard to see our beloved cat start to fade away just because of someone's negligence, but this has helped make his life more comfortable and helped keep him functioning better despite the challenges. I recommend this for dogs and cats. I can see where it would help dogs a lot too.

title: Incredible range!  I recommend using high quality wifi router connected to their LAN port.
text:
**update - no more drop issues - in my review below I was having internet drop-outs, but I found out it was an issue with my source wifi connection. The CC Vector device is amazing and I'm super happy with it. The best way to sum it up, is that it's not a super "smart" device - so you'll need to connect to a strong source wifi signal - if you get ANY kind of drop out issues with the source wifi, you'll have issues. But if you have a WIFI source that is strong and consistent, this will allow you to connect to it from very far distances. I'm very happy with it!

**original review below**

We needed to get a wifi signal across a property to another building about 600 feet away, a property with scattered trees between the 2 locations. Nothing seemed to work, and I was hesitant to spend $300 for a solution, and I didn't want to pay for another internet line to the other building. I tried a few cheaper $100-$150 solutions, but they simply didn't work. The CCrane kit worked right away. It did take about an hour or so to assemble and setup, and it was by far the easiest long-range wifi solution in terms of the technical setup - it's no different than setting up a basic wifi range extender/repeater.

We connected the CCrane repeater to a 200Mb/s wifi connect connection, and with a 60% signal we were getting only about 10Mb/s download rate - it was slow, but usable. We generally range from 45-75% signal performance with where we setup the receiver antenna. I would HIGHLY recommend putting it as high as you can - we got about double performance when we put the antenna 15 feet high vs. 6 feet high (6 feet high gave us 10MB/s performance, 15 feet up we got about 18MB/s performance)

After a few months of on and off performance, I started to get tired of the slow and unreliable WIFI signal. It worked...good enough for browsing, but not good enough for taking business calls, Zoom meetings, etc. Wifi calling would constantly be unclear. We also ran into dead internet issues: a few times a week the wifi signal seemed fine, but would not allow for any internet activity and I'd have to turn off and turn on the wifi rebroadcaster to make it work again.

I almost gave up, but I decided to try to use the ethernet ports on the back of the unit. There is one wifi antenna and 2 ethernet ports on the CCrane unit. I simply stopped using the CCrane wifi, and I plugged an Asus AC1200 wifi router into the back of the CCrane unit. BOOM - we went from 10Mb/s performance up to 60Mb/s performance. NOW everything feels right. This number would be accurate - CCrane does say you get about 1/2 the performance of the base internet because it's a repeater and that's what they do.

Unfortunately I still get random internet drops - the CC Vector repeater will say it's connected to the internet, signals are strong, but the internet will not work. This happens about once a day and we have to reboot for it to work again. I'm currently working with their support to see if this can be resolved. (review update - this was because of an issue with the source wifi signal - I ended up connecting a Wavlink Ariel HD2 bridge to the source WIFI router, and now we're getting very strong and consistent speeds without any dropouts).

So all-in-all - I'm happy with it. The included CCrane wifi could use some technology improvements and updates, but I think they make these things for random couples who RV around the country and don't need blazing internet.

Once you bypass the CCrane wifi and use the ethernet in the back with your own high performance WIFI router, you'll notice much improved performance.

I hope they update the built in WIFI - it would have been nice to just use one router with a $300 setup!

title: Beware: No in-case pamphlet, No saves to Media..rant in progress!
text:
I am sure others have already ranted about the fact that you are only purchasing access to 97% of the disc content unless you happen to have high speed internet access. So I'll leave that gripe alone.

I would give this game concept 10 stars out of 5, except there are some execution problems (largely due to politics, why does that have to infringe on my gaming pleasure???)

The game:
I love the environments! The game play is very similar to the latest elder scrolls, but greatly improved IMHO. I like the rendering engine they used better than the one in Elder scrolls. I like the way that they implemented "mapping" as a "skill" so you can enhance your mapping abilities if
that is something that is important to you. Things like that are really thoughtful. I love the brighter than usual dungeon environments and the stylized graphics, especially how some plants glow and grow as you approach akin the Avatar movie. So, I wanted to support the fantastic work done on this game, I even bought a new copy for the PS3 (on Amazon) instead of used.

The execution: (the new politics of gaming)
With the lack of in-case pamphlet and the save game copy lockout and the online activation codes, I can't recommend buying this new. I don't have high speed internet, so I am locked out of part of the game until I can find some way to get online, update to the latest firmware (losing the "other OS" option that I currently have) and get the game registered online...that's a pain. For me, I would get all the same stuff with a used copy. The online codes are useless to me.
So unfortunately, I have to give it only 2 stars because of the glitches and politics of EA and Sony.

Problems:
I got about 46 hrs of playtime into it (13% trophies). I have experienced some oddities with the game. Some of the quests are kind of glitchy. On one, I was supposed to kill 5 of something. I killed 2 of them and happened to kill the main one (I suppose) and so it marked the quest as completed, weird. Also, I got to level 12 and could no longer purchase skills from the basic trainers, even though I only had a 1 in Mercantile, for instance. I am not certain if there are secret qualifications you have to meet to be trained or if it was glitching.

EA seems to have decided for us, that an in-case pamphlet is no longer viable, to tell you things like, what the screen icons mean and how to attack and special attack, etc. They un-thoughtfully included a "manual" on the in-game menu, if you can find it. The in-game manual, besides seeming grossly generic and incomplete (it refers to the "attack" button instead telling you its the "square", etc), is a pain to go back and forth between the game screen and then back to the soft copy of the manual to glean the information you need. When you could have just consulted a small booklet in your hand. 10 hrs into the game you really don't use it much. But at first, you might use it a lot and I think there is no excuse for it. They have no problem including plenty of other papers and codes in the case, they really aren't saving any paper. Plus, that was one of the reasons I always preferred to buy new games when possible instead of used games...I hope this is not a new trend. You need to let them know if you are dissatisfied with these new trends and commit to boycotting EA games if this is important to you.

As I mentioned, I am one of the tiny minority of 75% that DOESN'T have high speed internet. Another BIG problem I found is that EA has LOCKED OUT backing up your games onto media like memory sticks, etc!!!!!
They now try to FORCE you into buying a PS Plus membership to back up your games. This is getting ridiculous! Would like to know how this is implemented on Xbox, maybe I should have gone that route instead. I discovered this great injustice, because my install got corrupted somehow while I was sleeping and the machine was off...Hmmm.
I lost 46 hours of in-game time (about 60 hrs real-world time). I tried reloading the game and it wouldn't even run after that. I finally had to add a USER2 login to my PS3 and install Amalur under the new user before it would even install properly. Have never had this type of problem with any other PS3 game.
Also, this is the ONLY game I have seen so far that requires PS+ for backups. Once again, if you don't let EA know about your feelings regarding these changes, they will become permanent. I had heard of people boycotting EA starting last year. It didn't really mean anything to me until I became a victim of their new paradigm first-hand. It's obvious to me they have no desire to take care of their customers.

I can't say whether the game was to blame for the PS3 corruption or not.
Bottom line - Sony and EA have gotten WAY too greedy for me.

title: not grain free-- yay!, pricey but quality, 414 cals per cup
text:
Instinct is a quality brand. Made in USA. Wheat free but made WITH grains. We incorporate grains, so this is great. We aren't one for raw, but I'm ok with small addition- nutritional variety.

AS with ANY new food, to help avoid diarrhea & tummy upset, transition food over slowly. I use as a topper, puzzle treat, snuffle mat/nose work food.. so it is more like a treat. BUT if you are providing as a meal, add it in slowly.

A few year back I thought grain free was the way to go, and have since changed my mind. I remember going with Instinct as the ingredients are so healthy and rated very well. I always had two brands of food in the house. This was always one of them. Eventually I got away from it as at the time I think all the options were grain free (I don't recall), and/or Amazon may have stopped carrying what we got (this was before other online options)

In terms of pricing, it is seemingly high, but I had compared a few top contenders-- took a look at the amount of servings rather than price per pound. I looked at the serving of food we would give our dogs and price it that way. One cheap brand may have 50 lbs in it, but directions would have me serving them 8 cups a day (low calories, filler), for example. This one is 3-4 cups per day, or less if monitoring weight. 414 calories per cup. ALL that info is in the feeding description. If you have a tubby dog (my girl is on a diet) I give her less of her usual kibble, and my boy gets the typical recommended amount for that brand. So a good quality food like Instinct wont require as much food. There are many high quality foods out there, this is one of them. If you dont want to use it as whole meal, it can be used as a topper to their usual kibble.

We have used Instinct brand on and off over the years for our two labs. This is the first time trying the lamb variety, and first time WITH grains. I have a very picky boy and not so picky girl. Neither are all that food motivated, but I do engage them in some food based games. One of which is to utilize a snuffle mat and sprinkle kibble all through it. And/or I will sprinkle kibble in various spots for them to find. When one doesn't have food motivated dogs-- LABS- at that, it can be tricky to get their interest in something. They are usually excited enough about the game that the food is secondary. When it came time to present this to my boy, he had no interest in it. My girl was skeptical at first then seemed to enjoy rooting around the mat to find the kibble. Since my boy is so picky, I dont blame the food. He may eventually come around to it, or I may need to try another flavor. Lamb is new to them, hence why my boy is backing away.

Knowing the brand, and seeing all the good stuff in the ingredients, I think it is worth the try. It is nice that they have a variety of proteins available in addition to the usual chicken for those that have allergies and sensitivities.

The food is all stages, all sizes. The size of the kibble reminds me of adult dog food, so your super tiny doggos or pups may have trouble. Not sure, I just know I have seen what small breed/non large breed puppy food looks like and it is way tiny compared to this. I'll include pics.

INGREDIENTS:

Lamb, Menhaden Fish Meal, Oatmeal, Barley, Millet, Turkey Meal, Canola Oil (preserved with Mixed Tocopherols and Citric Acid), Dehydrated Alfalfa Meal, Ground Flaxseed, Freeze Dried Beef, Montmorillonite Clay, Natural Flavor, Salt, Freeze Dried Beef Liver, Pumpkinseeds, Freeze Dried Beef Heart, Carrots, Freeze Dried Beef Kidney, Freeze Dried Beef Spleen, Potassium Chloride, Blueberries, Apples, Cranberries, Vitamins (Vitamin E Supplement, Niacin Supplement, L-Ascorbyl-2-Polyphosphate, Thiamine Mononitrate, d-Calcium Pantothenate, Vitamin A Supplement, Riboflavin Supplement, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, Vitamin B12 Supplement, Folic Acid, Vitamin D3 Supplement, Biotin), Choline Chloride, Minerals (Zinc Proteinate, Iron Proteinate, Copper Proteinate, Manganese Proteinate, Sodium Selenite, Ethylenediamine Dihydriodide), DL-Methionine, Freeze Dried Lamb, Yeast Culture, Dried Lactobacillus acidophilus Fermentation Product, Dried Enterococcus faecium Fermentation Product, Dried Aspergillus niger Fermentation Extract, Dried Trichoderma longibrachiatum Fermentation Extract, Dried Bacillus subtilis Fermentation Extract, Dried Kelp, Salmon Oil, Freeze Dried Lamb Liver, Freeze Dried Lamb Spleen, Freeze Dried Lamb Heart, Freeze Dried Lamb Kidney, Rosemary Extract, Dried Bacillus coagulans Fermentation Product.

FEEDING:
Ideal feeding amounts will vary by age, weight, and activity level so the guide below should be used as an initial recommendation. Divide the cups per day by the number of feedings per day. Be sure to always provide clean, fresh water. Along with dry food, we recommend feeding raw or wet food to help increase the amount of water in your pet’s diet.

Daily Feeding Guidelines (standard 8 oz dry measure cup): 414 calories per cup

ADULT Maintenance (cups per day):
5-15 lb: ½ - 1 ¼ cups;
16-25 lb: 1 ¼ – 1 ¾ cups;
26-50 lb: 1 ¾ - 3 cups;
51-75 lb: 3 - 4 cups;
76-100 lb: 4 – 4 ¾ cups

WEIGHT LOSS (cups per day):
5-15 lb: ¼ - ¾ cup;
16-25 lb: ¾ - 1 cup;
26-50 lb: 1 - 1 ¾ cups;
51-75 lb: 1 ¾ - 2 ½ cups;
76-100 lb: 2 ½ – 3 cups

PUPPIES (Except Large Breed [70+lbs as an adult]): Feed up to twice the adult maintenance amount.

Pregnant/Nursing Females: Feed up to three times the adult maintenance amount shown above.

Transitioning to Instinct: Always introduce a new food over a period of 5 to 7 days, mixing increasing amounts of Instinct with the current food each day. Visit the Instinct Pet Food website for more specific feeding recommendations and information on how to easily combine different forms of food.

I love being able to use a controller for games. This controller fits great over my phone, has a long battery life, feels well made, and does the job for most games. I play mainly classic games and emulators so it's been great for that.

I love this controller. It's not perfect, it's a tad small for my hands, but there are few really good solutions that I've found that do the job. Plus, apparently you can plug a keyboard and mouse into this sucker and play games that way. Really? That's an excellent bonus. I haven't tried it, but knowing they put more effort into the design to add something like that tells you that a gamer made this and wanted it to make it as versatile and useful as possible. Excellent value and a solid solution for portable gaming.

title: Great and clear audio and classic gamer style!
text:
I've had good experiences with Skullcandy before, but this is my first time trying their Wage brand of headsets. I'm happy to say the experience was positive, the headphones were comfortable to wear and the sound was excellent- definitely crisper and better bass response than the classic Apple buds I've been using on this laptop before trying these (and what I'm using for baseline comparison purposes). The microphone is excellent as well, I like that it aims in front of your mouth so it doesn't pick up ambient room noise and echo voice like other headsets which have the mic on the line or even worse, on the earphone itself (I've almost never had a good experience with a mic on your ear!). And the best feature is the way the mic will mute if you lift the mic boom arm up away from your face, and then come back when repositioned. A physical action like that is far better than a button or switch.
The only catch is that you need to be into the gamer's aesthetic. Someone in our home wanted to use these for Zoom meetings, and found that she didn't like looking like she had such a large headset- it didn't go with the look she wanted to have on camera. But that's no fault of this product, as gamer / audiophile 'phones are usually the bulky variety and it is expected. I think this is a really solid options for gamers.
