title: Amazing light!
text:
I ordered this 'D&O Lighting 180W Pro LED Panel Series V-Mount (120º Beam Angle)' for review.

Let me start off by making clear that I am not a professional photographer or videographer by any means. I am however aspiring to be both. My passion really is photography but I am learning more about video and someday I hope to turn my hobby into something where I can make money at it. With that said, I had the opportunity to order and review this incredible 180W LED light by D&O and I have to say that this is the best LED light I have ever used. I Truly never thought I would own such an incredible professional grade light. It's super bright and adjustable from 3200 - 5600K so you really have some good range of color there. The light comes with a nice padded case and also includes the AC power cord as well as a remote control which gives you all the functions that is available on the back of the light itself. The light is of incredible quality and everything packs nicely and is well protected in the included case. I had had zero issues with this kit but if I were to complain about anything it would be that it did not come with a C-Stand or anything to mount it to. I had to order a C-Stand just to be able use it, as it will not mount to a tripod. Another thing that I might mention is that the mounting adapter is made of plastic and does not mount very solid to the C-Stand Baby Pin. I worry that over time this plastic mount bracket may break. Since I have never owned anything like this before, I am not sure if this is how all lights of this type are, but I really would have thought that if this was made to mount onto a C-Stand with a "metal" Baby Pin, that the mounting bracket itself would also be metal and made to fit tight and secure to this pin. I have had several times where this light would spin while mounted and I was afraid it was going to break off as the light is pretty heavy. This may be my fault as I am still learning how it works and I have gotten better at getting it tight and secure. Plastic vs metal and metal is always going to win right? Overall however, I am super happy to own such an incredible light and I hope to take my photography to the next level. I do feel that for what you get, it's a bit pricey, but not being familiar with what other kits like this cost, I honestly don't know for sure. I just know for myself, I would have a hard time justifying the price until I was making more money from my "hobby". I hope that this was helpful.

title: OK Budget Phone, no NFC, bad sound
text:
This phone A10s is basically the worse version of the old Galaxy S7 Edge from seven years ago. Slightly higher battery capacity - 4000 instead of 3600, same screen size, but the quality of the screen is not as good. S7 screen glass is much better quality, it's smoother and it's scratch resistant. A10 touch screen response time is worse than S7. There is some kind of a split second lag which feels strange after using S7.

Unlike S7, A10 doesn't have wireless charging :(

Blue light functionality doesn't work when I flip the blue light button. Button is there but functionality is not. No physical home button anymore.

NFC is not supported, can't pay in the store using this phone. Item specs here says "Connectivity NFC" which is misleading. Old S7 supports NFC.

Sound is HORRIBLE for single built in speaker. Comparing to old S7 playing the same song this phone is missing low frequencies, sound is flat and unimpressive, no Dolby. S7 sound has lots of volume, low and high frequencies and it feels like surround sound, like movie theater experience.

Dolby Atmos is disabled on A10 for built in speaker. Adaptive sound functionality is completely missing, nada. When I plug in earphones, Dolby Atmos gets enabled but doesn't make any difference and left ear piece is much more quiet than the right one. The phone doesn't distribute sound equally between the left and right ear pieces.

Not possible to opt out from sending Samsung all your phone logs info. All preinstalled apps had rights to mess up phones operation system and access everything on the phone and send your private info everywhere. I had to go through every setting to change that. New icons look ugly.

Good features are dual sim and a radio tuner so one can listen to the local FM radio without wi-fi or cell service. It still has a jack for wired ear phones, the wire is used as an antenna for the radio tuner. Fresh battery holds charge better than a seven years old Galaxy S7 Edge. It was easy to set up and install applications from Google Play. Phone is unlocked and can be used overseas.

It's an OK unlocked budget phone for everyday use that works with certain carriers only. But lack of NFC, no wireless charging, and bad sound is a big No.

title: greatly helps my arthritic 18 years old kitty to get to where he wants to go
text:
I think how well this style will work for you will depend on the needs of your animal. Works great for my elderly cat who at 18 has some arthritis in in rear legs. He goes up and down them just fine. Very sturdy! I can lean on the steps and am not concerned with it falling apart.

Height: 29" (as tall as most desks)
Width: 15.5" roughly
Depth: 23.5"
There are 4 steps contained within that 23.5" base & 29" height.
The height from step to step is 7" (bottom of one step to top of the next), and
The depth of the step is 8", but since there is a little overhang from step above, then I would say 6.5". Keep this in mind as it may not be deep enough for some dogs to comfortably navigate the steps. I think most cats could handle this. In short: consider how much clearance they need.

This is a TALL 29" unit. Is same height as most desks and some beds. The material is a smooth almost plush feel. Some animals may do better with a carpet style. If you have cats and are familiar with the Furhaven self warmer pads, or have Amarkat items, then the material is the same. I have no idea if a dog would use this. I would think that unless they are cat sized, then they would most likely need a less steep angle. This is perfect for a cat.

This unit has been FANTASTIC. It was easy, and kind of fun to put together. The instructions were clear, and the labeling of each piece was correct. No headaches or frustration. Put together inside of 15 minutes.

The base is a hinged board that becomes one solid board once the poles are attached.

I am impressed with how sturdy this 4 step unit is. The carpeting is a soft, plush material. Smooth and short napped, much like their other products.I find it to be amazingly sturdy, especially when it butts up against something.

It took my cats a few days to come around to using it, then once they did it became a normal part of their routine.

At time of purchase, it was bought for use with my two elderly cats in mind, now at time of writing this just the one :( Both have/had weakness in their rear legs, especially my boy who seems to not be able to jump up. He can pull himself up if it is a soft surface to grab onto, or if the steps are short. My girl, who has passed, was able to jump up and down, but I wanted to provide her the added benefit of not having to. We have a younger cat who has used this, but hasn't had a need for it since he can just jump up and down from places. But it also has a lot to do with the current placement.

The 4 step unit is tall. It is 29", so taller than some bed heights. If placed up against a basic bed, it my cat has to step down once he reached the top. If I wanted the steps to be about same height, then I would have gone with the 3 step unit, as it is 25". Anyway, it is exact same as my desk height. It is used as a step to get up onto my desk, which works well. I have an odd set up, which I will explain. My desk then has a twin bed along the same wall, and then another to form an "L" shape.. then a table (which at this point would be on wall across from my desk) where his food and water are. The spot where the table and 2nd bed meet has another set of stairs, but of a different kind (and are shorter). Anyway, this room is set up for the comfort and care of my boy, as well as for my two dogs and other cat. It is where I hang out a lot, so it is where they hang out a lot.

For my boy, I like that he can wander the house, then come back to his room and have a couple of options as to how to get on and off the desk/bed/table set up. From there, my kitty can hang out on my desk with me, or he can walk across the bed to another area to rest. Anything for my babies, and this has been a great addition.

Now, if I didn't want to use this as a step system for the purpose described, I would find it easy to use it elsewhere in the house, or as part of a larger cat climber set up.

title: GOOD RPG
text:
Reading some of the other reviews here I was feeling I had made a mistake in buying this game. Truth is I got quite involved in it from beginning to end.

As some other reviewers have noted, about halfway through the game narrows down to a single purely hack-n-slash non-stop all-out war but a few things keep the game interesting: The character will keep leveling up, so directing his skill points and perks provides variety to the otherwise repetitive and seemingly endless confrontations. Almost every locale has its own types of foes and tactics that work on one type of foe may not work on another. Inventory can be very important in this game, particularly enchanted armor and weapons, and partly because there is no prohibition against changing armor and weapons during a battle. At times inventory management is the name of the game.

I purchased a French edition to get practice in French but wound up playing the English version because the French edition still had English voiceovers anyway. The French edition does a complete install to your hard drive and once installed you can run the game without the CD in your CD drive. Using the multi player option on a home network is thus facilitated.

As others have noted, the game plays only 800X600 resolution in non-zooming isometric view but the graphics were colorful and imaginative. The characters seem to be fully 3D and even cast shadows. The result is that this game is a lot easier on your eyes than the Infinity Engine games like Baldur's Gate and Icewind Dale.

Miscellaneous: Sound track music is good though not memorable. Spell effects are not terrifically spectacular but there is an interesting variety to them. Game ran well on an older AMD Duron driven system with FX 5200 graphics board under Windows 98SE although I had to turn off overclocking on the graphics card to get to El Calle Perdido. Perhaps because it is part 3D, the game make considerable demands on the graphics subsystem and overclocking the FX 5200 notably improved the rate of motion and action.

title: Miles Morales Spider-Man is Amazing!!!!
text:
I loved Spider-Man on the PS4 so this was always going to be an easy launch day purchase even if it is not a full length game. The game is jaw droppingly beautiful and Insomniac continues to make beautiful and spectacular games. The game continues Spider-Man The City Never Sleeps story with Miles taking over as out main protagonist. It would be easy to say that if you enjoyed the first Spider-Man you should really enjoy this game as it really is more of the same but in the best possible way. One of my few complaints about the game is how short it is as I would say you could finish this doing almost every side mission in 6-8 hours. It definitely feels like this was meant to be an amazing DLC but I found myself wanting to play a lot more. I actually wanted more side stories and to delve more into Miles personal relationships. If anything I wish this was the sequel and a full game of 25-30 hours like the first. That being said I loved the game and plan to play through again on New Game plus. It was great to play Spider-Man man with Miles different move set and feel. I also enjoyed the more modern soundtrack reflecting more of Miles New York much like was done with the phenomenal Into The Spider Verse movie. For me this is one of the best launch games you can imagine as it plays smoothly and looks incredible. In the performance mode the ray tracing looks amazing so you don’t mind sacrificing the always great 60FPS. The only thing I would say it doesn’t take all that much advantage of is the Dualsense haptics but otherwise it is the perfect showpiece for the launch of the PlayStation 5.

Spider-Man remastered looks great as well and improves on the already beautiful PS4 version. I did not really think they need to change the look/model for Peter Parker to this newer Tom Holland look alike but the game still impresses! I do wish I could continue my PS4 save though so I could just play new game plus on the remaster though.

title: Very Good Starter Camcorder
text:
My two girls love their electronics. Mom and dad love them too, so we can’t really fault the two pre- teens from using and enjoying their electronics to the fullest. We like it best when they are at least devoting some of their electronic time to doing things more constructive and/or creative, and this is what convinced me to get my hands on this SOSUN Camcorder.

I had not heard of SOSUN until I got this camcorder, but I had read good things about the brand and decided that such a large percentage of customers must be right about something. One of my girls wanted a camcorder and this one seemed to have what she needed and seemed good for a beginner. The camera is lightweight and easy to hold. It can be used for regular picture taking and for video. The quality of video produced is good, too. There are better camcorders out there that create better videos and have more features, but this one is still good for a beginner like my 13 year old.

The battery life on this camcorder is about 2 hours. Given my kid’s short attention span, this is more than enough to keep her happy. In fact, she typically creates videos that are only two to five minutes in length. Unless her habits change, the 2 hour battery life is more than sufficient.

Camcorders can get expensive , especially if your needs and demands are high. But if you’re looking for a good starter camcorder for a very low price, this SOSUN is going to be difficult to match. The low price and above average quality make it worth the purchase and my increasingly more creative middle school age kid can vouch for its worthiness.

title: Be the Map
text:
Is Killzone 2 just another FPS? Yes and no. Yes because, well, it is what it is...it's indeed a First Person Shooter. But is it done better than the most popular releases of late? I'd have to say that KZ2's online play is the most diverse, best looking FPS ever released for the PS3. The campaign--while fun, a fair story and fantastic looking--stands in the shadow of online play. So much so that I only played up to the second chapter of the campaign; KZ2's online play is so compelling fun while the campaign seems to just be there because "it has to".

I loved [[ASIN:B000TG72TM CoD4]]...both the (short) campaign and the endless hours that I spent playing it online. What I like about KZ2 more in the online play area is its diversity. You can set up or just join games that are large or small; you can play in one game mode or join a match that strings together all or various game modes...this latter being my favorite way to play. I think that there are like 5 game modes: Let's see...Body Count (like TDM), Assassination, Search & Destroy, Capture & Hold, and Search & Retrieve.

You rank up similar to CoD, but you reach the top rank of general very quickly in KZ2. However, you are rewarded most is for earning "ribbons" associated with how effective you are with weapons and with the abilities that come with each of the 7 character customizations or "classes".

You start as a Rifleman (you just fight), but you can quickly complete the challenges necessary to unlock all of the 6 other classes that include Medic (you still fight but you can revive team mates), Engineer (you can deploy bots), Tactician (you can plant a strategic respawn point near a target), Scout (you can be pretty much invisible), Assault (makes you run really fast), and Saboteur (makes you look like a friendly to your enemy).

Campers still exist in KZ2 like they did in abundance in CoD4, but in KZ2 camping is naturally deterred because if all you do is camp with the same character you will very very quickly fall wayyyy behind in strength and abilities rewarded for completing the challenges required in all the classes of soldiers. The quickest way to rank up is learn and be familiar with the maps, and the quickest way to learn the maps is not to camp.

The classes of soldier are all fun to play. Every time that I think that I've found my new favorite class, I get a Ribbon that awards me new abilities and new challenges in another class that make switching new and exciting. If you play with a Clan or with friends you'll find that having a diverse set of classes on your team will greatly increase your chances of victory...so strategize prior to play, and if you join a match and see that a class of soldier is missing, take one for the team and switch to the missing class.

Initially I complained about the controls, but I did get used to them. Strangely, at first I thought that they were too sensitive. Then I thought that they were too slow to react to certain movements. Perhaps this was because I had just finished [[ASIN:B000X1TC0U Dead Space]], and I was used to the perfect controls associated with that game. But like I said, KZ2's controls seem fine to me now, so all I can say is if you don't like them try adjusting them or just get used to 'em like I did.

The graphics are great, the sound is perfect and online play is as fluid as it gets. I've seen no load issues or more importantly no issues with host ending game or lags that were common in CoD4 and [[ASIN:B001AWBYNE Call of Duty: World at War]]. During the short period that I played the single player KZ2 campaign I noticed some load-lags, but they weren't that bad. Again perhaps I was sensitive to this after player the most perfect campaign EVER (Dead Space) that never had a noticeable load.

So overall, Killzone 2 doesn't bring the next gen FPS to the table or present something that really hasn't done it before, but it does present PS3 owners with the absolute best online shooter on the market today...in my opinion anyway. The campaign, while okay I guess, is really there simply because I think too many people would have complained if it wasn't. KZ2 is an online shooter game developed for online shooters...and stands head and shoulders above the rest.

title: Windows 10 Pro with energy efficient hardware...
text:
We've been grabbing a few of these mini pcs to test them out and see if they're good for Distance Learning. We have a lot of spare pc peripherals including old school 4:3 screens. But for many, an all in one chromebook or cheap laptop is still infinitely more convenient. But if you do have these accessories laying around, and you're curious how this Minix works for Distance Learning, I'm happy to report it's great! I just reviewed a Beelink mini pc that is very capable too.

The 1080p camera, microphone, speakers and monitor connected with no issues. Windows did all the firmware work. The only software we had to fetch was Logitech's unifying receiver for the keyboard and mouse. In California, many k12 schools are using CLASSLINK and GOOGLE CLASS. I went into my child's account, played around with all the apps. Opened and closed browsers, everything was pretty snappy.

It's mind-boggling that Windows 10 Pro is $200 alone. Of course if you're going to pay full price for Windows 10 pro, you wouldn't put it in a low end computer. Nevertheless, it is awesome that it's included here. I recently reviewed the Beelink T4 which has the Z8500 cpu. On paper, that's slightly a faster cpu, but interestingly, the Z8350 in the Minix is a newer cpu. They may have made the Z8350 more efficient or something. In any case, normal human beings won't be able to tell the difference. LOL! The MINIX Z83-4 Plus is a little bigger than the Beelink T4, but comes with a wifi antennae, and a built in micro SD reader.

Basic activities such as web browsing, watching Netlfix, Youtube, kids doing work on ClassLink, etc., this mini pc is very capable.

League of Legends (LoL) is the largest (in terms of players) game of its genre -- the "Multiplayer Online Battle Arena" genre of game, or "MOBA". The first MOBA was Defense of the Ancients (DOTA), which originated as a player-made modification (mod) to the real-time strategy (RTS) game Warcraft III. Lots of acronyms, because this neck of the gaming community is very acronym-heavy. The idea of an RTS is to collect resources and build a base, with structures to create and upgrade various units, and then use these units to defeat the enemy generally by destroying its base. Warcraft III introduced the concept of having "hero" units which would be present from the start of a game, and would have various abilities to help the other basic units, and sometimes battle the enemy's hero unit(s). The DOTA mod sought to remove from Warcraft III the entire dynamic of collecting resources and building a base, and replace it with a larger number of heroes competing over a map with preset structures. So while the basic idea of the game has its roots in the RTS genre, it doesn't play really like an RTS at all, but is essentially its own genre of game.

What does that look like? In a MOBA game, generally five players are teamed up against another five players. Each player controls a hero character (known in LoL as a "Champion"). Each champion (LoL has something like 102 of them now and periodically releases new ones) has a unique set of abilities, and is designed to play a specific "role" on a team. In this area, there is some variety between different MOBA games, but in LoL, champions are generally either physical melee damage dealers, ranged magical damage dealers, ranged physical damage dealers, tanks, or support (buff/heal/scout). Each champion has four abilities (the Q, W, E and R abilities) which get upgraded during the course of a match as the champion increases from level 1 to level 18 (which is the cap in any given match). In addition, there are two "summoner spells" that the player selects before the match begins which are more situations (teleports, blinks, situational damage spells) with longish cooldowns. Champions upgrade their abilities by gaining levels and, especially for certain kinds of champions which scale in power much more by acquiring items, by using the gold gained by last-killing the enemy's minions (known as creeps) to purchase upgrades at the store at the team base. Gold is awarded to a champion only if the champion deals the killing blow (the "last hit") to a creep, so the skill of "last hitting" is critical for most champions in the game (other than support champions, who generally seek to avoid last hitting so that the other players can raise more gold and upgrade themselves as a priority for the team).

All five on five MOBA games have a very similar map (LoL has three-player maps as well, but most games are played on the familiar 5 vs. 5 map). The map has the enemy bases at opposite corners (southwest and northeast) and three pathways between the bases (known as the top, mid, and bot (for bottom) lanes). Each lane has turrets located on it which attack champions for a lot of damage, and which must be destroyed to advance along the lane to the enemy base. Each base has turrets and structures in it which must similarly be destroyed before the enemy base itself, known as the nexus, can be attacked and destroyed -- the team to first kill its opponents nexus wins the match. Between the lanes is a series of wooded areas with winding pathways through them referred to as the "jungle" -- it contains monsters that can be killed for gold and XP gains of varying difficulty. There is also a river running through the middle of the map, roughly from northwest to southwest, which intersects with all three lanes and forms the border between each team's side of the map. There are two "super" monsters located along this river which can be killed by a team for a substantial bonus.

During the course of the game, each team's base spawns creeps at a regular pace, which automatically march down each lane towards the enemy base, attacking enemy creeps and turrets along the way. The course of the game generally takes place in phases, with the initial phase consisting of "laning", which is essentially when players in the lanes will be trying to last hit the enemy's creeps (for gold gains) while simultaneously interfering with the enemy player(s) trying to do the same thing - something which is known as "harassing" - without generally pushing into the other team's side of the river very much. Of course, players will also be trying to kill other players during this phase as well, but there is a greater emphasis on acquiring gold to upgrade the champion gear as quickly as possible, while gaining levels and ability upgrades. Around the middle of the game, the focus tends to shift towards "pushing", which involves moving onto the enemy's side of the river, destroying the enemy's turrets, and eventually pushing into the enemy base to destroy its structures (which results in your side spawning much tougher creeps) and eventually win the game by destroying its nexus. From the mid-phase of the game on, the focus tends to shift to team fights where one team tries to eliminate a good portion of the enemy team at one time so as to make advances quickly while they are on a respawning/dead timer and not active in the game. Games generally take at least 30 minutes, and can last 45 to 60 minutes depending on the players involved.

LoL is the most accessible of the MOBA games because it has been designed with streamlined mechanics in many areas as compared with other DOTA-type games. So the game is easier to get into than its competitors, which is likely why it has grown to the enormous size that it has (something like 14 million players per month and over a million playing at any one time). If you have never played a MOBA game before, it's a good place to start.

In terms of competition, the main competitors are DOTA itself (which is a mod for Warcraft III and requires Warcraft III to play), DOTA 2 (currently in beta, and which will not require Warcraft III to play) and Heroes of Newerth (HoN). Both DOTA/DOTA2 and HoN are smaller, with a more hardcore (and more rough) community than LoL's and are considered to be (and frankly just are) unfriendly for new players - you will get yelled at, cursed at, belittled and so on with ferocity and regularity in these games by more advanced players, so best advised to have a very thick internet skin before wading into those pools. The DOTA games and HoN both have somewhat less streamlined mechanics in several areas (some of which the DOTA/DOTA2 and HoN players specifically prefer to LoL's mechanics) such as (1) the ability to "deny" the XP and gold gain for one's enemies in the lane/farm phase by killing friendly creeps before the enemy does, thereby starving the enemy of gold for advancement and upgrades), (2) the use of a player-controlled courier for ferrying gear upgrades from the shop to the player rather than LoL's instant return to base mechanic, (3) the absence of stealth bushes present in LoL (places players can hide from attack), and (4) an embracing of relative lack of balance with several overpowered abilities by design (whereas LoL tries to balance these out of the game). When Riot Games created LoL, two principal ideas of the design were to avoid things that they considered to be "anti-fun", as well as experiences which emphasized "the burden of knowledge". In general, this has meant making the game more accessible, avoiding abilities which are so overpowered that they one-shot a player who doesn't already know to stay away from the other player due to knowing the abilities of the other player inside-out, balancing champions/heroes in a relative sense and the like. It is, however, a major source of disagreement within the MOBA community, and the main dividing line between the fans of LoL and the fans of many of the other games in the genre. Another new MOBA called "SMITE" developed by Hi-Rez studios is currently in closed beta testing, and incorporates some of the more entry-friendly aspects of LoL with a third person perspective (rather than the more common isometric "top down" perspective in other MOBA games, including LoL), which may also be worth a look for players new to the MOBA genre.

Having said that, LoL itself has a significant learning curve (even if, by comparison, the other MOBA games pretty much have a nearly vertical learning cliff), and also a fairly rough community (although much less so than the DOTA games and HoN). It's generally the place to get started with these kinds of games, but expect to spend quite a bit of time reading guides and looking at videos if you wish to improve your game, as well as a lot of practice with certain mechanics such as last-hitting. These are games meant to be played competitively for years on end, and will repay that investment if you are willing to make it, and even LoL, which is relatively more accessible, is still not generally designed as a game you will do well in if you just play casually every once and a while.

title: Decent price for name brand, but USB2 speed
text:
I love and trust Lexar products for my work jobs (professional grade memory cards and other solid state storage), so I had high expectations for this product. I love the build quality of this material, it's a solid feeling metallic body instead of cheap plastic, and it gives the impression of a product that will hold up to the test of time.
The price is also impressive for a name brand product with this kind of build quality. However, I had almost forgotten how slow USB2.0 can be. I'm so used to USB3 storage speeds of easily over 150MB/s, that the benchmarks on this one seem almost painfully slow at around the 20MB/s mark. But, that's par for the course with the older standard, so I can't really fault the product for it. This is a great value but you could easily get a much faster storage stick for a bit more money. I could see this being useful for someone who wants to distribute a hard-copy of something by hand and would like to order a bulk supply of durable and fast-enough but still affordable media. Otherwise, I think I'd recommend one that is USB 3 compatible at least since you can always be backwards compatible with 2.0 if necessary, but have the increased speed when available.

title: Balanced Sound Spectrum
text:
Bose is primarily known for their active noise canceling (ANC) phones though they have for years offered non-ANC phones. This is my first pair of Bose phones that are not in the ANC class of headphones and my impression of them is mostly positive. I do see some room for improvement, though.

First off, these are without question the lightest headphones (aside from ear buds) that I have ever worn. I am a bit odd in that I actually prefer heavier headphones but this is strictly a preference, not a criticism. In spite of the weight, the phones fit very nicely and do not feel like they're about to slip off if you lean down. This is not to say they're tight, but they are tight enough to hold well. They're easy to adjust too, so getting them to fit just right is simple enough. If exceptionally lightweight headphones are your thing, this is what you want.

The cord is a little different than other phones I have used in that the jacks on either end are of different sizes. This is good and bad. It's good in that there's no question of how to attach the cord because it only fits one way. But, it also means that a normal cord that comes with practically any other headphone will not work.

The sound quality is definitely better than average but not perfect (certainly not audiophile-level). The sound spectrum seems to be fairly well balanced. The highs are good and the "edges" are crisp and clean for most tracks. The midrange is ok but slightly hollow. The bass is very good without being overdriven. One of the problems with a lot of headphones is that they tend to overdrive the bass which is fine if you really like your bass, but too much can overpower the rest of the spectrum and give some of us headaches. That these phones do not over-amplify the bass is a pleasant surprise.

Having a pair of Bose QC-15 ANC phones, I can compare the two models' sound profiles and there are some slight differences. Where the QC-15s are great at the highs and overdrive the bass, the midrange is sorely lacking. The SoundTrue get the bass right and have good highs but fall slightly short on the midrange (though still better than the QC-15s). Comparing just the sound profiles and ignoring the ANC function, I prefer the SoundTrue over the QC-15s.

The carrying case is nice and should provide some protection when packed for travel. I would have preferred a slightly harder and more crush-resistant case but that's me being picky. There's not a lot of extra room in the case so storage is not really an option with the case.

The price is a little high ($180 as I write this) and that might be a little steep for some. It comes down to whether a less expensive set of phones delivers the same (or better) sound profile.

My overall impression of the Bose SoundTrue headphones is positive. These are very comfortable and exceptionally lightweight and the sound quality is good though not perfect. These phones are above average and are worth consideration if you want non-ANC headphones or if you're looking for very lightweight headphones.

title: Enjoyable Adventure
text: I am an avid player of HOS games. As an amateur player, I struggled with HOS-heavy games, but have moved to the more complicated HOS/puzzle/inventory object puzzle games with story lines. I get tired of demons and evil villains, and several games that I purchased only lasted a couple of hours -- not enough scenes or puzzles to justify the money spent. This game, however, is quite lengthy. A complex story involving the writer Hawthorne and his ancestral connections to the Salem Witch Trials send you through locations in time from the 1800s to the 1600s, seeking answers to the mystery. HOS are well rendered. Puzzles to enter doors, etc. are varied in type and level of difficulty. Object gathering is sufficiently difficult to present a challenge. The added bonus is that if you want to know more about the background of the trials and the individuals involved, the information is provided; but you aren't forced to stop to read historical information if all you want to do is play the game. Each scene provides two specific hidden objections -- one to increase hints and the other to unlock bonus games at the end. The unlocking is a challenge. Like other games of this sort, there is a lot of moving back and forth between locations hunting for clues, but the locations are very interesting. I truly enjoyed this game and would highy recommend it and the other Midnight Mysteries titles as well.

title: Good sound - good price
text:
I'm somewhat particular about my music and my headphones and have specific things I look for. I'll try to touch on those items in this review.

Sound Quality: obviously most important. I look for solid bass (not boomy or hyped). And clear trebles (not sizzling or hyped). These headphones performed okay on both counts although it did seem the bass was a little hyped. I have some expensive headphones that these did not compare favorably to. I also look for general clarity in vocals... here, they did good... nothing nasally or buried in the mix. The exception came when turning on the noise reduction circuit. More on that later.

Comfort: okay, I have a big head (size xxl hat). So comfort is important to me. These headphones are adequate in that regard. I had to extend them fully, but at full extension they fit me properly and comfortably, sealing off around the ear. They did not completely surround my ears as some studio monitors do, but they did cover my ears. The padding is decent and I was able to listen for a reasonable amount of time before they became uncomfortable pressing on the perimeter of my ear. If your head/ears are smaller, my guess is they'd be plenty comfortable.

Noise reduction: I'm not used to using this feature and wasn't sure how to test it, so I simply sat down next to an air cleaner I have in my home and tried turning noise reduction on and off to see what happened. There was definitely a reduction in the noise... mainly in the lower frequencies. It didnt completely eliminate the sound of the blowing air, but what was left was a thinned out version of the original noise. It was definitely an improvement in the level of noise. The only thing I didnt care for was that there seemed to be an impact on the sound of the music also. Again, the noise reduction thinned the music and left it a little nasally.

Controls: straight forward controls. Theres a slider to turn noise reduction on and off and an adjacent button to activate the phone function. Since the phone button was just below the slider, I kept accidentally turning on the phone when trying to activate the noise reduction. Better button placement would have helped.

Overall, I was reasonably impressed with these headphones. Especially considering the price, they seem to do well. They come with a nice, soft sided carry case and needed cables. I expect I'll get some good use from these.

title: Great case at a great price!
text:
Purchased a month ago, I've been using this case constantly as I drive a semi and use my headset to watch movies and game. Here are my thoughts so far:

Pros
- Build quality is ok, it's well made and I really like the pretty Khanka zipper pulls.
- You have to adjust the front of the headset all the way in, but THE HEADSET FITS FINE. I'm not sure what the other reviewer's problem was, but adjust the headset and it's nice and snug.
- I like the layout. Everything in the launch bundle fits and they include a nice fake leather pouch for your cables; cables have to be wound up well in order to fit.
- The price is great for this case. None of the other cases hold everything while still being fairly compact. This case does this and is one of the cheaper ones available.

Cons
- It would have been nice if Khanka had put their logo on the top of the case so you wouldn't open it upside down! Fixed this with a piece of glow tape donated by my disc golfer son. Still, the Khanka logo stitched in the top would look sharp.
- Velcro that holds the camera and move controllers is starting to get a little weak. When it fails, I'm going to replace it with either better quality 2 piece Velcro or magnetic strips. Khanka should have used 2 piece Velcro, the surface on the inside of the case is not the greatest attachment as is.
- I'm concerned about the cords or anything else touching the inside of the lenses in the headset. The cord pouch is intended to nestle within the headset. I placed a piece of stiff foam as a barrier, and usually put the cords in the backpack with my ps4. This is why my review is 4 stars.
- I wrap the camera in some soft flexible foam to protect the lenses, also the reason for not rating 5 stars.

Overall it's the only case that perfectly fits my needs in containing the psvr and it's accessories. The price is great, however I would be willing to pay a little more is the few design flaws were fixed. As it is I'm still happy using the case every day ave would recommend it with a few small modifications as discussed in the last two points I discussed.

text:
I have this L 7" pack of 2 CHICKEN rolls as well as the variety in Peanut Butter (9"). Both smell pretty good. The aroma piqued the interest of my curious labs. I can see why my babies were eager to check them out. Having the two flavors to review worked out well since I have two labs, and while one isn't a fan of peanut butter the other really hates it. When presented with both flavors, my girl opted for the peanut butter over the chicken and my boy opted for the chicken over the peanut butter. That made things easy :) My boy is so picky about food that I wasn't sure if he'd even like this, but he did. Because I have the two flavors, my reviews will be pretty much the same.

They BOTH enjoyed their treats- such delight watching them take one and find a place to eat it. I was particularly amazed that my picky boy enjoyed his chicken one as much as he did. He will sometimes take a treat-- like he is being polite-- and then go deposit it somewhere. Cracks me up. But with this, he really got into eating it. The next day he was given the other one. My girl loved her peanut butter roll. The rolls are long and dense. These are an occasional treat, or super special treat because they are high in calories (332.7 calories per roll!), and last 6-7 minutes (I timed). My dogs are not big chewers, but they chomped these down real easy. I could tell that they were able to chew and eat them no problem- they weren't swallowing big pieces, gulping it down. I am pleased about that.

I'm not upset that the treats didn't last long, so I just consider it a special treat. They really enjoyed them, so I will consider these again for their birthday or Christmas. Price isn't bad for a high value treat.

My labs had no problem chomping on these, and seemed to handle them well (didn't notice diarrhea or tummy upset). They sure look like raw hide, but they definitely are not. title: Made Well and Works Well
text:
USB-C cables are the one cable type I usually have trouble putting my hands on in my house, and I need them for charging my tablet as well as my video lights. I selected this one because I like cables with braided insulation and so far this one has worked out well for me.

This is a 6' cable which is just about right for my needs. It is long enough to reach my devices when I have it plugged into my USB brick on my desk without requiring rearrangement of everything on my desk just to make it fit. Longer would be handy but unnecessary, but shorter would make it a lot less useful for me.

I have not used it for data transfer, just charging up devices, and so far it has worked out well in that capacity. The connection is snug and I have not noticed any particular difference in charging speeds between this cable and the OEM cables that came with my devices.

I am especially pleased with the build quality. The cable is stiff (as to be expected) and it should hold up for a long time against kinks and twists. The junctions where the cable goes into the plastic casings for the connectors are tight and allow no play which is a big plus for me as these are the spots where I have had cables fail most often. Overall, I am not unhappy with the build quality.

This is a decent third-party USB-C cable that works very well for me. It is made well and it does a fine job charging my devices. It isn’t too expensive either, making it easy to recommend.

title: Farm Sim 2017
text:
Since it's asked in the questions, and altho answered, I figured it can't hurt to mention: this is not Farmville, Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, or any of those social farming games. This is straight up a farm management simulation, and you have to take care of every little detail, from sowing seed, to harvesting and selling, and if you find any free time, you might want to try your hand at animal husbandry or forestry.

There's a steep learning curve. I wouldn't even call it a curve. It's kinda like they say, here's a jumbo jet, you can figure the rest out. The tutorials only mention basics like "oh, you need to feed and water your animals". But in between that is figuring out what do to. Every task has a tool, and there's not a whole lot of in-game documentation to figure it out. Wanna fertilize your newly sown wheat? You need to buy a front-loader attachment for your tractor, but before you do that, you need to customize said tractor so it can USE front-loaders. When you do that, you need to buy a pallet loader to load and transport fertilizer. If you've figured all that out, time to bring that fertilizer back to the farm and load it in to your fertilizer attachment, which you forgot to buy when you were in town! You'll use every single button and combinations of buttons on the Switch. Individual shoulder buttons or both at once, sometimes a shoulder button and left stick down. If you have multiple attachments on your tractor, you need to select which tool you want to use.

There are plenty of on-screen status indicators, and sometimes some brief descriptions text to help you along. You can hire workers to help with some of the drudgery, like sowing seed, which is just driving back and forth for an hour or so,. but workers cost money. Haven't been able to figure out, or even tell, if workers can deliver goods to sell.

The graphics are pretty amazing, and you can jump out of your tractor at any time and walk around. You'll even see other people wandering around town, and if you want, there will be cars on the road, always getting in your way.

I've played FS on a 3DS, which is an extremely simplified version of FS, kinda like they just took the Android mobile app and ported it to the 3DS, so I thought I was prepared. But the 3DS version is a Tonka toy in comparison. As far as I can tell, the only thing that is lacking from other versions is multiplayer and mod support.

If you're already a fan of the franchise, you'll know what to expect, but this time, it's portable. I would point out that tablet mode may be a bit stressful on your eyes, as some of the fonts are pretty tiny, so I prefer docked mode.

If you're new to the franchise, give yourself a few hours before making judgement. This is not the kind of game you can pick up and 15 minutes later make a call. You'll want to spend time in the tutorials, and then a few hours in career mode, and you might want to even restart career mode. It's a long term game, so the initial time investment is going to reflect that.

title: Decent, An Upgrade, but needs Improvement.
text:
Playing this game as an upgrade from NCAA 2011, it is pretty good. People expressed a lot of freezing or lagging, I haven't had any as I have played 2 seasons so far. I play 6 minute quarters because honestly.. 15 minutes in game time each in my real life? That would be almost 2 hours or more of playing this game each scenario. If you play your quarters with lots of minutes, that might be why you have so much freezing up on your Dynasty mode, but not mine.

Gameplay, I can't say much for it. Honestly I play on All-American and it's really crap. This is why I give the game a 3 out of 5 overall. When I play this game I realize, when I do screen passes the linemen really run past a block, without any effort of the computerized programmed linemen, are suppose to block.. No not really they run to the right or left then up the field without blocking.

When passing, I cannot express how much B.S. you will experience in the pass game. INT after INT. It is outrageous honestly. You can be a A+ team and play a C- team. If you air raid or pass the ball a lot, then INT's just come as nothing. They are much more common in this football game than I have ever experienced.

The other thing is, when ever I call an audible to make a run-play, the computer instantly picks this up, automatically sends the SS, FS, and all Linebackers to the front of the line showing blitz. --- Really ??? Yes. Really, the computer can read your mind and your plays. It doesn't matter what you do unless you want to burn a timeout on 4th and 1 with a minute to go in the 4th qtr. down by 3. Sure thing.

The Computer also can gut you in the air pass game whenever it feels like it too. This is another thing about the game. You can play a 3 man d-line and have everyone else playing pass with zone coverage and Man-2-Man. This will not work, when the computer wants to score or make a play, it makes a play unless you somehow switch your player and make the play happen yourself, thus making it a "User Pick" or "User Sack" etc.

The Graphics are good, they are an upgrade from '11 but they could have been better honestly. When playing, I noticed the entire marching band in the background of the stands were all the same people and all colored Black. I'm not saying anything bad, just saying the game creators need to put time into the detail and environment and not just copy paste every thing.

What gamers are looking for now, is feeling the atmosphere when playing, thus making it feel real.

I really feel no connection with the game other than I am a college football fan who happens to play games as well.

title: This Sorrowful Life
text:
Disclosure: Played as a PSN download

TellTale has done it again! The Walking Dead Season 2 is an extension of the awesome 5 part series that was [[ASIN:B007WWW2C8 Season 1]] which was a story arc to the popular [[ASIN:1607060760 comic book series]]. This game is for and will AGIAN be loved by--and loved by is a guarantee, graphic novel readers--any true fan of Robert Kirkman's source material. Anyone looking to run and gun down zombies will not get that out of this game. You certainly don't have to have read the book or have seen the AMC TV show to enjoy this game; just be sure that you are planning to get into and be part of a story-rich experience..

You start the game pretty much where Season 1 left off, but this time you play as Clementine (the little girl that you took care of as Lee in Season 1). You don't have to have played Season 1 to enjoy and get into Season 2, but I would highly recommend it, 1) For perspective sake, and 2) Because your decision choices in Season 1 (and 400 Days) are carried over (optionally) into Season 2.

Right from the get-go Clem is thrown into a chaotic journey by herself to find other survivors. There are plenty of action sequences, but your time in this game (just like the first) is mostly spent literally being a part of the story making some tough (and some not so tough) decisions. It's the tough decisions that will affect how the rest of the game unfolds for you, and you'll have to live with the consequences of every option you choose.

The game does give you the option of "rewinding" back to a specific checkpoint, and you can go forward from there and choose a different option that overwrites your original decision if that's your style. But I don't do that. The game gives you three save slots, so I'd prefer a complete reply in a new save slot. I've already played through the first episode twice. I tried to make Clem call "the right move" when presented with choice; but there is a time limit when decision time comes, and sometimes you may regret a hasty decision. For example, in just Episode 1 you'll have to choose taking one route versus another, and by the end of the game and choosing both routes in two separate playthroughs I'm not sure that I made the "right" choice either way. The game certainly gets an A for replay value.

Just as in the graphic novel (and the TV show), the story is much less about zombies and more about what happens to society, its morals, laws and standards when government is lost and the planet becomes mostly uninhabitable. But this time you don't just watch it unfold on paper or on your TV screen; in this game you're part of the story...you control your integrity, your morality and ultimately your destiny. And there's real, heartfelt emotion in The Walking Dead games combined with very believable scenarios. You will be emotionally affected by this game, and if you aren't, well then you've got ice in your veins just like some of the characters in this story.

The Walking Dead game is excellent...especially for just a point and click. It's as gritty and graphic as the comic book, and it's very story-rich. If you read the comic as I do...you'll love it. The graphics are appropriately very comic-bookesque. I really do feel like I'm part of a different story arc in the freakin' book! The first episode only took about an hour an a half to get through which is relatively short compared to the individual episodes of Season 1 or the 400 Days arc. But the length of the episode is made up for by terrific storytelling and an emotionally memorable episode.

The Walking Dead game is a deep, personal and emotional adventure that will leave you looking for more.

title: A great investment: the delayed gratification of home consoles
text: The console clearly has potential and Microsoft is making several customer friendly moves to try and rebuild customer confidence. This includes expanding game pass and commiting to late scale backwards compatibility. I havent had an xbox in over a decade. I managed to track down my log in and found that all my games could be re downloaded to my series x. If Microsoft can successfully build a stable home console with the scalability of a PC, it will be well worth the money.  The only major issue is with the lack of software that takes advantage of the new hardware. Because the console is still relatively new, developers are simply porting titles instead of building them from the ground up.  This means that game will only look marginally better. This console is a fantastic investment though. Because Microsoft owns the world, they've been buying developer studios left and right. This means large AAA titles like Elder scrolls will be completely free under game pass. This generation boils down to the PS5 have more immediate benefits in terms of titles while the series X will only start showing its worth in a year.

title: Fortnite: $200 A40 vs $40 Turtle Beaches. Worth it if you have the money
text:
Skip to the bottom for a shorter review (Upsides and downsides). Only reason I gave it a 4 star instead of 5 is because of the price and some other minor downsides. However, if you have the money, definitely worth it!

Great headphones with fantastic sound quality. I was lucky to get these on sale for $130. I would say $200 is too much for these headphones, $100-$130 would be about right (you're really paying for the Astro brand). But $200 is too much for any gaming headphones honestly, but if you have extra cash then go for it! I used to own a pair of $40 Turtle Beach Recons before these A40s and they were very satisfactery. They worked fine for Fortnite, which is the main game I play. I could hear the basics like footsteps and which direction gunfire was in (they had surround sound speakers too). If you don't have $200, the Turtle Beach Recons will get the job done fine. But if you do have the money, the A40s are on another level. There's a Pro mode setting on the mixamp (there's 3 preset modes) that lowers the base (and the base on the Pro setting is way better than the Turtle Beaches) and raises the highs so you can hear footsteps and gunfire better. It's super nice. It's especially nice for indoors fights because you can hear which level the enemy is on, whereas before you had to guess before. Higher levels/lower levels are quieter and the level above you/below you are louder. The sound is also placed in the appropriate level of the ear. Lower levels are in the bottom part of the earcup and higher levels are in the top part of the earcup. It's also easier to hear other fights going on around you while you're in a fight/if somebody else is coming up on you while you're shooting. The mic is great too and the mixamp is very easy to use.

Downsides: 1. Price. 2- The headphone is slightly heavier than my old ones but it's not too uncomfortable. 3- The earcups are a foam type material (as opposed to a leathery material like in the Turtle Beaches) so the A40s get a little hot when wearing them for more than an hour (but it's not that bad). 4-The mixamp takes up some space on your controller so it's a little awkward to hold at first--especially if you have a XB1 elite controller, it feels a little weird to use the paddles on the back with the mixamp on but I've gotten used to it. 5-You don't get to use the special Astro app like you can with the mixamp Pro (but those are like $250+). All these downsides are very minor and are not really a big deal.

Upsides: Great sound quality, better than any headphones I've tried. Great mic quality. Comfortable fit. Easy to use mixamp that has a solid level of customization (there's 3 different preset modes). Don't have to charge it. You can customize them too with your own logo but I didn't do that (you have to order it from the Astro website and I think it costs extra too).
Overall: Buy it if you have the money, it's worth it. If you have a lot of extra money, buy the mixamp pro version for extra customization. Great for games like Fortnite.

title: Not the RPG maker I hoped for...
text:
There's enough here to make a decent adventure game, thanks to variables and events in the world maps. It would take a lot of work-arounds, but it can be done. However, you can't use events in the combat system, so it's super generic, and there's not much you can do to change that. For example, you can't make a special move do damage AND set a status effect. You have to choose one or the other. You also can't even tweak hit chance on your attacks. You basically just make it hit one enemy, or all enemies, and do damage 1-3 times OR apply a status effect.

And, no, you can't tweak how status effects work either. There's only a handful of them, and they, and the elemental weakness system, are set in stone....Leveling and class systems are probably even more barren when it comes to ways to customize, tweak, and make it into something you like. If you want to make an RPG with a fun or unique combat system, this is not for you.

Unfortunately, even if you want to make games that focus on the story, this game is still kind of a let down. There's already almost enough paid DLC on the store to equal the same price as the full launch MSRP game. Though to be fair, there's also some free DLC that helps to make up for what's missing, and there's a fair amount of content once you get the freebies downloaded. It's also neat that other 3DS owners can play your games at no cost. However, you can only have one game uploaded at a time. It costs $1 a piece for additional upload slots. The corporate greed is real.

I got this for ~$6, so it's hard to feel like I overpaid... If nothing else I can pull my 3DS from my pocket when away from home and work on some silly little adventure game that may never see even a single player. However, unless you can also get it super cheap too I recommend you steer clear. Check out RPG Maker MV on PC for a more tweak-able, time-worthy, and complete experience.

title: Gorgeous picture, full rich sound, easy to set up
text:
After almost 3 weeks with this television, I am amazed and very, very happy with it. There's a lot to like here and a couple of things that I wasn't expecting from any television.

First is the ease of set up. Our previous smart tv was a ROKU and reasonably simple to set up as well. The Google connection here means just signing in with your existing Google info and the tv uploads your existing apps. Just like moving to your new Android phone or tablet. All of our streaming apps populated and we were able to sign in without drama - HBOMAX, Prime, Paramount Plus, HULU and Netflix. We only stream and haven't used cable or satellite in 5 years, so easy app access with a new tv is important.

The 4K picture is outstanding. There's no distortion in picture quality or digital noise even from old 1940s movies. The colors are rich and full and the tv settings let you adjust to your preference as well. We've watched a lot, A LOT of tv recently and every show on all platforms has been gorgeous. Frankly, we probably watch way too much tv as a rule and that's not going to change. I've been amazed at the picture quality difference between our year old HD tv and this one.

We've connected Alexa to this tv and the voice controls work...most of the time. Using the voice control via the remote control renders better responses for sure. The tv has recognized a Fire stick, Roku Express stick, and a portable DVD player for us without any drama. We don't have a gaming system, though.... I'm considering buying one for this giant screen.

But my final show stopper moment with this television has been the sound quality. We've never had a tv that didn't require a sound bar. Until now. Despite the tv being quite thin and lightweight, the speakers still produce a deep sound quality without any tinny undertones. The settings have a calibration option for the speakers that you definitely need to do for the best sound - it works. I truly believe this is the best television we've ever owned.

title: Works perfectly in my Note 4
text:
I purchased this because I had run out of space on my old [[ASIN:B00AK31M3G Samsung micro SDXC UHS-1 Card PRO 64GB Class 10 for Galaxy Note 2 II]]. That card had followed me from a Note II to a Note 3 to my current Note 4. I was a little concerned about compatibility and reliability because a few years ago tried to save a buck by getting a tier 2 brand card that literally melted down.

This time I took a chance with this non-Samsung card and cannot be more pleased. For one thing, the transfer from my old card to this one did not cause this to get hot. Considering that there was about 29GB involved that was my first indication that this is a well made card.

Another thing is after I transferred the contents to this card (via a card reader), as soon as I popped it into my Note 4, it immediately mounted and everything on the older card was there. I took the time to look for corrupted files, sampled a lot of random music, and checked a few videos. Zero issues and the Note 4 did not balk at this card or any of the files on it.

As for speed, I am not going to make claims one way or the other. I did not test it with benchmarking software, and since I use this mainly for streaming music the additional speed (if any) is not noticeable anyway. What is noticeable is the total compatibility with my Note 4 and the extra breathing room the capacity provides me.

Overall I am not only pleased, I feel as though this card is a better value than the Samsung brand cards that I had been purchasing. And every bit as reliable too.

title: The Honeymoon is Over
text:
Last XMas on a whim I bought my sisters a shiny new red Wii. We had a lot of fun playing with the Wii Sports game that came with it. So much fun that I thought I'd buy one for myself too.

But after months of trying various games and accessory items, I now mostly use the Wii for the Netflix streaming. I can honestly say that Wii Sports is the best game overall, which is sad considering it's over four years old and the one that comes with the system.

The reason is that the motion control that made the Wii Sports game so fun doesn't work that well on other games. Even some of the minigames on the sequel Wii Sports resort don't work all that well. Just try playing the Wii Sports Resort golf versus the Wii Sports golf and you can see the difference.

I think the biggest problem is that other game manufacturers haven't really found a way to make very good games for it. Most of the ones I've tried you wind up just shaking the remote now and then. Or else with some sports games they ask you to do too many motions at once to throw a pitch or make a shot and it becomes tedious. Really the closest I got to the fun of Wii Sports was EA's Grand Slam Tennis, though only if you don't use the advanced controls with the nunchuk.

The nunchuk is the biggest drawback of the system. Specifically that they made the nunchuk so you have to plug it into the controller with a cord. What happens then is the nunchuk restricts how much you can move your arms around without losing your grip on it or whipping yourself in the face with the cord.

I've also found most of the add-ons to be a waste of money. First I bought a tennis racket but found the Wii didn't read my swing about 40% of the time. Later I bought the Dance Dance Revolution game. But the pad is so small that my feet (which are below-average size for an adult male) overlapped the buttons so it would constantly say I was hitting B or A when I wasn't.

Then I bought the Wii Fit Balance Board. That was a huge waste of money. A lot of people like it, but I found it to be an overpriced exercise video. Because here's the thing with that and "Just Dance" and other games: the Wii isn't really following your whole body. The balance board just reads your feet and the way you shift your weight. "Just Dance" type games just read the controller in your hand(s) so that you can be sitting on a chair shaking it and it doesn't know the difference! So yeah those can work for exercise and stuff, but so does any DVD you buy for $5 at Wal-Mart.

So when all is said and done, I feel disappointed. The promise of Wii Sports in my mind has never really been delivered upon. Plus the graphics are very much inferior to the XBOX 360 or PS3.

Basically if you want to really play games, buy either of those systems. Or if you want something cheaper for watching Netflix and playing minigames then buy this.

That is all.

title: Burned
text:
The short version: don't buy this game.

Any innovative features are buried under the fundamental flaws that exist in the game. I only wish I waited a week after release, but now I'm out $80 with nothing but a not-so-warm and happy feeling that I've spent my money on a product which implies my endorsement this type of system, and by purchasing the game, I've contributed to the mess that is the video games industry by spending my money to support online-only DRM.

Out of the almost 2,000 reviews here, various gaming blogs and other news sites, if you're not already aware, this game has the 100% necessary requirement of online play. If your internet is down, no game for you.

Basically, you're leasing this game, and only under the good graces of EA. If they decided to shut the game down, you can't play. No online, no play. Servers overloaded, no play. This is NOT an MMO, where you are logging in to a server to play a game, this is DRM (digital rights management) which is the authentication method used to verify the license of the game.

Oh sure, they'll eventually fix it, and they've already promised us a free game, currently unidentified, from the EA catalog, but don't be surprised if it's some kind of bargain-barrel game. But what they HAVEN'T promised is a method to fix the online-only DRM, so their promise of a free game is just to dangle a carrot in front of us in the hopes that we'll forget how thoroughly they're burning us.

The DRM method used is the new trend in video games, and the only way to express your dissatisfaction is to NOT buy the game. Compare this to video games ~10 years ago, where you got a CD, and you can install the game at any time. Nope, even if you got the physical media for this game, you might not be able to play this next year, or whatever. I can pull out my old Doom or Quake games, each easily over 10 years old, and still play them today.

Social features of this game aside, this is NOT an MMO (I know I'm repeating myself). 100% online is not a requirement for a game like this.

Save your money, send a message, don't buy it.

title: Keeps Dogs Busy Longer than Most Treats
text:
Dogs love their treats. As dog parents, we try to keep their treat- eating under control, but we love to pamper our pups whenever we can. I prefer dog treats that are a little longer lasting and this is why I like Purina Busy Bones Mini.

Busy Bones Mini are made without rawhide and they have a meaty core that dogs love. They are made with real beef hide and that means dogs are certain to go for the taste! I said that I prefer dog treats that are longer lasting and Busy Bones Mini do last longer than the typical dog treat. But because they are small, they don’t last that long, so don’t serve these to your dog thinking it’s going to keep them preoccupied for the next half hour. I like to feed my dogs the occasional treats and I like Purina Busy Bones Mini. They last longer than the usual dog treat and with 20 bones in a re-sealable pouch, they are good to have around when you need to give your dog a treat and buy yourself a small amount of time.

title: My three cats won't use this litter; I also do not like that I cannot sift through the crystals with my largest scoop
text:
I've been using Fresh Step clumping litter for over 20 years and have tried other litters during that time. There is no litter that comes close to the quality of Fresh Step, not even Tidy Cat, Cat's Pride, or Arm & Hammer. Nevertheless, I wanted to give this brand a try.

Over the past week I have tried to get my three cats to use this and they will not even venture into the litter pan. I then combined some of this litter with their Fresh Step scoopable and they begrudgingly used the box as long as this litter was no more than one scoopful. Nevertheless, even if they used this, I would give it one star.

NEGATIVES

- The litter has such large rock-salt-looking crystals that it will not sift through my widest spaced scoop. (See picture of my scoop and also a picture of the litter just pleasantly sitting in my scoop.) The instructions say to fully empty the box every two weeks or when the litter becomes saturated. However, in my house the litter would not last more than two days because so much of it will be removed when scooping the waste.

- Although it says 99% dust free, I am not so sure. A cloud of dust went into my face as I was pouring this in the pan.

POSITIVE

- The side handle on the package makes the litter easy to pour and grab

OTHER CLAIMS
- The bag says this litter traps and eliminates urine and feces odors. I cannot attest to this because my cats will not use it.

- Also, the large crystals are supposed to reduce tracking. This may be true but once again, unless my cats use this litter, I cannot tell. They did not track any of the crystals when I combined it with my Fresh Step but that is not a definitive test.

In summary, my cats give this one star because they will not use it and I give it one star because it cannot be sifted while scooping as the crystals are too large.

title: Perfect replacements for my G930, some people must not know how to install them
text:
My old G930 ear pads were flaking like crazy after several years of daily, all-day use, and I was hesitant to buy these at first because several people said they were too small. But I figured it's only $5, so it's worth a shot.

They arrived this morning and all I can think of is that whoever thought these were too tight or too small wasn't putting them on correctly. Maybe they thought they were just push-on instead of realizing that they have a flap (just like the ones that come with the headset) that needs to be lifted to go over the plastic part of the earpiece. That's what actually holds these things in place, people - otherwise they'd just fall off! Or maybe people aren't actually matching up the shape correctly. Either way - if you install them CORRECTLY, they fit perfectly.

These things are the correct size and I took some photos to compare the old Logitech-made pads with these. I also measured separately and they are the exact same size. If you take the time to look at how the original ear pads come off, you'll know exactly how to put these replacements on, and it'll take you all of about 10-15 seconds per ear pad.

These are virtually indistinguishable from the originals. I put these on and at first they seemed a little firmer than the original ear pads. However, I actually have a total of three G930 headsets (different purposes), so I was able to compare the feel of these ear pads to the original ear pads on one of the lesser-used, newer headsets. Again, pretty much identical - I guess they just get softer with use. Still, they are very comfortable even in their brand-new state, and I'm happy not to finish the day with black flakes on the sides of my face again.

PHOTOS:
I have three photos, two that are just comparing the back and front of the old pad to the replacement pad (and showing where the flap is that some people are apparently missing). The third photo is just showing the headset with one pad replaced so you can actually see that it looks pretty much the same as the original when installed correctly on the headset.
