title: A Few Frustrations But Overall Great Gaming Experience So Far (And Some Things I Wish The Instructions Said)
text:
My entire family is into gaming and other applications that use headphones and speakers, so I was very interested in try out the Siberia P800 series wireless gaming headphones. There are a lot of excellent highly technical reviews out there for these, but I intend to approach these headphones for someone who is not as into gritty tech details as they might be into practical every day applications.

I am writing this review for those who really want to know about products prior to purchase. I am as detailed as I can be without being overly so, because I want to provide information that I would like to know before purchases. This is an expensive purchase, so it deserves some explanation and time given to research.

WHAT COMES IN THE BOX?
The box that these come in is excellent. It is sturdy and you can keep it for storage of the extra cords and parts if you like. Inside the headphones come carefully pressed into a molded insert. It comes with a wireless transmitter box, every cord you might possibly want to connect it to the Playstation, PC,or Xbox. It also comes with a mobile cable and analog cable for use with TV or mobile device.

The startup guide is, well, let me say really not as good as it should be with an expensive set of headphones like this. For visual learners, you might have some issues unless you are a real techie. There are no pictures of the back of the transmitter box or of the back of the playstation (or other items) you want to connect to so if you are not really good at understanding what goes where, you might have to look up online somewhere how to hook this up to your console or other devices.

WHAT ARE THE HEADPHONES LIKE?
The headphones themselves have a cushioned top and small ear covers on them. The retract and get slightly bigger, but not a huge amount. The top is cushioned and they hold onto the had pretty well, at times feel a bit tight. That will loosen up over time, I am sure.

The left ear pad has a retractable mic in it. When the mic is turned on, a red ring lights up. The disc on the outside of the left ear pad also twists off and that is there the lithium battery is put. When you want to replace, you quickly twist off the cover, replace the battery and you are good to go. There are two arrows that line up for you to replace the cover quickly so you don't have to fumble with it in a hurry to continue your game.

The right ear side has the on off switch on it located just slightly toward the back of bottom of the circle. If the ear pad was a clock with 12 at the top and 6 at the bottom and 9 toward your front with these on, it is about at 5 o'clock. To turn it on, you press for about a minute or so. The switch will light up. If you want to turn on the mic, you tap the same switch once and the mic goes on. Tap again and it goes off.

On the right ear side, there is also a control. It is a wheel which controls volume, but when pressing it, will change the menu on the transmitter box. Then if you move the wheel it will scroll the menu.

The ear pads do fold flat which makes them a bit easier to store when not in use.

I also find that the longer I use these, the more comfortable they seem to become- I imagine they will continue to loosen up over time.

HOW DOES THE TRANSMITTER BOX WORK?
I tested these headphones out on a PS3. I found very little on the internet about using these headphones with a PS3, so knowing that many still use the PS3, I wanted to test using that gaming console first.

SET UP WITH PS3
Optical cable- plug in to optical out on PS3 in back then plug into optical in on the back of the transmitter box.
USB- plug in mini USB side of the cable to the transmitter box and plug the regular USB side into the front of the PS3

POWER - this is optional. The power plug can be plugged in where it says DC but keep in mind that means the transmitter box will be on at all times. If you prefer that it turns off when your PS3 is off, then don't use it. The advantage of the power plug is if you want your battery to charge up when the unit is not on, you can have it plugged in for that. Once done, you can still remove the power plug until needed again.

SIDE SLOT
This package comes with an additional battery. One battery had a single bar of charge on it and the other had two bars of charge on it. So, while using on, the other is charging in the box. I found that with the power plugged in, it took about 45 minutes to reach a full charge or so. One battery took almost an hour. The battery pushes in and locks into place while charging, and then if you push on it again, it will dislodge and come out so you can use it and replace with the other one if you like.

FRONT PANEL
The front panel has a white light up design. It shows the battery charge, that the headphones are on and if you are using gaming and voice and the balance of the two. There is a dial on the right and a back button to the left of that. When turning on the headphones, I get a light that shows they are on then a quick large display of battery power left in them, and then it goes to the screen that shows me PS3 and how much volume is being used at that point. It will also show me the current battery charge of the battery that is charging on the side of the unit too so I can keep track of when it is ready to use should I need it.

The menu is pretty simple to adjust. You press the button to change menu and turn the dial to run through it. There are presets for equalizer and you can also set custom.

WHAT THE DON'T SAY IN THE INSTRUCTIONS
Call me dumb if you want, but although I have programmed computers and done a lot of technical work, I guess I was having a dull moment when I set up these headphones. I could not get them to work. I went through every setting over and over again and just could not make them work right.

Since I have never had headphones on my PS3, (I am the only one who hasn't) I did not realize that I had to change the settings in the sound menu. I should have, but I didn't remember. So, after much looking around, I finally found the setting that has to be changed. There is no mention of it at all in the instruction book. Since this review is geared more toward the casual gamer, I thought you might like to know that small important fact.

You have to go into the PS3 settings menu for sound and pick either the optical sound or you can have both going if you like- through the TV AND headphones. I like to do that when the family wants to be in the room and see what is being played but I want to hear details of sound you normally don't catch on just the TV speakers. You just have to remember to change the settings when you change how you prefer to transmit the sound.

HOW WELL DO THESE HEADPHONES PERFORM?
I am going to have to really work with these for a while to find the ins and outs of them. My first impression of them was awful. I really was disappointed. There was hissing, crackling and all sorts of noise with sound effects on various games. The music seemed fine, but every time there was an explosion or some sort of noise that was supposed to be electronic in nature, the headphones had so much other noise in them it was distracting and annoying. I messed with volume and settings and everything and it just didn't get as good as I thought it should have.

I kept on, however, changing to various games. As I moved through all sorts of different games, I realized that some games must be designed with engines that do not seem to transmit clearly over the wireless headphones. They just are awful. Then other games seemed to be clear and a lot easier to play.

DOLBY
So far, I have had the best results when removing Dolby on all of the games I have tried. I am not sure if that is because the headphones are designed for 7.1 and the PS3 is designed for 5.1, but it seems to be more muffled with the Dolby on and there are more annoying features that come up with sound effects. I will continue to play with this and see how to make it work if I can. I will update this review at that point. We have several different gaming consoles we can try these with, so over time I will elaborate if I find solutions or differences. The listing on these headphones does specify that it will work on both PS3 and PS4 so I plan to see what I can find out about this over time.

MUSIC
I have watched videos on these headphones and found them to be excellent. I can hear all sorts of nuances that I did not catch on just the TV speaker. I watched them via Netflix and also Bluray on the PS3. Sound was much better than some games. Like I said, however, it could just be the software used when developing some games that does not translate as well into the headphones as others.

I do want to point out, that these are GAMING headphones. They are not going to be the top of the line for music listening, so if that is primarily what you want them for, they probably will not be what you want. For the variety of needs I have on the PS3 of videos to music in games and movies, they are surprisingly good.

MICROPHONE
I have not had the opportunity to test out the mic yet with other players. I will update as that opportunity presents itself and will comment on performance during gameplay.

THE BOTTOM LINE
So far I really like these headphones but have a few issues with them. Some games do not sound right in these at all, and others sound beautiful. That is not always the fault of the headphones, but it does make for annoying experiences in some games. The design of the headphones is nice and I do love how they work when they work well with games. The transmitter is easy to use and battery life seems a bit shorter than 20 hours, but I like the fact that you can keep a battery charging while playing so when you need to replace you can.

I also like that you can opt to have the power on to them while the PS3 is off so you can recharge battery, but then unplug it so that it only turns on when the PS3 is on too.

For the price, I have rated these four stars at this time. As I continue to use them and learn more about them and the ins and outs over time, I will update and amend my rating if need be.

FUTURE UPDATES
I plan to test these out with other games as well on my PC games as well as tablet in the future and will comment on those experiences as well.

GAMES TESTED SO FAR (more coming soon)
Monkey Island (newest one)
Hydrophobia
Zen Pinball
Peggle
Planet Minigolf
Spellunker HD
Beyond Two Souls

title: Of Course You Realize This Means War
text:
Call of Duty 3 is a really fun game with extremely realistic battle sequences. The downfall is that you can only play in single player mode unless you want to do/are set up for online play.

In single player mode, you're a first person shooter soldier on the frontline in WWII France. You arrive in camp, learn how to maneuver around, shoot your weapon & throw grenades (smoke and explosive). Then you're immediately strewn into various battle.

You start out as private Nichols (American) in the first chapter, but depending on which chapter you're in, you might also find yourself playing as Doyle (British), Cole (Canadian) or Boharter (Polish).

You fight you way through intense battle chapters (there are 14 chapters). You're mostly shooting whichever weapon you happen to have picked up (mostly from dead soldiers on the ground) along your objective route (a barrage of automatics and rifles). Your objectives that guide you along are updated regularly as you complete each task throughout each chapter. And some of those tasks are brutal.

No matter which chapter you're in you are mostly using your primary weapon (a rifle or machine gun), but you'll also need to engage in some exhilarating hand to hand combat, you'll need to guide tanks, fire mortars, row boats, drive jeeps, attach and arm explosives to enemy weapons, disarm booby traps and man other stationary weapons.

To me, all of the chapters are equally difficult. So if you figure out how to unlock them all like we did, there's no reason to play them chronologically (perhaps at least for consistency chapters 1 & 14 should be played respectively first and last).

So all in all Call of Duty 3 is intensely fun, but like I said earlier, the biggest drawback to this awesome game is that multiplayer mode is only available with online play. I'm sure that online play is spectacular for advanced players, but my kids and I 1) are not advanced, and 2) we'd rather just play amongst ourselves for now. I'm no software expert, but if multiplayer capability works online, some genius should have figured out that multiplayer would be equally fun with friends/family at the same console. Hence, that is the only reason why I've deducted a star from the overall rating.

title: Good'n'Fun Pork Chews? My Dog Says No
text:
Dogs love treats and they especially love treats that are meaty or at least flavored like meat. This was enough to convince me and my vizla/shepherd mixed breed to give Good-n-Fun Pork Chews a try.

This dog treat is made to be chewy and long- lasting, keeping dogs occupied and happy. Straight from the package, they emit a strong, chemical like aroma that is not very appealing. True, other dog treats stink also, but most dog treats that claim to be meat flavored at least smell like meat. These have an odd smell and I wasn’t sure my dog would take to them.

Once I removed the first stick, my dog came running over so apparently he doesn’t find the smell that bad. He took the treat and headed to the carpeting, where he proceeded to chew. These chews are meant to keep a dog chewing and occupied for a while and my dog did spend a good deal of time with his. But then something unusual happened: He dropped the chew and started doing something else. I went and picked it up and he did react, demanding I give it back to him. But once I walked away, he dropped the chew again. He apparently didn’t want me to have it, but he also didn’t really want it that badly for himself.

A couple of days later, the chew is still lying there, on the carpet. I finally took it and discarded since it was clear this treat just wasn’t to my dogs liking. He acted the same way when presented with another chew from the package. I don’t know if I got a pack that was lower quality or what, but it is clear that my dog doesn’t deem these treats worthy for canine consumption and for that reason, I have to give them a thumbs- down rating. They might work for your dog, if you’re willing to take the chance. But they are a no- go for my 2 year old mixed breed and they are not a treat I would purchase again.

title: Ahhh, Just Gotta Love That "Click!"
text:
Mechanical keyboards. There's nothing better.

You're instantly lured in by their siren song of "clicky keys."

So obnoxiously noisy, but you welcome it. You love it. You need it!

OK, that's a little much, but if you've ever used a mechanical keyboard before, then you feel me.

If not, then get ready to be freed from that mushy, muted excuse for a keyboard that you're using now.

The cat daddy of all mechanical keyboards is, of course, the IBM M model. If you've used one of these guys at any time over the last 30+ years, then you know what a quality mechanical keyboard is like.

Those things are like boat anchors. Heavy & huge, but oh so clicky.

However, this keyboard from FIODIO is so well made (& has some awesome extras not available on the Model M) that the IBM will soon be a faint memory.

Measuring just 17" long X 5" wide, this keyboard has plenty of room to stretch out on, but without taking up a ton of desk space.

And even with its compact stature & being constructed of ABS plastic, this little guy is still heavy enough (at 1lb 8oz) that it won't get pushed around on your desk.

The keys sit high, are well placed, & are thoughtfully arced. They also have a nice, long travel distance.

And, as you (& your neighbors) will quickly learn, this keyboard makes a lot of beautiful noise.

This can be attributed to the "blue switches" (although I'm not sure who the manufacturer is) installed under each key cap.

Blue switch keyboards are typically the most "clicky" keyboards you will find (outside of the Model M). There is an audible "click" about halfway down the key press before the key bottoms out on the keyboard frame.

So you get both an audible & tactile response which is very satisfying & helpful while typing.

If you've never owned a blue switch keyboard, then be prepared. It's noisy, but so worth it! (however your family may disagree).

Be warned that this is a WIRED keyboard. So you will need a free USB port. However, the keyboard instantly auto-detects (under Windows at least). So no drivers required.

You also get built in RGB lighting which is also programmable.

I haven't messed with trying to record any lighting preferences. Honestly, the keyboard looks very slick with the default lighting it ships with. But the option is there if needed.

As well, with RGB you instantly have a back-lit keyboard for typing at night. So the RGB lights not only look cool, but are also functional.

I haven't used this unit for any gaming. But it is being marketed as a gaming and/or office keyboard. However, for office use (many hours per day in my testing), you will have no issues.

You will also get a FUNCTION (FN) key that has presets for multimedia controls (mute, vol down, vol up, etc..) plus lighting adjustments.

And lastly it's spill-proof. Which is a bonus to everyone with a drink at their desk & too much stuff in their way.

So there it is. Overall, I'm extremely happy with this keyboard. If you're on the fence, give it a shot. I don't think you'll be disappointed.

title: Delivers Adequate Power to Charge Four Devices; Features Small Tabletop Footprint
text:
What I really like about the CHIL POWERSHARE 5.1 AMP REACTOR is the small tabletop footprint. This charging station consists of a white 4-port USB charger (reactor) inserted into a black silicone stand (tower). The silicone is stiff enough to support the charger, but still flexible enough to allow removal of the charger if you don't want the stand. However, the tower stand is what makes this charging station fit so conveniently into a small space. And because the stand holds the charger with the ports facing up, the charger ports are highly accessible and it's fairly easy to coil and manage the USB cables that are plugged into the ports (and into your mobile devices).

The charger has three 1.0 amp ports (each suitable for charging power banks, Kindles, small tablets, and smartphones), and one 2.1 amp port (suitable for charging iPads, iPods, and large tablets). Thus the ports deliver a total of 5.1 amps. These particular four ports are adequate to keep all of my family's daily-use mobile devices charged, because we rarely need to charge two devices that require 2.1 amps at the same time.

To test this Chil Powershare Reactor, I plugged in an iPad (2.1 amp), a Kindle Paperwhite (1.0 amp), a Motorola Droid Razr smartphone (1.0 amp), and a Qi wireless charging pad (1.0 amp).

---My devices to be charged began with varying amounts of charge: iPad (77%); Kindle Paperwhite (nearly empty); Motorola smartphone (86%); and Qi-enabled Samsung Galaxy SIII smartphone (45%).

---After 55 minutes, the charges had increased: iPad (97%); Kindle Paperwhite (about 50%); Motorola smartphone (100%); Samsung smartphone (82%). This was much better than I expected; definitely as good as or better than other charging stations that I've used. Qi wireless charging is generally slower than direct charging, so the Samsung smartphone was charging as expected. At this point I unplugged the iPad and the Motorola smartphone, as both were almost completely charged.

---After 85 minutes, the remaining two devices had added to their charge: Kindle Paperwhite (about 75%); Samsung Qi-enabled smartphone (95%).

I'm completely satisfied with these results. Any 1.0 amp port and a Kindle USB cable will charge any of my Kindles (Fire 8.9" tablet, Keyboard, Paperwhite); any 1.0 amp port will power my Qi-charging pad for the Samsung smartphone and other devices; and any 1.0 amp port plus an appropriate cable will charge my power banks and Motorola smartphone. The charging occurs rapidly enough for my needs.

If you're concerned, as I once was, about plugging an older USB device into a USB port that delivers more power than the device really needs, you needn't worry. The device will NOT blow up--what's likely to happen is that the device will charge a little faster, although some older USB devices won't charge at all. (For a clear explanation of this, look online for the enlightening ExtremeTech article, "How USB Charging Works, or How to Avoid Blowing Up Your Smartphone".)

The Chil Powershare Reactor has an ordinary wall-outlet plug (no extra grounding prong--just two prongs, one wide, one narrow). It has a moderately short power cord (about 45"), but the cord can be coiled inside the silicone tower or around the reactor for portability and "cable management".

title: 5 gallon vertical tank easy to set up, awesome looking
text:
It's still early on for me, but so far I am liking this fish tank. I have the vertical 5 gallon. It has been years since I have had a fish tank. I normally had the 10 or 50 gallon horizontal style. They just took up too much room and was too much work. I was terrible at keeping fish alive. I have been missing the serenity of gazing into a fish tank, so I have been considering one if I could find a spot for a small one. When I saw this vertical one come up as an option, I knew I had to try it out.

Instead of taking up width it is taking up height. I like that there are lots of accessories available. I looked online to determine how much gravel I would need (5 lbs for 5 gallons). I used a little less since it is a more narrow design. I added in some other GloFish items- rocks, fake sea anemone, plants, etc.. I'm giving the water a few days to settle before I add actual fish to it. I was going to wait to review until later in the week, but I was eager to make comments. I'll be sure to add pics soon. (EDIT: added 6 male guppies to tank, and added pics here)

The set up is easy. There isn't much to do. It comes with filter system and lights. Both are attached in same spot. There is a glass lid that gets set on top. Good thing, since I have 4 seriously curious cats. Pretty sure this system will be secure from prying paws once the live fish go in. Pretty sure..

The tank is placed on a short base (included). It isn't attached, just placed on top. It is sturdy and has a rubber grip to keep it from sliding off. I imagine it would be fine not using the base.

Lights turned on create a cool look on the accessories I picked up. So awesome. Natural, Bright blue, low blue, black/purple light, off.

I'm excited to have a fish tank again, even if it is smaller than I am used to. I have it at my home desk (edit: moved it into my family room) so I can look at it easily. And my cats.

I'll keep playing around with this thing and I will be sure to come back to update as I learn more.

Edit: still Loving it. Back wall on tank is black, so no need for background paper (not ability to add it). I definitely recommend glofish accessories if wanting to use purple light. I am using regular guppies, but there are fish out there that will pick up black light effect.

title: Hope you don't have a bad Xbox
text:
I like the game, good graphics, great voice acting/sound effects, good story. My main problem with the game isn't really the game itself. LONG STORY...I got my first Xbox for Christmas 2001, and always had "dirty disk" errors. It finally got to a point that it stopped recognizing ALL disks, even CD's and DVD's. Thankfully my brother got the extended warranty. So, here I am with this newer one, and still have that problem. It is compounded much more with this game just because of the way the game is played. Just as I'm getting into it, it says "dirty disk". And because the people at Microsoft didn't put a power or eject button on the remote, I have to keep getting up and restarting the Xbox. Not really a big deal, just a big pain in the butt. The biggest problem with this is that I have to get the game restarted again. Then, I may have gone a ways since my last save point, and have to trudge through the same spot again. I have a very hard time getting into the game because I feel like I spend more time restarting my Xbox. After looking at Xbox message boards, I see that this is a known problem. Not for this game specifically, but for the system itself (have a lot of the same problem with Halo and Morrowind). It seems they deny this when someone calls customer support. Like I said, it just makes it very hard to get into and want to continue playing it. If you've had these "dirty disk" problems with your Xbox, you probably would want to stay away from this title.
Another problem I have with it is the turn based fighting. They could have made it a 3rd person shooter for the fighting, not that there is really THAT much of it. It's hard to enjoy the fight sequences when you have so little control. They went for something different, I'll give them that. But, it just doesn't make the game flow smoothly. This does seem to get better as you get further. Not that the style changes, just don't seem to mind the style as much as when you first play the game.
Also, there is just too much talking. I get tired of listening to the people talk and just want to play. The way they have it set up isn't the best. They may show three options of things you can ask someone, but even if you don't ask them the other two things, your character asks anyway after the one question you picked. Why even give a choice if you're going to ask all possible questions anyway? It should just start talking and have the whole conversation right then and there. That would help move the game along more quickly.
With all this said, I still like the game, just wish I could play it. Even with the other issues, I would probably LOVE this game if it wasn't for the "dirty disk" errors. I find myself just looking at a blank screen because I don't feel like getting up AGAIN to restart the darn thing.
Hope this helps...

title: good hardware, terrible migration software
text:
The drive delivers on the SSD promise: very fast access times, even on an older computer supporting SATA1 only. The computer boots up so fast it reminds me of old days before operating systems became so bloated. (Yes, I'm talking pre-history.)

However, as others have noted, the software supplied with it for migration is just terrible, it only works if everything is perfect. And the instructions and error messages are completely inadequate (mostly missing, really).

I wanted to do more than complain, however. I figured I'd share some experience and some tips, that might help another user.

My existing disk was a 1TB hard drive that had some bad sectors (hence my desire to replace). I removed enough data from it to reduce the usage down to about 160GB, figuring that was good for a 250MB destination disk. Then I tried the Samsung cloning software. Many times. It kept failing, sometimes early, often after a few hours. With no useful information (unless you count obscure error codes that are not documented to be information). I tried running disk defrag, achieved no useful result, other than a failure after the cloning reported 100% complete. Deeply frustrating.

I couldn't do a system image restore, because Windows (Microsoft is another producer of dumb and unfriendly software) will only do a restore to a disk of the same configuration. (Here the message is simply that it "can't find a suitable disk", you have to hunt to figure out why.) And I wasn't about to buy a 1TB flash drive.

And I wanted to give it one good try before settling for reinstalling from scratch, because I didn't want to spend several more days getting my computer back to where it was.

Solution: I highly recommend using defraggler (from Piriform) to clean up your disk. You might also find it useful to shrink your partition to the minimum possible, using the WIndows disk management tool. Then I highly recommend using the Macrium Reflect Free Edition to do an "intelligent" clone of your OS volume to the SSD.

After I did this, everything worked perfectly, no problems. Wish I'd known about these tools and all the gotchas ahead of time.

Another tip: If you want to set AHCI in the BIOS (yes, now I'm getting to advanced users), you may need to first enable the AHCI drivers, otherwise Windows will not boot up (you'll get a BSOD). Do a search for this, there's a Microsoft KB article.

Good luck!

title: Suprisingly Great Game, Better than Nocturne
text:
Before I played this game I played SMT: Nocturne. I was impressed with the game mechanics, as well as delighted with the difficulty of the game (unlike FF games, it was possible to be wiped out by even low level monsters if you weren't careful). So, when I saw another game sporting the SMT engine was coming to the PS2 I reserved it immediately.

Frankly I found this game to be better than SMT:N in most respects. True you don't get to create an "army" of monsters as in SMT:N (probably one of the better features of SMT:N), but you do have a greater control of the growth of your characters than you did in SMT:N (you no longer loose forever the skills that you replace).

So here is a breakdown of the game:

Plot: 4/5 Very good plot, somewhat confusing, but most of us who play Japanese games and read Mangas are used to being kept in the dark about what is really going on (as well as spending much of the earlier moments confused as hell... Big-O is a great example of this). Much like Xenosaga, there is a lot of information available that can be used to help figure things out, but you have to pay attention and be ready to think a little outside the box. The only thing I disliked was the use of the "silent protagonist". I hate this technique with a passion, where the main character is only given choices every once and a while, and in the meantime doesn't say a single word. Some of you may be familiar with this technique, as it's been used in a lot of games, such as Chrono trigger (and cross as well), SMT:N, the Breath of Fire games, and a couple of the Suikoden games (the first one for sure). The reason I dislike this technique? It causes the main character to be flat, shallow, and pretty much iconic. Basically, it prevents a lot of possible character development for who should be the focus of the plot. But with the Silent Protagonist character, you can only learn about the main character through others, and the others are of course allowed to reach a depth the main character cannot obtain. In SMT:DDS the main character "Serph" is the allowed only to reach a state that I would call "Robotic." There are a couple of moments where he is portrayed as having more depth, but those are fleeing and overall you are left with a character who seems to lack a personality. This aside, the other characters are developed fairly well, with enough left unknown to merit the sequel.

Graphics: 3/5 Good. This was made stright up using the SMT engine from nocturne. They even kept most of the demons from nocturne. The backgrounds and dungeons are somewhat drab, but that is done intentionally because of the setting in which the game takes place. The only negative side to the graphics is that sometimes the resolution is somewhat low, which can lead to problems with positioning.

Sound: 5/5 Excellent. This is one of the few successes in voice acting I've seen in a dubbed video game recently. While the voice acting isn't the best in the world, it at least portrays the characters well, and the lines aren't given with a constant tone of wooden indifference. There are a couple of voices that don't quite hit the mark, but the core cast is very well done. The music is excellent, many of the tunes fit the atmosphere, and the introduction reel by Etero Anime fits the intro scene.

Control: 5/5 Great. The controls are almost exactly as they were in SMT:N. The battle system uses the same attack number determination as well. Most controls are straight forward, although the battle system is more complex for those used to FF turn based style combat. But if you pay attention and read up on the combat, it becomes second nature after a while.

Novelty: 2/5 Below average. This is the one low point of the game. It is unfortunate that they chose to keep so many of the monsters from SMT:N. It made the game feel more like a mod than an actual self enclosed game. By keeping so much of the SMT:N system they pretty much lost all ability to consider the game a novel creation. Although DDS is a great game, if you've played nocturne, you'll find yourself saying "hey wait a minute I've seen this before" quite a bit. The plot is quite original, as is many of the items and some new skills. But for the most part, it feels like you are playing a game with 40% new material and 60% recycled material.

Overall: 5/5 It's a great game despite a few flaws. If you liked SMT:N then you'll love this game. If you hated SMT:N or found it frustratingly difficult, then you'll find this game much the same.

title: Prints Anything and Everything From Galaxy Phone; Easy to Set Up
text:
I really like this HP ENVY 6055 WIRELESS ALL-IN-ONE PRINTER (5SE16A). Finally I’m able to print anything and everything from my Samsung Galaxy S10 cell phone! To set it up with an Android phone, you need two apps from Google Play: HPSmart, and HP Print Service Plugin.

SETUP. Once you have HPSmart, you turn on the printer, open the app, and follow the prompts. The app finds the printer, helps you connect it to your home network, and takes you through the process of loading paper, installing two ink cartridges, and aligning the copier. From time to time, a prompt will tell you to press a lighted or flashing button on the printer in order to proceed.

The setup process isn’t difficult, but you should start it when you have maybe 20-30 minutes to devote to it. There are enough steps that you don’t want to get interrupted in the middle.

HPSMART APP. Something that I really love about the printer, is that I can use my phone to make it scan a document and send the document to an email address. The phone can control all of the printer functions through the HPSmart display--it just takes a tap on a virtual button. I asked the printer to print a photo from my phone’s Gallery, and it came out beautifully. The photo that I took outside my home with the phone’s camera and immediately sent to the printer also came out beautifully.

MANUAL CONTROLS. You can also control the printer manually, at least for copying. When you open the printer cover, the buttons for the number of copies and copying light up. However, this printer is easiest to control with the HPSmart app. (I need to visit the HP web site and download the full manual--the closest now is the Envy 6400 all-in-one printer manual--because the lighted buttons aren’t quite intuitive.) Other mobile devices on my home network (e.g., my iPad Air) are able to find the printer and use it like any other printer on my network.

SPEED; COPY QUALITY; INK The printer is quite fast, and the quality of the printing is excellent. The ink colors are bright and the printing is extremely crisp and clear (even with fine print). The printer uses HP 67 ink cartridges--which are definitely NOT discontinued (as another reviewer reported). My local Staples store has the ink in stock right now (July 2020).

title: Once you embrace the strange passage of time it becomes a fantastic story-heavy RPG.
text: Once you accept the rules of this game it is amazing! I had played the original ps1 persona a very long time ago so Persona 5's formula was very new to me. I almost quit playing this in the first few hours due to the strange setup of time passage. I would pause it and leave it paused for hours and then come back because the Story and style had sucked me in, but the game play was meeting extreme resistance. Time is not set up as hours, but slots, during school you will usually see clips of your day. Your playable time consists of mostly 2 time slots of afterschool and evening. If you socialize with someone it will take up a timeslot. In the begining going to a palace will have to be done after school and when you return you will be too tired to do any other activity that day.(Two of your male friends have a request involving a maid, take it as soon as possible and do everything you can to level up the maid as quickly as possible, she will help some with your time crunch) I gave this game 5 stars because it is a very great RPG and you just must accept that the passage of time is how this is structured and embrace it. Find ways to make the most of your time. Try to prepare enough that you can go all the way through a palace to its stopping point in one day, Stack quest for mementos as much as it will workout progression-wise, level up your confidants and social stats in the most productive ways possible. It will make you think about each choice you make and who you spend your time with and when. You will hate the cat early in this game as it will often tell you that you need to sleep and will not take no for an answer. This game is great for RPG fans, but it may be hard to just jump into a story heavy game that does have a lot of rules about time. I like to roam around a game for hours and explore, you can not do that in the same manner in this game, but it is a fantastic game in its own league.

title: Large 21" screen for better drawing experience
text:
I'm not a professional artist nor do I have a lot of experience with digital art, but that is one of the reasons that XP-Pen is a good choice for someone like me. Wacom rules the digital art world but for someone who is only a hobbyist when it comes to digital media, I have a hard time justifying paying the price that they charge. With that in mind, XP-Pen and Huion are the brands that I target for my budget.

Previously, I purchased a Huion Kamvas 13 and it was a great product but with my aging eyes, I needed a larger screen as even the 1080p resolution screen on that 13" screen was a little bit difficult for me to see without reading glasses. So when I had a chance to upgrade to a 21" XP-Pen, I took it.

This puts me in a situation where I am able to compare the two brands with each other. Both brands sport very similar pens and both screens have a matte surface to give the pens some friction for that "paper-like" feel. I'd say it's more like pen on paper feel, whereas I would've preferred to have more friction but it's something I think is worth training myself to get used to.

The XP-Pen drivers are on-par with the Huion drivers. Once the drivers are installed, it will show a preview of the screen layout that you have set up in Windows and it's quite easy to select the correct screen area that the pen should direct its touch to. From there, the pen buttons can be customized to macros that fit your needs and of course you can set up a different macro for each app that you use.

There are no additional macro assignable buttons on the XP-Pen screen, but there are standard OSD menu buttons at the top of the monitor, just like any other monitor you may own.

I'm happy to report that the XP-Pen drivers run alongside the Huion drivers without conflict. I have a Huion macro pad to make up for the buttons that are missing on the XP-Pen monitor.

So not being a professional artist, I do still try to spend as much time as I can to learn digital drawing and painting. In addition, I have interest in video and photo editing, so this pen tablet is great for selecting subjects using the rotoscope tool in video editor or smart select tools in image editors. Then there's 3D modeling. The pressure sensitive pen is great for sculpting in Blender and other 3D modeling programs. This is also something I'm trying to learn as well.

Despite the multitude of uses that I described above, I also don't have the desk space to devote to this 21" beast. It means that I needed a way to safely stow it. I didn't expect that I would find a carrying case for a large monitor, but to my surprise, that's exactly what I found! This [[ASIN:B099ZSDQ6V KISLANE travel carrying case]] fits the XP-Pen perfectly. It is big enough for the monitor, including its adjustable height stand and has plenty of pockets for the power adapter, pen, usb cables and my Huion macro pad. I didn't think there would be a market for people who thought "hey, it'd be great if I could bring my 24-inch iMac on my trip!", but thanks for that! Now I have a case for my 21" pen tablet.

One thing to note: I ran into an issue with inconsistent pressure with the XP-Pen drivers where I would run the pen across the scree and the darkness or width of the line would be very jittery. It was only alleviated by turning off the setting called Microsoft Ink. After my computer upgraded to Windows 11, I haven't seen this issue. So if it happens to you, try turning of that setting.

title: Possibly the worst tablet ever made
text:
I've been a professional software developer for more than twenty years, and in that time I've used a very large variety of computing devices for both personal and professional use. I don't think I've ever hated a computing device more than I hate this abomination. Actually, I can't remember actually hating any device prior to this. The touch-screen is terrible and inconsistent, and I frequently need to tap things multiple times in order to get a response.

Windows 8 might be okay if it weren't so completely locked down on the Surface RT. For instance, you cannot install any other browser; you're stuck with Internet Explorer, the worst browser available on any device, and cannot even install plugins to block spam ads and malware. The web browsing experience is truly terrible, and the design of the browser is sufficiently different from *every other browser* to make it as counter-intuitive as possible.

There is almost no software that will run on the device except what can be obtained through Microsoft's online store, which is a fresh hell that deserves it's own product review. At least with my Android devices I have broad compatibility and a wide variety of software available for just about every purpose.

The on-screen touch keyboard is clunky and poorly designed, and is at times incredibly difficult to use. For instance, trying to compile an email in GMail is pathologically difficult, since the keyboard takes up literally 75% of the screen, leaving almost no space to see what you're typing and making it incredibly difficult to scroll down to the "Send" button to actually send the email. There appears to be no support for swapping the built-in touch-screen keyboard with a better version like Swype, which is incredibly disappointing.

Attempting to connect USB devices is extremely hit or miss, and many I've tried simply do not work due to lack of "official" driver support. For instance, I purchased a "Belkin F4U047-RS USB 2.0 Ethernet Adapter" on the advice of several websites saying that they'd been able to use that specific adapter to add an Ethernet adapter to the Surface RT. Unfortunately, Microsoft has asked those websites to no longer distribute the drivers that made the device work, and have disabled the use of such drivers on the Surface RT since they are not Microsoft certified drivers, leaving me with no Ethernet and twenty dollars wasted.

I could go on for several more paragraphs, but I've wasted enough of my life on this piece of offal. If I didn't require this device to be physically present to test software builds on, I would have sent it back almost immediately.

title: Just what I needed for game sounds & Discord chat
text:
I still can’t believe the Nintendo Switch doesn’t support Bluetooth headphones out of the box … it seems like such a no-brainer. Especially for a console that has the draw of being able to take it anywhere and game!

I play my Switch in handheld mode 99.9% of the time, and usually play with the sound off 99.9% of the time so as not to bug anyone else in the house. When I play co-op games with friends and use Discord for voice chat, I have to keep my sound off then too, because I can’t hear everything. Splatfest is just not as fun without music, and how am I supposed to hear a shooting star in Animal Crossing??

I mention all of this to say that the HomeSpot Bluetooth Adapter Pro is *exactly* what I needed. The adapter allows me to pair my Switch, headphones, and phone so that I can listen to game sounds *and* be able to chat on Discord or listen to music on my phone.

The instructions are clear and easy to understand. It took me about 3 minutes to connect my Switch, headphones, and phone. Now I enjoy playing on my Switch even more because I can hear game music and sounds!

The Bluetooth adapter can also be used in docked mode. The box includes a USB-C to USB-A Adapter to connect it to the dock.

I love the form factor. The adapter plugs in flush against the bottom of the Switch. Some adapters stick out a lot, but this one is small. I’m currently using a Satisfye grip, which adds a bit of length to the Joycons, so I can rest my Switch on my lap or stomach and not have the weight of it resting on the adapter.

The only thing I am disappointed about is that the adapter doesn’t support pass through charging. The description doesn’t say that it does, but I personally didn’t realize I wouldn’t be able to charge my switch while using it. I just wanted to mention that for anyone else who might not realize.

I would love to give a higher rating, but I think "1 star" is the only way to summarize my experience with this product.

Amazon shipped quickly (as usual). I tried to put it together the night it arrived. It comes in 3 pieces: base, arm, and monitor. The only instructions were a simple diagram showing how they roughly fit together. The base and arm fit together nicely, but the arm would not snap into the monitor. I could see how it was designed to snap together, but the metal part was too large to fit into the space on the back of the monitor. I could technically place the monitor on top of the arm+base, but it was very loose and could easily fall over if bumped slightly.

I called Acer tech support, hoping there was some trick I couldn't figure out. There wasn't. After suggesting that I push harder (I had already pushed hard enough that I was worried about breaking the monitor), go back to the store for assistance (huh?), and return the entire monitor, they agreed to send a replacement part.

1.5 weeks later, I called back asking for a status update on the part. I was informed that the part hadn't been ordered (huh?) and that I could call back the next day to have it ordered (wtf?). title: Aims But Misses
text:
Physically, the mouse shape is a low, not filling a medium-sized hand, but has a nice ridge on the right side of the mouse, that almost lets the user grip it. The mouse weight is light enough for extended use. The mouse is covered with a thin coat of rubber-like material, but that material is somewhat slippy, because neither the mouse nor the coating has any texture. With the mouse shape, and coating, the mouse is not that grippy.

The buttons and scroll wheel are excellent, and well placed. The mouse wheel, unlike the rest of the mouse is very grippy, with a rubber ring around it. The extra buttons are reachable, but not in my way. I like that the extra buttons aren't large, flimsy, or heavy.

The lighting, though frustrating would be novel if it all of it could stored in the mouse. As the computer boots, the mouse shows a colored mess. The front light is a great idea. I suspect that the overall durability of the mouse has been compromised so that Corsair can have their logo light up. I worry, that the rubber material will wear off, leaving an ugly white mouse body behind. The mouse wheel lighting is a good feature, which makes it quick to find the mouse, if you take your hand from it.

The cord is braid-covered, and nice and long, but sadly, not user replaceable. Neither strain reliefs are pliable enough to function as strain reliefs. The USB plug body is excessively long, providing too long of a lever arm.

The software needs usability testing. You do things on one side of the screen, that cause buttons to appear on the other side of the screen. There are thing that are really going to need some experimentation to discover. The software itself takes up over 400mb.

It's disappointing that many settings are not saved in the mouse, leaving your computer to boot up with odd colors, and likely no stored keystrokes available.

The mouse software involving the DPI and colors is buggy.

My first day, I found a surface that made the mouse skip, which is a stark reminder that this is not a laser mouse. Standford University's excellent printed booklets made great ad-hock mousepads, but the Corsair Sabre, skips and chokes, mousing on a printed page. On a real cloth-covered mousepad, it seems to work well.

The price point for the mouse is excellent, but there's no reason why the Sabre's software and memory issues need to exist. Still, the mouse needs to be grippier, because at times the needs to lift the mouse.

title: Arcade Flight Sim in 3D With Wonky Dynamics
text:
I was excited to find a flight sim with both WWI & WWII planes for the PS3. I had hoped this would be a mix of Rise of Flight (PC) and IL-2 Sturmovik (PC or PS3) which allow you to customize the gameplay to make it as realistic or arcade like as you prefer. Unfortunately (for me), the customization is minimal and the gameplay is much like an arcade with some wonky flight dynamics and a story thrown in.

The story is told in comic form and fully voiced. Not the best voice acting or story, but still a nice touch.

The graphics and audio are nothing special. There is constant screen tearing regardless if you use 3D mode or not.

It provides 3D gaming which is nice. The text (subtitles & alt/speed) is not done right in 3D and messes with your eyes during missions...otherwise, the 3D effect is pretty well done. I played 2 missions in 3D but preferred non-3D due to the text and comfort.

Online play ... it's in the game, but I tried to find someone to battle online for two nights and found ZERO people. Don't buy this game if you are mostly or even interested in online dogfights.

If you are looking for an arcade plane game with a story and planes from WWI & WWII, then give this a try for cheap. If you are looking for something more realistic or historical, then go with IL-2 Sturmovik or Rise of Flight.

title: This capture device came with a HDMI cable, it's a lot of bang for your buck, and works great...
text:
[[VIDEOID:6fbb7930c23f2b3918bfee62b7dbdebc]] THE GOOD:
---------------
* Price. Wow, less than $20. I just reviewed another usb capture device for $60. I'm not sure it does anything better than this one, except in the looks department. This $20 version even came with a HDMI cable. What? Compared to the other, this is a crazy deal.
* Plug and Play for people familiar with these devices. If not, you'll need to learn about capture software. If using this at the PC, then a popular software people use is OBS.
* However, there are higher quality capture devices for your desktop. These little usb versions are better fro DSLR camera users who want to create a second monitor screen with their smartphones.
* Personally, a fun use case scenario for me, is turning spare phones into mini tvs.

USING YOUR SMARTPHONE TIPS:
----------------------------------------
* The type of USB adapter you use will matter. If your phone has a USB-C port, then you'll need a female USB A to USB-C adapter. If it has a micro usb port, you'll need a female USB-A to micro usb adapter. I found that the ones with a little cord are finicky. A solid one piece, cordless usb to usb-c adapter solved the issue for me. Watch my video to understand what I'm saying.
* Many USB Camera Viewer apps won't work. It's not an exact science because you're dealing with so many variables such as app version, phone brand, android version, not to mention your hardware. Some apps gave me video, but no audio, some slam you with so many ads, it's annoying unless you pay. The best paid app is USB CAMERA PRO by Shen Yao, their free version is good too, but has ads. The best free app that virtually has no ads is USB CAMERA VIEWER by Homesoft, LLC. This is the app you see in my video demo. I'm using a Pixel 6 Pro.
* If connecting a media device such as fire stick, roku, etc., you will need to bypass HDCP, and you'll have to trial and error with the different types of splitters on the market. The GOXMGO splitter in my video demo worked nicely.

THE BAD:
------------
* Well, as mentioned above. I had reviewed another usb capture device that cost $60. The only advantage it has is that there is no dangling cord, and it's a colorful red. In terms of function, I don't see an advantage. At $20, you get the usb capture device and a HDMI cable. This is an amazing deal compared to the other. This product is 5-Stars!

title: Wow!
text:
If you're looking for a workout program for the Wii, this is it!

PROS:
+ each workout is about 30 minutes, which includes 5 minutes for warm ups and 5 minutes for cool downs.
+ the workouts are more fun than the previous ones
+ you definitely feel the burn after each workouts
+ your avatar looks a lot more human than in Personal Trainer. I hated the shape of the head in the original game. This one is much nicer
+ the game uses the resistance band in different ways which helps add resistance and make the workout harder (which is good)
+ you can now weigh yourself directly through the game if you have the balance board
+ journal, trophies, and goals help you stay motivated and make better decisions throughout the day

CONS:
- the workouts that were included in the original EA Sports Active Personal Trainer are not included here
- warm ups and cool downs don't use the wii remote so it doesn't actually sense if you've started or not
- if you lose the beat (or if you made the motion and the game doesn't recognize it), it's often hard to re-gain that rhythm. Your next moves end up being opposite of what is shown on the screen (if i'm lifting my arm, it shows me as lowering my arm on the screen). This is very annoying but not a huge deal ultimately
- graphics are still not great, but let's face it - nobody buys this 'game' for the graphics :-)

With the Personal Trainer, I saw results after one month. This 'game' is even better than the previous one so I'm excited to see what this next month of training will do :)

title: Near-Perfect  Faux Crocodile Cover With Intriguing Stand Design
text:
I love the look and feel of this VERSO "DARWIN" CROCCO standing cover for the Kindle Fire HD 8.9" tablet. Red is my favorite color, and the faux crocodile texture is really fun.

This cover holds the tablet firmly with silicone-enhanced elastic corner bands (patent pending). The bands have a rubbery material on the underside of the elastic that grips the surface beneath it, so the tablet does not slide around inside the cover or want to fall out. (I have screen protector film on my tablet, which seems like a good idea when a tablet is held in place by elastic bands rather than a hard plastic shell. This [[ASIN:B009NHU556 3-Pack Ultra-Clear Screen Protector)]] is easy to apply, and you get three chances to get it on right.)

The cover's built-in stands are quite intriguing. There are two of them attached to the inside of the front cover. One stand supports the tablet at a low angle for typing; the other supports it more or less upright for watching movies. Both provide comfortable viewing angles. The stands themselves are flat, microfiber-covered pieces that match the rest of the cover's interior. You pick the stand angle you want, and open out the appropriate stand. The stand is connected to the cover on top and also with a ribbon underneath, so that the stand converts into a triangular support for your tablet. This design is very clever, and I would consider it perfect if I hadn't already tried the [[ASIN:B009X0167Y Marware Vibe Standing Case]], which is a little easier to set up and offers more viewing angles.

This Verso "Darwin" Crocco cover has an elastic band that holds it tightly closed inside a book or tote bag, as well as an automatic magnetic wake/sleep feature. For the wake/sleep feature to work, you must insert your tablet with the camera at the left and the charging port at the right. This I don't like, because the charging port ends up at the tablet's bottom edge when you use the stands. This means you are limited to using the low-angle stand whenever your tablet is plugged in, because the plug contacts the table top. (With the Marware Vibe cover, the charging port ends up at the tablet's top edge, so you can use the tablet at any angle when it's plugged in.)

According to the accompanying retail literature, this Verso "Darwin" Crocco cover is "compatible" with the Kindle Fire HD 8.9", the Nook HD+, "and more". Because the cover holds the tablet with elastic bands, it should fit any tablet near in size to the large Fire or the large Nook. However, it is definitely too small for an iPad 2.

For me, it's difficult to choose between the Marware Vibe cover and the Verso "Darwin" cover. But in the end, as usually happens, good looks win out. My 8.9" Kindle Fire HD tablet is going to stay in the red faux-crocodile-skin cover, which is eye-catching, looks and feels luxurious, and is extremely well made.

title: My first impression is a good one.
text:
This 75% 84 key (tenkeyless) keyboard with Gateron Blue switches was bought to replace a several year old Das Keyboard (with Cherry Blue switches) configured for Mac. There is nothing wrong with the Das Keyboard except that it has that annoying array of number keys on the right side which throws off its ergonomic fitness for typing, making me have to constantly look at it and sometimes miss keystrokes from being off center. (The previous 104 key Das Keyboard was initially installed to replace the OEM Apple keyboard with its Chiclet style membrane switches which severely limits my typing speed and makes me feel like I'm typing in boxing gloves. I also replaced the Apple mouse which has all the ergonomic fitness of a wet half used bar of Ivory soap.)

It is advertised as a gaming keyboard. Fine. Gamers need a reliable fast device, capable of prolonged constant pounding with good tactile and auditory feedback. This is fast and I'll get back with you in a few years as to reliability.

However people who write also need a good keyboard, but without the bells and whistles. Which is my reasoning for immediately pressing the Fn+Light keys to turn off backlighting. I'm still getting used to the feel of it but my first impression is entirely favorable. After just a few hundred words I find that I've entirely stopped looking at my fingers while typing, which is a very good prognostic sign for the future.

The keys have sufficient resistance for fast typing, and the Gateron Blue switches have just a bit more 'jiggle' than Cherry Blue switches. I hadn't anticipated this but it makes for a little more clicky sound and reminds me of the early electric typewriters and Apple II-e keyboards. This is not a bad thing but will take a few minutes to get used to.

I'd prefer Green switches to Blue due to their greater resistance, but apparently there just isn't the market for these switches in Apple users, especially when paired with tenkeyless design.

title: Very good desktop replacement system
text:
I decided to purchase a new laptop after my old laptop was taken over by the family for a variety of tasks. I was mostly happy with the system I had, a nice HP Pavilion system with a decent feature set, but considering that it is 2-3 years old and does not run everything I want to run anymore I wanted to make my upgrade to a new system worthwhile. In researching I found this particular system and I pounced on it, as I found it at a steal of a price. It is not perfect, but there is an awful lot in this notebook.

My very first notebook was a Sony Vaio, so I imagined that this would be familiar territory. I was greatly mistaken, as things have changed dramatically since then, mostly for the better.

First off, this is a fast system with lots of expansion room. This is very important to me because I do a little bit of everything - I do some gaming, I write software, I write short stories, I hang out online. I am not considered a power user in that regard so an AlienWare ultra-high-powered expensive gaming rig is not really what I need, but I don't need an entry-level system that is good for little more than checking email either. My needs are for a well-rounded machine that can do most things well. This notebook fits that need.

I am especially impressed with the bright, large screen. I do occasionally toss a movie DVD into the system and treat myself to a private showing of whatever movie I have chosen, and all of that screen real estate makes for an enjoyable experience.

As for DVDs... With Blu-ray built into this system, watching new media movies is not a concern. That's a very nice plus.

I like the fact that this system has two individual hard drives instead of one large one, as I want to create a dual-boot system and not wipe out the whole thing. I was unaware of this when I purchased the system, thinking I had a unified drive, though that was an oversight - the labeling and documentation are clear.

The system comes with 3 GB RAM, expandable to 4. Up to this point things seem to be comfortable in that amount of room.

My first task was to strip off the trial software I don't want or need, which includes MS Office 2007, Webroot SpySweeper and Norton 360. Some people will appreciate these applications but for me they are in the way and clutter the hard drive with unneeded stuff. If these applications were full-release apps with more than 30-90 days of use, I likely would keep them all but in my case I already have licensed software to use that meet the same needs.

The documentation states that there is a firewire port, a VGA port and an S-Video port, and it took searching the web for a manual with technical diagrams to reveal that these are hidden on the right side, under a cover. Nothing that came with the system says where to find those ports, and the cover that conceals these ports blends in well enough to truly hide them - I did not find them without help.

Even more concerning to me is the number and placement of the USB ports. There is one on the back, and two on the right side close to the front edge. I work with an external mouse but I use the built-in keyboard, and I am right-handed. So, if I plug anything at all into those two front edge USB ports, the cords interfere with my mouse use. The solution, then, is to plug a 4-port hub in the back and then plug everything in there.

The built-in speakers are all right, though nothing special. If you want better speakers plug them in and all is well. That said, the built-ins are quite acceptable for most use. You would not want to use them for listening to symphony music, of course, but they're just fine for gaming and general music.

I am very pleased with the graphics. My litmus test for gaming is Neverwinter Nights 1 & 2, and both of these play quite smoothly. I have not loaded up Unreal Tournament 3 yet - that's next - but it should have no difficulty at all with that game.

I did run into one problem that required a call to Sony technical support. Because Sony does not include recovery media with their systems, it is up to the owner to create them and Sony makes it easy with included utilities. There are two options for creating the media - 1 dual-layer DVD or 2 single-layer DVDs. I chose the single dual-layer and after an hour of writing and grinding, the DVD ejected and the system said the creation failed. Assuming it was the target medium, I tried again with the same result. I called Sony thinking I needed to request the recovery DVDs and the technician told me that the single-layer DVD creation would work but that a glitch with this specific model prevents the dual-layer media creation from working. When I used two single-layer DVDs, everything created without a hitch.

This brings up a good point. Some places provide horrible service with operators that no one can understand. I got through in a reasonable amount of time (it was 5am but I still had a brief wait) and I got a very pleasant fellow who was very easy to understand (he did have and accent, though I could not place it) and was very helpful.

This is my desktop replacement system. It does everything I need it to do, it works well and it has a good feature set. It is certainly not perfect, but even at full price it is a good deal for what you get. It is NOT a top-of-the-line gaming rig but it's not marketed as such. If you want a good well-rounded machine, give this one some consideration.

title: Great To Have In Case Of Power Outage
text:
When it comes to fish, power outages can be stressful. One thing that is most important is maintaining and oxygen level in the water of the tank. This pump is great for that.

HOW TO CHARGE
You take out the pump door and it leads to the USB charger. It is a micro USB port, not a Type C. It took a few hours to charge up fully.

HOW TO TURN ON
You press the solid screen top on the power button. That will turn on the unit. The bar at the top will light up green.

LEGS
The legs on this are rubberized to reduce traveling and vibration.

CLIP
There is a clip on the back of this pump so you can clip it or hang it instead of laying it on a table top.

HOW TO CHANGE
If you hit the power button a 2nd time, you will get intermittent setting which has the air flow for a bit then shut off again intermittently. A blue light at the end of the green bar will light up to show you that.

HOW TO SHUT OFF
A 3rd press to that power screen will turn off the unit.

CAREFUL
Be careful because after you shut off the pump, it won't turn on again for a while.

DOES IT PERFORM WELL?
This definitely performs well. I have a variety of tanks, so I can put in the air stone and tubing (with check valve) in one tank for a bit and then I can move it to the other (being careful not to turn it off).
I leave it on intermittent so it saves battery power.

NOISY?
This is not at all noisy, in fact I have plug in pumps which are noisier.

PROBLEM
This is VERY easy to accidentally turn on. You have to be very careful to not only carry it but also store it where it won't be accidentally pressed into the on position.

BATTERY LIFE

The bag says that these are " proudly produced in Purina owned facilities in USA" and that the label is "Printed in USA". In addition to that, the bag says, "no artificial FD&C colors", but in ingredients has a vague "added color" listed- yet doesn't say where the coloring is derived from. That bothers me. Anyway, thought I would mention it. If that isn't a concern..

These are pretty well priced for a 10 count (2lbs, 4oz) package of rather large treats. If you have a large dog like I do, the size will likely appeal to them. These have an aroma, and I think they smell pretty darn good. I didn't try them (tempted), but know the odor was enticing to my and my cats who were nearby and caught a whiff.

We have dark carpeting, fur covered, not sure if there was any dye stains left behind. I didn't notice, but O also think there wasn't enough time given how quickly my dogs munched these away.

So I gave them one yesterday, and they seem fine in terms of bowel and tummy. No issue, thankfully. I will likely finish off the bag, but slowly. The calorie content is really a concern for me (and I need to look further into Purina company to see where ingredients are sourced).

Other than that, if size seems appropriate to your dog, and the prices seems right.. go for it.

3/5 rating because of super high calories, no specific source for coloring, no clarity on where ingredients comes from. However, they are a good size, reasonably priced, smell really good, and my dogs enjoyed them. Hope this helps!!

title: Really cute, cat-friendly, but misses the target
text:
We bought two of these birds for our kitty cats. I think Hartz could have done better though.

The look is great - like a mini-pheasant, which immediately grabbed both cats' attention.
The chirp is very loud. I SAID, THE CHIRP IS VERY LOUD! At least ours were! Yikes - sort of like a bird with a megaphone! It got on my nerves, but didn't seem to bother the cats that I could tell. (They might have been wishing for ear plugs, but who knows.) Annoyance factor for me was slightly less than the battery-operated chimp with the clapping cymbals (but I can take the batteries out of the chimp).

Now the downside - the interest lasts about as long as it is making noise.
It makes noise upon impact with something, and it takes a fairly hard impact to get it chirping. Slapping against your hand is the best way, or slapping it on a hard surface. However, unless your cats are different than the two we have, the cats will not be able to turn on the chirping themselves. You know how cats like to grab and toss things like this type of toy into the air? You'd think the mechanism would have been made sensitive enough to turn on when it hit the floor. Not so - the cats are not strong enough to turn this bird's sound on. It will take YOUR interaction.

Now, I love to play with the cats and don't have a problem with it. However, I thought this would be a cute toy to keep them busy while I was on the computer. Instead, it was either brought back to me to slap/throw it again (yes, one of our cats acts like a dog and retrieves toys), or was left on the floor as soon as it stopped chirping. They did carry them around the first day or two, but that novelty wore off uber fast. Right now, I think one is laying dormant under our china closet, and I don't know where Bird 2 is. The cats don't really care either. They lost interest right away.

If Hartz revamps these and makes the chirp-triggering mechanism more sensitive, then this toy would be a winner. You can't deny it looks great. But, the cats got as bored as I did, because the noise is part of the appeal. It goes silent, then it is no longer a prize to be obtained. So, I think you can do better than this toy for your favorite kitty.

title: Definitely Cuts Down on Debris Getting Tracked; Wish it Was Larger
text:
We have two cats and two litter boxes (one for the basement and one for the main level of the house). Our cats are good girls and have always used their litter boxes, but the issue we have seen is that they tend to track bits of litter from the box out of the room and all over the floor and carpet close by. It’s an annoyance and we have to vacuum more often as a result. This mat has helped tremendously, though it would be more helpful if it was even larger.

The mat itself is a web of rubbery fibers and doesn’t look dissimilar from a very dense loofa, only close up. The webbing is designed to catch bits of litter from the cats’ feet before they leave the area, so that cleanup is easier and involves shaking the mat and cleaning in the immediate vicinity. It does this well.

However, it is not perfect and our cats do track stuff out anyway. We have a larger mat we have been using on one of the litter boxes and the extra size is enough to reduce quite a bit more stuff that gets tracked. It also is not perfect but it does help.

The cats do not seem to be deterred by the mat, and the mat is not unattractive. It’s about the same color as a loofa.

This mat does a decent job and it’s definitely cutting down stuff getting tracked from the litter box. I just wish it was larger.

title: Solid Single Player RPG
text:
Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning is the first offering from 38 Studios, the game development company founded a few years ago by former Major League pitcher Curt Schilling. The game's world and lore has had substantial creative input from the best-selling fantasy author R.A. Salvatore, and has also had substantial input from several well-known game designers and developers at Big Huge Games, a company that 38 acquired from THQ a few years ago. In a nutshell, the game has a good deal of quality development power behind it, and it shows.

38 Studios is mostly focused on MMORPG development, and has a project already in the works. In some ways, this is reflected in this game, because the game often plays like a single player MMORPG. This has good and bad aspects, and may not appeal to all gamers, for the reasons I describe below.

First, graphically the game feels like World of Warcraft. That is -- the graphics are more of the cartoon/stylized variety than the more realistic kind found in single player games like The Witcher 2 or Skyrim. The color scheme of the world also tends toward bright, vivid colors in a way that reminds one of WoW's artistic approach. As a result, less of an emphasis is placed on extremely high-resolution textures, and more on overall feel and style. It's inevitable that this will turn off some single-player game fans, who prefer games like Skyrim with realistic, high-resolution graphics.

Second, the progression in the game is not as linear as something like Mass Effect, but instead features zone progression -- as in, you start in one area/zone, complete the quests in that zone, and then are moved on to the next zone, where there is another pack of quests. The NPC enemies/monsters in these zones do not scale, unlike a game like Skyrim, so as your character levels, the open-world monsters will become trivial in earlier zones. In that sense, although it is more of an open world game than something like Mass Effect or Dragon Age: Origins, in that you are actually moving around in the open world rather than porting between snippets of it, it nevertheless plays more like an MMO in this respect than a game like Skyrim. I do not see this as a drawback, but some players may.

Beyond these, the game plays like a good, polished single player RPG. It does feel like a console game at times, even when playing on the PC, due to the control scheme, the camera angles, and the way the character moves and feels -- this is becoming fairly common in computer RPGs these days, and similar kinds of issues were present in Skyrim's menus system as well.

Combat is probably the highlight of the game, and in this aspect it does not play like an MMORPG at all, or like a traditional RPG (as the first Dragon Age did) but like an action RPG. The combat is fast-paced and fluid, the character is responsive, and the ways and means are quite varied. The player can choose a melee warrior setup, a rogue/stealth setup or a mage type setup, or any combination of the above, in going about combat. The game makes it very easy to change one's approach (for a smallish in-game currency fee) to suit a different kind of combat style, and the game offers a substantial variety of weapons and skills that all can be used to alter one's approach to combat and how one essentially plays the game. One point worthy of mention is that the game's default difficulty setting is probably too easy for advanced gamers, and the hard setting probably feels like a normal mode to hardcore gamers -- at some point perhaps a true nightmare mode will be released for hardcore gamers.

The story is well-done, as one would expect with the input of someone like Salvatore, and functions as a good introduction to this new setting and world. The game accomplishes this credibly and well from the very beginning, with an interesting, fully-blown world and lore revealed gradually to the player. The larger implications of the story are also fairly interesting, particularly once one advances along the quest lines a bit further. The voice over dialogue scenes are not going to be confused with a BioWare game, but at the same time the overall game design for Amalur is much more open world than is the case for a BioWare game, and the voice over dialogue is present but much less of a focus. The use of lorestones and other means to tell the story is an interesting and enjoyable approach, in my opinion.

In all, this is a very good effort as the first release from 38 Studios. It's polished, deep, long and fun to play. Hopefully we will see more of this interesting world and setting in future games from 38 -- maybe even in the MMORPG they are currently developing.

title: It's cheap because you don't get much for it
text:
This (G413 SE TKL) is a very basic mechanical keyboard with no bells and whistles. If you're looking for something inexpensive in a mechanical kb, this is possibly worth considering, but you can get a lot more for just a little more money. (Check ratings and reviews on a site like PCMag or Wirecutter.)

The good: it's compact, and the mechanical keys are ok. It has key backlighting (with brighness adjustment, see below). That's it.

Not for the not so good:

The keys are a bit stiff, and typing on this is going to take an adjustment. My much more expensive Razer keyboard is a whole lot smoother and has a significantly better feel. (I no longer recommend Razer because their Synapse software is horrible, and is blocked by some corporate IT departments because of perceived vulnerabilities.)

This is not an RGB keyboard (no colors): all you can do is adjust key brightness (using FN + F1/F2) through a few preset levels. You can't customize anything.

(Note that some reviewers complain about the side-by-side key symbols: that's what you get in a backlit mech keyboard, because the middle can't be lit, being blocked by the post. IMO you get used to this pretty quickly.)

Overall I can't recommend this, and I'm still considering returning it to Amazon. I bought this because I needed something "good enough" in a hurry, and it was available and on sale. In retrospect I should have spent a little more to get a better keyboard.
