title: She Sat With Her Head In The Bag Frozen For Five Minutes
text:
We have a funny cat. She is pretty easy going and she tends to like everything except for turkey. Our last cat would not eat anything except turkey. When I saw this set, I thought it would be perfect. THAT was an understatement.

BAGS
The bags are sealed at the top and I cut them open with scissors so I can have the longest edges to pull when opening later and sealing with the zipper seal on them. They are pretty thick and keep the food dry.

FOOD QUALITY
The food quality is excellent. The shrimp and fish smell very appetizing, and the chicken also smells good.

DOES THE CAT LIKE IT?
Well, the cat went so berserk when I opened the bag of shrimp, she literally crammed her entire head into the bag, locked her jaw on the edge and refused to budge for FIVE MINUTES. I was laughing so hard, I could not stand it. She would not budge.

Finally I got her to let me in enough to push her head out, as her jaw was locked on the bag. She was not letting go. When I gave her shrimp, she leaped and danced so much, I could not believe it. She also did the same for the fish. The chicken she likes to, but the fish make her crazy.

WHAT DO I USE THESE FOR?
These are tidbits. I use these for giving our cat a snack to make her feel happy when she comes in from outside at night, or when dinner is late, or other reasons. I only give her about four or five pieces at a time, except when she knocks the bag out of my hand and manages to get her head stuck again.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These foods are VERY appetizing. Our cat loves to eat, but she rarely goes THIS nuts over food. She has loved all of the fish, and even liked the chicken too.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. These bags don't look like much, but they are freeze dried so they hold more than they seem to.

I tried to get a photo of this crazy cat with her head in the bag, but I couldn't. She held me prisoner.

Prices are a little high for this device compared to normal wifi routers but I couldn't put a price tag on a kid safe network along with easy to use Parental Controls. Shop for the best prices. I'm a avid Amazon shopper but I did find this elsewhere. There's also something to be said for an easy installation. No computer necessary. It's completely installed from your smart phone. Just follow the instructions. It's that easy!

The new generation 2 eero systems comes with an eero and additional beacons. As to the number of beacons that are needed, they provide recommendations but this will depend on the structure and layout of your home. The other thing to consider is the entry point of your homes internet.

Our two-story home is pretty square, constructed of your basic framing materials and drywall. I had previously run our cable internet to a centralized broom closet on the main level of the home about a year ago. It was a great location for our previous router. Having said that, installation of the main eero gave me similar to slightly improved performance throughout the house. I'm not sure if I really needed any additional beacons but I had purchased the recommended 1 eero + 2 beacons for a home with 2-4 bedrooms. With the simple installation of 1 beacon I was able to improve the "fair" wifi connection of a computer in our bonus room to "excellent". Improving download speeds marginally from 25 Mbps to 30 Mbps. Similar speeds could be reached from the mailbox as determined with fast.com. The second beacon still remains in the box.

title: One giant step backwards for gaming-kind
text:
At first glance, Lightbringer: The Next Giant Leap for Mankind seems to be a standard hero scenario where the main character saves his crew mates and salvages the first manned mission to Mars. Unfortunately, the plot is made overly difficult by design, and the puzzles are beset with problems.

Instead of being innovative as intended, the alien language used throughout the game is actually a frustrating plot device. Since we're on the first manned mission to Mars, and presumably the first human contact with extra-terrestrials, how can the ship's computer have access to a complete database of the alien language? A much better plot development would be to discover and learn the language on the way, instead of having unexplained total access from the start.

Some of the puzzles are very simple, others exceptionally difficult, and still more ridiculously repetitive -- one puzzle in particular has to be completed nine separate times to advance the game. Many of the puzzles involve translating the alien language, and since you can't access the language translator screen and view alien writing simultaneously, you're forced to use pen and paper to complete translations from alien to English.

Even more unfortunate is a serious glitch that occurs when switching CDs, which causes the game to auto-load even though you're already running the application -- it's a bug that completely halts progression in the game. Even though a patch is available, you still need to download it in order to finish the game, a fact some gamers may not know, or, be able to do if they don't have ready access to the Internet.

The game has some interesting video sequences, but includes far too many of the character simply walking -- up and down stairs, through corridors, and down shafts, which cause the action and plot to unfold very slowly. Combined with the space-based soundtrack, the presentation is likely to put some gamers to sleep. A trip to Mars may well be a giant leap for mankind, but this adventure certainly isn't one for gamers.

I had a very specific need for this style of bowl, and it surprisingly met that need. I have two young adult cats that I recently adopted. We already have 2 dogs and a cat and we knew that the transition would be slow. I set the new cats up in my office with all their needs. Door closed so the resident fur balls can sniff through door with new furballs. Then, at some point every day I close off the resident animals in part of the house and let the new kitties roam the other part of the house. This includes a sunroom with a screen door. After roaming around awhile, I close them off in the sunroom (had lots of windows, and totally outfitted with floor to ceiling climbers. Cat dream house!). When I do this, I make sure they have some food and water out there with them. I need the food and water containers to be easy to handle, and preferably something I can grab all at once to empty/clean/refill. That is where this set of elevated bowls come in.

The bowls are ceramic but light weight. I needed this. I did not want heavy for my very specific use. The bowls are small but effective-- again, exactly what I needed for my specific use. The framework holds the bowls securely and is easy to grab the whole thing-- perfect for my needs. So.. so far it has met and exceeded my expectations.

I use much larger, heavier bowls as the main food bowls any other time-- especially in a multi cat household (prior to adopting these cats, we had recently lost our 2 geriatric babies at 18+ years old.). This would not be something I would use as sole feeding station unless I had one small cat. Basically, know what you need, the size that you need, and the degree of weight you prefer for your bowls.

I mainly use [[ASIN:B002GOYU0O 12 pc Velcro Ties Reausable Electrical Wire Cable Strap]], which meet most of my needs. I also use these and like them a lot.

Where these come in handy, and even augment my preferred strap, is they are nearly immovable once you tie them to a brace of other anchoring point. For example, if you are setting up with a keyboard, the stand makes a good anchor point for cross-stage cable runs. This is especially true of Z-style stands like the [[ASIN:B0002F6JH6 On Stage 2 Tier Folding Z Keyboard Stand]] (although X-style stands work well). This does take some pre-planning because you do not want to interfere with other musicians or, worse, create trip hazards.

Because you loop the narrow end through the eyelet on the wider end and pull this strap has more holding strength than someone who is only running cables on stage and in a studio will ever need. Frankly, I augmented my preferred brand and model with these because of cost - and they are worth every penny. At 8" you can safely run more than a few instrument, speaker and microphone cables through one anchored to a frame like the Z-stand I mentioned above, and still keep the strap sufficiently loose to prevent stretching or breaking cables run through it.

title: Easy setup, works well.
text:
Update: After like 2 months of use, it's having a meltdown for some reason. I keep it hooked into a surge protector and we've had no storms so it's not electrical on my end. This thing beeps often and spins around in full circles and since it wasn't designed to work in a full circle- it throws litter out the front all over the place when it does a full circle. Eventually I can get it to stop and go back to it's normal position but a couple hours later I hear non stop beeping and see it making circles and throwing litter out. This things gone crazy!

This was very easy to set up and it works well, with no major complaints. It also works without the app for those who don't use apps for things like this. I pushed the four feet in, put the tray in the bottom, filled it with litter, put the scent thing in the tray, and plugged it in and it cycled it to level the litter and the litter is like perfectly level once that's done. The next couple of days a couple of cats have gone #1 in it and it did a good job at sifting it into the tray in the bottom and I notice no smell around the box at all. The cats still currently prefer one of their old boxes as they hate change, but I'm hoping they realize this box is always clean and go to it in time.

SO functionality, this waits a bit after your cat is out and then it rotates very quietly to one side to dump the waste into the bottom and rotates a bit back the other way to level the litter. If you put your hand up to the doorway of it in this cycle, it will stop until it's sure there are no cats in/ around the box- great safety feature that works well.

This box looks nice and is well enough made. I would point out that it's maybe best suited for a small to medium size cat. It's not a tiny box and a large cat could fit in there but it won't be that roomy and our big boy seems to love to stretch out as he does his business so I think he'll probably never touch this box but the two smaller cats will possibly. So my recommendation is to keep at least a box or so in the house if you have multiple cats. This box does not count as more than one for multi cats, it still counts as just one box. Cats that are territorial might be upset by there only one box and start spraying around the house. Don't blame them if this happens, it's your fault for not having researched it first. Cats and their litterboxes are a delicate ecosystem that if you upset it, causes chaos. So be careful whatever you do or you'll upset the balance and have spraying everywhere.

Overall this is a pretty nice-looking, well-made, functional box, I do recommend it if you understand what you're getting into. There's always the possibility that your cat will want nothing to do with it so always have at least one box available.

title: So much better than my Ronin S!
text:
I own a DJI Ronin S which I use with my Sony A7 series cameras (an A7S and A7Rii). It worked well enough, but after trying this Crane 3 Lab, I'm blown away and ready to sell my Ronin for this.
For starters, I love the ergonomics of the extra handle. Being able to hold onto it with 2 hands and shift from the handle to the pistol grip makes using this thing far more stable than trying holding just the pistol with both hands. It also makes it easy to pass and shift to a low angle mode, as well as seamlessly pass it to another person easily for those really impossible looking tracking shots (thought a window, down a staircase, etc). I'm also really impressed with the buttons and controls- if you've got a USB cable controlling your camera, there's a lot more you can easily access right from the gimbal without touching the camera than you can with the DJI Ronin S. With the Sony cameras, unfortunately, you can't control the focus motor of an automatic lens with the follow focus wheel... that's a limitation of the camera since Sony doesn't have that protocol in their USB remote interface. Other features work perfectly, however, and I've been told that other cameras like Canon and Nikon work with the focus control as well (this is something I'm hoping Sony changes in the future, but for now I'll just rely on auto-focus during gimbal shots).
Another HUGE improvement over other stabilizers is the ability to LOCK the axis motors in place. This is a fantastic tool to help when balancing (you can lock the other 2 axis and work on balancing them one by one, rather than holding the other positions in place as you work backwards like on the Ronin), and its also great to lock it in place when you are powered down and carrying it around- I've found that when taking a break with my Ronin, it is always awkward to walk around with it since the camera can flop and swing around as I walk. The Crane 3 doesn't have that problem if you just lock the motors in place with a little red switch.
Honestly, I wish I would have waited just a little bit longer before buying my Ronin S so that I could see how much better this is. The app is honestly just OK, I've heard people say they like the DJI app better and I would probably have to agree with that, but this just does everything else so much better that it I'd still say it is worth it in the end. The crane 2 is easier to balance in my experience, more forgiving (less crazy vibrating when the gimbals shifts out of balance), has better features and ergonomics and overall just seems to do a better job.
I STRONGLY recommend it if you are shopping around between those two options.

title: Saved The Lives Of My Rainbows- VERY Thankful For This
text:
EDIT FEB 3 2023
My rainbows are still doing great. The ones who were on their way out are full of energy and swimming around with gusto. If I didn't know for a fact they were not doing well,, I would be tempted to think I imagined it. All of the fish in this tank are more energetic than ever. Even my kids have commented.

Just wanted to update for anyone interested.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
--------
I have had aquariums for quite a few years. Recently, due to some issues with a nearby tower, tanks on one wall have developed some issues and they have been nearly impossible to remedy. I tried everything, including cleaning out the entire tank and replacing the fish.

The direct result of the problem nearby is high increase in parasites. Nothing was working. This was hitting all of us including other pets and us humans too.

Once we got some remediation going on our house, this one tank was giving me issues. I lost all of my fish that I raised from babies and then lost another school and was down to two. I got one last school after cleaning out my tanks and revamping, but once again evidence of parasite activity was starting and I was really frustrated.

I saw this UV filter and got it right away. I had two fish which were already showing signs that they would not likely make it past the following week.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a pretty generic box. It has everything you need inside. You have to put the suction cups in the back and then choose your water distribution and assemble that.

ASSEMBLY
I decided instead of heavy current that I would turn this on the lowest flow I could and opt for the sprinkling spout on top of the water.

MY TANK SET UP
I have a 75 gallon tank which has two 110 filters and two heaters in it- one on each end. I also have a circulation pump for waves so the rainbows can swim for exercise.

HOW I USED THIS
After putting this in the water, I turned it on 24 hour mode for a week. The gentle stream is perfect for adding oxygen to the water. After the first week, I used the timer to put it on 8 hours a day mode. After a few more weeks, I will probably go to 4 hours a day mode.

WATER CHANGES
When doing water changes, I always turn off and unplug my units. I do water changes every week or every other week depending on how things are going.

ALGAE
I did not get this for algae as I have a very hungry algae eater so he polishes off any algae that grows. I find myself harvesting from my other 6 tanks to put in for him to eat anyway. I can not say that this is stopping algae growth because he never lets it get very far.

SUCTION
So far the suction cups are great. They are tricky to get into the slots on the back though. Take your time. It eventually works out, but can be frustrating.

CLEANING
This is easy to take apart and it is easy to replace the bulb when it is time. I have not tried to get one yet, but will look for one as back up soon.

DID IT HELP?
Here is what has me so excited I am near tears when I talk about it. I have a beautiful tank of rainbows from all over. When they started dying again, I could not believe it. My filters were all cleaned out, the tank was balanced and I was doing weekly water changes.

Still my fish that were dying were starting to show they were on their way out. It was just a matter of time before the whole school would be gone.

After running this 24 hour mode for several days, I was shocked to see a change in my fish. They were very active and energetic. The two fish that were hanging near the top and side were swimming a little more than they were. By the end of the week, All of the fish were behaving normal and energetic and none of them were acting sick.

It is the end of the 2nd week and so far all of the fish are showing beautiful color, acting all normal and full of life and for the first time since this nightmare began, they are doing well. I hope this continues.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This UV filter has been a godsend. My fish rarely have recovered from this parasite problem caused by a nearby tower. I can not go into it, but I know that is what happened without a doubt. This is a great filter

MY RATING
FIVE STARS does not seem high enough for my excitement about this filter I am really thankful to have this and so far it has turned around my tank for which I am thankful.

title: The best Call of Duty game I've played yet
text:
I am a huge fan of World at War, finding the zombies, multiplayer and single player to all be excellent game modes. I was also very impressed by Call of Duty 4's single player and multiplayer, but found myself very let down by a short, offensive and unentertaining single player campaign in MW2, coupled with a buggy multiplayer experience that I gave up on within a few months of purchasing the game. (For a long list of my complaints, see the Amazon review I wrote for MW2: http://www.amazon.com/review/R2ATUPNS1NWWKR/ref=cm_cr_rdp_perm )

I was tentatively hopeful that Black Ops would provide a more enjoyable experience. I was blown away by how good this game is. First, if you view my MW2 review, every single one of the key issues/suggestions I had has been fixed/implemented in Black Ops. Beyond that, the single player is longer, more entertaining and more interesting than MW2. The multiplayer feels more like COD4 and COD:WaW than MW2, which is a very good thing in my book. However, the game does borrow many of the ideas, perks and tweaks that MW2 implemented, which results in the best COD multiplayer experience I have seen yet.

Zombies also makes a return in COD:BO, with two full fledged maps, as well as a hidden game (Dead Ops Arcade) and the classic game Zork both being accessible through a PC terminal hidden in the main menu of the game.

All said and done, a fan of the single player will find that the intel, variable difficulties and enjoyable campaign will provide over a dozen hours of entertainment. I know first hand that zombies alone can provide dozens and dozens hours of entertainment, and the multiplayer is the best online FPS experience I have had on the 360 to date. (I consider it superior to the past COD games, as well as Halo, Gears of War and Battlefield games.)

I've spent well over 250 hours on both COD4 and COD:WaW, and I highly expect to find even more enjoyment and reasons to keep playing with Call of Duty: Black Ops. While not all game types will align with everyone's tastes, I fully expect there to enough here for every fan of first person shooters to be able to find enough entertainment to justify a purchase.

title: ATTENTION! Do you like to play with friends online? Not so fast...
text:
A lot has been said about this game and many of the things I agree with.
I waited over a decade for Diablo III (as many of us did) and I held my breath for a port which, when it was
announced it would be coming to consoles, I was very excited!
There have been many games like this that I love (Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance 1 & 2, Champions of Norrath 1 & 2, Marvel's Ultimate Alliance 1 & 2, etc) even the "not so very good ones" (Sacred 2, Dungeon Hunter: Alliance).
All I can say about Diablo III is that I've been enjoying it since I got it and I would recommend it except...

YOU CANNOT CONNECT TO PLAY/INVITE YOUR FRIENDS!

This is a huge problem if you want to play NON-LOCAL. I bought this game so I could play with my brothers who live in a different state and we always received this awesome message "Error: There was a problem joining the game."
We tried for over an hour. The online connectivity function is broken and it is a problem that Blizzard has to fix.
I thought they would have learned from their PC troubles but apparently not.

Bottom line: The game is great fun! Single and Local Co-op works fine. Online play with friends does not or has not been.
Until this is fixed, I would say this game is incomplete and is not worth the full price.

I don't usually write reviews but when its a huge bug/mistake like this, it should be publicly known.

**UPDATE** After many hours online, I found that many people were having the same problem. There is a "temporary fix" you can do manually and then inviting your friends to play is possible. Apparently all you have to do is disable your Media Server and your UPNP. The way you do that is by going into your Network Settings>Internet Connection and then choose Disable when those options come up so anyone who's had this problem, that "fixes" it, but its still on Blizzard to properly patch it.

They are minor issues that would not prevent me from buying this strap again but hopefully, the manufacturer will read this and take the issues under consideration when they design any future models. The issues I had were one, the directions were a little complicated and it took me a few minutes to get the strap put together and on my head correctly. I couldn't figure out how to attach the top strap (over or under the sides?) Two, the strap was more comfortable than the one that came with the Oculus but not as tight as I would have liked and I was still able to see light around the bottom (over my nose). I did purchase a sweat band to wear underneath the Oculus and now I have a nice tight fit (the sweat band also keeps me from getting too hot so that issue worked out in the end. Three, the strap does not fit inside any of the Oculus carrying cases. It is wider than most other 3rd party straps and after trying all the different 3rd party cases, I gave up  and found a nice sized box and lined it with felt to protect the Oculus. I am hoping the strap manufacturer will come out with a carrying case that the strap will fit inside of. Fourth, I bought extra batteries to use when I am playing but when I plug them into the strap nothing happens except the battery falls off. I still have not figured out any work around for this problem so I have to stop playing and plug the Oculus up to a power source to restore battery life. Like I said, all minor issues that don't reduce the quality of the strap and it is still better than all the other straps I tried.

We take a two fold approach with an avacado oil based moisture treatment directly on the hooves twice a week and dietary supplements. This works and my horses are sound with stupid hard feet.

This is a clean, highly palatable pelleted add in to their breakfast every morning. The supplement mixes easily and nobody has refused to eat it or had any side effects. I don't know if it is doing anything directly for their feet, but I haven't noticed any degradation of the hoof walls or soles. This review is for the 3 pound bag of pork, barley, and beef which is competitively priced at $10.50 per bag.

The first eleven ingredients are:
- Deboned Pork

- Turkey Meal

Overall, this took a bit before my friend's dog would eat this but eventually she loved it enough to inhale the entire bowl.  At the current price of $10.50 per 3 lb. bag it is a little pricey but competitive with what is on the market. I do feel the ingredients are nutritious.

title: If you've never gotten into Blazblue, now is the time!
text:
To anyone that has never experienced Blazblue first-hand, this is the game to buy. Or if you missed out on the previous game, this "Extended" follow-up is really the way to go. People who may have bought the first version of Continuum Shift, please note that this isn't a continuation as much as it is an update with a few character additions and changes to modes.

**Why Newbies to Blazblue should buy:
- The first game is re-told: In story mode, the Extend version gives a condensed retelling of the first Blazeblue game, Calamity Trigger. The re-telling of the Calamity Trigger tale is actually pretty lengthy and Arc System Works discovered ways to involve more characters in the story that were vaguely featured in the first game (such as Tsubaki, Makoto and Hazama). The drawback to the condense version is that it doesn't feature some important unique characterizations found in the first game. You don't learn about Tager and his connection to Kokonoe, Hakumen's role is awkward and never really explained, and the fun-loving Bang doesn't get his moment to shine (does "talk to the hand girlfriend, for I am Bang Shishigami" ring a bell?).

- Not as demanding the the previous Continuum Shift: The last game was hardcore. I would put it on the same level as Super Street Fighter IV due to the online and offline requirements for trophies/achievements. In the Extended version, the game still finds ways to challenge you like the previous game, but it's much more relaxed. Combo trials now feature a lot more variations (15 trials instead of the previous 10), which can help the player learn tactics they may not have even thought of using in battle. Another change involves the way the player levels up in the game, which is no longer dependent on playing online, but playing offline counts much more this time around. Basically, doing anything in the game will earn you points to help you level up!

**Why Blazblue Fans should grab this:
- New stories for new faces: The last game introduced three new DLC characters. In the Extended version, their never-before told tales get included in the Blazblue saga. This version also introduces a brand new playable character, Relius. If you've played Continuum Shift's story previously, you might want to know all the stories featured in the last game are exactly the same with no changes. Players that have completed parts of story mode in the previous version of Continuum Shift will be happy to know a nice feature is made available to import the save file from the older game into the new game. It will definitely save you time from having to unlock items in the Gallery mode all over again.

- Legion mode begone and enter the Abyss: That's right. Legion mode this time around has been traded in for Abyss mode. The Abyss is you taking a character into the depths of world and facing waves upon waves of enemies. The further you travel, the more powerful and complicated your enemies become. You'll eventually unlock perks to use in battle to make your character more even against your foes.

**Overall: If you've never had the pleasure of playing Blazblue, do yourself a favor and give it a try. What makes Blazblue special is that it does something many fighting games don't do. First, story is just as important as the fighting. It's rare to find a fighting game that takes time to not just create a story, but create a world of history and interweaving relationships. Secondly, every character is unique, different and down-right bizarre. You won't find character clones or similar move-sets in this. Lastly, the voice acting is top-notch. Usually if a Japanese game gives the option of selecting the original language track, I go for it. Blazblue is a rare, shining example of how an English dub can be as equally great as the original voice-over work. This is seriously one of the best fighters you can own.

To those familiar with Blazblue, it might be discouraging for some players that it's just an update of the last game. To those who really are true fans of the series and even if they may own the original Continuum Shift, you can't go wrong with this. If anyone is thinking of purchasing the Limited Edition, do know that the calendar is very tiny and the art book is just as small.

title: Good, but could be better in some obvious areas.
text:
I've been playing it for a little while now, and I have noticed that it is NOT surprising. Nothing will surprise you or WOW you in this game. It's good; it works; will definitely satisfy your desire to play a golf game on your PC, but...

I figured that they would spend a little more time and put some more effort into the stuff that matters instead of additional customizable details for your player's face and whatnot. Who cares? A scar? Whoop-de-do. 4,000 choices of clubs that all play about the same? Dozens of hats? Big deal.

1) We want the Course Architect! The skate board games have had that ability for years, and has become integral with the games. Why would you put it on SOME TW games and not this one?? Seems really cheap of them to leave it off. Are they going to ask us to buy it as an add-on? Good luck.
2) More natural ball movement and bouncing (i.e. when a real golf ball hits concrete it takes of like a rocket, but in the game it bounces and rolls like its in med rough.)
3) Hitting irons off of the carpet is no better than med rough? Since when?
4) The computer-driven golfer can often get stuck in parts of Central Park course. They choose to hit a ball in the rough with a 3W and it goes 3 feet only to have them turn 180 and hit it with a 3I and go 100 feet -- out of bounds. This repeats until the golfer concedes. The out of bounds on the 18th hole of Central Park green is inaccurate and absurd.
5) The mp3 for the creek/brook sounds like a skipping record.
6) When you play against a better golfer, but have them nerfed to 'novice', they will almost always hit the hole and roll over it if they are more than 10 feet away - you're pretty much guaranteed that. Gets annoying after awhile.
7) The people are obstacles, and seem to have some kind of sticky clothing?? Since when does a ball hit by a driver "land" on a guy's shirt? Or sort of stick to him and slide down? They people should have no surface and let the ball fly through them -- (most of the time) they would be moving out of the way during real golf.
8) How 'bout adding a golf cart racing secret code or something fun? I know you want it all serious and whatnot, but those that would like to pimp out a golf cart, jump one off a bunker or whatever could seek out the code. Those that are not into that could be none the wiser and still think it serious.

I'm guessing that the "PGA" in "Tiger Woods PGA Tour 07" is what keeps it pretty boring. Oh well, I'll have to look elsewhere for the fun in golf.

title: Flexible Scheduling and Portion Controls
text:
We recently needed to leave our cat alone for a week in the house. This was the first time we had to leave her completely alone and we had some concerns about making sure she had enough kibble during the day. I selected this feeder with that thought in mind. We ended up not using it during the time we were gone as it came too close to the time we had to leave (no time to learn how to use it) and we had someone reliable come to feed her anyway, but we have since worked with it and are pleased with it.

The idea behind this feeder is straightforward. It dispenses food automatically, portioned and timed as needed. There’s no real mystery there. However, this is more than a simple “dumb” feeder that spits out a cup of food every so often and has one setting. Multiple feedings can be set up and portion sizes are adjustable to make getting the amount right without a lot of guesswork. Everything is programmable so that odd times can be set up instead of setting the feeder to go off at fixed intervals or at specific times of day.

In use it works well. We can set it to feed our girl twice a day (it’s capable of more) which is plenty. She’d eat as much as we’d feed her if we gave her more, and weight control is an issue with her, so controlling the portion side is important for us.

Assembly doesn’t require much effort and in no time at all we had it ready to roll. The instructions are fairly easy to understand too, though the controls are straightforward.

This is a good automatic feeder and it will serve well when scheduled feedings are necessary without having to be around. It works as designed, does more than the average automatic feeder and is easy to maintain.

title: CAUTION:  Does NOT work with Surface Pro
text: This may be an eminently useful connector when used with the Surface RT - I simply don't know - however, I can attest that it does not work with the Surface Pro.  For reasons which elude logic, the two tablets require signficantly different connectors: the Surface RT's looks like a mini USB and has an angled connection base; the Surface Pro's is apparently a much larger, proprietary design.  Don't be misled by the photographs of the two products on Microsoft's own website which make it appear that the two are identical.  They're most definitely not, which Microsoft customer support acknowledges with an apology for being so vague on this point.  The front of Microsoft's packaging of both units states simply "SURFACE - VGA Adaptor."  Only on the back cover will you find in 6pt type that it's for an RT (or presumably for a Pro).  The major retailers selling the Surface Pro (Staples, Best Buy) both seem confused--though as nearly as I can tell their websites only stock the RT version adaptors.  Pro owners proceed with great caution - it may well be for the moment that the Microsoft Store is the only sure source of the right adaptor. And in any event, the SRP of the adaptor, in either version, is forty percent less than what is being offered on Amazon on 3/1.

title: Phenomenal
text:
This is an excellent game.. Some people are complaining that it's the same exact thing as Modern Warfare 2.. Overall, it pretty much is, but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing.. I'm a strong believer in not fixing what isn't broken. MW2 was amazing, as is this game. So far I've invested about 30 hours in this game between campaign, multiplayer and the new spec ops modes, and I still have a long way to go!

In the campaign, you continue on with Soap and Price's story. The campaign is fun, enthralling and action-packed. I played it on normal difficulty and it took me about 6 hours to complete. Again, a lot of people complain about the fact that the campaigns in the COD series are too short, but we don't buy these games for the campaigns, we buy it for the multiplayer.. However, in my opinion, the campaign is still a lot of fun.. From team-sniping with your AI partner to using predator drones, the campaign is still as awesome as ever.

Regarding multiplayer, it seems like it has improved! When it switches hosts I've yet to be dropped out of a game. I also get put into matches pretty quickly. There are also new game modes which are excellent! Team Defender is a variation of capture the flag. There is one neutral flag with no destination for it.. Your objective is to simply capture the flag and hold onto it as much as possible while teammates protect the flag carrier. Then there is kill confirmed, which is a variation of team deathmatch. In this mode, when you kill an enemy you must pick up his dog tags for points. You must also try to retrieve dog tags from fallen teammates before the other team picks them up. Both game modes are very intense and fun to play. In this game, each weapon has its own level so not only do you level up, but your weapons do too. The higher your weapon level, the more attachments and camo you unlock for them. Finally, killstreaks are better than ever! You make a different killstreak with EACH class.. You can also choose between assault, support and perks. It adds an entirely new element of strategy when making your classes.

Finally, there is spec ops mode. Spec ops mode brings back missions like there were in MW 2. I haven't played much of this mode so I don't have much to say on it, but also in spec ops mode there is survival mode! Survival mode alone is worth the price of the game! You can play solo, split-screen or online with 1 other player and you fight off waves of enemies. You can choose from any of the multiplayer maps (which there are plenty of!) and you start off with a pistol and fight off the first wave... Each kill earns you money which can be used at any of the three crates placed throughout the map... A gun crate where you buy guns, an air support crate where you can purchase predator missiles, air strikes, and even AI-controlled delta squad support! Then there is the equipment crate where you can guy frag grenades, flash bangs, turrets, etc. They are usually placed pretty far apart and you only have about 30 seconds between waves, so you need to prioritize what you need for the upcoming wave.. You start by killing foot soldiers in the first wave that take a few shots from a pistol to put down, and before you know it you're fighting attack dogs with C4 strapped to them, juggernauts, choppers, massive infantry forces, and eventually combinations of all of the above.. It gets INTENSE and this game mode is INCREDIBLY fun. Like I said, this mode alone makes MW 3 worth every penny.

So if you liked MW and MW2, definitely get this.. You will not be disappointed. Again, it is pretty much identical to MW2 in a lot of ways, but I think that's a good thing.. When Black Ops came out, the number of players seemed to dramatically decrease on MW2 to my disappointment.. Now Modern Warfare is back, and I will probably never touch Black Ops again. Also, since comparing MW to Battlefield seems to be the thing to do in reviews, in my opinion this game beats the living hell out of Battlefield.. It did win shooter of the year.. And if anything else, if you buy MW3 used, you won't have to spend extra money on an online access pass like BF 3 (which is ridiculous)

Hope this review helped!

title: (UPDATED)-Cats Are Like People, Except People Don't Lick Peppers Or Pretend They Are Dead With A New Toy
text:
(SEE UPDATE AT THE END)
Our cat has had quite a dietary journey. When he first picked our family to adopt, he showed up at the door and was absolutely frantic to eat. He even ate ears of corn that he dragged out of our compost. As we trained him to eat really good food (and yes, taught him how to catch a mouse, because he had no clue), our beloved Tom has developed quite a discriminating palette. In short, he only likes high quality food. He won't touch anything with grain in it anymore, and he really only likes the high quality stuff. He also is not a fan of food that has too much meal or legume protein in it.

WHAT IS THIS FOOD LIKE?
First of all, this food is packed in a vacuum sealed metallic colored bag. The bag, once opened, does not have a zip or reseal capability. It is best to close it with a large rubber band or put it into an airtight container. The food itself is quite dry. It does not have the usual fillers in it, and each piece is rather hard, although it is not too hard so that the cat can not chew it. Aroma wise, it does not smell overly appealing like some cat foods, but it is okay.

WHAT OTHER FOODS I CAN COMPARE THIS TO
We have had a variety of other grain free foods to compare this with:

[[ASIN:B00PAV2DQI Solid Gold Indigo Moon Chicken Holistic Dry Cat Food, Chicken & Egg, Grain & Gluten Free, Cats & Kittens of All Life Stages, All Sizes, 12lb Bag]] - We used to get him this before they changed their packaging and our cat would eat it for a while and then prefer other food. It was one of the few he wanted to swap out now and then. This food is from the same company.

[[ASIN:B00D0TEX9C Blue Buffalo Chicken & Duck Cat Treats, 2 oz Bag]] (we have tried this one in every flavor)

[[ASIN:B0018CJYCO Taste of the Wild Dry Cat Food, Rocky Mountain Feline Formula with Roasted Venison and Smoked Salmon, 15-Pound Bag]]

We have tried others, but those are the main varieties that we have used repeatedly for our cat.

HOW DID OUR CAT REACT?
Well, before I tell you that, I feel it fair to say that Tom does not like chicken. He does not like chicken as a meat fresh, or in cat food usually. Once in a great while he can be coaxed to eat chicken that is in cat food, but that is usually short lived. So, this food is chicken based and that was a risk, but we were willing to take it to see if he would eat it to add variety to his diet.

When Tom was sleeping, he was already full. He had eaten his morning meal, so I knew if he did not stick his nose up at this food in that state, he would be saying something significant. He poked his head up and sniffed the food and gobbled it from my hand. My husband, rather excited, ran right over to his bowl and put some more food in. Tom went over, sniffed the food, asked to be let out and then went on the porch and licked peppers. Okay, so he was full. I thought we would wait until later.

Later on, he approached the food, and sniffed and then went out and licked peppers. We have a half bushel of peppers on the porch that had dew on them, and he was apparently licking the water off of them. He prefers rain water to any other water, even though he has filtered water in his bowl.

Okay, our cat is weird, granted, but we were NOT expecting that reaction.

So for a couple of days, when we give him this food, he goes on the porch to lick peppers. He has never licked peppers before. But then again, when we tested a new toy with him, he would watch it go round and round and then fall over as if dead. So, we are not dealing with a typical cat here.

THE BOTTOM LINE
So far, not sure if it is the chicken, or if our cat is just being weird, but our cat gobbled this up at first, but now seems to be avoiding the issue. This could change at any minute. Although it claims to not have any meat by-product meals in it, there are three listings for meal on the package. I am not sure what that means. Meal is meal, isn't it? There are also quite a few types of beans and peas in this, perhaps another reason our cat is not enamored with it at this point.

Cats, as many of you know, are goofy finicky animals, so after I get done submitting this review, he could decide to go ballistic and eat this stuff like a starving creature. For now, well, he would prefer to go lick peppers. Um. Okay, then. Cats are like people- each one is different, but of course people don't lick peppers or pretend they are dead when you give them a new toy.

I will update if our cat changes reaction to this food. I am also trying another fish flavor of this food, and perhaps he will like that better. In any case, my current rating based on his reaction is THREE stars, but I will change if his future reaction to it changes, which is a good possibility.

UPDATE 10-8-16
After several days of disdain and preferring to lick peppers, and then the porch, and then turning his nose up at the chicken cat food, we finally decided it was time to try out the fish version of this food- the turquoise bag.

We put it in his bowl and waited. He ate a few morsels, got an angry look on his face and began meowing in a "yelling at your stupid humans"sort of voice. We tried everything. He would not stop.

Finally, out of trying anything, my husband put a handful of the rejected chicken version of this cat food in his dish, and the cat ate it all up and went outside... to lick the porch.

So, now, he does not want the fish version only, he prefers to have the chicken after two tastes of the fish. If we give him a few morsels of fish first, he eats them up (won't eat at all if you give him more) and then looks up and meows until we give him the chicken. You know- the one that he refused to eat until now?

What changed? Who knows? Like I said, our cat is a weird one, but he sure is entertaining and loving- just weird.

He probably says the same thing about us to his friends.

I will update when he decides he likes the fish too and if he still likes the chicken.

For now, I am changing this to four stars as he has decided he likes it, but only after a few morsels of fish flavor first.

title: my dogs like it, my cats like it, and so momma likes it
text:
We're kind of loving this bolstered furniture protector. And my we, I mean my 2 labs and 4 cats.

The item is packaged as a long tube of polyester filled soft squishy pillow and the protector material. The main material is the typical quilted furniture protector material- water proof quilted material on one side, lightly nubbed no skid material on the back. The spot that the bolster pillow is placed is a solid plain material. The pillow is zipped into place.

What I like:
--full length zipper
--I thought for sure it was going to be a pain in the rear to place tube pillow into the protector, but it was the easiest, quickest placement of pillow into casing that I have ever experienced. ZERO STRUGGLE. Good!
--Medium size 30"Lx31"Wx6H" is good size for cats and smaller dogs* (I have big dogs, but still works)
--quilted material is soft and cozy
--bolstered pillow part is soft and plush
--nice colors to choose from, matte look. I have navy blue; very nice.

What I dont like/have concerns over:
--material that bolster pillow sits in is basically like bed sheet material. If you have a digger, I am not sure how well it will hold up to it. Nothing has happened with mine, but I am skeptical. I have no concern over the quilted part.
--and by no means is this going to hold up to a chewer. It isn't meant to, but just keep that in mind.
--6" high pillow bolster--while soft and plush, might be too soft for your needs. I don't know what the norm is. It feels comfy to me, and my lab likes laying his big gorgeous block head on it. So I guess that says something :)
--price. I hate to say it, but it is the most expensive one I have seen on Amazon. Maybe this one is different enough to warrant price difference, but with such a simple design, I doubt it? I could be wrong, of course. If it fits your budget, great. I am not deducting rating from it, but I am bringing it up. I know we all already spend good money on our furry babes, and I just wanted you to be aware of the other options.

My thoughts/experience:
--I do like it, and I like having it as part of our pet care, pet comfort, pet amusement arsenal. I started of with the intent to put it on my couch for the cats (or the dogs), but then decided to put it on the dogs large sized elevated pet bed (see pic!). The medium fits on it placed in the most narrow position. I am thinking this is a really nice way to add a pillow to an otherwise flat bed. We also have a toddler mattress as dog bed that this would go on in the same manner (or I could buy a large size for even better fit). After that, I tried it inside my young labs crate (please don't judge, he is rarely in there, and in pics the door is wide open). He likes to snuggle with pillows, so I thought this might be nice for him. I also tried it on top of the crate, where we have blankets and a cat bed for the cats to make use of the vertcial space. It works out really well there too. So while I am not currently using it as a furniture protector, it is being made of great use in other areas. Lots of options!

All my babies enjoy snuggling up to a pillow, and this is what it is being used as. The flat bottom makes it nice for use on the couch without it taking up extra room like a bed would. My couch happens to sit real deep and has couch pillows and toss pillows that are needed in order to sit upright, so that is why I ultimately decided against using this on my main furniture. I am considering another color for another set of furniture we have (leather) that could benefit from the protection as well as add comfort for my babies (as regular toss pillows just slide off leather).

Anyway, if my babies like it, then I like it. And they like it!

My baby boy is modeling it for you today.

I hope this information helped you today. If I learn anything new, good or bad, I will be back to update this review. Take care :)

title: Worst remote ever
text:
This is quite possibly the worst remote I’ve ever used. If you think of any problems with remotes you’ve had in the past, this one has somehow managed to include every one of them.
1. The remote has to be pointed with laser accuracy at the front of the Xbox to work. If you are pointing a bit high or low, or if there is anything blocking the beam (like a coffee table) you can forget it.
2. The main button you’ll be using is the directional pad to navigate around the Xbox menu. This button is recessed into the remote and requires a great deal of force to make it click. As a result, if you use your thumb, half of your finger will be squished painfully on the the hard remote surface. If you switch to a smaller finger like your index finger it barely fits but the force and strange angles needed to get it to work gives you arthritis like pain after a short search through Netflix.
The other buttons are very small and hard to find especially the much-needed back button.
3. Possibly the most hilarious thing about this remote is that it works better upside down. Somebody got the angle of the IR signal wrong.
4. The volume, channel and off/on buttons do not work because they are not universal. They will only work if you run your TV through your Xbox. There are many reasons why nobody does this. The main one for me being degraded resolution.
5. Note to manufacturers. If the remote came with an IR repeater and if you raised the directional pad and made it less hard to push this might be worth buying.

title: A Really Nice Backpack With Electronics Perks
text:
First a caveat: I am not of the generation who grew up carrying backpacks to school and I do not have a lot of shoulder/upper arm strength; in addition I have arthritis in my neck, so to me any backpack seems a bit strange, stiff, and awkward. Frankly, I think if I'd had to carry around all the books I did in junior high school in a backpack (none of my classes were near my homeroom locker, so there was none of this dropping books off routine--we only had three minutes to get between classes), I'd have severe back problems right now, remembering the thick English, math, science, Italian, and history textbooks, plus a full size ring binder. Oy.

Now to our backpack: I like this. We have less expensive backpacks in our home, to use as a "bug out" bag in case of emergency. This is much nicer: padding, quality of material, and lots of nice pockets (I am a pockets-type person). I particularly like the "hidden pocket" that faces your back, which would be useful for money or any other valuables if you were backpacking or traveling. I have preliminarily tested this by putting my laptop and my 10-inch tablet in the space provided and walking around for a bit. My laptop is six years old and weighs a ton. However, the padded shoulder straps and the sternum strap were helpful in keeping this balanced well on my back. I went up and down stairs a few times and did not feel unbalanced or "top heavy." (I do now, however, understand why people like Airbooks.)

In addition to the laptop pocket with the inner sleeve for the tablet, this has a central compartment with two pockets, one zipped, and an outside compartment with all sorts of slots for pens, memory cards, CDs, whatever. A small pocket on the top of the back could hold a cell phone or perhaps your printout of a boarding pass, parking ticket receipt, whatever, and there are two small pockets, one on each side, one with an opening so you could put an .mp3 player in the pocket and have your earbuds come out through it. This is all in addition to the "hidden pocket." There is a strong handle at either end of the backpack as well as a handle.

My goal is to give this a better workout at Dragoncon, where I can carry lunch and snacks and juice boxes in the central compartment, carry my tablet in the laptop compartment, and also carry my camera, instead of slinging a lunchbox and my camera case over my shoulder. It seems like a much better option. I also see it being useful on the occasional weekend trip. If it works out for me, it's possible my husband might enjoy one as well.

[September: This was really, really good at Dragoncon; I will be using a backpack again next year. Much better than carrying the lunchbox and the camera separately and wearing a pouch. I put my tablet in the laptop pocket, my lunch things (juice boxes, sandwiches, snacks, fruit) in the middle pocket, and the camera in the outermost pocket. The little pocket at the top held my spare cell phone batteries, and my wallet was in the hidden pocket. This backpack needs a strap at the bottom, and, instead of an iPod holder, a water bottle holder. That's the only thing I can see wrong with it. Yeah, I could have put a water bottle inside with my lunch.]

[PS I liked this so much I bought my husband one for Christmas.]

title: Decent Slider, but Room for Improvement
text:
I am primarily a stills shooter. That said, I do have an excellent camera that is very capable of shooting video and I do need it for such on occasion. I was interested in this camera slider as a way to get smooth shots and to reduce reliance on lens-based stabilization which is not included in my camera body. This has been a learning experience and while I like this slider there is definitely room for improvement.

I will start with the basics. This is a large and fairly heavy animal, which is to be expected. It is roughly 3' long and in it’s most basic configuration rests on a flat surface with no issues. It does have some adjustments that can be made to the individual feet on the frame so it can be adjusted slightly for uneven but mostly level surfaces without using any other equipment. To get much more versatility out of it, though, it can be mounted on tripods on either end to raise it higher or to set up angular shots.

The motor on the frame is controlled by a remote which comes with a battery pack. The remote is not wireless and has to be connected to the motor via the provided cabling. This is all right, but wireless functionality would make it much more versatile. It should be noted that the remote controls the slider, not the camera. I had some concern about this in the very beginning, thinking that the remote would be incompatible with my camera and that this unit would not work for me.

I encountered some issues that bother me. First, when powered on and running the motor runs the slider down the track until it is either stopped or a stop point is set. If one is not set, it bumps into the end and keeps trying to go beyond, making an awful noise that will surely mess up any video that requires sound. In my mind, the motor should detect when it hits the end and stop, even if start and stop points are not set.

When the motor is running and it is not near a stop point, it runs at constant speed and it is very smooth. When manually paused, it stops quickly but it doesn’t jerk to an abrupt stop like it hit something. But, if one of the end points are set and is reached, the motor slows down, then jerks to a stop, enough to notice in video footage. This is most obvious when the remote is set up to film in a loop as the issue can be observed repeatedly.

The motor is not silent, though it is quiet. It is not loud enough to ruin a shot unless absolute quiet is needed, and the motor produces a low-volume, low-frequency hum that slightly resembles the sound of an electric trolling motor on a bass boat, but quieter. The point is that it is by no means silent, but it should be good enough in the majority of cases. This is out the window if the motor is allowed to reach the end of the track before it is stopped, in which case the noise is likely to be a serious issue.

This is a decent slider and if used with some thought will serve nicely. There are definitely some places where it could be improved, particularly in the way it fails to handle reaching the end of tracks.

I decided recently to upgrade both of my keyboards to mechanical ones, and after doing quite a lot of research, I decided that these BlackWidow TKL linear switch keyboards were the best fit for me with price and performance in mind.

Overall I'm pretty happy: the touch and feel of the keyboard is wonderful (I really prefer the linear switches), the wrist rest is essential and quite comfortable, and the TKL size allows me to position the keyboard near the mouse, which for me is ergonomically much better. (I had been using a Logitech Wave for years, and I'm still a bit surprised by how much better this keyboard is for me overall.)

Downsides? Firstly, these are the keys with the secondary characters not lit: if you want those lit, you have to spend about $30 more to get the PBT keycap upgrade package. (Or you can buy another Razer TKL product, most likely without a wrist rest.) Secondly, I don't like the light under the keys, I think that's quite unnecessary and distracting, actually making it harder to read those unlit characters. Oh, and my pet peeve is the Delete key being the same size as the others: I happen to use it almost as often as I use backspace, and much prefer keyboards where that key is made larger.

Finally, you want to hope you never need Razer customer service. text:
I have a six foot PowerLine cable that's just about a year old. That's twice as long as any other cable, braided, cloth, heavy duty, whatever, has lasted. Where I keep my tablet in the pocket of the grab bar on my bed puts a fairly sharp bend in cables. I've had them cracking and splitting at the plug as soon as a week and never more than two or three months. I'm replacing the six foot cable for two reasons. The six foot cable just isn't long enough, it's really close and the ten foot cable is going to be more than I need but I think it's better to have the extra length. The cable has developed a permanent bend at the small end but still shows no signs of cracking or splitting. The other reason is the connector has loosened up a little which I've noticed in both my tablet and Kindle but it still works so it's a good backup cable to have around. The new cable end are very tight fitting which I'm happy with, the old one was getting a little too easy to pop loose but it got a LOT of usage so I really can't complain seeing as how much longer the six foot cable lasted. If this ten footer lasts that long I'll be quite happy.

Update 01/23/2018 - I bought this 10' cable based on the longevity of the company's 6' cable of the same style. My 6' cable lasted nearly a year of numerous daily times plugging and unplugging my tablet. With no discernable change in usage or handling the 10' cable is now disconnecting from the tablet at the lightest touch after less than three months. Very disappointed.

Update: 02/08/2018 - I contacted Anker about warranty support for this cable. They were very quick to respond, friendly, concerned and quickly sent me a braided upgrade cable to make up for this cable failing. title: Don't Be An Idiot Like Me- Let Me Save You The Trouble..
text:
When I got this light, I got it to supplement a Finnex 24/7 planted plus light which I have on a large tank. The idea is that I wanted to have an extra light on for just a few hours that would augment in one area only and then shut off again. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
LENGTH
This light is about 16 inches long without the legs on it. It comes with two legs that push into the OUTSIDE holes. That will give you a few more inches of tank you can stand it on for each side.

CORD
The cord has a timer on it which is very basic. It allows you to control the level of white light, blue light, together light, and the timer of 3 choices of time.

WHAT I FAILED TO NOTICE AT FIRST
The thing that I failed to notice at first was that the cord has a join in it which allows you to unplug the plug side from the light side, so you can feed it up through narrow places easily, or replace one of the parts if you can get one.

PLUG
The plug is a very large transformer with rigid prongs on it. I mention this because I had a problem trying to get this through the back of my built in fish tank unit. It was too big to fit between the wall and the unit.

DON'T DO WHAT I DID
I spent a long time trying to figure out a way to get that plug behind the 90 gallon fish tank unit. I could not get it through and I could not get the light up through- finally I noticed that it had the connector. I felt very stupid. By disconnecting the cord halfway through, it was easy to feed the cord behind the unit and connect to the light on top.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
I have a Finnex Planted Plus light which I was using on this particular tank. That is not the one with all of the colors or timers, but it is a straight foward blue and white light. This little light is about 2/3 the size of that Finnex, but it is a very night clean light that really does bring out the colors of the tank.

ALGAE
I highly suggest you keep an eye on the tank that you use this on because algae has a tendency to grow fast with this type of light. I have it on six hour timer and it is working out well. I might have to completely turn it off some days as I am battling with hair and black algae. THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice clean light for the fish tank. They have a cord that connects so you can easily work it up through your unit, and the timer is a great feature. I like that you can dim the lights as well.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great little light. It has more light than some of the brands I have worked with and even is a cleaner light than my Finnex planted plus without overloading the plants. Finnex does not have a dimmer on it, so having this one with a dimmer is much nicer for me.

PHOTO
I tried to get good photos to show you, but they are not turning out so far. I have one of the light itself that is not too bad, but not great.

If I get some that look good, I will try to remember to post them for you. This is a much nicer light than others I have seen in big box stores. I still like my Finnex 24/7 light best, but this one is a nice added bonus. I would buy it again.

title: Netgear couldn't have made installation any simpler
text:
I wanted a wired connection in a far room out of reach of my router. This works perfectly for that by allowing me to use any power outlet in my condo as a way to extend my wired network.

I tested my upload and download speeds with a network cable plugged from my laptop directly into my router and compared it to a wired connection with the Netgear Powerline Outlet. There was no discernible difference either positive or negative. I even ran video under both scenarios and I detected no difference in performance.

When my laptop was plugged directly into the router, my ping was 12 ms, download was 17.08 Mbps, upload was 5.17 Mbps.

When my laptop was plugged directly into the Powerline using my electrical house wiring, my ping was 12 ms, download was 16.63 Mbps, upload was 5.20 Mbps.

Although these speeds are not great, that is the performance I usually get with the router and service provider I have. Based on my results, this works as designed. Below is a list of what comes in the package and the PROS and CONS.

The package includes two Netgear Powerline 1200 Outlets each with an extra outlet and one Gigabit Ethernet port, two 6.5 foot Ethernet cables, and a quick start guide. For the initial installation of these units, both outlets have to be used because one Powerline must be plugged into an outlet near the router so that the Ethernet cable from the Powerline can plug into the router. The other Powerline can be plugged into an outlet anywhere else in the home. The other Ethernet cable is then plugged into this unit on one end and an Ethernet-enabled device such as a laptop, SmartTV, etc. on the other. If additional Powerlines are purchased then both units can be used for two additional wired connections.

PROS
- The LEDs on the Powerline enable the user to diagnose if there's power, Ethernet connectivity, or the ability to "Pick A Plug" (a.k.a. electrical outlet) with the strongest performance.

- There's an extra outlet on each Powerline. This unit covers the second outlet if it's plugged into the top outlet of a two-outlet receptacle. However, I do not see that as a problem for two reasons. First, there's an extra outlet on the unit. Therefore, I am still getting the ability to plug in two items like I would have had I not been using the Powerline. (In this case the Powerline is one item and a light is another.) If I want to turn my outlet into a three outlet receptacle, then all I have to do is plug it into the lower outlet. This would allow me, for instance, to plug in a lamp in the top receptacle, the Powerline in the bottom receptacle, and another item into the extra outlet on the Powerline.

- According to the manual, the network can be secured by pressing the security button for two seconds and then pressing the security button on one of the other adapters in the existing network. If additional adapters are added throughout the house when security is already enabled, then ALL the adapters should be factory reset. To re-enable security, all that has to be done is press the security button for two seconds on one adapter and then select any ONE other adapter (it's not necessary to do all adapters) and press that security button for two seconds. Both security buttons have to be pressed within two minutes time.

- There's a 1 year warranty plus 90 days basic customer support.

CONS

- I see none at this time.

I will write Netgear to find out what is meant by security with these security buttons. Up to 16 adapters can be installed in a home. I know if I were to install another set of these, I would actually be able to use both Powerlines for extra wired connections, thereby increasing my wired connections to three from one. It's only for the first installation that the extra Powerline is lost because that is used to connect to the router.

In summary, I feel this Netgear works as designed with no discernible difference in speed over a wired connection whether I was plugged directly into the router or the Powerline. Installation was simple and turning any one of my electrical outlets into a wired connection was practically instantaneous.

UPDATE April 27, 2015 - I contacted Netgear for an explanation of why there's a security feature on these adapters and exactly what that means to me. Below is Oleg Fishel's (of customer support) response which I slightly paraphrased.

The security refers to encryption between each of the Powerline adapters on my network. A random key is generated and shared among the adapters when the security setup button is used. All traffic is then encrypted using the highly secure 128 bit AES encryption protocol that prevents any unauthorized person from accessing the communication on my network. The reason enabling this security is recommended is to prevent someone from coming into my home with another Powerline adapter and connecting directly into my network to get information or for free Internet access. Although this scenario might be rare, this may be a concern with apartment buildings and offices where electrical circuits might be shared and in the case of homes that have outdoor electrical sockets. In summary, it is best to enable security. It is especially important when the Powerline is on a shared electrical circuit where someone can come along and plug one of these adapters in and piggyback off the network.

In regard to another question I had regarding the use and installation of 16 adapters all at once, he said "The HomePlug standard (HPAV2) used by the PL1200 supports up to 16 adapters on the network working together simultaneously. So if you purchased 7 kits (14 units) in addition to the original kit, you could have a 16 node network."

One day I turn it on it the screen goes blue but the fans don't come on, no text is on the screen, and I can't get the lights to turn off unless it's unplugged. title: Excellent Sound, Frustrating At Times For Certain Devices
text:
Some of my devices lack really nice speakers, so I like to have a speaker handy so that I can listen to music or presentations as I go about my day. Let's take a look at this one.

HOW THIS COMES
This speaker comes in a foam liner inside a sturdy gift appropriate box. It has an audio 3.5 cord as well as a Type C charging cord with USB at the other end. It has a carry handle on it too. There is a basic instruction manual in a variety of languages.

BLUETOOTH
The connections are usually pretty stable, but once in a while depending on the device, we have to remove the speaker and reboot the device and speaker to get it to line up again even if it has already been connected previously with no issues.

SOUND
The sound of this speaker is surprisingly fantastic. It depends on the source recording, of course, but in most cases, I have to say that the sound of this little guy is really great. The top however, does move in and out so you can not block it or put anything on top of it or it can break the speaker.

MICRO SD CARD SLOT
I have to be honest here. I can not get the Micro SD slot to work correctly. I have tried many times to get it to play, but it won't. The directions say that you can hit the mode button and it will get to the micro SD card mode but it just sits and goes back to blutooth mode again. I am not sure why this is happening. The same card plays on other devices just fine so I know it is not the card.

AUDIO
I have also not been able to get my audio cord to work but I think that is because my old MP3 player I was testing it with was not working correctly and that is the only device I would use with that feature of this speaker.

CALLS
I don't use this with my phone so I don't answer calls with it.

CHARGE
A charge generally lasts me about 10 hours or so, depending on usage periods and how spread out they are. It takes between 1 and 2 hours to recharge.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great small speaker. It is waterproof (I did not test that aspect at this point) and sounds great. The MicroSD slot has not worked for me yet, but otherwise it is a good speaker.

FOUR STARS. I like this but wish that the other features worked a bit more easily. I will update if I find solutions to the issues I have been having.

title: This is the best e-reader I've ever seen
text:
It's just plain spectacular how good the Kindle Voyage is.

I'm kind of a gadget junkie. Whenever a new Kindle reader comes out, I pass on the old one and buy the new. So I'm coming from a place that has used everything from the old Kindle Keyboard through to this, my newest Kindle, the Kindle Voyage 3G.

First, screen quality. I knew it had 300 v. 221 PPI I had on my PW2, but until I saw it, couldn't believe how much of a difference it made. Now, the PW2 screen is great, but this beats it soundly. Storage/Memory: I wish it were a bit bigger. Not that I have any desire to have 2,000 on my Kindle at any given time, but once you get into using about half the memory, these devices always slow down and get ornery.

I got this for my son who has the type of ear that doesn't fit earbuds, and type of head that headphones don't stay on. title: You�ll know when you need it.
text:
Don't buy this memory card until you need it. Mine works well, but it only has one use: it transfers files from X-box to X-box.
The X-box has a huge hard drive, and since the hard drive is what you use to save your games, you can play for years without a memory card.
After fully testing the memory card, here are the restrictions:
-You can't directly transfer files from X-box to X-box, even with the system link cable, so the only way to transfer files is with the memory card.
-You can't transfer music files on the memory card. It would hold about two files, but the X-box won't let you. You can only transfer game saves.
-You can only transfer character profiles, so you can't transfer the progress on a game like Dead or Alive that doesn't have character profiles.
-You have to transfer character profiles one at a time.
Probably the best use for this memory card is if your friend has an X-box, and has unlocked a bunch of special features on a game, you can save the profile off your friend's X-box to your memory card and then transfer it to your X-box.

title: These are a hard pass for me...
text:
I purchased these with high hopes but was horribly let down. Plugging in via on-board (both front case and main back) they sounded weak and tinny. Plugging in via my Sound Blaster Z, the powered boost helped in terms of volume, but the lack of substance / tinny undertone was now even more dominant.

Going even further, I plugged them into a GoXLR to utilize even more of a 'boost', still tinny. My XLR makes a $15 headset from Walmart sound amazing, it did no justice here. I even went as far as purchasing a USB adaptor in one last effort to know for sure that it wasn't a lack of power to the unit, it's just the quality of the speakers, still tinny / no substance.

The default leatherette ear pads are comfortable, but cheap feeling and I could tell that they would crumble over time because it's the 'thin' material that just flakes when they dry out OR get overused. Because of this, I did purchase Felt earpads (search for Genuine Sennheiser HZP 26 Replacement Ear Pads Cushions). They fit beautifully and made the unit more comfortable, this did not assist with the sound, if anything made it worse because your ear was no longer 'locked' into the leather, so they were swapped back to the original pads.

I'm not looking for headphones that will rattle my eardrums, by any means, but having absolutely no substance on any song listened to, or game played, just takes away from the overall experience, especially on the higher end of $150. An audiophile would absolutely hate these, and the sound issues (no matter having an EQ adjustment or flat) caused issues in-game where I didn't hear any footsteps for anything going on around me. In an FPS it's essential to know your surroundings, no settings anywhere on my PC allowed for this without having to full crank these to 100% on both the computer AND the headset.
