title: Incredible...but the fun and plot are short lived.
text:
I'll admit it, I'm an RPG junky. I've always been drawn to games where you the player gets to make the decisions to influence the outcome of the game. The more decisions, the better!

Fable and Fable II are pretty unique in how they allow the player to interact with the non-player-characters (NPC), and how your decisions impact the appearance of your character.

Basically you're presented with a series of missions, some are honorable like "rescue the slaves" while others are rather evil like "assasinate a good person." As you work your way through these missions, you begin to build a reputation for your good and bad deeds and the townsfolk respond to you appropriately.

You can interact with the town in the same manner. If you knock on someone's door and they do not answer, you have the option of smashing the door in. While you're walking around a shop, you can choose to steal things...it's all up to you.

There is actually ALOT happening in this game. There are several mini-games (jobs) such as blacksmithing, woodcutting, bartending etc. These involve hitting a button on the controller within a certain window of opportunity for the character to complete an action. You will receive gold and unlock achievements by blacksmithing for example.

When interacting with shop keepers, you can actually get lower prices by treating the shop owners in a certain way. If you flirt with them or dance for them, they will usually change their prices. You can also buy shops and earn money or buy homes, redecorate them and rent them out.

Unlike Fable I, you have a dog that follows you around and helps you find treasure chests and dig-spots. I found that most of the treasure was absolute junk. You could easily go through the entire game without needing to dig or discover and open chests.

Many of these actions aren't really necessary to move forward in the gameplay/plot...so it's really a matter of how fast you want to move through the game. Once you've managed to get your hands on a master-level weapon with an augmentation like GHOUL, you won't have too difficult of a time with killing anything...so what use will you have for gold?

The plot had many simularities with Fable I and I actually think it was weaker in many respects. The sole complaint I had with Fable I is that it was too short! Once you finish the storyline, there's very little to do...it makes you almost not want to advance in the game!

Great game, outstanding graphics, cool gameplay, cool features etc. but the developers could have done a much better job in tying everything together in a cohesive manner to make more of these mini-games an actual part of the story/game.

I would recommend you rent this badboy from blockbuster for 10 days. If you've got 10 days to devote to playing it, you'll probably have it finished off in about 7 depending on how long you play each day...you'll save money doing this...trust me.

title: Not professional, but one of the better ones this price bracket
text:
[[VIDEOID:91ed971de75e2a1d366c0694560e3ad4]] Let's get this metric straight: Those who are saying a projector under $300 looks good, are probably comparing it to other cheap off-brand projectors. I've tried a few of these to use as throwaround backyard movie night things, when I don't want to get my expensive prosumer home theater ones dirty or burn out the bulb, and they all suffer from things like flat colors, lack of brightness (fudging the lumens numbers) and the worst: Inconsistent focus. Nothing makes me crazier than trying to nail the focus and finding the center focuses while the borders are out of focus, but adjusting for the edges makes the center out of focus. Usually this is because the lens is cheap and lacks proper rectilinear support, and it is MADDENING once you notice it. In short, sometimes you might find it looks better on a smaller TV than a bigger washed out and fuzzy projector.
But... usually, you should expect to pay somewhere towards DOUBLE this for a brand name projector that looks decent, so I'm trying to keep my expectations realistic for the price range. And I have to say, this is the first one that actually seems to have proper focus across the projected image! I mean, you do get some chromatic aberration in the corners (see image and video attached), but this is nothing compared to others in the sub-300 dollar range. I love that this also has built in features like miracast (which I tried and works great!) as well as an Office Suite so you can technically show a presentation without a laptop or casting device- just plug in a USB stick with your content and go!
These are not necessary in my opinion, I'd rather have better colors and sharpness than gimmicks, but honestly I think this might be the best of the lower end projectors I've tried yet! If you care about how your movies and presentations look, I'd still recommend a brand name like Viewsonic at the bare minimum. But this is fun for the kids, backyard movie nights, or impromptu presentations when a bigger and more expensive projector wouldn't be cost justifiable.

I bought smaller hard molded plastic pools from a local variety store. They worked enough to play around with or drink from, but neither dog could really play in it or lay down. A larger one (similar to this XXL) wouldn't fit in my truck. It is perfect for my labs- They can both lay down with some room to spare. Since the areas the pool is set up in has a lot of dirt, the pool water needs to be changed frequently. The drain on the bottom side makes it super easy to do so. YAY!!!

My labs aren't likely to chew on the pool, but they may dig at it a little. I keep my dogs nails trimmed, so hopefully that will greatly reduce the risk of harming the pool. The package includes a small tear repair patch and adhesive.

As the season is just starting it will be awhile yet before I have a need to fold it up and put it away. I suppose if I wanted to take it with me somewhere.. title: You did it again Enix
text:
What a game- let me tell you. There are some great parts from the original one they included; unique bosses, awesome new weapons, a great storyline. Though were there are some great parts there must be bad.

Kingdom Hearts II was a blast, I loved battling enemy after enemy, the tiny stars that flash up when you attack something with your keyblade reassured me of that. Let me tell you though the beginning started off very slow and confusing. Let me tell you now if you haven't beaten Kingdom Hearts 1 you'll probably be scratching your head the whole game.

You first start off as Roxas, a boy who is suddenly plunged into the Kingdom Hearts storyline. Similar to Kingdom Heart's first part of the game, I can honestly say(and I'm sure many would agree with me) that is was extremely boring and slow. Agh chore after chore, job after job. I hated collecting all that money, preforming stupid tricks on some skateboard that you couldn't skip! The only thing that really struck my attention in that part were the dreams Roxas had- It got me interested in the mysterious, devolping storyline yet to come. Well you can't blame Enix I suppose, I guess they were only trying to build up to the juicy parts.

Oh yes the juicy parts, chopping and slicing every enemy I see with my trusty keyblade- classic Kingdom Hearts. The "ultima" keyblade has returned, just as hard to make, just as powerful, and just as awesome looking. Saving world after world, it was very entertaining how different and unique each world was.

Although I was not use to the whole new gummi ship system, I grew to like it and now I realize it was a ton better than the first one. The trips where you battle hoards of flying enemies might be a little slow and easy at first, but trust me it really starts heating up when you get to the harder worlds. They now have a new boss system, where a boss might randomly attack you in battle. These guys are toughies if you don't have the right equipment, and I think Enix really tried to encourage that. Not only that, you can now travel to the same trips but on a different difficulty level. Rewards for completion include rare gummi peices. Perfect Enix, perfect.

One of my favorite parts were the drive powers. The game so totally needed this. Sora now has the power to weild TWO keyblades at once. That's right... you heard me, two! There are four drive powers that you can activate with a new drive bar similar the magic bar. Already the first power given to you early in the game allows Sora to weild two keyblades. I won't go over the next two, but the last one is a whopper! The final form, as Enix named it is just awesome. Sora's clothes turn totally silver and black, two keyblades hover(that's right hover!) around his hands, he hovers around in midair, and to top it all off when you attack you do insane damage, along with special moves you couldn't do with regular attacks. I would have to say this was one of the most enjoyable parts of this wonderful game.

I'm sorry to say though that the game was really quite easy. Now if I recall correctly one of the fairy people in the beginning mentioned something like "This adventure is going to be twice as difficult!". Man I was all prepared for this great journey, but at the end when I beat it I felt a sence of dispair. I felt as if I had just pressed the "x" button over and over, as a previous customer mentioned. Bosses that use to take quite a long time to kill can now be killed in less than a minute, and you don't even have to be a high combat level. When I defeated bosses in the first one, I felt a sence of accomplishment, but now I don't when the bosses kneel before me in KH2.

Overall- I like to say congratulations Square Enix for once again creating a great game.

title: Perfect For A Teething Puppy
text:
[[VIDEOID:7c28a174a3e9f7715e82aca00f8ca517]] I recently got a new puppy because of the sudden death of my Service Dog, Harvey. I was always planning on getting another Plott Hound, same breed Harvey was, with the hope that Harvey could help me train him. Unfortunately Harvey went WAY sooner than expected.
Now I have the new puppy, Camo, but I guess I completely forgot how crazy & energetic they are. One day we were in the living room and we noticed Camo going through all of Harvey's old toys. We had already showered him with so many things to chew on and couldn't have imagined that he dug down deep into Harvey's old box and pulled up the smallest stuffed red bell pepper and I think he thought he won the lottery. I noticed that it was part of a collection that I had bought for Harvey on Amazon when he was a puppy.
Camo carried his pepper with him everywhere. So I immediately went on Amazon and bought him his own collection. It just now arrived and my husband brought it back to the room that Camo and I were playing. As soon as I opened the bag of small squeaky toys Camo was so excited. As I was opening one of the individual bags to get it out Camo was going nuts because it was taking me to long. That's when he made it clear to me that he also liked the clear plastic bags that each one came in. Once he does make it to the stuffed toys that when I realized his teething had gotten worse and these toys were perfect!
They're so soft and have a small squeaker that he can finally squeak a toy with his mouth. Plus they're durable enough for him to play with until his teething is done, but just in case he does get to the stuffing I can order more of these at a price that makes him feel better with one click on Amazon.

title: Life saver must have for sick pup
text:

Next 2 days went fine but on day 3 in the middle of the night I heard him get up and the other end of him started having trouble. What a mess !!! It was so bad . Some of it was on the disposable puppy pads but not all on it . Idk what would have if I didn’t have this pad ! Geeze it really performed beyond any expectations I had . The worst of it wiped up so easy . Then in the washer it went and came out clean like nothing happened 6 hrs earlier . My dog is over the worst of it and I’m so thankful I had this to use while the worst side effects were happening. I really would have had to throw away my bed and mattress pad if I had not had this . I’m forever a fan of this puppy /whelping pad . I wish I knew this existed years ago when my kids were little , I know it’s made for animals but it would be fantastic to use for kids too ! For doing arts and crafts or to sit on inside or even outside with coated bottom . I’m seriously considering sending my dad and sister a couple of these for their dogs to sleep on . It had a coupon that took a bit off the total and made it a fair price . Affordable for sure . It shipped faster then it said it would thank goodness and I had it in place when it mattered the most . I will update this review once Iv washed it a bunch and see how it holds up . I feel like Iv gotten my monies worth out of it already but if it lasted a long time thru tons of washings I would not be mad about it at all . It also helped keep
My little guy warm . I pushed some of the extra fabric around his body while he was laying down feeling bad and it helped him be warm and comfortable. title: Delicious sound and comfortable on my average sized ears
text: The [[ASIN:B009FHFFIG Sennheiser Momentum Over-Ear Headphone]] are circumaural  which means they cover the whole ear and they have a closed-back.  They are lightweight, gorgeous with soft brown leather cushioned earpieces, have two easily switchable cables, one for general use and the second for specified mac devices.  A MacBook is not one of the specified devices, but my iPod is.  With its swivel plug and embedded on the cable remote, I'm sure iPhone and iPad users will be as thrilled as I was when I tried it on a friend's devices.  Crisp, clear, complete, these need no amplifier, but they do need ears which are not larger than average or the whole ear coverage is lacking and therefore, so is the desired effect of a circumaural earpiece.  I've listened to music on a MacBook, an android phone, a Kindle Fire, and tested these on the aforementioned iPad and iPhone.  In each and every case, the sound was outstanding and my ears did not tire, nor did they feel uncomfortable or overheated.  Most sounds surrounding me were not heard and those nearby did not hear what I was listening to at any time.  Watching movies is enhanced every time and I'm finding that even when impulsively finding a video on the Web in my usual activities, I tend to grab these headphones to listen instead of simply hearing through the computer.  My favorite music in these earphones thus far today has been John Coltrane's [[ASIN:B000V698WE A Love Supreme]].  I tend to switch genres throughout a day, but thought this was worth mentioning.  Nothing like really hearing the instrumentals as they were intended to be heard!  Outstanding headphones.

title: Somewhat useful...
text:
The Gorillapod Video Tripod (Black/Blue) is a good idea on paper but in real life it just doesn't quite measure up.

The pan & tilt head is incredibly stiff which leads to jerky motion and bounce in your video. There also, on mine at least, appears to be a good bit of free play or slack in the vertical movement of the control arm. I've tried to tighten this down to no avail. The mounting screw seems to be a bit long. It wasn't bad mounting my RCA Small Wonder video camera but when I mounted my Kodak still camera the screw bottomed out and left the camera loose on the mount. The mount itself seems quite secure tight and sturdily attached to the tripod.

I like the adjustability of the legs but if you're not using the tripod on a metal surface for the magnetic feet to cling to it tends to just slide around when adjusting the pan or tilt. The magnets do appear to be strong for their size and will hold my RCA Small Wonder video camera fully horizontal on the 'fridge or door of my car. I tried this with my Kodak Z-650 still camera and it was too heavy for the magnets to support.

While on the subject of the magnetic feet I wanted to add a warning that if you're using an older CRT style monitor care should be taken to keep this tripod several feet away from your monitor. Even being more than a foot away from my 19" CRT cause distortion and image warping. There is the potential for damage to CRT monitors.

As a stationary camera mount this is a pretty cute product; easy to carry, lightweight with near infinitely adjustable legs. If you just want to plop down your camera so you don't have to hold it this product works fine. When you bring the flaws of the pan and tilt features into play the enjoyment goes downhill fast.

All in all it's not bad but it really isn't great.

text:
I actually needed a mouse clicker, and for some reason I just thought all these "jiggler" products would have that option, but they don't. All they do is jiggle or move your mouse. It is completely plug and play, no software. Your PC should set-up device automatically, when it's done, this is how you operate:

1. Long press the only button on the device. It will turn on to A3 mode. This is the slowest mode. The mouse will move imperceptibly.
2. Short press button again to toggle to get to A1 mode. This is the fastest mode. Your cursor is flying around fast.
3. Short press button again to toggle to A2 mode. This is the medium speed mode.
4. If you want to leave this thing connected, but don't want to use it all the time, then simply long press again to turn jiggler off when not in use.

In every mode, there is a timer that shows you how long it's been moving. If you're looking for a cursor mover, this guy gets the job done. But don't make the assumption that I made. These things do not have an option for clicking. That's not the product's fault, it never claimed that, it was my assumption. title: Despite the price, it's a convenient tool to have
text:
After buying this through one of Amazon's partner sellers three years ago, I noticed no one has bothered to review this thing. I think it's about time someone stepped up, so I'm here to describe my experience with the XCM K.O. device. In the three years I've owned this, the XCM K.O. Gear has helped me earn a platinum trophy on the PS3 for the following fighting games: Blazblue (CT, CS & CS Extended), Soul Calibur V, Mortal Kombat vs DC Universe, Mortal Kombat and Marvel vs Capcom 3. Let's start with the basics.

**The Good**

-5 programmable memory buttons that can hold 20 button inputs in each memory slot: You can program any set of button combinations into this thing. It's perfect for complicated combos. Let's look at a small combination of buttons. Ibuki in Super Street Fighter IV has a great Ultra attack which requires you to do a half quarter circle twice + 3 of the punch buttons. When things get heated in a fight and I need to unleash this move, I have a hard time doing it because I suck at doing this properly on the d-pad. This is why the KO Gear is handy. I can program the Ultra attack before hand, so when I need to use it, I can just press the memory button and it will unleash it on the fly! You can even chain other combos together, which leads into the next topic.

-The difficulty in combo challenges diminish: Before I bought this, I hadn't completed a single combo challenge in MK vs DC Universe. But guess what? It only took me less than two weeks to do them all using this device. This is because you can link combos together using the KO Gear device. Let's say a combo requires you to do a multitude of inputs. If your button to eye coordination is bad and your memory sucks, you're in luck. You can program half of a combo string in one memory slot and the second half in another memory slot. Time it right and you can literally unleash a full combo string with just the press of two buttons. The KO Gear also remembers the timing of each button, so if a combo requires a late button input, the device will remember. Though sometimes the device may not register the combo correctly and it takes a bit of trial and error to get it right.

-It's an awesome learning tool: From what I noticed, people seem to define this device as a cheating tool. When I bought it, I even considered it as such. However, this device has taught me how to examine fighting games in advanced ways. Without this, I never would have paid attention to hit boxes, nor would have known how to cancel dash to continue combos. I wouldn't have known how to time my attacks on falling opponents to make sure they don't wake up in time to counter. Overall, I never would have learned that doing these combos isn't a natural born skill nor impossible, as it just takes time and practice. After entering so many combos, I began to learn and understand the timing of attacks. The repetition of button inputs, as well as trial and error, caused me to sometimes stop using the device and rely on my skill instead. This device has really helped me get better at my own pace and taught me methods that I thought were only reserved for fighting game pros.

-Good for non-combos and non-fighting games as well: Since this has a programmable turbo inputs, you can be creative in how this device can help you. For instance, in Soul Calibur V, there's a trophy called "Wind of Battle" which requires you to move over 87,600m throughout the game. You can set this device to do it for you by programming your movement and placing either a rubber band, book or tape over the memory button to keep it held down. You can use this to even get other trophies and achievements in non-fighting games. LittleBigPlanet 2 for example has a trophy for spending 24 hours in create mode and not be idle. With the KO Gear, you can set it to open and close the menu in the hub over and over. Just walk away from the PS3 and come back 24 hours later to see your trophy popped.

-The front light: It helps you see, especially if you're doing this in a darkly lit room.

**The Bad**

-The price is not ideal for this kind of technology: The price is a bit absurd. When people ask me if I think it's worth buying, I always say "it depends." If you have $80 to waste and have a bunch of fighting games in your catalog that you've put on the back burner because you have a hard time doing combo challenges in, then by all means go for it. If your the type of person that has just SFIV and KoF XIII on your shelf and think this may help you get a few trophies/achievements, seek out to buy a cheaper turbo controller instead. If your fighting gaming library is limited, you'd get a better value out of a controller than a macro device any day.

-Not ideal for charge characters: SFIV, SSFIV & KOF XIII have a lot of charge characters and this device doesn't work well with charge inputs. It takes too much trial and error to get it to work. For instance, Balrog in SFIV charge attacks work only in the beginning phase of a combo string. So I could only program the 1st half and do the rest of the string using my own skill.

-The cord is too short: I'm amazed the cord hasn't been ripped out of the device. You don't know how many times I've tripped over this thing. You have to be in a very close proximity due to its length.

-Sometimes it syncs the controller incorrectly: It's best to plug in the device before starting a game. When plugging a dual shock controller into it, the device will set the controller as player 2 or 3 and needs to be reassigned. It's not a big deal and only takes a few seconds to correct on the PS3 but it is annoying sometimes.

**Overall**

It's a great little tool to help you learn the basics and advance methods of every fighting game out there based on the repetition of button inputs you'll have to do. After a while, chaining combos will begin to feel natural and you won't need to use this anymore. It's great for a fighting game enthusiast that has a bad memory or just needs a little help to get past certain elements of gameplay they find to be a challenge. If you just have a single fighting game like Street Fighter IV, I honestly recommend a turbo controller or a fight stick over this. The price is what kills the value of the K.O. Gear. There are much better options out there.

EDIT: I also wanted to confirm that this doesn't work for the PS4. I think this might be because the PS4 controller uses digital input instead of analog. Try researching the Hori Pad FPS Plus controller, which has a turbo button, or look into the USB devices CronusMax or Titan One if you want something for PS4.

title: soft 4.5" easy to tear strips, great for puzzle/mats, salty, smells & tastes like chicken jerky
text:
If you want the variety that contains glucosamine, chondroitin & New Zealand green mussel, then make sure you select from on of the "hip joint" options. The "Chicken Grilled Jerky Strips" do not contain joint health supplements. If you are looking at reviews, you may want to search through them based on that.

This review is for the Dogswell Grilled Jerk Strips in chicken. The ingredients are: Chicken, Dried Egg, Vegetable Glycerin, Salt, Vinegar, Natural Smoke Flavor, Mixed Tocopherols (Preservative), Rosemary Extract.

Each treat has 55 calories.

Is it chewy, but soft enough to tear into smaller pieces. Not a traditional stringy, tough jerky. This is soft, easy to bite into. Ask me how I know ;) lol

Treats come in big pressure seal bag, weighing 2 pounds. I estimate there are at least 50, 4.5" jerky strips to a 2 lb bag. I had already doled out several over the past few days, and there were a few broken pieces at bottom of bag, so my count isn't exact but I am confident with 50. All looked fresh-- no molds. Looks great, smells great!

So how does it TASTE? Yep, I can answer this too. While I am not into munching on dog treats, I will try ONCE a bite of something dry or chewy. Never ever wet food. But I do take a bite so I can tell how hard or soft something is, what taste stands out, and if it is too sweet, or too salty depending on what piqued further exploration after reading ingredients. Trust I don't try everything, but items that don't appear to be super gross I will take a bit from. Also my LABS are more apt to try something novel if they seem mommy noshing first.

As far as um.. dog treats go in a jerky style.. the are mild flavored with quite an emphasis on salt. The addition of vinegar might amp up that flavor a bit, not sure. I can taste the briny bite of a "salt and vinegar" flavor. It is actually not bad, haha. Contains glycerin, which can be sweet, but I didn't pick up on that flavor. Contains smoke, but it is super mild in taste and aroma. It basically smells and tastes like what it is: a jerky chicken treat. For a dog treat, I wish I knew how much salt these contain. Since they are treat, and treated as such.. my labs aren't handed out treats day and night every day. Its more occasional, and it has more to do with the fact that one hates food, and one is on a diet.

The one who hates food, my boy.. he is a skeptical kid. He rarely LIKES a treat. I was surprised that he not only looked interested in what I had, but was first to take a jerky treat from my hand (see pics..his sister is still sitting n floor waiting). THEN he came back for more. So Mister Picky Pants likes the smell and taste of these treats. WIN.

My girl, who is dieting is less picky about treats. She is still picky about some foods, but she seems keen on being my #1 dog treat tester (after me, of course. I kid I kid! haha). She really likes these. I'm not sure she really tasted it she ate it so quickly. I then decided to tear up the jerky strip and sprinkle it into her slow feeder bowl (purple bowl in picture).

Ingredients seem good, seems to be the treat they are both most receptive to receiving, so that says something. I'm still not sure about the salt content (try one, its salty!), but since it is a treat and not a meal, it may be ok. It certainly lends flavor that they like. Also, I really like that the strips can be easily torn up for use as a reward treat, or for using in snuffle mats, slow feeder bowls, and other treat puzzles.

Any reservations about the saltiness is reduced in light of all the positives about this big bag of treats. Not enough of an issue to peg it down to 4 stars (if we had 1/2 star ratings, then yes). Since there are so many positives I give it a full rating. We will go through so few, so I am going to divvy up the bag into smaller baggies to store in the fridge. text:
I have used and tested more Ethernet cables than I can remember and there is no question, all Ethernet cables are not created equally. Every one of the AmazonBasics branded items I’ve tested has been excellent and this cable is no exception.

Typically any device requiring an Ethernet cable will come with one in the packaging - it will work (usually). A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without fail.

This Cat7 is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin PVC package contains aluminum shielding and 100% bare copper wires for super fast transfer speeds. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The plugs have a protective rubber boot guard that protects the clip on the plug - this becomes very important when snaking the cable through walls and tight spaces. Prior to doing this I wrap the boot and plug with a small piece of electrical tape to make sure I don’t unintentionally snag anything.

I love the white PVC shielding on this cable - not only is it durable and will help the cable withstand damage but it can be run along a wall and then painted to match the wall color.

I used this 100 foot cable to run between my router to a PoE switch that branches to several power and transmit data to and from one zone of my security cameras - a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

This has proven to be an outstanding, dependable Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love. This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.

They should really consider making one of these boards with a more vanilla font.

Conclusions: Just get this keyboard. Ignore the Cherry MX Blue/Green switches, after using them for years, I'm not coming to this keyboard thinking I'm using cheap, crappy switches. This keyboard is a total bargain. The switches are rated at I think 50M clicks, so lets hope that's true. But even if it was half that, I'd buy this keyboard again. I actually just had an opportunity to try the pink version of this tablet, which you can find under a different listing here. The only thing I'm not crazy about is that the case makes the holes and buttons a little bit difficult to reach/line up. text:
I order two Xbox 360 Wireless controllers for the Christmas holiday as a gift for my nephew. The product was in excellent condition as the seller described and worked perfectly. However I was under the impression that I would received the merchandise before the 24th of December 2009 based on Amazon's website.

Amazon states if you selected the expedited shipment for items you would receive the product before the holiday...totally sham! This seller used USPS and unfortunately I receive the items AFTER the holiday. I was extremely disappointed by the deceitful advertisement Amazon displayed on their site. They claimed that I would get my product at my residence by a specific date, not that the product would be in my city by that date.

Overall great seller, awesome product but inaccurate shipping details on Amazon's part. I recommend Amazon require all sellers to use Fed Ex, DHL or even UPS for all expedited, overnight, or 2-day shipments instead of charging customers for rush packages when their using regular USPS. title: These won me over
text:
Prior to receiving this review sample I was happy with in-ear type phones, but always grabbed headphones when I wanted to listen to music without disturbing others, These phones changed that. For one thing they are super comfortable. For another the sound is incredible. In fact I have been testing various phones - mainly from this brand, but also some Sennheiser models - and this is head and shoulders above the pack.

I'll be honest and disclose that comfort edges out sound when phones sound good enough. I will normally not quibble over a few hundred Hz one way or the other as long as I can wear the phones without noticing them. These are not only unobtrusive, but downright comfortable, which is a major reason why these have now replaced my trusty [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]].

Soundwise the specs do not begin to describe the richness, especially bass. In fact, when I read the 20 Hz to 20 MHz range I thought that the sound would be somewhat generic for phones in this range. I own a pair of IEMs (in-ear monitors) that go as low as 18 Hz at the same 95dB at 1mW sensitivity, yet these sound much deeper than those. I love the balance of sound across the frequency spectrum as though it's on a smooth continuum. Every one of my test albums I played through these phones sounded so good that I decided that it's time to hang up the headphones and go with these.

Part of the reason why I love these from a comfort perspective is the over the ear memory wire. I prefer that style, but not everyone does. They are definitely stiff and take on a shape that will be uniquely yours over time (and a very short time at that!) Also, while this ships with a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] the phones will not fit after you have contoured them to your ear. The case is useful for carrying around the array of adapters and tips that are included. In fact, the final reason I love these phones is the included triple-flange style silicon tips, which block out the rest of the world and allow me to focus solely on music.

If you love music and want to hear every note faithfully reproduced in their natural frequencies these phones are it. I can honestly say that I have not used a better set of phones from any brand in this price range, including some Sennheiser models that have a street price of fifty to seventy-five dollars more than these, so the value is definitely there.

title: This is a rare, perfect game.
text:
Let me start by saying that I don't even like Space Invaders. The 1978 classic was before even my time, and the lack of sophistication always turned me away. When Space Invaders Extreme came out in 2008, however, I was attracted to the colorful and chaotic yet retro presentation, and decided to buy the game on a whim. It surpassed any expectations I could have reasonably had, and SIE quickly became one of my favorite games on the DS thanks to its creative use of sound, unique soundtrack, pseudo-retro graphics, and amazing challenge.

A little over one year later, a sequel was released exclusively for the DS, and wanting more invader goodness, I hastily purchased a copy on release day. I would have been happy with just more of the same. Instead, it absolutely DESTROYED my expectations, and improved on the original in every conceivable way - more enemies, better bosses, better music, better scoring system, better leveling system, even harder challenges, and better difficulty balance with no more "cheap" deaths. SIE2 is so great...so satisfying, challenging, and well thought out, that for the first and only time in my life, I chased the global leaderboards (I got in the top 10 in three out of four). It's the kind of game that should satisfy everyone...there is that intense, high speed pressure that you only find in arcade games, yet the extremely sophisticated scoring system requires you to keep a cool head and plan every move as you play. The system is incredibly flexible, and works just as well for time trials as it does for high scores. Even if you don't care about leaderboards and simply want to make a run through each path, the variety of enemies, stages, and increasing difficulty will satisfy. It is so good that I went out the next week and bought several extra copies to distribute to my friends.

This is a special game...a fully realized and masterfully crafted product that defines its platform, and perhaps even genre. For DS and 3DS owners, as well as arcade junkies of years past, this is an absolute must have.

title: My Fish LOVE This Stuff - I Have SEVEN Tanks Of Fish
text:
As it said in the title, I have SEVEN fish tanks. My fish vary from neons and other tetras, to rainbow fish and even Apistogramas. I try to vary their food. This bag looked perfect to round out my food storage.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This food is rated for medium to larger fish. It is made sort of like small Grape Nuts type cereal bunches. These are not hard like that though. They are hard enough to stay together, but will work well for the fish to eat.

HOW DO THE FISH LIKE THEM?
I have crushed some of these into smaller pieces for the smaller fish. I then blend the sizes depending on the tank. Every single fish I have loves these things. The fish continue to eat these up every time I feed them with this.

CONTENTS
The bag has more than enough food to get me through a couple of months with all of my fish. If you have less fish, this will last longer for you most likely.

ANY ISSUES?
I have not had any problems with clouding of water, refusal of food, or rotting in the tanks. The fish polish this off every time. Even the plecos come out to eat when drop these in.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great food to round out a fish diet. I feed this to my fish every other day and they love it. For smaller fish, I crush some up for the smaller fish.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This resealable bag of food is perfect for me. My fish love it and I am happy with it. I will buy it again.

title: Freedom comes at a price
text:
After playing Batman: Vengeance, it was an exhilarating change to have a protagonist who could fall off the side of a building and survive. My first impressions were: freedom!

But freedom comes at a price. Superman: Shadow of Apokolips is the first of its kind to allow you to play Superman with all of his abilities and in a fully rendered three-dimensional environment, but there are clipping errors and strange forced perspectives that ultimately dampen the game's enjoyment.

The plot is a loosely connected series of events involving the extra dimensional arch villain, Apokolips. Through his minion, Canto, he sets up a series of military-style attacks with "Apokoliptian technology" that he provides to Lex Luthor. Lex eventually sets a series of super villains free from Stryker Prison, including Livewire, Parasite, and Metallo. Or just Metallo's head in this case.

Lex is provided with a cadre of Interbots, strange goggle-eyed guys in masks. But don't worry, they're robots, so Superman can punch them without any gore. I was willing to accept the old G.I. Joe chestnut (i.e., "we have powerful guns, but let's run up to the bad guys and smash them in the face with our rifle butts!").

Punching Interbots is decidedly unsatisfying. Killing Interbots can be amusing at first. Setting them on fire with heat vision causes them to run around, arms flailing. They will sometimes run away, screaming in mechanical voices "This unit is compromised" or something like that. And yet, there's no feeling of Superman's awesome strength. When he hits Interbots, I want to see them go through walls, not just bounce around like rag dolls.

And there are so MANY of them. Superman fights Interbots, Interbot tanks, Interbot missle launchers, Interbot troop transports, Interbot gun emplacements, Interbots with jet packs, and Interbot helicopters. I don't ever recall seeing this many Interbots in the Superman cartoon.

Because of the sheer number of opponents, certain tactics are encouraged over others. Superman has a wide variety of abilities, including his x-ray vision, heat vision, super breath, super speed, flight, and super strength. But his best ability is an area attack slam that drops him at high speed onto the ground, knocking back and destroying everything in sight. This ability was more useful than punching Interbots. So suddenly, Superman becomes a living torpedo. Not necessarily a bad thing, but hardly representative of the Superman cartoon.

The game looks exactly like the movie, rendered in cell-shaded animation. All the voices actors are present, including Lori Petty as Livewire and Malcom McDowell as Metallo. But even those villains aren't the type who can go punch for punch with Superman.

Of all of the villains, only Livewire can fly. Superman slowly regenerates his damage and his super abilities. This means that if he is significantly harmed, you can just fly him away to a safe place and heal there. When fighting Metallo, I did this several times, while Metallo patiently waited down on the ground.

But I don't want to put the game down entirely. The game's plot is entertaining and even has a few twists. When the villains do show up, they are fully realized. I had a difficult time beating Livewire so I had plenty of opportunities to hear her wax poetic about electricity. I can't stand Lori Petty (except for her role in Tank Girl), but she really does act her heart out mocking Superman. Metallo does the same thing. There's a lot of entertainment value in just listening to them mock Superman. Superman returns the favor by talking to himself. Over and over and over. It gets annoying.

In terms of gameplay, there are a few high points. Superman must achieve the random feat of strength - plugging a damn, struggling through a wind tunnel. The game represents these challenges by requiring the player to tap a button repeatedly. Sadly, that mechanic isn't used enough.

The parts of the game that were most challenging (and sometimes frustrating) are the timed events. In essence, Superman must run an obstacle course before time runs out. If he fails...the screen goes white.

OH NO, SUPERMAN MUST BE DEAD!

Ahem. Given that Superman is near immortal, it's difficult to comprehend losing the game because, say, he didn't successful stave off a wind tunnel. So what? Superman would probably end up destroying the fan behind him without a scratch on him. Batman's mortality is precisely what raises the stakes - in Superman, it's hard to feel a sense of urgency for a man of steel.

At one point, Lex releases Metallo and encourages him to go after Superman. But Metallo, a cyborg, was originally created by Lex Luthor and ultimately betrayed by him by removing Metallo's head from his body. The first order of business for Metallo is to go after Lex.

The best part of the game is when Metallo shows up at Lex's office.

LEX: "Hello, Metallo. I was expecting to you."
METALLO: "Good, now stand right still while I remove YOUR head from YOUR body."
LEX: "Mercy?"

Lex nods towards Mercy, his female bodyguard who is carrying a large machinegun.

METALLO: "Not even if you beg."
LEX: "No you idiot, I mean her, behind you."
METALLO: "Do you seriously think I'm going to fall for-"

And that's when Mercy cuts loose with her machinegun, inflicting absolutely no damage whatsoever to Metallo. Unfortunately, Superman steps in at that point. It's telling that the best part of the game is a cut scene.

Overall, Superman: Shadow of Apokolips is an excellent realization of everyone's favorite superhero. Unfortunately, the game developers had difficulty providing challenges for the man of steel.

title: This bluetooth speaker makes me feel like I'm in a theatre when watching movies or listening to music
text:
I had been eying up the [[ASIN:B00B981XQC Ion Audio Job Rocker Bluetooth Portable Jobsite Sound System]] for a while. I was interested in a highly rated Bluetooth speaker because I had been using my [[ASIN:B00MPMK3GW Goal Zero 94014 Rock Out 2 Green Solar Rechargeable Speaker]] with my Google Nexus 7 since last year but was disappointed with it because that was the only device that the speaker would work with. I could not use it successfully with my HP OMEN Gaming Notebook or my boyfriend's iPhone 5 or iPad 3.

I almost purchased the old Job Rocker but did not like that it did not have a USB port. Therefore, when I saw that this recently released Block Rocker IPA76C was on sale at Costco for $119.99 plus tax, I purchased one immediately and I am thrilled that I did.

FEATURES

- This Bluetooth speaker pairs beautifully with my Nexus 7, my boyfriend's iPad 3 & iPhone 5, my BLU Life One 4G LTE SmartPhone that I use only as a portable tablet, and my HP OMEN. All I had to do was press the Bluetooth button on the speaker after I activated Bluetooth on the devices.

- There's an auxiliary cable with stereo 3.5mm (1/8") input that can be used to connect a CD or MP3 player and such to the unit.

- A microphone is supplied with volume control. At first I had trouble getting the MIC to work but once I turned off Bluetooth, it worked okay. It's not a great microphone but good enough.

- There's AM/FM radio with 6 presets and a "rubber" covered antenna.

- This Block Rocker can be paired / linked with another one for even more amplified power.

- There's an On/Off power switch in the back.

- It has wheels, side carrying grips, and a luggage handle making it portable enough to roll it around like luggage.

- There are two 5V 1A USB ports for charging devices. I charged my phone with this port.

- When not connected to a wall outlet via the supplied power plug, the internal battery is rated at 75 plus or minus hours of battery life depending on conditions associated with temperature, age of battery, and volume usage of the speaker.

- The manual also says that it can be left plugged in indefinitely and it will not damage the battery (for those like me, who are not planning on taking this to a job site or garden party).

I'm truly impressed with the sound and functionality of this speaker; so impressed that I am tempted to buy another one. In addition to home use as a theatre producing surround sound experience, this would also be great for outdoor parties and construction sites and such where there is limited or no electricity.

I will update this review if I experience any issues but so far it's WONDERFUL! As I was leaving Costco, one of their employees said I was going to love it as he purchased one the day before. Also, at another Costco today, they were sold out when I went looking for another one.

In the comments section of this review, I attached a link to someone else's great video review on this product. He does a great job of explaining the features of this unit.
